title: [Bug]: Corrupt PNG image in request returns HTTP 500 "broken PNG file (chunk ...)" instead of a client error
body:
### Your current environment
Output of python vllm/collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 CMake version : Could not collect Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.14.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 Python platform : Linux-5.15.0-198-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H100 PCIe Nvidia driver version : 550.163.01 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM version : 0.32.1rc1.dev117+gdf3bd094a (nightly) VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT : df3bd094aeea829f27baa0a5282830464f601d9f VLLM_IMAGE_TAG : vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-df3bd094aeea829f27baa0a5282830464f601d9f VLLM_USAGE_SOURCE : production-docker-image ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug A chat completion request containing a **structurally-corrupted PNG** (garbage chunk header after a truncated IDAT stream) returns **HTTP 500** with the raw Pillow exception message, instead of a client-side 400 error. Sending invalid image data is a client problem, so it should fail fast with a clear 400 like other malformed images do. Minimal reproduction — serve any vision-language model (reproduced with `google/gemma-4-26b-A4B-it` on the nightly above; the failure is in the model-agnostic media loading path) and send: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:8003/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it", "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "What color is this image?"}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAQAAAAECAYAAACp8Z5+AAAAFElEQVR42mP8z8DAwMDAwMDAwMDAwMAAAA4AAf8Cq842iQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="}} ] }] }' ``` Actual response (HTTP 500): ```json {"error":{"message":"broken PNG file (chunk b'\\x00\\x00IE')","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}} ``` Expected: HTTP 400 with a message like `Failed to load image: broken PNG file (chunk ...)`, consistent with the other malformed-image paths. For comparison, the **same server** already returns a proper 400 for other corrupt input: - random non-image bytes → `400 BadRequestError: Failed to load image: cannot identify image file <_io.BytesIO object>` - truncated PNG → `400` (OSError path) Only the chunk-structure corruption takes the 500 path. ### Root cause `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` (`vllm/multimodal/media/image.py`) wraps decode failures in a client-facing `ValueError`, but its except clause only catches `(OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)`. Pillow raises a plain **`SyntaxError`** ("broken PNG file") for corrupted chunk structures — which is neither — so it escapes unwrapped, and the request-level error mapper only promotes `ValueError` to `BadRequestError` (unmapped exceptions become `InternalServerError`). ### Related work (not a duplicate) #60303 / #60308 cover the sibling case where Pillow raises `DecompressionBombError` from the same except clause. That PR does not cover `SyntaxError`, so this case is still broken on the latest nightly (`df3bd094a`, verified above). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: v0.32.0 official image: deepep_v2 fails with ZeroDivisionError after ibstat bandwidth detection fails
body:
### Your current environment

Container image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0 (official upstream image, no custom vLLM modifications)

Deployment: Kubernetes, using LeaderWorkerSet

Hardware: 2 nodes, each with 8 × NVIDIA B300-SXM6-AC GPUs

NVIDIA driver: 580.178.04

Python: 3.12

Model: GLM-5.3, loaded from a local directory

Parallelism: TP=8, DP=2, PP=1, expert parallelism enabled (EP=16)

All-to-all backend: deepep_v2

Networking: InfiniBand with mlx5 adapters

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Using the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0` image, a two-node GLM-5.3 deployment fails during initialization with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`.

The workers load the checkpoint, but during model post-processing / DeepEP initialization they report that `ibstat` cannot be executed. Startup then fails with `ZeroDivisionError` in `deep_ep/buffers/elastic.py`, inside `get_theoretical_num_sms()`.

This happened across two consecutive startup attempts, with failures on workers on both nodes. The server never became ready.

### Deployment configuration

Each node has 8 × NVIDIA B300 GPUs. The deployment uses TP=8, DP=2, PP=1, and expert parallelism enabled, giving EP=16.

Relevant arguments from the failing deployment are shown below. This is the observed configuration, not a separately validated minimal reproducer. `<DP_RANK>` is 0 on the leader and 1 on the other node; `<LEADER_IP>` is the leader's reachable address.

```bash
vllm serve /models/glm-5.3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --distributed-timeout-seconds 1800 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --data-parallel-rank "<DP_RANK>" \
  --data-parallel-address "<LEADER_IP>" \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_v2 \
  --max-model-len 524288 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45
```

### Actual behavior

vLLM selects `DeepEPV2All2AllManager`. After checkpoint loading, workers report:

```text
Failed to get RDMA connection speed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'ibstat'
```

Initialization then fails with the following traceback.

The log export reordered some lines sharing the same timestamp. The traceback below has been reconstructed into call order using the recorded frames and source lines; timestamps and pod prefixes have been removed.

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 920, in worker_main
    worker = WorkerProc(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 687, in __init__
    self.worker.load_model()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 594, in load_model
    self.model_runner.load_model(load_dummy_weights=load_dummy_weights)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/tracing/otel.py", line 175, in sync_wrapper
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 396, in load_model
    self.model = model or model_loader.load_model(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/base_loader.py", line 109, in load_model
    process_weights_after_loading(model, model_config, target_device)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py", line 180, in process_weights_after_loading
    quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(module)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 760, in process_weights_after_loading
    self._init_moe_kernel(layer)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 700, in _init_moe_kernel
    self._setup_kernel(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 693, in _setup_kernel
    self.moe_kernel = make_fp8_moe_kernel(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py", line 847, in make_fp8_moe_kernel
    prepare_finalize = maybe_make_prepare_finalize(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/all2all_utils.py", line 291, in maybe_make_prepare_finalize
    handle = all2all_manager.get_handle(all_to_all_args)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py", line 1181, in get_handle
    self._num_sms = handle.get_theoretical_num_sms(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/deep_ep/utils/semantic.py", line 23, in inner
    return _func(weakref.ref(self), *args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/deep_ep/utils/semantic.py", line 19, in _func
    return func(_self(), *args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/deep_ep/buffers/elastic.py", line 662, in get_theoretical_num_sms
    if self.num_scaleout_ranks > 1 and (rdma_traffic / rdma_gbs) > (nvlink_traffic / nvlink_gbs):
ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
```

### Suspected cause

The RDMA bandwidth probe cannot execute `ibstat`. DeepEP's bandwidth detection returns zero on failure, which is subsequently used in the SM-count calculation without a sufficient validity check.

The logs establish that `ibstat` is unavailable to the worker process. I have not yet independently confirmed whether the executable is absent from the image or outside the process's `PATH`, nor whether making it available is sufficient for startup to complete.

### Expected behavior

- The official image should include the runtime utilities required by its supported DeepEP backend, or clearly document any additional prerequisites.
- Required utilities should ideally be checked before the lengthy checkpoint-loading stage.
- Failed bandwidth detection should produce an actionable error identifying the missing prerequisite, rather than an unhandled division by zero.

Could you confirm whether `infiniband-diags` should be included in the official image, and whether the bandwidth-validation fix should be handled in vLLM, DeepEP, or both?

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: `cudagraph_mode=FULL` + FA3 split-KV returns wrong logits: the combine kernel's tile scheduler is chosen from the capture-time dummy batch
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.30.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0`), torch 2.13.0+cu130
- 8× H100 80GB SXM (also reproduced on 8× H200)
- FLASH_ATTN backend (FA3, vllm-project/flash-attention @ 506341a)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--compilation-config.cudagraph_mode=FULL` and FA3, some steps that replay a captured graph return wrong logits: errors of several nats, a different argmax, and sometimes the correct token missing from the top-20. Setting `--attention-config.flash_attn_max_num_splits_for_cuda_graph=1` (default 32), which turns split-KV off inside captured graphs, fixes it. The default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` mode and FlashInfer are not affected.

We see two triggers:

- **A. Exactly 2 new tokens on a prefix-cache hit**, with any `max_num_seqs`.
- **B. Small `max_num_seqs`** (16 and below; also some large graphs at 64): ordinary prefills, including cache misses, that replay a mixed-batch FULL graph.

#### Repro (trigger A)

`Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, TP=1, synthetic prompt. Cache a 128-token prefix, then run a prompt that extends it by `q` tokens, so the step computes exactly `q` new tokens:

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt

def run(**kw):
    llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-8B", enable_prefix_caching=True, block_size=16,
              max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85, **kw)
    ids = llm.get_tokenizer()(" ".join(f"item {i} is red;" for i in range(200))).input_ids[:256]
    out = {}
    for q in (1, 2, 3):
        llm.reset_prefix_cache()
        llm.generate([TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids[:128])], SamplingParams(max_tokens=1), use_tqdm=False)
        o = llm.generate([TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids[:128 + q])],
                         SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0, logprobs=5), use_tqdm=False)[0]
        tok = o.outputs[0].token_ids[0]
        out[q] = (tok, o.outputs[0].logprobs[0][tok].logprob)
    print(kw, out)

run(compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL"})
# run(compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL"},
#     attention_config={"flash_attn_max_num_splits_for_cuda_graph": 1})
# run(compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"})
```

Compare each `q` against `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, or against prefix caching off. In our grid (6 prompts, cached lengths 64 / 128 / 176, q = 1–32), q = 2 was wrong at 11 of 17 points, with errors ≥ 3 nats. All other q stayed within bf16 noise (≤ 0.19). Public models, synthetic prompts:

| Model / TP | Q / KV heads per rank | Wrong points (all at q = 2, cached 128 / 176) | Max error |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3-32B, TP=8 | 8 / 1 | 4/48 | 4.5 nats |
| Qwen/Qwen3-8B, TP=1 | 32 / 8 | 4/48 | correct token falls out of top-20 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-8B, TP=8 | 4 / 1 | 0/48 | < 0.0005 |

With a cached length of 64, q = 2 is correct: the KV is short enough that it is not split.

#### Root cause

The FA3 combine kernel, which merges the split-KV partial results, picks its tile scheduler and grid on the host from the arguments of the call that is being captured. The CUDA graph freezes both.

1. **Capture uses a dummy batch.** vLLM captures mixed-batch FULL graphs with `num_reqs = min(num_tokens, max_num_seqs)` dummy requests ([`cudagraph_utils.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L305), [`input_batch.py` `make_dummy`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py#L142-L152)). The captured call therefore sees `max_seqlen_q = ceil(num_tokens / num_reqs)` ([`model_states/default.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/default.py#L189-L195)). Example: the 168-token graph at `max_num_seqs=16` has b = 16 and `max_seqlen_q` = 11.
2. **The scheduler is chosen on the host.** [`StaticVarlenTileScheduler::choose_scheduling_algo`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/506341a143fcabd4bb79052a7605ada727d6b3f5/hopper/flash_fwd_combine_kernel.h#L279-L287) picks STANDARD when `2 * ceil(total_q / kBlockM) >= b * ceil(max_seqlen_q / kBlockM)`, otherwise LINEARIZE_M_AND_BATCH. For head dim 128, `kBlockM = 8` ([launch template](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/506341a143fcabd4bb79052a7605ada727d6b3f5/hopper/flash_fwd_combine_launch_template.h#L68)). In the example, `2 × 21 = 42 ≥ 16 × 2 = 32`, so STANDARD is chosen.
3. **STANDARD binds CTAs to requests.** Its grid is `(ceil(max_seqlen_q * h / 8), k_blocks, b)` ([`get_grid_shape`](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/506341a143fcabd4bb79052a7605ada727d6b3f5/hopper/flash_fwd_combine_kernel.h#L302-L318)), here `(11, 1, 16)`: each request gets 11 CTAs through `blockIdx.z`. This is the launch configuration the graph records.
4. **Replay runs a different batch on the frozen grid.** One request with 161 tokens replays the graph, because dispatch only checks the `num_tokens` / `num_reqs` upper bounds ([`_is_compatible`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L102-L126)). The kernel reads the real `cu_seqlens`: 161 × 8 = 1,288 rows, which need 161 tiles. Request 0 still has only 11 CTAs, so only rows 0–87 are combined. Rows are head-major ([L476-483](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/506341a143fcabd4bb79052a7605ada727d6b3f5/hopper/flash_fwd_combine_kernel.h#L476-L483)), so only head 0's tokens 0–87 get a final value. Every other output row keeps whatever was in the buffer. The 15 padded requests have length 0, so their CTAs return ([L443-454](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/blob/506341a143fcabd4bb79052a7605ada727d6b3f5/hopper/flash_fwd_combine_kernel.h#L443-L454)).

This rule predicts every case we measured:

| Case | Captured b × `max_seqlen_q` | STANDARD tiles vs `2 × lower bound` | Chosen | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 168-token graph, `max_num_seqs` 8–40 | 8×21 … 40×5 | 24 … 40 ≤ 42 | STANDARD | wrong |
| 168-token graph, `max_num_seqs` 48 / 56 / 64 | 48×4 … 64×3 | 48 … 64 > 42 | LINEARIZE | correct |
| 2-token graph (trigger A) | 2×1 | 2 ≤ 2 | STANDARD, 1 row per request | 2nd token of a 1 × 2 replay is never combined |
| Graphs ≥ 256 tokens, `max_num_seqs=64` | 64 × ≥ 4 | 64 ≤ `2·ceil(N/8)` | STANDARD | long prompts wrong when KV is split |
| Split cap 2 / 4 / 16, `max_num_seqs=16` | 16×11 | 32 ≤ 42 | STANDARD | wrong |
| Split cap 1 | — | — | no combine | correct |

We predicted the `max_num_seqs` 40 / 48 / 56 / 64 and split-cap cases before running them.

A torch profiler trace of the 1 × 161-token replay shows the frozen grid directly (one combine launch per layer):

| Config | `FlashAttnFwdCombine` grid at replay | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `max_num_seqs=16` | `[11, 1, 16]` (STANDARD) | wrong |
| `max_num_seqs=48` | `[216, 1, 1]` (LINEARIZE, `ceil(168·8/8) + 48`) | correct |
| `max_num_seqs=16`, split cap 1 | no combine launch | correct |

#### Workaround

`--attention-config.flash_attn_max_num_splits_for_cuda_graph=1`. This turns split-KV off inside captured graphs, so the combine kernel never runs. For long-KV, few-new-token steps it may cost latency.

#### Possible fixes

- **FA3:** for the varlen combine, always use LINEARIZE_M_AND_BATCH when the call can be captured, for example when `scheduler_metadata` is passed or `num_splits` is fixed. Its grid depends only on `total_q` and `b`, which are the padded values and the same at capture and replay. Each CTA then finds its request at run time.
- **vLLM:** capture mixed-batch FULL graphs with `max_seqlen_q = num_tokens`, an upper bound, instead of `ceil(num_tokens / num_reqs)`. We have not validated this. `max_seqlen_q` also drives main-kernel choices: the main kernel's block size already follows the capture shape (384 vs 256 threads in the traces above). This fix could therefore change performance.

#### Possibly related

- #57822

title: [Bug]: TurboQuant on hybrid (GDN) models: manager block cannot be split into kernel blocks, and a quantized-KV drafter inflates all KV pages (pool 97k vs 235k tokens)
body:
### Your current environment

collect_env.py was not run on the serving host (container without a Python environment for it); the relevant facts, taken from the running server:

Hardware: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB, 64 KB LDS per workgroup), power limit 250 W
vLLM: 0.32.0rc1.dev281 (vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly), ROCm 7.2.3, PyTorch 2.13.0, Triton 3.8.0
Model: Qwen3.5-27B-class hybrid (16 full-attention + 48 GDN layers, head_dim 256, 4 KV heads, vocab 248320), MXFP4 W4A8
Serve flags (relevant): --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc --kv-cache-memory-bytes 6535819798 --max-model-len 131072 --block-size 16 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2560 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"(fp8 drafter checkpoint)","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8"}'

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Disclosure: this report was investigated and written with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code), working on my hardware under my direction. The numbers are my own measurements and I reviewed the text.

Problem 1, startup fails. With --mamba-cache-mode align the attention block becomes 1712 tokens (--block-size 16 is ignored). TurboQuantAttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes returns [16, 32, 64, 128], so the manager block is split into 107 kernel blocks and startup fails with: "The resolved KV cache layout (LBNHC) does not store blocks as dense, unpadded pages (block stride 3506176 != page 1794176), so a manager block cannot be split into 107 kernel blocks of 16 tokens." Returning [MultipleOf(16)] lets the manager block be used as one kernel block. The TQ Triton kernels use BLOCK_SIZE only for // and %, so a non-power-of-two value works.

Problem 2, the KV pool is much smaller than it should be. After that change the server starts, but with a GPU KV cache of 97,517 tokens instead of 235,605 at the same --kv-cache-memory-bytes. The fp8 drafter layers cost 2048 B/token, so at block 1712 their page is 3.5 MB while the TQ and mamba pages are 1.79 MB. unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size then pads every page to the largest one (3.5 MB). Giving the drafter layers the largest divisor of 1712 whose page fits the TQ page (856, padded to the common page) makes all pages equal again and restores 235,605 tokens (fp8 KV on the same stack: 137,124). The drafter's TRITON_ATTN backend then has to accept block sizes that are multiples of 8 (its kernel computes seq_offset // BLOCK_SIZE per element and handles this fine).

Also for gfx1201 (not a bug in vLLM itself): the SoA unified kernel is only used when FlyDSL is available (gfx950). Forcing it on gfx1201 works once fuse_q_rot is off (the 256x256 fp32 PiT is 262,144 B against 65,536 B of LDS, which gives OutOfResources: shared memory) and the prefill tile is at most 32 rows.

Result with the changes, via an OpenAI-compatible router: a 235,605-token pool (1.72x fp8 KV), decode on code prompts 115 tok/s (fp8 KV on the same stack: 116.5), a 20-task coding set with executed tests on par with fp8 KV (76-80/80 per set of 4 runs, run-to-run noise 17-20/20), 10/10 valid tool calls.

Related: #53334 (TurboQuant init failure on a hybrid model), #55312 (draft and target KV layouts), #41153 (page size unification for a hybrid model), #40914 (K+1 spec-verify routing; I added a data point there).

The changes are small and env-gated on our side. I can turn them into a PR if the direction is acceptable.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Sending a JPEG whose EXIF orientation tag is not 1 (e.g. any Samsung phone photo, orientation 6) to a VLM served with `--tokenizer-mode mistral` fails with HTTP 500: ```text {"error":{"message":"Expected there to be 1 prompt placeholders corresponding to 1 image items, but instead found 0 prompt placeholders! Make sure the implementation of `_apply_hf_processor_main` and `_get_mm_fields_config` are consistent with each other.","type":"InternalServerError","code":500}} ``` - Orientation 1 images work. - Orientation 6/8 (90°/270°) always fail with the error above. - Orientation 3 (180°) does **not** fail, but the model receives pixels in a different layout than mistral_common's own decode (silent inconsistency: the model answers orientation questions as if the image was pre-rotated, while the `[IMG]` token grid was computed from the un-rotated decode). **Root cause** (identified while debugging): with `--tokenizer-mode mistral`, the prompt is rendered by mistral_common's chat template, which decodes the image from the original bytes **without** applying the EXIF transpose. vLLM's `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` applies it (`normalize_image`, introduced in #44974). For orientations that swap width/height (6/8), the image token grid computed from the two decodes disagrees, so placeholder validation finds 0 `[IMG]` placeholders for 1 image item. The two decodes must agree. ### To Reproduce 1. Serve any mistral-format VLM, e.g.: ```bash vllm serve unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-FP8 \ --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral ``` 2. Send a chat completion containing an EXIF-6 JPEG (any Samsung portrait photo) via `POST /v1/chat/completions` with an `image_url` data-URI. 3. Observed: HTTP 500 with the placeholder error. The same image re-encoded with orientation stripped returns 200. Minimal generator for the four common orientations (identical pixels, only the tag differs — `pip install pillow`): ```python import base64, io from PIL import Image img = Image.new("RGB", (640, 480), (30, 30, 200)) # any non-square content for orientation in (1, 3, 6, 8): exif = Image.Exif(); exif[0x0112] = orientation buf = io.BytesIO(); img.save(buf, "JPEG", exif=exif) print(orientation, len(base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()))) # send each variant: 6/8 -> 500; 3 -> 200 but wrong pixel layout ``` Note: the image must be **non-square** — a square image produces the same token grid with or without the transpose and does not trigger the 500. ### Expected behavior EXIF-oriented images are served normally (HTTP 200), with vLLM's decode matching the mistral_common chat-template decode — the same behavior as the reference mistral_common inference stack. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

The code involved is unchanged in v0.32.0 and in `main` at 371745e. ### 🐛 Describe the bug Since #59533 (merged on 2026-10-05, first released in v0.32.0), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4Exp`) checkpoints that quantize the full-attention `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` but keep the QSA indexer projection `indexer.index_qk_proj` unquantized no longer load. Model construction stops at the first QSA layer: ```text ValueError: Found different quantization schemes for the shards of language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.qkv_proj. vLLM requires all to use the same scheme. ``` Before #59533 the indexer projection was a separate layer, so these checkpoints loaded. The checkpoint below was validated by its author on vLLM 0.29. ### Reproduce ```bash vllm serve ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ \ --revision 598afc96128f76a67117caf878f538d34f6f1e02 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel ``` - The checkpoint is compressed-tensors W4A16 (`pack-quantized`, `targets: ["Linear"]`). Its `ignore` list contains `model.language_model.layers..self_attn.indexer.index_qk_proj` for every QSA layer. - We ran it on 4x A100-40GB with more serving flags (context length, KV cache, multimodal limits). The error is raised while the layers are constructed, before any weights are loaded, so those flags should not matter. - Adding `--enable-lora --max-loras 1 --max-lora-rank 8` gives the same error at the same line.

ValueError( ValueError: Found different quantization schemes for the shards of language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.qkv_proj. vLLM requires all to use the same scheme. ```
### Root cause 1. `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` includes `indexer.index_qk_proj` ([model.py#L704](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.32.0/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/model.py#L704)). `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` reuses it. 2. `configure_quant_config` gives this class-level dict to the quant config before the model is built ([model_loader/utils.py#L88](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.32.0/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py#L88), [#L381](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.32.0/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py#L381)). 3. So even the plain `QKVParallelLinear` at [qsa.py#L410](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.32.0/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/qsa.py#L410), built before any fusion, is checked as a four-shard fused layer. compressed-tensors sees q/k/v quantized and the indexer ignored, and raises ([compressed_tensors/utils.py#L67](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.32.0/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py#L67)). `is_layer_skipped` in `quantization/utils/quant_utils.py` and `is_layer_gptq_quantized` in `quantization/utils/gptq_utils.py` have the same "all shards same precision" check, so GPTQ, AutoRound and FP8 checkpoints with this layout probably fail the same way (not tested). 4. The LoRA branch ([model.py#L724-L727](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.32.0/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/model.py#L724-L727)) rebinds `self.packed_modules_mapping` on the instance, but the quant config keeps the class dict from step 2. That is why `--enable-lora` does not avoid the error, although the indexer is not fused in that mode. ModelOpt FP4 is already special-cased with `without_modelopt_fp4`. Other formats are not. Changing the checkpoint's `ignore` list does not help. It describes how the weights are stored (q/k/v packed INT4, `index_qk_proj` BF16). The fourth shard comes from vLLM's `packed_modules_mapping`, not from the checkpoint. ### Scope We read `model.safetensors.index.json` of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next quantized checkpoints on the Hub (2026-10-18). In 26 of the 82 quantized (non-GGUF, non-MLX) checkpoints we could inspect, layer 3 `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` carry quantization tensors and `index_qk_proj` has only `.weight`. Examples with compressed-tensors and the indexer in `ignore`: - `davetha/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DERISKED-W4A16-AWQ` - `VnimanieAI/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16` - `primitive-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-mixed-NVFP4-FP8` - `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ` `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` and `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` leave attention unquantized and are not affected. ### Workaround we use A runtime patch sets `packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` to `["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"]` on both model classes and turns `fuse_indexer_projection` off. With it, the Swift checkpoint loads on 4x A100-40GB (TP4 + EP) and passes our functional and speed smoke tests. The indexer then runs as its own GEMM, as before #59533. ### Proposed fix Fuse the indexer into `qkv_proj` only when `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and `index_qk_proj` resolve to the same quantization. Otherwise keep the indexer as its own layer, and give the quant config a packed mapping that matches that decision (per model instance, not the class dict). This also fixes the `--enable-lora` path. I would like to send a PR for this. @gau-nernst, does this direction fit #59533, or do you prefer another approach? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Problem.** With `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` and `--enable-sleep-mode`, a start with empty compile caches (first start after install or upgrade) of the command below fails while allocating the KV cache (`allocate_kv_cache`, `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`):

```text
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 4.46 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.82 GiB of which 946.25 MiB is free. Of the allocated memory 26.80 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 4.76 GiB allocated in private pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 2.35 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.
```

With warm caches the same command started in our tests, so the failure looks intermittent. Seen with both `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and `nvfp4`. The model's weights are NVFP4, which is where the buffer below comes from; other weight formats were not tested, but the missing guards are not format-specific. v0.31.0 also lacks both in this branch (not run).

**Cause.** The `kv_cache_memory_bytes` branch of `Worker.determine_available_memory()` runs `profile_run()` without either allocator guard that the memory-profiling branch has:

1. **No cache release.** `memory_profiling` runs `gc.collect()` and `empty_cache()` on exit; this branch does not, so fully free cached segments (2.4 GiB here) stay reserved. The open PR #59893 adds this release.
2. **No split limit.** #58430 runs the memory-profiling `profile_run()` inside `_scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20)`; this branch does not. A snapshot just before KV allocation (both instrumented unpatched cold starts) showed a 2,426 MiB segment kept reserved by a single live 40 MiB FlashInfer scratch buffer (`flashinfer/utils.py` `_get_cache_buf`, from `mm_fp4`). `empty_cache()` cannot release that segment while the scratch buffer remains live; with #59893 alone, device-free memory also stayed lower after start-up and after a 10,408-token request.

With sleep mode the KV cache is allocated in the separate CuMem pool, so these retained default-pool reservations reduce the device memory available to it. `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` also sets `kv_cache_memory_bytes` (from a saved plan), so those starts take the same branch.

**Fix.** #59893 plus the split limit on the same `profile_run()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`, on top of #59893):

```diff
         if kv_cache_memory_bytes := self.cache_config.kv_cache_memory_bytes:
             # still need a profile run which compiles the model for
             # max_num_batched_tokens
-            with set_current_vllm_config(self.vllm_config):
+            # Same allocator split limit as the memory-profiling branch below.
+            with (
+                self._scoped_allocator_max_split(max_split_size_mb=20),
+                set_current_vllm_config(self.vllm_config),
+            ):
                 self.model_runner.profile_run(
                     randomize_inputs=self.randomize_dummy_inputs
                 )
```

#59893's test then needs the real scope on its stand-in worker (one statement, in the suggestion on that PR). With both, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py` passes on main `1b2a666` (26 tests, including #59893's GPU test), and so do vLLM's pre-commit hooks. The suggested source and test changes are posted on #59893; this report does not propose a separate PR.

**Verification** (vLLM nightly `0.32.0rc1.dev35+g656d0d450`). `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, 4.5 GiB KV budget, sleep mode. All rows used empty vLLM, inductor and Triton cache folders; in the last two rows, every start also completed a short request and a 10,408-token prompt:

| | KV dtype | Starts | Free before KV allocation | Free after the 10K request | Engine init | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unpatched | fp8 / nvfp4 | 3 / 1 | 3.49 GiB (2 measured) | - | - | OOM every time |
| Split limit only | fp8 / nvfp4 | 3 / 2 | 4.59 to 4.66 GiB | - | - | Starts |
| #59893 only | fp8 / nvfp4 | 2 / 2 | 5.79 to 5.81 GiB | 1.02 to 1.09 GiB | 94.2 to 107.6 s | Starts, serves |
| #59893 + split limit | fp8 / nvfp4 | 1 / 1 | 8.64 GiB | 2.15 to 2.27 GiB | 73.8 to 74.4 s | Starts, serves |

The last two rows were measured on the same day, with about 0.81 GiB of other GPU usage before start-up; engine-init times are as observed, not explained. The same code with a different comment wording also started 5 of 5 cold starts (fp8 2, nvfp4 3) with 8.64 GiB free before KV allocation. The open PR #56698 also avoided this OOM in our tests: it removes this branch, so pinned sizes are profiled and checked against an estimate; it targets a different failure (a pin too large for the activation peak).

Related but distinct: #54122 and #54209 concern cold-compilation peaks inflating activation estimates on the `--gpu-memory-utilization` path. The pinned path skips that sizing calculation, and #54209 resets peak counters without releasing cached memory or preventing live scratch buffers from pinning segments.

Workaround until fixed: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:20` (CUDA graph memory rose from 0.25 to 2.42 GiB here).

**Reproduce.**

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/cold/vllm /tmp/cold/inductor /tmp/cold/triton
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/cold/vllm TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/cold/inductor TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/cold/triton \
vllm serve unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --max-model-len 98304 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4831838208 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --enable-sleep-mode --language-model-only --max-num-seqs 2
```

Use new empty folders for each attempt; with warm caches it started in our tests.

Background: found while testing NVFP4 KV cache on SM120 (#46963, #60452). On v0.30.0, FP8 was the smallest KV cache type on this GPU; NVFP4 fits 54% to 57% more tokens in the same budget (Qwen3.8-27B: 109,794 to 169,082; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 157,640 to 248,200).

AI assistance (Claude Code, reviewed by Codex) was used for the investigation, the tests and this write-up.

### 🐛 Describe the bug For a tool parameter whose schema admits both `string` and `integer` (`"type": ["string", "integer"]`, or the equivalent `anyOf`), the Qwen3 engine tool parser (`qwen3_coder`, `qwen3_xml`, `mimo`) coerces the raw parameter text with `vllm.tool_parsers.utils.coerce_to_schema_type`. That function tries `integer` before `string` and returns `int(value)` whenever `int()` succeeds. A string value that only looks like an integer therefore reaches the client as a different integer: - `0017` becomes `17` (leading zeros lost), - `1_000` becomes `1000`, - `+17` becomes `17`. Quoting the value does not help: `"0017"` is kept as a string that includes the quote characters (`"\"0017\""`). For such a parameter, no model output can deliver the string `"0017"` to the client. We hit this in practice with Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B served through the OpenAI-compatible server. The user message asked the model to pass the **string** `'0017'`; the model wrote `\n0017\n`, and the client received `{"value": 17}`. Re-sampling the same request through `/v1/completions` (no tool parser) showed the model writing `0017` in every sample. Leading zeros and similar forms matter for identifiers, ZIP codes, account numbers and version components, and the change is silent to the application. Minimal reproduction (only the tokenizer is downloaded; no GPU or model weights needed): ```python from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager from vllm.tool_parsers.utils import coerce_to_schema_type # 1. The coercion helper used by the Qwen3 engine parser. for raw in ["0017", "1_000", "+17", '"0017"']: print(f"coerce_to_schema_type({raw!r}, ['string', 'integer']) -> {coerce_to_schema_type(raw, ['string', 'integer'])!r}") # 2. End to end through the stock qwen3_coder tool parser. tools = [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "normalize_count", "description": "Normalize a decimal count supplied as a string or integer.", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"value": {"type": ["string", "integer"]}}, "required": ["value"], }, }, }] request = ChatCompletionRequest( model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Call normalize_count with value the STRING '0017'."}], tools=tools, ) parser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("qwen3_coder")(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B")) for raw in ["0017", '"0017"']: model_output = ( "\n\n\n" f"{raw}\n\n\n" ) result = parser.extract_tool_calls(model_output, request) print(f"model writes {raw!r} -> arguments {result.tool_calls[0].function.arguments}") ``` Output with vLLM 0.31.0: ```text coerce_to_schema_type('0017', ['string', 'integer']) -> 17 coerce_to_schema_type('1_000', ['string', 'integer']) -> 1000 coerce_to_schema_type('+17', ['string', 'integer']) -> 17 coerce_to_schema_type('"0017"', ['string', 'integer']) -> '"0017"' model writes '0017' -> arguments {"value": 17} model writes '"0017"' -> arguments {"value": "\"0017\""} ``` The same code path is present on `main` (da9134bc89364465f68aa679564435936d157a14): `coerce_to_schema_type` in `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` still returns `int(value)` for the `integer` candidate before considering `string`. **Expected behavior.** When `string` is an admissible type, coercion should preserve what the model wrote. One option is to accept a numeric coercion only when it round-trips to the original text, e.g. `str(int(value)) == value` for `integer` (and the analogous check for `number`), and otherwise fall back to the next type, which is `string`. `0017`, `1_000` and `+17` are also not valid JSON integer literals, so leaving them as strings matches what the model wrote. **Related.** #47179 discusses Rust/Python divergences in union coercion, and #47203 aligns the Rust frontend with the Python precedence (`null > integer > ... > string`). Neither covers the information loss for non-canonical integer text, which the Rust frontend would inherit after #47203. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Summary: - vLLM 0.31.0, CPU wheel `vllm-0.31.0+cpu-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_39_x86_64.whl`, torch 2.13.0+cpu, Python 3.12.3 - Ubuntu 24.04.5 on WSL2 (kernel 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), 48 GB RAM given to WSL - AMD Ryzen 7 5800H (Zen 3): AVX2 only, no AVX-512, so the `_C_AVX2` kernels are used - The server was started with `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14` and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` (collect-env was run from a separate shell, so they are not listed above); the per-CPU vulnerability lines were omitted from the collect-env output ### 🐛 Describe the bug On the CPU backend, when a server is started with `--enable-lora`, requests to the **base model** (no LoRA) that are scheduled in the same batch as **LoRA** requests are computed **with the adapter applied**. It sends 40 greedy prompts in three phases: base alone (concurrency 8), LoRA alone (concurrency 8), then base and LoRA interleaved (concurrency 16). It then compares the outputs. ```bash python repro_mixed_lora.py --base base --lora lora ``` Expected: `base mixed == base alone` is 40/40, and `base mixed == lora alone` is about 0. Actual: ```text prompts: 40 base alone == lora alone (sanity, should be ~0): 0/40 base mixed == base alone (expected 40): 0/40 base mixed == lora alone (expected ~0): 35/40 lora mixed == lora alone (expected 40): 40/40 example, prompt 0: 'Write one sentence about the number 0 and name a fruit.' base alone: 'The number zero is a fundamental concept in mathematics, representing the absence of quantity or the absence of a quantity. In the context of the number zero, it is' base mixed: "'])?…ory粉手_through.addHandlerrom啖 modelAndView明llHasColumnTypeリングHasColumnType楼oose逐Sort билет块userratl嗪手 term大次祁ormsghtags" lora alone: "'])?…ory粉手_through.addHandlerrom啖 modelAndView明llHasColumnTypeリングHasColumnType楼oose逐Sort билет块userratl嗪手 term大次祁ormsghtags" ``` With a random adapter the effect is unambiguous: not a single base request in the mixed phase matches its base-alone output, and 35/40 are byte-identical to the adapter's output (the base is served the random adapter's gibberish). #### Original observation (real adapters, 80-item eval) I found this while evaluating two PEFT adapters trained on a ticket-triage task. The base is `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` and the adapters are r=8 and r=32, all-linear. The server command was: ```bash vllm serve ~/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --served-model-name qwen05 --dtype float32 \ --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G --max-model-len 4096 --generation-config vllm \ --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 32 --max-loras 2 \ --lora-modules ticket=$HOME/lora/b-05b-r8 ticket32=$HOME/lora/c-r32 ``` All requests were greedy (`temperature=0`), and each eval used the same 80 prompts. | Run | Concurrency | `ticket` acc. | `ticket32` acc. | base (`qwen05`) acc. | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | each model alone | 1 | 98% | 100% | 10% | | base alone | 8 | – | – | 10% (same per-field scores) | | all three interleaved | 8 | 98% | 100% | **62%** | A per-item comparison of the base outputs in the interleaved run: - only **5/80** are identical to the base-alone output - **50/80** are byte-identical to the `ticket` output for the same prompt - **50/80** are byte-identical to the `ticket32` output for the same prompt (the two adapters agree on most items) - the rest look like a blend of base and adapter behaviour Batch non-invariance does not explain outputs that are byte-identical to the adapter's. As a control, I ran the same experiment on llama.cpp `llama-server` (b11346, f16 base + the r=8 adapter as GGUF). I mixed per-request `"lora": [{"id": 0, "scale": 0}]` (base) with `scale: 1` requests at concurrency 4 + 4. Base accuracy stayed at 8%, the same as base-only, and the adapter stayed at 96%. #### Possibly related - Enabling `--enable-lora` also slows base-only requests by about 20% on this machine. Single-request decode drops from 17.0 to 13.7 tok/s, and concurrency-8 throughput from 97.2 to 76.5 tok/s. - LoRA requests themselves are about 4.7× slower than llama.cpp on the same CPU (2.31 s vs 0.49 s per item, about 17 output tokens). I searched existing issues (`in:title lora cpu`, 42 results) and found nothing reporting this. The closest is #33704 (LoRA dtype mismatch in the XPU and CPU punica wrappers, closed as stale), which touches the same code path but is a different symptom. I have not read the CPU punica code closely. My guess is that the slot for "no LoRA" in the per-token LoRA index mapping is not being masked out on the CPU path, so those tokens pick up an active adapter's weights. I can test a patch if that helps.
make_random_lora.py ```python """Create a randomly initialised LoRA adapter for Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. init_lora_weights=False makes both A and B random (B is normally zero), so the adapter visibly changes the output. That makes any leakage into non-LoRA requests easy to spot. pip install torch transformers peft python make_random_lora.py --base Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --out ./random-lora """ import argparse import torch from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base", default="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct") ap.add_argument("--out", default="./random-lora") ap.add_argument("--r", type=int, default=8) a = ap.parse_args() torch.manual_seed(0) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(a.base, dtype=torch.float32) cfg = LoraConfig(r=a.r, lora_alpha=2 * a.r, init_lora_weights=False, task_type="CAUSAL_LM", target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"]) model = get_peft_model(model, cfg) model.save_pretrained(a.out) AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(a.base).save_pretrained(a.out) print("saved", a.out) ```
repro_mixed_lora.py ```python """Repro: non-LoRA requests batched together with LoRA requests get the adapter applied (vLLM CPU). Server (any OpenAI-compatible vLLM started with --enable-lora and one adapter, e.g. named "lora"): vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --served-model-name base --dtype float32 \ --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G --max-model-len 4096 --generation-config vllm \ --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 8 --lora-modules lora=./random-lora Then: python repro_mixed_lora.py --base base --lora lora Phase 1 sends the base prompts alone (concurrency 8), phase 2 sends lora-only (concurrency 8), phase 3 sends the same base and lora prompts interleaved (concurrency 16). All greedy (temperature 0). Expected: base outputs in phase 3 == phase 1. Only the Python standard library is used. """ import argparse import json import urllib.request from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor PROMPTS = [f"Write one sentence about the number {i} and name a fruit." for i in range(40)] def chat(url, model, prompt, max_tokens): body = json.dumps({"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max_tokens}).encode() req = urllib.request.Request(url + "/v1/chat/completions", body, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r: return json.loads(r.read())["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip() def run(url, jobs, conc, max_tokens): with ThreadPoolExecutor(conc) as ex: return list(ex.map(lambda j: chat(url, j[0], j[1], max_tokens), jobs)) def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:8000") ap.add_argument("--base", default="base", help="served model name of the base model") ap.add_argument("--lora", default="lora", help="name given in --lora-modules") ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) a = ap.parse_args() n = len(PROMPTS) base_alone = run(a.url, [(a.base, p) for p in PROMPTS], 8, a.max_tokens) lora_alone = run(a.url, [(a.lora, p) for p in PROMPTS], 8, a.max_tokens) mixed_jobs = [job for p in PROMPTS for job in ((a.base, p), (a.lora, p))] mixed = run(a.url, mixed_jobs, 16, a.max_tokens) base_mixed, lora_mixed = mixed[0::2], mixed[1::2] same_base = sum(x == y for x, y in zip(base_alone, base_mixed)) base_eq_lora = sum(x == y for x, y in zip(base_mixed, lora_alone)) same_lora = sum(x == y for x, y in zip(lora_alone, lora_mixed)) base_vs_lora_alone = sum(x == y for x, y in zip(base_alone, lora_alone)) print(f"prompts: {n}") print(f"base alone == lora alone (sanity, should be ~0): {base_vs_lora_alone}/{n}") print(f"base mixed == base alone (expected {n}): {same_base}/{n}") print(f"base mixed == lora alone (expected ~0): {base_eq_lora}/{n}") print(f"lora mixed == lora alone (expected {n}): {same_lora}/{n}") for i in range(n): if base_mixed[i] != base_alone[i]: print(f"\nexample, prompt {i}: {PROMPTS[i]!r}\n base alone: {base_alone[i]!r}" f"\n base mixed: {base_mixed[i]!r}\n lora alone: {lora_alone[i]!r}") break if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```

title: [Bug]: Model Runner V2 hangs during speculative decoding warmup with pipeline parallelism
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Description** Code version: based on `main` commit [`[de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995). With pipeline parallelism and speculative decoding enabled, Model Runner V2 runs the additional greedy warmup pass only on the last PP stage. Upstream stages skip this pass, leaving the last stage waiting for intermediate tensors that will never arrive. This can be reproduced during GLM-4.7-Flash initialization, before serving any requests. **Reproduction** Use four GPUs for TP2 × PP2. Save the following as `repro.py`: ```python from vllm import LLM if __name__ == "__main__": LLM( model="zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash", dtype="bfloat16", tensor_parallel_size=2, pipeline_parallel_size=2, distributed_executor_backend="mp", max_num_seqs=1024, max_num_batched_tokens=8192, gpu_memory_utilization=0.65, speculative_config={ "method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1, }, kernel_config={"enable_jit_warmup": True}, cpu_distributed_timeout_seconds=120, ) ``` Run: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \ VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ .venv/bin/python repro.py ``` The CPU communication timeout is shortened to 120 seconds to obtain the failure sooner. **Actual behavior** The first PP stage finishes warmup and CUDA Graph capture. The last PP stage blocks during the additional greedy warmup pass and eventually fails: ```text warmup_kernels # additional greedy=True pass → _warmup_kernels → worker_execute_model(prefill_output) → irecv_tensor_dict → recv_object → torch.distributed.recv RuntimeError: ... Timed out waiting 120000ms for recv operation to complete ``` **Relevant code** In [`[vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py#L232)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py#L232), the additional pass is gated on the rank-local sampler: ```python rejection_sampler = model_runner.rejection_sampler # ... temporarily disable adaptive verification ... try: _warmup_kernels(model_runner, worker_execute_model, worker_sample_tokens) if rejection_sampler is not None: # Greedy batches skip logits processing, so rejection kernels # also see model-dtype logits instead of FP32. _warmup_kernels( model_runner, worker_execute_model, worker_sample_tokens, greedy=True ) ``` However, [`[vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L465)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de7eeaa87bc19ecf088472d5f4471cdc9a5ab995/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L465) initializes samplers only on the last PP stage: ```python if self.is_last_pp_rank and not self.is_pooling_model: # ... initialize self.sampler ... custom = self.model_state.custom_sampler(self.sampler) if custom: self.vllm_config._check_supports_watermarking(custom_sampler=True) self.sampler, self.rejection_sampler = custom elif self.speculative_config is not None: self.rejection_sampler = RejectionSampler( self.sampler, self.speculative_config, self.device, watermark_key=speculative_target_watermark_key( self.vllm_config.watermark_config ), ) ``` Consequently, non-last stages have `rejection_sampler=None` and skip the second pass, while the last stage executes it and waits for their inputs. **Expected behavior** All PP stages should execute matching warmup forward sequences. The additional speculative warmup pass should use a condition shared across PP stages, rather than the existence of a rank-local rejection sampler. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug


## Description

With `quantization="mxfp8"` and `moe_backend="humming"`, the engine dies **after the weights have been loaded**,
while converting them to the kernel format, raising a bare `KeyError` with no context at all:

```
KeyError: 'weight_scale'
```

Three problems:

1. **A bare `KeyError` with no diagnostics.** It does not say which tensor's scale is missing, which sublayer, which
   weight schema, or whether the combination is supported at all. The exception even escapes from a third-party
   module (`humming/schema/modelopt.py`).
2. **The selection stage could have rejected it — and that rejection machinery already exists.** MXFP8 has its own
   MoE backend oracle (`oracle/mxfp8.py:129 select_mxfp8_moe_backend` → `:102 _select_kernel_cls`), which rejects
   `deep_gemm` cleanly and states why:

   ```
   ValueError: No supported MXFP8 expert class for DEEPGEMM: kernel does not support current device cuda
   ```

   `humming`, by contrast, is **accepted by that oracle** and only then raises a bare `KeyError` several hundred
   lines later, inside `process_weights_after_loading()`. So the "select a backend and report why" machinery
   already exists; the `humming` branch just does not validate the incoming schema.
3. **The failure is too late.** It happens in `process_weights_after_loading()`, after the weights have already been
   allocated and moved into a kernel format that can never work, so it cannot be rolled back into the "rejected at
   config time" semantics.

The `mxfp8` weight/activation schema simply does not match the `modelopt` schema that humming expects
(`weight_scale` is absent). That is a legitimate "backend × quantization scheme" limitation, and it belongs in
`_select_kernel_cls`, not on `tensors["weight_scale"]`.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B",       # hybrid MoE
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.464,        # lower if your GPU is smaller
    dtype="bfloat16",
    allow_deprecated_quantization=True,
    quantization="mxfp8",               # online MXFP8
    moe_backend="humming",              # <-- accepted at selection, bare KeyError at conversion
)
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

Control (same model, same `quantization`, only the backend changed) — rejected cleanly by the **same** oracle:

```python
moe_backend="deep_gemm"
# ValueError: No supported MXFP8 expert class for DEEPGEMM: kernel does not support current device cuda
```

## Expected behavior

Reject it at backend-selection time, saying that humming needs modelopt-style MXFP8 weights (with `weight_scale`)
that online `mxfp8` parameters do not provide, for example:

```
ValueError: moe_backend='humming' cannot be used with quantization='mxfp8':
the humming kernel expects an MXFP8 checkpoint with per-block weight scales
('weight_scale' tensors are missing for <module>). Use a pre-quantized MXFP8
checkpoint, or moe_backend in {'triton', 'deep_gemm'}.
```

At minimum, a third-party schema converter's internal `KeyError` should not be surfaced to the user verbatim.

## Actual behavior

Model load completes → `process_weights_after_loading` → `Mxfp8OnlineMoEMethod._setup_kernel` →
`convert_to_fp8_moe_kernel_format` → `convert_to_humming_moe_kernel_format` → `_process_single_sublayer` →
`_convert_sublayer_to_humming` → `humming.schema.modelopt._convert_humming` raises `KeyError` on
`tensors["weight_scale"]` → EngineCore dies → the client only sees
`RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}`.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (sm86) and NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89) — both reproduce
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.15, kernel 6.8.0-138
- Model: `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator pairing `quantization` with `moe_backend`. `moe_backend="humming"`
  combined with other `quantization` values (`None`, `fp8_per_tensor`, `experts_int8`,
  `int8_per_channel_weight_only`) never produced this error in the same batch, and `mxfp8` combined with other
  backends (`deep_gemm`, `emulation`, `flashinfer_trtllm`, `triton_unfused`) did not either. So the defect is
  exactly the intersection `quantization="mxfp8"` × `moe_backend="humming"`.
- **Why this is not #54959** (`[Refactor] Complete the MOE oracle / linear kernel migration`): that tracking issue
  lists `HummingMoEMethod` as a class that bypasses the oracle. This crash is not in `HummingMoEMethod` — it is on
  the *migrated* online-MXFP8 path (`online/mxfp8.py:178` → `oracle/fp8.py:610` →
  `quantization/utils/humming/moe.py`). The oracle ran and selected humming; the missing piece is a
  schema-compatibility check at selection time (or a fallback), not a migration.
- **Related but distinct from #60162** (`Humming FP8 linear crashes on per-tensor/per-channel FP8 weights`):

  | | #60162 | this report |
  |---|---|---|
  | path | `kernels/linear/scaled_mm/humming.py` → `utils/humming/linear.py:39` | `online/mxfp8.py` → `oracle/fp8.py:610` → `utils/humming/moe.py` |
  | function | `convert_linear_layer_to_humming_standard` | `convert_to_humming_moe_kernel_format` |
  | error | `RuntimeError: self.stride(-1) must be 1 to view Float8_e4m3fn as Int` | **`KeyError: 'weight_scale'`** |
  | quantization | `fp8` / `fp8_per_tensor` / `fp8_per_channel` | `mxfp8` |

  Same root-cause family (the humming converters do not validate the incoming schema) and likely fixed by one
  change, but a different function with a different failure mode. If maintainers prefer, this can be folded into
  #60162 as the MoE-side data point instead of a separate issue.
- Same defect **class** as #61316 / #61854 / the CUTLASS-FP8 report: a MoE backend is selected without a
  schema-compatibility check, and the failure surfaces deep in the load path with a message that cannot be acted on.
  This one is the sharpest of the four, because the correct behaviour is already implemented two frames above the
  crash site (`_select_kernel_cls` rejects `deep_gemm` with a reason).

### 🐛 Describe the bug



## Description

With online FP8 (`quantization="fp8"` or `"fp8_per_tensor"`) plus an explicit `moe_backend="cutlass"`, model
loading dies inside `select_fp8_moe_backend()` with:

```
ValueError: vLLM CUTLASS FP8 MoE backend is disabled for this configuration.
```

Three problems:

1. **The message carries no reason.** "disabled for this configuration" does not say whether the compute
   capability is insufficient, whether the CUTLASS kernels were not compiled into this build, or whether the
   weight/activation quantization keys do not match. And `'cutlass'` is a **legal value** of `moe_backend`, so the
   user has every right to request it.
2. **Behaviour is inconsistent with the sibling backends, and the inconsistency is inside the same function.**
   In the same `select_fp8_moe_backend()` call, every other backend reports its rejection reason through
   `_make_log_unsupported(backend, reason)`:

   ```
   ValueError: FP8 MoE backend HUMMING does not support the deployment configuration
   since kernel does not support quantization scheme
   QuantKey(f8e4m3fn,scale(f32,static,per_tensor),symmetric)xQuantKey(f8e4m3fn,scale(f32,dynamic,per_tensor),symmetric).

   ValueError: moe_backend='emulation' is not supported for FP8 MoE.
   Expected one of ['triton', 'deep_gemm', 'cutlass', 'flashinfer_trtllm',
                    'flashinfer_cutlass', 'marlin', 'humming', 'aiter', 'hpc'].
   ```

   So the machinery for "select a backend and report why" **already exists**; the `cutlass` branch simply does not
   use it.
3. **The validation happens too late.** It raises in `initialize_model()` → per-layer `FusedMoEFactory` →
   `RoutedExperts._get_quant_method` → `Fp8OnlineMoEMethod.__init__`, i.e. after model construction has already
   begun; yet both `quantization` and `moe_backend` are static information known at `EngineArgs` level and could be
   decided in `create_engine_config()`.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B",       # also reproduces with Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B / OLMoE / Trinity / PowerMoE-3b
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.464,        # lower if your GPU is smaller
    allow_deprecated_quantization=True,
    quantization="fp8_per_tensor",       # online FP8
    moe_backend="cutlass",               # <-- the only backend that produces a reason-free error
)
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

Control (same model, same `quantization`, only `moe_backend` switched to `humming`): still rejected, but the
message names the backend and the actual reason:

```
ValueError: FP8 MoE backend HUMMING does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not
support quantization scheme QuantKey(f8e4m3fn,scale(f32,static,per_tensor),symmetric)xQuantKey(
f8e4m3fn,scale(f32,dynamic,per_tensor),symmetric).
```

## Expected behavior

Behave like every sibling backend — report the **backend name + the real reason + usable alternatives**:

```
ValueError: FP8 MoE backend CUTLASS does not support the deployment configuration
since <actual gate: compute capability < 90 / kernel not built for sm86 / ...>.
Candidates that do support this configuration: ['triton', 'humming'].
```

Ideally the decision is made in `create_engine_config()` so the engine is never constructed at all.

## Actual behavior

Config passes `create_engine_config()` → `initialize_model` → `FusedMoEFactory` →
`RoutedExperts._get_quant_method` → `Fp8OnlineMoEMethod.__init__` → `select_fp8_moe_backend()` raises a bare
`ValueError` at `oracle/fp8.py:468` → EngineCore dies → the client only sees
`RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}`.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (sm86, 48 GiB) **and** NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89, 47.4 GiB) — both reproduce
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.15, kernel 6.8.0-138
- Models: `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`, `arcee-ai/Trinity-Nano-Preview`,
  `ibm/PowerMoE-3b`, `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct`

## Full traceback (crash site, from EngineCore log)

```text

  routed_experts = routed_experts_cls(
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py", line 145, in __init__

File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py", line 218, in _get_quant_method

quantization scheme QuantKey(f8e4m3fn,scale(f32,static,per_tensor),symmetric)xQuantKey(
f8e4m3fn,scale(f32,dynamic,per_tensor),symmetric).
```

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator pairing `quantization` enum values with `moe_backend` enum values.
  5/5 automated points, five distinct MoE architectures, both GPU architectures:

  | point | model | GPU | `quantization` | `moe_backend` | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | cir_0279_L1 | LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B | sm86 | `fp8_per_tensor` | `cutlass` | **`ValueError: vLLM CUTLASS FP8 MoE backend is disabled ...`** |
  | cir_0019_L1 | arcee-ai/Trinity-Nano-Preview | sm86 | `fp8_per_tensor` | `cutlass` | same |
  | cir_0060_L2 | arcee-ai/Trinity-Nano-Preview | sm86 | `fp8` | `cutlass` | same |
  | cir_0102_L1 | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat | sm89 | `fp8_per_tensor` | `cutlass` | same |
  | cir_0023_L2 | ibm/PowerMoE-3b | sm89 | `fp8_per_tensor` | `cutlass` | same |
  | local repro | LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B | sm89 | `fp8_per_tensor` | `cutlass` | same (1/1) |

- **Why this is not #54959** (`[Refactor] Complete the MOE oracle / linear kernel migration`): both rejections come
  out of the *same, already-migrated* function `select_fp8_moe_backend()`. Its HUMMING path already calls
  `_return_or_raise` → `_make_log_unsupported(backend, reason)` (`oracle/fp8.py:472` → `:445`); the CUTLASS path is
  the hardcoded `raise ValueError` at `oracle/fp8.py:468`. The reporting helper exists two lines away, so this is a
  single branch not using it — not an unmigrated quant method.
- The same `quantization` values combined with `triton` / `triton_unfused` / `deep_gemm` / `emulation` /
  `flashinfer_trtllm` / `flashinfer_cutlass` / `marlin` / `humming` never produced this error in the same batch
  (they either started, or were rejected with a message naming the backend and the reason).
- Because it also fires on **sm89** (RTX 5880 Ada), where CUTLASS FP8 kernels are normally available, the gate
  cannot be explained by "sm<89 lacks CUTLASS FP8" alone — which is exactly why a reason-free message is not
  actionable here.
- Upstream prior art at the same site, all closed and all different root causes:
  - #36105 (closed, ROCm) — `NotImplementedError: No FP8 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration`
  - #32109 (closed, SM120) — `No compiled cutlass_scaled_mm for CUDA device capability: 120`
  - #34249 (closed, Hopper) — `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` auto-selected instead of `DEEPGEMM`
  - #33333 (closed) — the *reason-bearing* form of the same class:
    `NvFp4 MoE backend 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not
    support current device.`

  None of them contains `is disabled for this configuration`, and none is about an explicit `moe_backend="cutlass"`
  request on sm86/sm89.
- Same defect **class** as #61316 (fp8 *linear* kernel chooser discards `failure_reason_list`) and #61854 (mxfp4
  *MoE* oracle names AMD-only remedies). This is the third site: the fp8 **MoE** oracle's `cutlass` branch has no
  reason at all. Filing separately because parameter, oracle module and message differ; happy to merge if
  maintainers prefer one tracker entry for "MoE backend oracles must report per-backend reasons".

### 🐛 Describe the bug


## Description

`speculative_config.method="ngram_gpu"` (the GPU n-gram speculative-decoding proposer) constructs its kernel
unconditionally through `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper`, so it **depends** on `compilation_config` actually
having a compile backend. There is no compatibility check between `compilation_config.mode` and
`speculative_config.method`: when the user explicitly disables compilation (`mode="NONE"` — a documented value,
whose purpose is to skip the torch.compile overhead), the engine raises while constructing the drafter inside
`GPUModelRunnerV1.__init__`.

Two problems:

1. **The error does not point at the parameter the user set.** `ValueError: No compilation mode is set.` says
   neither that `compilation_config.mode="NONE"` caused it, nor that `ngram_gpu` needs a compile backend. A user
   reading that line will go and re-check their `compilation_config` spelling, even though "disable compilation"
   is perfectly valid for ordinary models (in the same batch, `mode="NONE"` + `method="ngram"` points all started
   and generated normally).
2. **The validation happens far too late.** Both values are individually legal, and the conflict only surfaces in
   EngineCore's `init_device`. It could be decided in `create_engine_config()` with a message naming both sides of
   the conflict and the way out.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t",   # also reproduces with state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.464,           # lower if your GPU is smaller
    compilation_config={"mode": "NONE"},    # <-- compilation explicitly disabled
    speculative_config={                    # <-- requires a compile backend
        "method": "ngram_gpu",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 2,
        "prompt_lookup_max": 3,
        "prompt_lookup_min": 2,
    },
)
# The LLM(...) call itself raises:
#   RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
# (the real cause is on EngineCore stderr: ValueError: No compilation mode is set.)
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

Control (same model, same `compilation_config`, only the proposer switched to the CPU-trie `ngram`): the engine
starts and generates normally.

## Expected behavior

Either reject the combination cleanly at `create_engine_config()` time, naming both sides of the conflict and the
way out:

```
ValueError: speculative_config.method="ngram_gpu" requires torch.compile / CUDA graph support,
but compilation_config.mode="NONE" disables it.
Use method="ngram" with compilation_config.mode="NONE", or enable compilation.
```

or make `ngram_gpu` fall back to a proposer that does not need compilation, instead of being constructed and then
failing.

## Actual behavior

Config passes `create_engine_config()` → EngineCore `init_device` → `GPUModelRunnerV1.__init__` →
`NgramProposerGPU.__init__` → `NgramGPUKernel.__init__` → `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper.__init__` →
`compilation_config.init_backend()` raises `ValueError: No compilation mode is set.` → EngineCore dies → the client
only sees `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}`.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89, 47.4 GiB) and NVIDIA RTX A6000 (sm86) — both reproduce
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.15, kernel 6.8.0-138
- Models: `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t` (dense), `state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf` (pure mamba)

## Full traceback (crash site, from EngineCore log)

```text
File ".../vllm/tracing/otel.py", line 175, in sync_wrapper
  return func(*args, **kwargs)
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 526, in init_device
  self.model_runner = GPUModelRunnerV1(self.vllm_config, self.device)
File ".../vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup.py", line 1032, in wrapped
  init_fn(instance, vllm_config, *args, **kwargs)
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 632, in __init__
  self.drafter = NgramProposerGPU(self.vllm_config, self.device, self)
File ".../vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer_gpu.py", line 254, in __init__
  self.kernel = NgramGPUKernel(
File ".../vllm/compilation/decorators.py", line 406, in __init__
  TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper.__init__(
File ".../vllm/compilation/wrapper.py", line 89, in __init__
  backend = vllm_config.compilation_config.init_backend(
File ".../vllm/config/compilation.py", line 1091, in init_backend
  raise ValueError("No compilation mode is set.")
ValueError: No compilation mode is set.
```

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator that pairs documented enum values of
  `compilation_config.mode` / `compilation_config.cudagraph_mode` with `speculative_config.method`.
- Three points, two model families, identical stack:

  | point | model | `compilation_config` | spec method | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | cir_0010_L2 | stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t | `{"mode": "NONE"}` | `ngram_gpu` | **`ValueError: No compilation mode is set.`** |
  | cir_0051_L1 | state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf | `{"mode": "NONE"}` | `ngram_gpu` | same |
  | local repro | stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t | `{"mode": "NONE"}` | `ngram_gpu` | same (1/1) |

- Controls, all clean:
  - `mode="NONE"` + `method="ngram"` → engine starts and generates (a dozen points in the same batch; also
    confirmed by the bundled script).
  - `mode="NONE"` + `method="suffix"` → same.
  - `ngram_gpu` without an explicit `compilation_config` → `init_backend()` takes the default backend and the
    engine starts.

  So the dependency is specific to `ngram_gpu`, and specific to the "no backend at all" state:
  `mode="DYNAMO_TRACE_ONCE"` + `ngram_gpu` also initialises, because a compile backend exists.

- **Distinct from #61317** (`jit_monitor_mode="error"` → `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel`): that bug is a raw
  `@triton.jit` kernel invoked directly and therefore *invisible* to the JIT warmup registry. Here the `ngram_gpu`
  kernel is deliberately wrapped in `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper`, so the two are opposite failure directions
  on different kernels; `jit_monitor_mode` is not set in any of the points above.

- **Secondary observation, not the subject of this report.** The same configuration family has a second, different
  failure surface worth knowing about: with `compilation_config.mode="STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE"` the engine *does*
  start, and then dies on the first `generate()` while proposing draft tokens. One automated point captured a full
  stack there:

  ```text
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 5014, in propose_draft_token_ids
    draft_token_ids, num_valid_draft_tokens = self.drafter.propose(
  File ".../vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer_gpu.py", line 383, in propose
    draft_tokens, num_valid_draft_tokens = self.kernel(
  File ".../vllm/compilation/decorators.py", line 520, in __call__
    return self.aot_compiled_fn(self, *args, **kwargs)
  File ".../torch/_dynamo/aot_compile.py", line 243, in __call__
    raise RuntimeError(f"GuardManager check failed, reason: {reason}")
  RuntimeError: GuardManager check failed, reason: GuardDebugInfo(
  result=0, verbose_code_parts=['GLOBAL_STATE changed: grad_mode num_threads '],
  num_guards_executed=2, user_stack=None)
  ```

  A standalone rerun of that configuration did not reproduce the same message: the engine started and then died on
  the first request with `EngineDeadError` and **no traceback at all** in EngineCore stderr (silent process death).
  So both runs fail at the first request, but with two different error surfaces — which suggests the AOT artifact
  compiled under one `torch.no_grad`/thread-count state is replayed under another, and the proposer never
  re-enters the guarded state around the call. Reported here as context only; the reproducible, fileable defect is
  the `mode="NONE"` case above.

- Upstream prior art for the *message text* (not this defect): #27286 (closed CI failure) contains
  `GuardManager check failed reason: 'GLOBAL_STATE changed: num_threads '`, but on the
  `determine_available_memory` path with no `ngram_gpu` involved — mentioned so triage does not mistake the two.
  I could not find any upstream report of `No compilation mode is set.`, nor of a `ngram_gpu` ×
  `compilation_config` incompatibility.
