title: [Bug][Rust Frontend] DeepSeek V4/V4.1 renderer rejects `latest_reminder`, which the Python encoder renders
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug cc @BugenZhao @njhill @Isotr0py @YeonwooSung DeepSeek-V4 accepts a chat role, `latest_reminder`, that the Python encoder renders as `<｜latest_reminder｜>` plus the text. The Rust DeepSeek renderer rejects every custom role. The same request fails on vLLM’s Rust HTTP frontend and on the router’s gRPC path, which renders with that same library before it sends token ids. ### Reproduction (According to https://github.com/vllm-project/router/issues/318) Router in front of a rust grpc (or http) vLLM worker serving DeepSeek-V4: ``` curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the context."}, {"role": "latest_reminder", "content": "Keep the answer concise."} ] }' ``` Actual: Rust DeepSeek renderer -> `Error::UnsupportedChatRole` (HTTP 400). Expected: a role the model’s Python encoder can render is rendered to token ids and reaches the worker. Python `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4_encoding.py` already does this. ### Context The vLLM router’s Rust gRPC backend (https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/283) renders the chat template in-process with `vllm-chat` and sends `GenerateRequest.token_ids`. The role string never crosses the proto. A role the renderer cannot represent never reaches the worker. https://github.com/vllm-project/router/issues/318 is that gap for model-specific roles. This is not specific to the router or to gRPC. Any caller of the Rust DeepSeek renderer hits it, including vLLM’s own Rust HTTP frontend. ### What main already does https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58311 added `ChatMessage::Custom { role, content }` and `ChatMessage::custom()`. The HF renderer passes that role string into the Jinja template unchanged. That covers templates such as MiniMax-M3 `root`. The same PR makes the native renderers return `Error::UnsupportedChatRole`, including DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1, and locks that in with `custom_roles_are_rejected_as_request_errors`. Python still has a real branch for this role: - emit `<｜latest_reminder｜>` plus the message content - if the next message is `latest_reminder`, still open the assistant transition after the previous user turn, the same way a following `assistant` message does - do not treat `latest_reminder` as a user/developer turn for `find_last_user_index` A request the Python frontend accepts is a 400 on the Rust DeepSeek renderer. ### Ask Please steer which fix belongs in this repo before we send a PR. 1. DeepSeek-only. In `rust/src/chat/src/renderer/deepseek.rs`, render `role == "latest_reminder"` to match the Python encoder, and keep `UnsupportedChatRole` for every other custom role. Harmony, Inkling, and Kimi K3 stay closed, as #58311 set them. 2. A shared rule for native renderers. If other dedicated renderers also drop roles that their Python path accepts, say how those roles should be added (per-renderer allowlist, or something else). We would rather follow that than special-case one token in a one-off PR. We can send the DeepSeek renderer change once the scope is clear. A PR from someone closer to the renderer is just as welcome. No `inference.proto` / `control.proto` change is needed for this. The gRPC worker already consumes token ids. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

Reproduced on main at 5555a2d8f (editable install with the precompiled kernels), NVIDIA driver 617.42, which `collect_env` does not pick up from the WSL `nvidia-smi`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug When a request sets `truncate_prompt_tokens` together with an explicit `truncation_side`, the special tokens that the tokenizer adds around the prompt are cut off at the truncated end: `[CLS]` or `[SEP]` for BERT-style encoders, BOS for Llama-style models, and the EOS that Qwen3-Embedding appends for last-token pooling. With `truncation_side` unset, the tokenizer truncates the prompt itself and keeps them. The side doesn't have to differ from the tokenizer's default; spelling out the default is enough. Cohere `/v2/embed` with `truncate="START"` maps to an explicit `"left"` and takes the same path. Reproducer, CPU only (the render server runs just the preprocessing): ```bash vllm launch render hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM --port 8123 ``` ```bash for side in null '"left"'; do curl -s localhost:8123/v1/completions/render \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\": \"hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM\", \"prompt\": \"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\", \"truncate_prompt_tokens\": 4, \"truncation_side\": $side}" \ | python -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]["token_ids"])' done ``` ```text [1, 17366, 11203, 29889] [278, 17366, 11203, 29889] ``` With the side unset, BOS (`1`) is kept. With `"left"`, which is this tokenizer's default side, it is dropped. For embedding models I compared the tokens vLLM keeps with `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, truncation_side=side)(text, truncation=True, max_length=k)`: - `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` (CLS pooling): `"right"` drops the final `[SEP]` and `"left"` drops the leading `[CLS]`. Served on the GPU with `truncate_prompt_tokens=16`, the embeddings of three sentences have a cosine similarity with the HF model's (on HF-truncated tokens) of 0.9890, 0.9700 and 0.9917 for `"right"`, and 0.9978, 0.9995 and 0.9971 for `"left"`, against 1.0000 with the side unset. `/v1/embeddings`, Cohere `/v2/embed` (`truncate="START"` for `"left"`) and `LLM.embed` give the same numbers. - `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` (last-token pooling): `"right"`, its default side, drops the `<|endoftext|>` the tokenizer appends, so the pooled position is a text token. The cause is in `TokenizeParams`: with an explicit side, `get_encode_kwargs()` turns tokenizer truncation off, because the tokenizer can only truncate from its own side, and `_token_truncation` then slices the token ids, special tokens included. Cross-encoder pairs (`get_score_prompt` in `vllm/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py`) and the Rust frontend (`PromptTruncation::apply`) also truncate by slicing, so they are likely affected too; I've left them out of the fix. I have a fix and will open a PR. AI assistance was used to investigate this and write this report. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

The drafter-only eager setting doesn't seem to stop drafter graph capture under Model Runner V2. | | `--compilation-config.cudagraph_mode NONE` | ✅ Works, but loses the CUDA graph speedup, which removes much of DFlash's benefit. | So there are two related problems: 1. `_prepare_dflash_inputs_to_capture` doesn't set `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` when building capture metadata, which FlexAttention requires. 2. `speculative_config.enforce_eager` is apparently not respected by `capture_model` → `speculator.capture()` in the V2 model runner. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

The crash happens with both an untrained drafter (from `speculators train --dry-run`) and a trained one, so it isn't caused by the weights. **Command** Run in the `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` Docker image (vLLM 0.30.0) on a single GPU, with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` set to get an accurate error location: ```bash CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b \ --served-model-name openai/gpt-oss-20b \ --enforce-eager \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": "/path/to/dflash-drafter", "num_speculative_tokens": 15}' ``` The drafter was created with `speculators train --speculator-type dflash --verifier-name-or-path openai/gpt-oss-20b --dry-run` (speculators 0.9.0a67), then rebuilt with intermediate_size changed to 8192, so its weights are untrained. Its `config.json` is attached below. A trained drafter crashes the same way, so the weights don't matter. **Error** (with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `--enforce-eager`) ``` CUDA error (/workspace/.deps/vllm-flash-attn-src/hopper/flash_fwd_launch_template.h:171): an illegal memory access was encountered ``` Without `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` (and with CUDA graphs enabled), the error is reported asynchronously during `compile_or_warm_up_model` as a device-side assert, pointing at `self.draft_tokens[req_idx].zero_()` in the DFlash proposer. That location is probably not where the failure actually happens. **Drafter config** (DFlash, built against gpt-oss-20b) - 5 layers, `block_size` 16, `hidden_size` 2880, `head_dim` 64, 64 query heads, 8 KV heads, `intermediate_size` 8192 - Full vocabulary (`draft_vocab_size` 201088, no d2t/t2d), `mask_token_id` 200019 - `aux_hidden_state_layer_ids` [2, 12, 21], plus the last layer for targets - Default drafter attention layout: sliding window 2048, with layer 2 set to full attention
Drafter config.json ```json { "architectures": [ "DFlashDraftModel" ], "auto_map": { "": "config.DFlashSpeculatorConfig" }, "aux_hidden_state_layer_ids": [ 2, 12, 21 ], "block_size": 16, "draft_vocab_size": 201088, "dtype": "bfloat16", "mask_token_id": 200019, "sample_from_anchor": false, "sliding_window_non_causal": false, "speculators_config": { "algorithm": "dflash", "default_proposal_method": "greedy", "proposal_methods": [ { "accept_tolerance": 0.0, "proposal_type": "greedy", "speculative_tokens": 15, "verifier_accept_k": 1 } ], "verifier": { "architectures": [ "GptOssForCausalLM" ], "name_or_path": "openai/gpt-oss-20b" } }, "speculators_model_type": "dflash", "speculators_version": "0.9.0a67", "target_hidden_size": null, "tie_word_embeddings": false, "transformer_layer_config": { "attention_bias": false, "attention_dropout": 0.0, "bos_token_id": null, "eos_token_id": null, "head_dim": 64, "hidden_act": "silu", "hidden_size": 2880, "initializer_range": 0.02, "intermediate_size": 8192, "layer_types": [ "sliding_attention", "sliding_attention", "full_attention", "sliding_attention", "sliding_attention" ], "max_position_embeddings": 131072, "max_window_layers": 28, "model_type": "qwen3", "num_attention_heads": 64, "num_hidden_layers": 5, "num_key_value_heads": 8, "pad_token_id": null, "rms_norm_eps": 0.00001, "rope_parameters": { "beta_fast": 32.0, "beta_slow": 1.0, "factor": 32.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 4096, "rope_theta": 150000, "rope_type": "yarn", "truncate": false }, "sliding_window": 2048, "tie_word_embeddings": false, "use_cache": true, "use_sliding_window": true, "vocab_size": 201088 }, "transformers_version": "5.16.1" } ```
### What we tried | Configuration | Result | |---|---| | `method: ngram`, `num_speculative_tokens: 15` (same target, same flags) | ✅ Works. Target verification of 16-token blocks on FA3 is fine. | | DFlash drafter with **all layers full attention** (no sliding window) | ❌ Same FA3 illegal memory access | | `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` | Not applicable. Fails with `All attention layers in the same KV cache group must have the same window size` because gpt-oss itself mixes 128-token sliding-window and full attention. | | `--speculative-config.attention_backend FLEX_ATTENTION` + `--enforce-eager` | ✅ Works. Outputs match the non-speculative server at temperature 0 (apart from rare late divergence), and a drafter trained with speculators gets non-zero acceptance. | The crash therefore seems specific to the DFlash drafter's attention running on FA3 when the target is gpt-oss. Our guess, not verified, is that it comes from the drafter's non-causal attention interacting with gpt-oss's hybrid KV-cache layout (sliding-window plus full-attention groups, attention sinks) when the attention metadata is built. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

On `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (hybrid conv + SSM + full-attention), **greedy decoding is not reproducible**: with the same engine instance, same seed and same prompts, `temperature=0` produces different token sequences across repeated `generate()` calls. The batch is identical across rounds; the only difference is time (and therefore kernel/scheduling order).

The divergence signature is consistent across every mismatching prompt: **a long identical prefix, a single differing token, then re-alignment** — the classic signature of a nondeterministic reduction order (atomicAdd / split-K accumulation) perturbing logits just enough to flip an argmax. Measured examples (128 generated tokens per prompt):

```
p0: common prefix 36 tok | A tail=[41677, 856, 21473, 3256, 779, 23981]
                         | B tail=[41677, 856, 21473,  884, 779, 23981]
p1: common prefix 66 tok | A tail=[523, 3604, 8676, 15637, 779, 2565]
                         | B tail=[523, 3604, 8676,  2316, 779, 5743]
p3: common prefix 75 tok | A tail=[51197, 11478, 968, 9029, 10222, 3604]
                         | B tail=[51197, 11478, 968, 12051, 10222, 3604]
```

Ruled out:

- **CUDA graphs**: the mismatch persists with `cudagraph_mode="NONE"` (3 of 4 prompts diverge; one diverges at the very first output token) → not a graph-replay artifact.
- **Sampling RNG**: `temperature=0` → pure argmax, no sampling noise.
- **Batch-invariance / cold-start cache state**: the divergence is between two **warm** rounds, not between a cold and a warm one; the warm rounds themselves disagree.

Ruled in as **LFM2/hybrid-mamba-specific**: the same probe on `Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat` (dense-attention MoE, same machine, same stack) is stable — warm-vs-warm and cold-vs-warm both identical.

Impact: greedy-decode reproducibility is a baseline expectation for evaluation reproducibility and A/B testing; any downstream harness comparing outputs run-to-run on hybrid models sees phantom diffs.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B",
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,   # lower if your GPU is smaller
)
prompts = ["The capital of France is", "Count from 1 to 10:"]
sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=64)

r1 = [list(o.outputs[0].token_ids) for o in llm.generate(prompts, sp)]
r2 = [list(o.outputs[0].token_ids) for o in llm.generate(prompts, sp)]
for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(r1, r2)):
    if a != b:
        d = next(j for j, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(a, b)) if x != y)
        print(f"prompt {i}: diverge at token {d}: {a[d:d+6]} vs {b[d:d+6]}")
```

## Expected behavior

Two consecutive `generate()` calls with identical prompts and `temperature=0` on the same engine return identical token sequences.

## Actual behavior

Warm-vs-warm rounds diverge at one or more prompts (see the evidence table below); the divergence persists across repeated rounds and is not removed by disabling CUDA graphs.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: **按实测填写**（复现时用 `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` 确认；示例：`NVIDIA RTX A6000, sm86` 或 `NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation, sm89`）
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13
- Model: `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (hybrid mamba, bf16 checkpoint)

## Evidence (standalone reproduction, same engine instance, warm-vs-warm comparison)

All rows below come from `repro_greedy_nondeterminism_lfm2.py` re-run outside the automated pipeline. "warm-vs-warm" means two rounds both executed after warmup; a mismatch there cannot be explained by cold-start cache state.

| # | config | warm-vs-warm | cold-vs-warm | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B** (primary) | `mamba_cache_dtype="float16"`, `cudagraph_mode="NONE"` | **mismatch 3/4** (p0 p1 p2) | mismatch 2/4 (p1 p2) | CUDA graphs excluded; no `use_fp64_gumbel` |
| **A** (secondary) | `mamba_cache_dtype="float16"` + `quantization="fp8_per_block"` + `use_fp64_gumbel=True` | **mismatch 4/4** | mismatch 3/4 | see note 4 in the submission note — verify `use_fp64_gumbel` semantics first |
| control | `Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat`, same probe/machine | identical | identical | non-hybrid-attention MoE is stable |

Per-prompt divergence detail for config B (24 generated tokens, `cudagraph_mode="NONE"`):

```
p0: common prefix  2 tok | A=[..., 5242,  523, 3604, 1098,  908]
                         | B=[..., 5242,  523, 1311,  856, 5408]
p1: common prefix  0 tok | A=[...,  730,  526,  521]
                         | B=[..., 3604,  526,  521]
p2: common prefix 15 tok | A=[..., 1883,  856, 28027,  797,  768, 32524]
                         | B=[..., 1883,  856, 28027,  988,  730,  1698]
```

Note that p1 diverges at the **very first output token** with CUDA graphs disabled — this is the strongest single datapoint that the nondeterminism is not a graph-replay or cache-state artifact.

## Additional context

- Found by an automated warm-vs-warm determinism probe in a config-interaction test generator, then reproduced standalone.
- Suspect areas (hybrid-mamba-specific kernels): the SSM scan / conv1d update path (`precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel`, `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel`, `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel`, `postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel` under `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py` and the model's mamba layers) for nondeterministic reductions; secondarily the fused-MoE routing/weighted-sum path if it uses atomics.
- Related observation, possibly relevant: the same run emits `jit_monitor` warnings for exactly those per-step mamba kernels being JIT-compiled **during inference** (i.e. they are not covered by the startup warmup). Since they are compiled lazily on the first step, any autotuning/scheduling difference between rounds could also contribute to round-to-round numerical differences.

## What is and is not being claimed

- **Claimed**: on LFM2, two `temperature=0` calls on the same engine can return different tokens, violating the usual expectation that greedy decoding is reproducible.
- **Not claimed**: that this is a specific kernel's bug — the responsible reduction is not yet isolated.
- **Open item for the harness side** (not a vLLM defect): a determinism probe that compares only *within* a single `generate()` call cannot detect this class of divergence; it needs an explicit "same engine, two separate calls" round. That gap is why this was initially mis-bucketed as cold-start noise.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

Starting an engine with `return_sampling_mask=True` imposes **two independent preconditions on every request's `SamplingParams`**, but they are enforced separately and discovered sequentially:

```
with top_k unset and temperature=0.0:
  ValueError: sampling distribution replay requires temperature > 0

with temperature=0.7 (i.e. the first condition satisfied) and top_k unset:
  ValueError: sampling distribution replay requires top_k > 0 to bound sampling mask size,
              reduce transfer overhead, and avoid potential OOMs
```

A caller who does the natural thing — construct `SamplingParams(temperature=...)` without `top_k` — satisfies the first check, then fails the second, and only learns the complete contract by triggering two separate errors. Nothing documents both conditions together, and neither check runs when the engine is configured, even though `return_sampling_mask` is an **engine-level** flag set at construction time: the incompatibility is only detectable per request, at `add_request` time.

Two distinct problems:

1. **The preconditions are split across separate raises.** Both belong to the same `return_sampling_mask` feature and are known statically at request construction. Raising them one at a time forces trial-and-error to discover the contract; a single error listing all unmet preconditions (`temperature > 0`, `top_k > 0`) would be actionable in one round-trip.
2. **The check happens too late to help the operator.** `return_sampling_mask` is set on the engine, not the request. If a server is started with `return_sampling_mask=True`, then *every* request must carry `top_k > 0`; a client that sends the default `SamplingParams(temperature=0.7)` is rejected at request time, after the engine has been built and the deployment cut over. At minimum this deserves a startup-time warning (or an explicit note in the flag's help text), and arguably a config-time validation of the combination.

Note the rejections themselves are **clean** — the request is rejected with `ValueError` and the engine survives (verified: a subsequent valid request on the same engine succeeds). This report is about the error contract and the validation timing, not about a crash.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,   # lower if your GPU is smaller
    return_sampling_mask=True,
)

# 1) first precondition
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=16))
#    -> ValueError: sampling distribution replay requires temperature > 0

# 2) second precondition, only reachable after fixing the first
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.7, max_tokens=16))
#    -> ValueError: sampling distribution replay requires top_k > 0 to bound sampling
#       mask size, reduce transfer overhead, and avoid potential OOMs

# 3) control: both conditions satisfied -> works
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"],
             SamplingParams(temperature=0.7, top_k=50, max_tokens=16))
```

A ready-made driver for these three cases on a single engine is in `repro_return_sampling_mask.py`.

## Expected behavior

Either of:

- **One combined, actionable error** at request construction listing every unmet precondition, e.g.
  ```
  ValueError: return_sampling_mask=True requires sampling params to satisfy:
    - temperature > 0 (currently 0.0)
    - top_k > 0 (currently unset; needed to bound the sampling mask size)
  ```
- or, better, the constraint is surfaced **when the flag is set** (config/startup time), since no request can ever satisfy it without those parameters:
  ```
  ValueError: return_sampling_mask=True requires clients to send top_k > 0; either set the
  engine flag only when your clients do so, or validate at request time with a single message.
  ```

## Actual behavior

`return_sampling_mask=True` is accepted at `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` time with no warning. Each request is then validated in `LLMEngine.add_request` → `InputProcessor.process_inputs` → `_validate_params`, where the two preconditions are raised as **separate** `ValueError`s on the same code path, in sequence (`vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:163-173`):

```python
if self.model_config.return_sampling_mask:
    if params.temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "sampling distribution replay requires temperature > 0"
        )
    if params.top_k <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "sampling distribution replay requires top_k > 0 to "
            "bound sampling mask size, reduce transfer overhead, "
            "and avoid potential OOMs"
        )
```

Client-visible traceback for the second case:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py", line 258, in add_request
  request = self.input_processor.process_inputs(
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py", line 356, in process_inputs
  self._validate_params(params, supported_tasks)
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py", line 170, in _validate_params
  raise ValueError(
ValueError: sampling distribution replay requires top_k > 0 to bound sampling mask size,
reduce transfer overhead, and avoid potential OOMs
```

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: **按实测填写**（示例：`NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation / RTX A6000`）
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (bfloat16 checkpoint)

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator probing engine-level sampling/output flags against request-level `SamplingParams` profiles. The generator's request profiles include greedy (`temperature=0.0`) and non-greedy (`temperature=0.7`, `top_p`, `min_p`) variants; the `top_k` precondition only surfaced on the second probe attempt — which is exactly the usability defect described here.
- Impact is one round-trip plus one wasted deployment step per operator; no correctness impact, and no engine crash.
- If the intent is that `return_sampling_mask` is only usable with `top_k`-bounded sampling, that intent is not discoverable from either the flag name, its help text, or a single error message.

### Related note for whoever triages this

This is a **validation-message / validation-timing** defect, not a crash. If the maintainers consider "two separate raises" acceptable, the minimum actionable change is to make the flag's help text state both requirements (`temperature > 0` **and** `top_k > 0`), since today the second one is only discoverable by hitting it.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

vLLM's JIT monitor (`vllm/utils/jit_monitor.py`) is activated at the end of `compile_or_warm_up_model()`; with `jit_monitor_mode="error"` every monitored Triton JIT compilation during inference raises. For a **hybrid mamba model** (`LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`, conv + SSM + full-attention), the built-in startup warmup is *not* sufficient to keep that promise: the engine completes the full "JIT kernel warmup (154 compile keys)" pass and CUDA-graph capture (56/56), then **dies on the first real inference step**:

```
RuntimeError: Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference:
precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider
extending warmup to cover this shape/config.
```

Root cause — a warmup coverage gap, not a user misconfiguration:

1. The per-step mamba pre-copy kernel `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` is a **raw `@triton.jit` kernel** invoked directly as `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel[grid](...)` (`vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:1212`, called from `preprocess_mamba` on every `execute_model`). It is not a registered `VllmJitKernel`, so the JIT warmup registry (`vllm/model_executor/warmup/jit_warmup.py`, which only pre-compiles registered kernels — the 154 keys above) never compiles it.
2. CUDA-graph capture does not execute it either: the pre-copy runs outside the captured region, so the first real `execute_model` is its first-ever invocation.
3. The monitor is already active at that point → triton's post-compile hook → `_handle_jit_event` → `raise RuntimeError` (`jit_monitor.py:134`) → **the EngineCore process dies**, and the client only sees an opaque `EngineDeadError`; the actionable message is buried in EngineCore stderr.

Net effect: enabling a *diagnostic* mode turns a latency-spike advisory into a fatal, unrecoverable crash on the very first request, deterministically, for every hybrid mamba model. Reproduced across 4 distinct configs × 2 variants (`mamba_cache_dtype` bfloat16/float16/float32, ±`use_fp64_gumbel`, ±`disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager`) — all identical; the same configs *without* `jit_monitor_mode` run fine.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B",   # hybrid: conv + SSM (mamba) + full attention
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,    # lower if your GPU is smaller
    jit_monitor_mode="error",
)
# Engine is up (warmup + CUDA graph capture both completed) — first request kills it:
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

## Expected behavior

The engine survives inference in `jit_monitor_mode="error"`: the per-step raw triton kernels of supported model families (here the hybrid mamba pre-copy) are covered by the warmup pass, so no monitored JIT compile occurs at request time. At minimum, if the monitor does fire, the client should receive the actual actionable message instead of a bare `EngineDeadError`.

## Actual behavior

Warmup (154 keys) → CUDA graph capture (56/56) → first `generate()` → `execute_model` → `preprocess_mamba` → `run_fused_precopy` → `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel[grid]` → triton `_do_compile` → post-compile hook → `_handle_jit_event` raises → EngineCore process dies → client sees `vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError`.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89, 47.4 GiB)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13
- Model: `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator probing diagnostic flags against model architectures.
- Cross-check on the same GPU (all with `jit_monitor_mode="error"`, all crash identically; all run fine without the flag):

  | config | outcome |
  |---|---|
  | LFM2 + `jit_monitor_mode="error"` (plain) | **EngineDeadError on first request** (2/2) |
  | LFM2 + flag + `mamba_cache_dtype` ∈ {float16, float32} | same crash (2/2 each) |
  | LFM2 + flag + `use_fp64_gumbel=True` | same crash (2/2) |
  | LFM2 + flag + `disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=False` | same crash (2/2) |
  | LFM2 without the flag (all other args identical) | OK |

- The three distinct defects, in decreasing severity:
  1. **Warmup coverage gap**: raw `@triton.jit` kernels invoked per-step from `execute_model` (mamba pre-copy) are invisible to the JIT warmup registry — hybrid mamba models can never satisfy `jit_monitor_mode="error"` as shipped.
  2. **Fatal escalation**: mode "error" converts a latency advisory into an unrecoverable engine death mid-serving (the process cannot be revived; in-flight requests are lost).
  3. **Opaque client error**: the client sees `EngineDeadError` with no pointer to the real cause; the "consider extending warmup" message is only in EngineCore stderr.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

`quantization="fp8_per_channel"` (online PTPC: per-token-per-channel weight scale + dynamic per-token activation scale, `kFp8StaticChannelSym` → `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod`) passes config validation, but the model load then dies inside `create_weights` with:

```
ValueError: FP8 PTPC online quant requires a kernel that honors per-token activation
quantization; MarlinFP8 is W8A16 weight-only. Requires SM89+ for Cutlass FP8 or
ROCm MI3xx for rowwise scaled_mm.
```

Two problems, both independent of which GPU model is used:

1. **The real per-kernel rejection reasons are discarded, so the error cannot be acted on.** `init_fp8_linear_kernel` walks `_POSSIBLE_FP8_KERNELS` (FlashInfer → Cutlass → B12xTensor → PerTensorTorch → ChannelWiseTorch → Marlin → …) and collects a `failure_reason_list` for the candidates it rejects. But Marlin's `can_implement` accepts everything, so `choose_scaled_mm_linear_kernel` simply **returns Marlin** — the collected reasons are never surfaced. Only afterwards does the PTPC guard (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py:386`) raise, with a message that names a generic capability requirement ("Requires SM89+ for Cutlass FP8") instead of saying *why FlashInfer and Cutlass were skipped for this configuration*. A user (and a bug report) cannot distinguish "this hardware genuinely lacks a PTPC-capable kernel" from "an earlier gate wrongly rejected the good kernels" — the message is identical in both cases.
2. **The guard fires too late.** It raises after `super().create_weights()` has already run, i.e. after the weights have been allocated in the quantized layout for a configuration that can never work.

Model-independent — identical failure on `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` (hybrid) and `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t` (dense), 2/2 each: the defect is in the kernel-selection / error-reporting path, not in the model.

> Note on hardware: the `fp8_per_channel` path was also observed on an RTX 5880 Ada. If `cutlass_fp8_supported()` (→ `ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp8(...)`) reports `False` on a device whose compute capability is already ≥ 8.9, that is an **additional** finding (the advertised fallback is unreachable); please see the probe output in the environment section. The two defects above hold regardless.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t",  # dense, small
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,   # lower if your GPU is smaller
    quantization="fp8_per_channel",
)
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

## Expected behavior

The failure should be reported with the actual per-kernel rejection reasons, so it is actionable, e.g.:

```
ValueError: quantization="fp8_per_channel" has no usable kernel on this device:
  - FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel: <reason>
  - CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel: <reason>
  (MarlinFP8 was selected but is W8A16 weight-only and cannot honor per-token activation quantization)
```

Ideally the check also happens *before* `create_weights()` allocates the quantized weights.

## Actual behavior

Config accepted → model init → `QKVParallelLinear.__init__` → `quant_method.create_weights` → Marlin selected by the kernel chooser (collected `failure_reason_list` discarded) → PTPC guard raises `ValueError` mid-model-load, with a message that only names a generic capability requirement.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: **按 `repro_fp8_per_channel_sm89.py` 的 `[probe]` 行填写**（示例格式：`NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation, device capability = sm89, 47.4 GiB`）
- `cutlass_fp8_supported()`: **按探针输出填写**
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13
- Models: `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t`, `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`

## Full traceback (crash site, from EngineCore log)

```text
File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/stablelm.py", line 133, in __init__
  self.qkv_proj = QKVParallelLinear(
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 1067, in __init__
  super().__init__(
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 519, in __init__
  self.quant_method.create_weights(
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py", line 386, in create_weights
  raise ValueError(
ValueError: FP8 PTPC online quant requires a kernel that honors per-token activation quantization; MarlinFP8 is W8A16 weight-only. Requires SM89+ for Cutlass FP8 or ROCm MI3xx for rowwise scaled_mm.
```

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator probing `quantization` enum values across model architectures; the two models below were then re-run standalone (2/2 each) to confirm the failure is not model-specific:

  | model | arch | quantization | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t | dense | `fp8_per_channel` | **crash: FP8 PTPC online quant … MarlinFP8 is W8A16 weight-only** |
  | LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B | hybrid | `fp8_per_channel` | same crash, same message |
  | stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t | dense | `fp8` (per-tensor online) | OK, engine runs — control isolating the PTPC path |

- Crash points:
  - kernel chooser: `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py` — `init_fp8_linear_kernel` → `choose_scaled_mm_linear_kernel` (returns Marlin; collected `failure_reason_list` discarded)
  - guard: `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py:386` (`Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod.create_weights`, after `super().create_weights()`)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

`max_lora_rank` accepts 256/320/512 as documented config values (`MaxLoRARanks = Literal[1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 320, 512]`, `vllm/config/lora.py:27`), and `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` accepts them. But on a **MoE model** (`allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct`, 64 experts), setting `enable_lora=True` with `max_lora_rank=320` crashes the engine during startup — in the dummy warmup forward, before any LoRA adapter is even loaded:

```
AssertionError: fused_moe_lora_one_shot supports max_lora_rank<=128; got rank=320
```

The MoE fused LoRA triton path has a hard kernel capacity limit of 128, enforced only as a raw `assert` deep inside a torch custom op (`_run_fused_moe_lora_one_shot`, `vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py:352`), reached via `triton_moe.py` → `punica_gpu.py` during the fused-MoE forward. Nothing reconciles the config-level `max_lora_rank` (which allows 512) against the selected MoE-LoRA backend's capacity (128), so a config-valid value produces an opaque `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed` with the assert only visible in EngineCore stderr.

The same model with `max_lora_rank=128` starts and runs normally, confirming the trigger is exactly the rank value hitting the MoE kernel cap.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct",  # MoE
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,   # lower if your GPU is smaller
    enable_lora=True,
    max_lora_rank=320,             # a config-valid value per MaxLoRARanks
)
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

No LoRA adapter request is needed — the engine dies during startup.

## Expected behavior

Either the MoE LoRA path handles rank>128, or the invalid-for-backend combination is rejected cleanly at config-validation time with a descriptive error, e.g.:

```
ValueError: max_lora_rank=320 exceeds the capacity of the fused MoE LoRA kernels (max 128).
```

Currently the mismatch is only discovered as a raw kernel assert mid-warmup, and the user-visible error is an opaque engine-init failure.

## Actual behavior

Config accepted → model loads → startup dummy forward through fused MoE → `apply_w13_lora` → `punica_wrapper.add_lora_w13` → `fused_moe_lora` → `_run_fused_moe_lora_one_shot` → `assert rank <= 128` fails → EngineCore dies → client sees `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`.

## Environment

- vLLM: 0.31.0 (official wheel)
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation (sm89, 47.4 GiB)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.35), Python 3.12.13
- Model: `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct` (MoE, bf16 checkpoint)

## Full traceback (crash site, from EngineCore log)

  ) = self.apply_w13_lora(

File ".../vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_gpu.py", line 637, in add_lora_w13

File ".../vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_gpu.py", line 492, in add_lora_fused_moe

File ".../vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py", line 1506, in _fused_moe_lora

## Additional context

- Found by a config-interaction test generator probing the documented `max_lora_rank` enum against model architectures.
- Cross-check on the same model/GPU:

  | config | outcome |
  |---|---|
  | `enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=320` | **crash: `AssertionError: fused_moe_lora_one_shot supports max_lora_rank<=128; got rank=320`** |
  | `enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=128` | OK, engine runs and generates |

- The assert is reachable through the standard fused-MoE forward (`moe_runner.py` → `routed_experts.py` → `fused_moe_modular_method.py` → `modular_kernel.py` → `triton_moe.py`), so it will hit any MoE architecture using the triton fused-MoE LoRA mixin whenever a config-legal rank > 128 is requested.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

For a **bfloat16** checkpoint (`allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct`) with **online fp8 quantization** (`quantization="fp8"`) and `kv_cache_dtype="float16"`, config validation passes, but the engine dies during startup memory profiling with the same raw kernel assert reported in #60859:

```
RuntimeError: mha_varlen_fwd, /workspace/.deps/vllm-flash-attn-src/csrc/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp:601, query and key must have the same dtype
```

Crash path: `determine_available_memory` → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `capture_model(profile_only=True)` → `forward_fn(CUDAGraphMode.NONE)` → flash-attn `mha_varlen_fwd`.

The point of this report: the missing dtype-compat validation is **not limited to plain bf16 checkpoints**. With online fp8 quantization the linear layers run quantized while attention still receives bf16 queries; nothing reconciles the triple (model dtype × quantization × kv_cache_dtype), and the FLASH_ATTN path again passes bf16 query tensors against fp16 KV cache without a cast.

Control: the same model + `quantization="fp8"` **without** `kv_cache_dtype` runs fine (2/2) — causality is isolated to `kv_cache_dtype="float16"` on the fp8-quant path.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct",  # bf16 checkpoint
    quantization="fp8",           # online fp8 quantization
    kv_cache_dtype="float16",     # <-- triggers the bug
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,  # lower if your GPU is smaller
)
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

## Expected behavior

Either the engine works (cast the query to the KV-cache dtype as the FLASHINFER path already does for fp8 KV), or the combination is rejected cleanly at config-validation time with a descriptive error, e.g.:

```
ValueError: kv_cache_dtype="float16" is incompatible with dtype="bfloat16" under quantization="fp8" on the FlashAttention backend.
```

## Actual behavior

Config accepted → EngineCore init → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `capture_model(profile_only=True)` → raw CUDA kernel assert → `RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

For hybrid mamba-attention models (e.g. `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`, conv + SSM + full-attention layers), setting the documented engine flag `disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=True` passes CPU-side config validation (`EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`), but the EngineCore process then dies during memory profiling:

```
ValueError: Failed to promote local KV cache specs to one unified type.
```

Crash path: `determine_available_memory` → `profile_cudagraph_memory` → `_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling` → `get_kv_cache_groups` → `unify_hybrid_kv_cache_specs` → `_promote_local_kv_cache_specs` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1901`).

The trigger is precisely the **flag × hybrid-architecture** interaction (same GPU, same stack, ~30 configs probed):

- The flag on 10+ **non-hybrid** models (bloom-560m, phi-2, opt-125m, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, OLMoE-1B-7B, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, ...) → accepted, engine runs.
- The same hybrid model **without** the flag (including with suffix spec-decode + `mamba_cache_dtype` variants) → engine runs fine.
- The minimal single-flag repro → crashes deterministically (2/2 independent attempts).

So on hybrid models the flag is either not honored (the hybrid unification path runs anyway and then fails) or unsupported — either way the combination should be guarded at config-validation time, not discovered as a deep `ValueError` inside EngineCore memory profiling.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B",   # hybrid: conv + SSM (mamba) + full attention
    max_model_len=4096,
    seed=42,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,    # lower if your GPU is smaller
    disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=True,
)
llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=8))
```

## Expected behavior

Either the fallback (non-hybrid KV cache manager) is honored and the engine runs, or the combination is rejected cleanly at config time, e.g.:

```

title: [Bug]: NixlConnector: KV blocks released on lease expiry while remote READ in flight, decode silently consumes overwritten KV
body:
### Your current environment

**Env:** vLLM 0.30.0 (aed92ba5), NixlConnector 1P1D on one host, UCX (`UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy`), Qwen2.5-0.5B, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 2048`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** With the pull flow, the producer releases a request's KV blocks when `kv_lease_duration` expires, unconditionally — it does not matter whether a consumer read is still pending or about to be issued. The consumer side has no content/identity binding on the block descriptors it received earlier, so it reads whatever bytes now occupy those slots (they may belong to a newer request that reused them) and feeds them to the model with no error or warning. Output is silently wrong.

**Repro (deterministic, no code changes):**

1. Start P (`kv_role=kv_producer`) and D (`kv_role=kv_consumer`).
2. Send a completion to P with `kv_transfer_params={"do_remote_decode": true, ...}` (max_tokens=1). Record the returned `kv_transfer_params` (remote_block_ids / remote_request_id).
3. Stall the decode engine for > `kv_lease_duration` (default 30 s). We used `SIGSTOP` on the decode processes to simulate an engine pause (GC / long step / scheduler stall); ~33.6 s total.
4. During the stall, P logs: `Releasing expired KV blocks for request <id> which were retrieved by 0 remote worker(s) before lease expired.`
5. Send new completions to P (same total token length) so the freed slots are reused and overwritten with different content.
6. Resume D and send the original completion to D with the recorded `kv_transfer_params`.
7. D performs the remote pull (`NIXL compatibility check passed` — the only check is the layout hash) and generates. The output continues *the other request's* content; there is no error or warning anywhere.

**Results:** 5/5 trials with default `kv_lease_duration=30` and 5/5 with `kv_lease_duration=1`. Decode output in every trial followed the reused content ("foreign") rather than the request's own prompt. Controls: (a) decode computing the same prompt locally → correct output; (b) decode consuming the producer's intact blocks (no reuse) → correct output; (c) canary-direction control → correct. All clean.

**Notes:**

- The producer already warns (`Releasing expired KV blocks ...`) and can log `Potentially invalid KV blocks for unrecognized request ... were retrieved by a decode worker. They may have expired.` (`pull_worker.py` notif handler) — but both are post-hoc: the bytes are already gone / already consumed when they fire, and in our latest runs the latter did not fire at all.
- `kv_lease_duration=1` is degenerate (`_lease_extension = 1*2//3 = 0`, renewal is a no-op), but the default-30s arm reproduces without any unusual configuration — a ~34 s decode-engine pause is enough.
- Two failure shapes observed depending on the model: with a hybrid (mamba+attention) model, reused slots tear across cache groups and the output degenerates; with a pure-attention model, the output coherently continues the other request's content. Both are silent.

**Suggested direction (not a patch):** some binding between what a descriptor names and what is consumed — e.g. hold/release driven by in-flight read tracking on the producer (refcount or a fence handshake with the consumer), or a generation/identity tag carried in the descriptor and checked before the received KV is consumed.

Happy to provide the trial logs and driver on request.

Both deployments reproduced the failures. We called them BAD and GOOD; initially, GOOD was just a copy. 2. **Build the tests:** With Codex, we built and ran a Python harness with four concurrent dialogs per system. Basic calls passed. Harder cases repeatedly failed, especially with reasoning enabled. 3. **Isolate technical failures:** We reduced the tests to an `echo_payload(text)` tool, fixed strings and tool histories. Replaying fixed output through the parser let us distinguish parser corruption from model mistakes. We compared Chat Completions and Responses. 4. **Upgrade GOOD:** We moved only GOOD from NVIDIA 26.06 to 26.09. Some older bugs disappeared, but reasoning markers inside tool arguments were still corrupted. 5. **Patch step by step:** We fixed marker handling, then incorrect cutoff reporting, then tool-result ordering. Each time, we restarted GOOD with patches loaded from the PVC and repeated the tests. No image rebuild was needed. 6. **Verify:** The final nonstreaming run covered 92 HTTP requests, including reasoning-enabled multicalls and follow-ups. The targeted regressions passed. Both GPUs reproduced the initial failures. Later patch comparisons were performed on GOOD, while BAD remained the baseline. ## Environment Full details are collected in `env.txt`. The patched deployment used: - Image: `nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.09-py3` - vLLM: `0.29.0+5013de39.dev` - Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` - Parsers: `qwen3_coder` for tools, `qwen3` for reasoning - Default model tokenizer template; no template override The samples below use the installed vLLM package and cached tokenizer. They require no model inference. Patches were tested on this build. ## 1. A literal `` disappears from tool arguments The reasoning parser removes a closing marker inside a tool parameter before the tool parser receives it. ### Reproducer ```python import json from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.parser import ParserManager from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest model = "unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4" tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, local_files_only=True) tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "echo_payload", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["text"]}}}] kwargs = {"enable_thinking": True} req = ChatCompletionRequest(model=model, messages=[], tools=tools, chat_template_kwargs=kwargs) factory = ParserManager.get_parser(tool_parser_name="qwen3_coder", reasoning_parser_name="qwen3", enable_auto_tools=True, model_name=model) parser = factory(tok, req.tools, chat_template_kwargs=kwargs) raw = ("Reason.\n\n\n\n" "\nalpha literal omega\n" "\n\n") _, _, calls = parser.parse(raw, req, enable_auto_tools=True, model_output_token_ids=tok.encode(raw, add_special_tokens=False)) print(json.loads(calls[0].arguments)["text"]) ``` ```text Expected: alpha literal omega Actual: alpha literal omega ``` ### Tested fix Preserve reasoning markers inside forwarded Qwen tool parameters and reset the tracking flag between parses. ```diff --- a/vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py +++ b/vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py @@ -207,6 +207,7 @@ self._message_header_buffer = "" self._message_header_token_count = 0 self._in_skipped_tool_span = False + self._in_qwen_parameter = False self._reset_args_state() def feed( @@ -361,6 +362,16 @@ def _on_terminal( self, terminal: str, value: str, token_count: int = 0 ) -> list[SemanticEvent]: + # Preserve literal reasoning markers in Qwen XML parameter values + # during the reasoning-only pass. The tool pass parses these next. + if self.skip_tool_parsing and self.config.name == "qwen3": + if terminal == "PARAM_START" and self._in_skipped_tool_span: + self._in_qwen_parameter = True + elif terminal == "PARAM_END": + self._in_qwen_parameter = False + elif self._in_qwen_parameter and terminal in ("THINK_START", "THINK_END"): + return self._emit_for_state(value, token_count) + key = (self.state, terminal) transition = self.config.transitions.get(key) ``` Parser checks improved from **48/240 to 240/240**. These include chunk-boundary tests, not 240 model requests. This patch does not cover marker quotations inside actual reasoning. ## 2. Chat reports a tool call as finished after hitting the token limit When the engine stops with `length`, nonstreaming Chat can replace it with `tool_calls`. We observed this in **22/22** budget-limited requests, including calls with empty arguments. ### Reproducer Evaluate the actual finish-reason expression from the installed server: ```python import ast from pathlib import Path from types import SimpleNamespace import vllm path = Path(vllm.__file__).parent / "entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py" expressions = [n.value for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text())) if isinstance(n, ast.keyword) and n.arg == "finish_reason" and "is_finish_reason_tool_calls" in ast.unparse(n.value)] assert len(expressions) == 1 print(eval(compile(ast.Expression(expressions[0]), str(path), "eval"), { "output": SimpleNamespace(finish_reason="length"), "is_finish_reason_tool_calls": True, })) ``` ```text Expected: length Actual: tool_calls ``` ### Tested fix ```diff --- a/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py +++ b/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py @@ -1084,7 +1084,9 @@ index=output.index, message=message, logprobs=logprobs, - finish_reason="tool_calls" + finish_reason="length" + if output.finish_reason == "length" + else "tool_calls" if is_finish_reason_tool_calls else output.finish_reason if output.finish_reason ``` This preserves the cutoff status; it does not repair partial arguments. [Upstream PR #58286](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58286) addresses this nonstreaming bug and was still open on October 12, 2026. It preserves all non-`stop` finish reasons, which is broader than our local fix. We would prefer to use that upstream fix. **Responses did better here:** all 22 corresponding requests returned global `status="incomplete"` with reason `max_output_tokens`. Individual function-call items still reported `completed`, so clients must check the overall status. Responses reported the cutoff better; it did not produce better arguments. ## 3. The template loses the link between calls and out-of-order results Two tool calls are emitted in A/B order. Their results arrive in B/A order with correct IDs. The template drops those IDs and leaves only the result order, so the model can swap the values. ### Reproducer ```python from transformers import AutoTokenizer tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4", local_files_only=True) tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "echo_payload", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["text"]}}}] messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "Return the receipt for A and the receipt for B."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [ {"id": "call_A", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "echo_payload", "arguments": {"text": "A"}}}, {"id": "call_B", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "echo_payload", "arguments": {"text": "B"}}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_B", "content": "3f84d6"}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_A", "content": "7c92e1"}, ] prompt = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tools=tools, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True) print(prompt) print("IDs preserved:", "call_A" in prompt, "call_B" in prompt) ``` The rendered prompt contains neither `call_A` nor `call_B`. Correct mapping is **A → 7c92e1, B → 3f84d6**, but the results appear in B/A order without IDs. We also confirmed this in actual server prompt tokens. This sample renders the template directly. It still shows the missing IDs after our preprocessing workaround, because it bypasses that preprocessing. ### Tested fix Before rendering, reorder complete adjacent result batches by their call IDs. We added this to both sync and async chat preprocessing, which also covers converted Responses inputs. ```diff --- a/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py +++ b/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py @@ -2117,6 +2117,37 @@ function["arguments"] = {} +def _order_qwen_tool_results(messages, model_config): + """Order complete adjacent result batches for this positional Qwen template. + + Never infer missing IDs or move results across another conversation turn. + A shallow list copy preserves every message and its content unchanged. + """ + if getattr(model_config, 'model', None) != 'unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4': + return messages + ordered = list(messages) + i = 0 + while i < len(ordered): + message = ordered[i] + calls = message.get('tool_calls') if message.get('role') == 'assistant' else None + if not isinstance(calls, list) or len(calls) < 2: + i += 1 + continue + ids = [call.get('id') if isinstance(call, dict) else None for call in calls] + end = i + 1 + while end < len(ordered) and ordered[end].get('role') == 'tool': + end += 1 + batch = ordered[i + 1:end] + result_ids = [item.get('tool_call_id') for item in batch] + if (all(isinstance(value, str) and value for value in ids + result_ids) + and len(ids) == len(set(ids)) and len(batch) == len(ids) + and set(result_ids) == set(ids)): + by_id = {item['tool_call_id']: item for item in batch} + ordered[i + 1:end] = [by_id[call_id] for call_id in ids] + i = end + return ordered + + def parse_chat_messages( messages: list[ChatCompletionMessageParam], model_config: ModelConfig, @@ -2128,6 +2159,7 @@ MultiModalDataDict | None, MultiModalUUIDDict | None, ]: + messages = _order_qwen_tool_results(messages, model_config) conversation: list[ConversationMessage] = [] mm_tracker = MultiModalItemTracker( model_config, @@ -2167,6 +2199,7 @@ MultiModalDataDict | None, MultiModalUUIDDict | None, ]: + messages = _order_qwen_tool_results(messages, model_config) conversation: list[ConversationMessage] = [] mm_tracker = AsyncMultiModalItemTracker( model_config, ``` This workaround is limited to our model. It leaves incomplete or ambiguous batches unchanged and never moves results across conversation turns. The template itself stays unchanged. Using the exact same requests with neutral result values, reversed-result cases improved from **0/4 to 4/4**. In **8/8** template checks, both result orders then produced identical prompts. ## Final results After all three patches, with streaming disabled: | Check | Chat | Responses | | --- | --- | --- | | Neutral results, both orders | 4/4 correct | 4/4 correct | | Reasoning-enabled multicall scenarios, including expected cutoffs | 10/10 passed | 10/10 passed | | Complete follow-ups with reversed results | 6/6 correct | 6/6 correct | | Budget cutoffs | 22/22 `length` | 22/22 `incomplete` | | Complete budget controls | 4/4 correct | 4/4 correct | These 92 requests validate the targeted fixes, not all possible tool-call behavior. Malformed model output and full streaming behavior remain outside this result. ## Upstream status As of October 12, 2026, [v0.31.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.31.0) was the latest stable release. Our source comparison still found the affected [parser handling](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py), [finish-reason logic](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py), and [input-order processing](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py) used with the [ID-less model template](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4/raw/main/chat_template.jinja). The three affected NVIDIA source files match upstream **v0.29.0** byte for byte. The relevant problems remain in **v0.31.0**, but the versions are not identical. We checked community source code, not a running community container; the patches need review before applying them to another version. We also tested the patch with **Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4**, where it resolved the tool-call errors we observed. ## Questions - Is protecting literal markers inside tool parameters the right parser fix? - Can our cutoff tests help validate PR #58286? - Should vLLM reorder results for ID-less templates, or should the template preserve the IDs? Kindly regards, Philipp ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--revision pre-final` and

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

startup fails:

```
File ".../vllm/config/speculative.py", line 1489, in __post_init__
    and self.num_speculative_tokens % n_predict != 0
ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero
```

For `method="mtp"`, `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` copies `model` (and `quantization`) from the target model config, but the draft `ModelConfig` is created with `revision=self.revision`, which is `None` unless set explicitly in the speculative config. The MTP draft therefore loads config (and weights) from the repo's default branch instead of the target's revision.

Passing the revision explicitly fixes it:

```
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"revision":"pre-final"}'
```

### Expected behavior
For `method="mtp"` (draft = target checkpoint), the draft should inherit the target's `revision` (and `code_revision`) when not set, the same way it inherits `model` and `quantization`.

### Additional notes
- If `n_predict` resolves to 0, the divisibility check should raise a readable error instead of `ZeroDivisionError`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug # 🐛 Describe the bug The Anthropic Messages request schema accepts a list of content blocks in the top-level `system` field, including `image` blocks. During conversion to vLLM's internal chat request, `_convert_system_message()` only appends text blocks. The request is accepted, but the non-text system block is omitted from the converted prompt without an error. ## Steps to reproduce Start vLLM with a local model that can be used with the Anthropic Messages API. If the model has no chat template, provide a simple one such as the following in a file named `chat_template.jinja`: ```jinja {% for message in messages %}{{ message['role'] }}: {{ message['content'] }} {% endfor %}assistant: ``` For example, start the server on loopback: ```sh vllm serve /path/to/local-chat-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --served-model-name local-test-model \ --chat-template /path/to/chat_template.jinja ``` Send a text-only control request and then the same request with an image block added to `system`: ```python import json from urllib.request import Request, urlopen url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/messages/count_tokens" base = { "model": "local-test-model", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}], } image = { "type": "image", "source": { "type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png", "data": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAwMCAO+jLioAAAAASUVORK5CYII=", }, } for label, system in ( ("text-only", [{"type": "text", "text": "Follow the instructions in the image."}]), ("text-and-image", [ {"type": "text", "text": "Follow the instructions in the image."}, image, ]), ): body = json.dumps({**base, "system": system}).encode() request = Request(url, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) with urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response: result = json.load(response) print(label, response.status, { "input_tokens": result["input_tokens"], "original_input_tokens": result["original_input_tokens"], }) ``` ## Expected behavior The Anthropic Messages API defines the top-level `system` field as a string or a list of text blocks. When a request contains unsupported non-text blocks in this field, vLLM should reject the request with a clear validation error or, at minimum, emit an explicit warning before discarding the unsupported content. This would be consistent with the warning-based compatibility approach adopted for the OpenAI-compatible API in PR #34072. ## Actual behavior Both requests returned HTTP 200 and the same token counts in the live test: ```text text-only 200 {'input_tokens': 17, 'original_input_tokens': 17} text-and-image 200 {'input_tokens': 17, 'original_input_tokens': 17} ``` `GET /health` returned HTTP 200 before and after the requests. The test confirms that the image block does not affect the request rendered and counted by this endpoint. It does not test generated model output. ## References - [Anthropic request schema for Messages](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py#L36-L50) - [Anthropic request schema for token counting](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/protocol.py#L321-L326) - [System-block conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py#L311-L346) Related issue and prior fix: - #33925 reported that the OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepted non-text system content. - PR #34072 introduced warnings for unsupported system content in the OpenAI-compatible request path to preserve backward compatibility. The Anthropic-compatible conversion path in `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py` is not covered by that change and still silently discards unsupported system content blocks. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

This means users cannot disable the compressed-file-size limit as the documentation describes. ## Steps to reproduce Run the following in an installed vLLM environment. The decoder is replaced with a stub so the test only exercises the size checks. ```sh for limit in 0 1; do VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB="$limit" python - <<'PY' import os from unittest.mock import patch from vllm.multimodal.media.audio import AudioMediaIO print("limit=" + os.environ["VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB"]) loader = AudioMediaIO() with patch("vllm.multimodal.media.audio.load_audio", return_value=(None, 0.0)) as decode: for label, load in ( ("bytes", lambda: loader.load_bytes(b"x")), ("base64", lambda: loader.load_base64("audio/wav", "eA==")), ): try: load() except Exception as exc: print(label, type(exc).__name__, str(exc)) else: print(label, "accepted by size check") print("decoder_called:", decode.called) PY done ``` ## Expected behavior Setting the limit to `0` should disable the compressed-file-size check, as described in the security guide. The separate audio-duration and decoded-audio-byte limits should remain in effect. ## Actual behavior With the limit set to `0`, both the bytes and base64 cases raise `VLLMValidationError` with `Maximum file size exceeded`, and the decoder stub is not called. With the control value set to `1`, both inputs pass the encoded-size checks and reach the decoder stub. The test uses a synthetic one-byte payload and does not claim it is valid audio. ```text limit=0 bytes VLLMValidationError Maximum file size exceeded (parameter=audio_filesize_mb, value=9.5367431640625e-07) base64 VLLMValidationError Maximum file size exceeded (parameter=audio_filesize_mb, value=2.86102294921875e-06) decoder_called: False limit=1 bytes accepted by size check base64 accepted by size check decoder_called: True ``` ## References - [Security guide: media-size limits and zero-value behavior](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/docs/usage/security.md#L94-L105) - [Audio encoded-size checks](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py#L540-L574) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Severe output degeneration on SM120 with Apertus-70B FP8 in vLLM 0.25.1; v0.22.1 works after rollback
body:
### Your current environment

Summary

We observed a severe text-generation correctness regression when upgrading from vLLM 0.22.1 to 0.25.1 using the same RedHatAI/Apertus-70B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic checkpoint on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120).

The v0.25.1 engine initializes successfully, reports healthy, discovers the correct model, and returns HTTP 200 for inference. However, even a direct, non-streaming, temperature-zero request produces incoherent repetitive text until the completion-token limit is reached.

After rolling back the Docker image to v0.22.1, normal generation was restored, including correct arithmetic responses through the application.

This is a silent generation-quality failure rather than an initialization crash or API availability issue.

Environment

Component | Value -- | -- GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition GPU architecture | SM120 NVIDIA driver | 595.99.02 Model | RedHatAI/Apertus-70B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic Model quantization | compressed-tensors, W8A8 FP8 Compute dtype | torch.bfloat16 KV cache | fp8_e4m3 Model context length | 65536 Tensor parallel size | 1 vLLM engine | V1 FP8 linear backend | CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel Attention backend | FLASHINFER Sampling backend | FlashInfer top-p/top-k Compilation | VLLM_COMPILE, Inductor CUDA graphs | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE

Docker image IDs:

  • Working v0.22.1: sha256:953d3a06d5e64ab582985cd7401289d3abf2a2c14ef2158e9a84313daeec77d7

  • Failing v0.25.1: sha256:e4f88a835143cd22aee2397a26ec6bb80b3a4a6fe0c882bcbc63822904766089

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Minimal direct reproduction on v0.25.1

Request submitted directly to the vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint, bypassing RAG, middleware, retrieval, conversation history, and application streaming.

{
  "model": "RedHatAI/Apertus-70B-Instruct-2509-FP8-dynamic",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": "Odpovedaj výlučne po slovensky, stručne a presne."
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Koľko je 1+1? Odpovedz iba číslom."
    }
  ],
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "stream": false
}

Expected response: 2.

Observed:

HTTP_STATUS=200
FINISH_REASON=length
COMPLETION_TOKENS=256
REASONING_CHARS=0
SEMANTIC_EXACT_2=False

Output excerpt:

The,,,,,,,,,,
,,,
 and,,,
 and,,
. and,,,
. of the of. of... the of and the of and...

The model continued generating repetitive, incoherent text rather than answering the question.

No API exception, model-loading exception, or container-health failure occurred.

Rollback observations

After restoring vLLM 0.22.1 using the original Docker image and preserving the model identity and operational configuration:

Container health: healthy
Application prompt: 1024 x 1024?
Answer: 1 048 576
Completion tokens: 10
Finish reason: stop
Deep Dive collection: COMPLETE

The successful rollback test used a different arithmetic prompt and the application's streaming path. An identical direct-request A/B replay has not yet been performed; therefore this should be treated as strong rollback-associated evidence rather than a fully controlled single-variable benchmark.

Dependency comparison

Exact versions obtained by inspecting both immutable Docker images:

Dependency | Working 0.22.1 | Failing 0.25.1 -- | -- | -- torch | 2.11.0+cu130 | 2.11.0+cu130 triton | 3.6.0 | 3.6.0 flashinfer-python | 0.6.11.post2 | 0.6.13 flashinfer-cubin | 0.6.11.post2 | 0.6.13 flashinfer-jit-cache | 0.6.11.post2+cu130 | 0.6.13+cu130 compressed-tensors | 0.15.0.1 | 0.17.0 transformers | 5.10.2 | 5.13.1 tokenizers | 0.22.2 | 0.22.2 accelerate | 1.13.0 | 1.14.0 nvidia-cudnn-cu13 | 9.19.0.56 | 9.19.0.56

The different versions are diagnostic candidates, not confirmed root causes.

Kernel-selection evidence

Both versions report:

Selected CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8
Using FLASHINFER attention backend
Using FlashInfer for top-p & top-k sampling

The failing v0.25.1 additionally reports:

FlashInfer resolved query dtypes:
prefill=torch.bfloat16
decode=torch.bfloat16
decode_backend=flashinfer-native
kv_cache_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
arch=sm120

The available v0.22.1 startup excerpt does not expose an equivalent decode-kernel resolution line. Thus identical backend names do not establish identical low-level kernel implementations.

v0.25.1 also initializes vendored DeepGEMM facilities, but the logged FP8 linear kernel is CUTLASS. We have no evidence that the specific DeepGEMM JIT selection failure described in #60261 is responsible for this issue.

Requested investigation

Could maintainers investigate possible correctness regressions between v0.22.1 and v0.25.1 affecting:

  • CompressedTensors W8A8 FP8 weight loading, scale interpretation, or CUTLASS integration.

  • FlashInfer 0.6.11 to 0.6.13, particularly SM120 decode with FP8 KV cache.

  • vLLM V1 model execution, graph capture, and compiled paths on SM120.

  • Interactions between vLLM and compressed-tensors 0.17.0.

We are not attributing the defect to any particular library or kernel at this stage.

The production system has been restored to v0.22.1. We can provide sanitized engine-startup logs, exact immutable image identities, generation metadata, and additional bounded reproduction results if needed.

Impact: A model that passes health and API readiness checks may return severely corrupted output without raising an error. This makes correctness regression detection particularly important for production deployments.

### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

We first hit it with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 and Gemma 4 31B, but the root cause is model-independent: `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`, used by `ops.swap_blocks_batch`, faults on this vGPU even for a single in-bounds descriptor. ### Minimal repro (no model) ```python import torch from vllm import _custom_ops as ops N = 4 << 20 # one 4 MiB copy gpu = torch.randint(0, 255, (N,), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") host = torch.zeros(N, dtype=torch.uint8) assert int(torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostRegister(host.data_ptr(), N, 0)) == 0 src = torch.tensor([gpu.data_ptr()], dtype=torch.int64) dst = torch.tensor([host.data_ptr()], dtype=torch.int64) sizes = torch.tensor([N], dtype=torch.int64) stream = torch.cuda.Stream() with torch.cuda.stream(stream): ops.swap_blocks_batch(src, dst, sizes, is_src_access_order_any=False) stream.synchronize() # vGPU: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure, host logs Xid 31 print("OK, data matches:", torch.equal(host, gpu.cpu())) ``` ``` torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure ``` Host side, one entry per run: ``` NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:15:00): 31, channel 0x03000000 nvidia-vgpu-mgr: error: vmiop_log: (0x0): XID 31 detected on physical_chid:0x2, guest_chid:0x2 ``` ### Narrowing it down A longer script ([swap_test.py](https://gist.github.com/jerry102039/860de1bb1810a962c58bab7668bd2a03)) moves random 4 MiB blocks in both directions between a GPU tensor and `cudaHostRegister`ed host memory, using vLLM's own descriptor buffers (`_new_descriptor_buffers`) and only in-bounds addresses: | Implementation (same descriptors, same addresses) | Result | |---|---| | `ops.swap_blocks_batch` (cuMemcpyBatchAsync), 64 descriptors/call, `/dev/shm`-backed host memory (as in `SharedOffloadRegion`) | ❌ launch failure + Xid 31 | | same, anonymous host memory | ❌ launch failure + Xid 31 | | same, **1 descriptor/call** | ❌ launch failure + Xid 31 | | one plain `cuMemcpyAsync` per descriptor | ✅ ~48 GiB/s both directions, 0 mismatches | So the addresses, the pinned host memory and the DMA path itself are fine; only the batched API faults. `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS=1` does not help for the same reason. ### End-to-end symptom `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":68719476736}}'` crashes deterministically on the first offload store (same scheduler state and block IDs every run). With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, all model kernels complete and the error only surfaces at the next event sync, consistent with an async memcpy fault: ``` gpu_model_runner.py:3813 self.prepare_inputs_event.synchronize() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure ... [gpu_worker.py:775] Failed to synchronize transfer end event; skipping 3 remaining transfers ``` ### Expected behavior / proposal `swap_blocks_batch` already has a per-copy `cudaMemcpyAsync` fallback (used for older drivers and the legacy default stream), but there is no runtime opt-out. I'll open a PR adding `VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_DISABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY=1` to force that fallback; with it, the repro above passes and end-to-end offload runs with stores at ~50 GiB/s and loads at ~49 GiB/s, no Xid. The underlying fault is most likely in the vGPU driver; I'm reporting it to NVIDIA separately. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (revision `2cba9e42`), 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, torch 2.13.0.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek-V4.1 served with a FlashInfer MegaMoE backend at TP=1 with DP+EP starts and answers short prompts, then crashes once it serves long prompts or batched prefills (here GSM8K 5-shot at `--max-concurrency 128`):

```text
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm

```

    torch.index_select(t, 0, rows, out=buf[:num_rows])
RuntimeError: Expected out tensor to have dtype int, but got long int instead
```

  File ".../vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 428, in _replay

  File ".../vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 217, in replay
    r()
  File ".../vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py", line 118, in <lambda>
    return capture.add_eager(lambda: fn(*weak_args, **weak_kwargs))
  File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/decoder_replay_layers.py", line 99, in _run_in_graph_break
