title: [Bug]: InternLM2 streaming tool parser drops characters from function arguments
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM 0.30.0 and 0.28.0, CPU, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `Internlm2ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` can emit argument deltas whose concatenation is not the final function arguments. Characters are silently dropped as the partially parsed JSON grows. Once the emitted text is no longer a prefix of the completed arguments, `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` cannot flush the missing tail. The attached `repro.py` feeds the same call using two chunk boundaries. For the failing split, it prints: ```text '{"location": "Beijing, "days": 3' ``` instead of: ```text '{"location": "Beijing", "days": 3}' ``` ### Expected behavior The concatenated streaming argument deltas should exactly equal the completed tool call arguments for every valid chunk boundary. ### Suggested fix Stream slices from the raw argument text while tracking the number of characters already emitted. Avoid reconstructing deltas from repeatedly serialized partial JSON, which can introduce temporary suffixes that later disappear. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

body:

### 🐛 Describe the bug `TensorizerConfig.__post_init__` derives `tensorizer_dir` only when `tensorizer_uri` is supplied explicitly. A configuration created using the documented LoRA-only form keeps `tensorizer_dir=None`. Code that writes the adapter then constructs a path such as `None/adapter_config.json`, and serializing and rebuilding the configuration changes its value. ```python from vllm.config.load import LoadConfig from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer import TensorizerConfig from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer_loader import TensorizerLoader tc = TensorizerConfig(lora_dir="/tmp/lora") print(tc.tensorizer_dir) # None print(f"{tc.tensorizer_dir}/adapter_config.json") # None/adapter_config.json loader = TensorizerLoader( LoadConfig( load_format="tensorizer", model_loader_extra_config={ "tensorizer_config": tc.to_serializable(), }, ) ) print(loader.tensorizer_config.tensorizer_dir) # /tmp/lora assert loader.tensorizer_config == tc # fails ``` ### Expected behavior A `lora_dir`-only configuration should resolve `tensorizer_dir` consistently, and `TensorizerConfig(**config.to_serializable())` should be equivalent to the original configuration. ### Suggested fix Derive `tensorizer_dir` from the resolved `tensorizer_uri` in all cases, including when that URI was inferred from `lora_dir`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: `validate_regex_is_buildable` (outlines backend) misses `\b` and backreferences inside groups
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM 0.30.0 (the latest release) and 0.28.0, CPU, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_outlines.validate_regex_is_buildable` rejects regex features that `outlines_core` cannot build (word boundaries, backreferences, look-arounds), but its helper `_check_unsupported` recurses only into `BRANCH` and `MAX_REPEAT` nodes, not into `SUBPATTERN` (group) nodes. The same feature wrapped in a group passes validation: ```python from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_outlines import validate_regex_is_buildable validate_regex_is_buildable(r"a\b") # VLLMValidationError (as intended) validate_regex_is_buildable(r"(a\b)") # accepted validate_regex_is_buildable(r"((a)\2)") # accepted ``` `outlines_core.Index` fails for both accepted patterns (`Failed to build DFA`), so such a request is admitted and fails later in the engine core (`StructuredOutputManager._create_grammar` logs a traceback) instead of being rejected with a validation error. Recursing into `SUBPATTERN` (`tval[3]`), as `_prefix_needs_context` in the same file already does, fixes it. ### Expected Patterns with an unsupported feature are rejected wherever the feature appears. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `PEFTHelper.from_dict` (`vllm/lora/peft_helper.py`) keeps only the `adapter_config.json` keys it knows and drops the rest, and `_validate_features` only rejects DoRA and unsupported `modules_to_save`. So an adapter that relies on a PEFT feature vLLM doesn't implement loads without any error or warning and is served with wrong outputs. This is the same class of problem as #59799 (`rank_pattern` / `alpha_pattern`), for other fields. Repro on main (0872ddf4b9), tiny random Llama, PEFT 0.21.2, RTX 3090. Each adapter is saved with PEFT and reloaded with `PeftModel.from_pretrained` for the reference (`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` only because this machine has no `nvcc`):
repro.py ```python import os import sys import tempfile import torch from peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, LlamaConfig from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest T = ["q_proj", "v_proj", "down_proj"] CASES = { "plain": dict(), "lora_bias": dict(lora_bias=True), "pissa": dict(init_lora_weights="pissa"), "layer_replication": dict(layer_replication=[[0, 2], [1, 2]]), } def main(): tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp() torch.manual_seed(0) cfg = LlamaConfig(vocab_size=1024, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=64, tie_word_embeddings=False) AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg, dtype=torch.bfloat16).save_pretrained(f"{tmp}/base") def base(): return AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(f"{tmp}/base", dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda() prompts = [torch.randint(10, 1024, (48,), generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(i)).tolist() for i in range(4)] def peft_logprobs(model): out = [] with torch.no_grad(): for ids in prompts: x = torch.tensor([ids], device="cuda") logp = torch.log_softmax(model(input_ids=x).logits[0, :-1].float(), -1) out.append(logp.gather(-1, x[0, 1:, None])[:, 0].tolist()) return torch.tensor(out) ref = {} for name, extra in CASES.items(): torch.manual_seed(1) model = get_peft_model(base(), LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=T, **extra)) with torch.no_grad(): for n, p in model.named_parameters(): if "lora_" in n: p.normal_(0, 0.05) model.save_pretrained(f"{tmp}/{name}") # reload the way a user would, so PEFT applies the config on load ref[name] = peft_logprobs(PeftModel.from_pretrained(base(), f"{tmp}/{name}")) ref_base = peft_logprobs(base()) llm = LLM(f"{tmp}/base", skip_tokenizer_init=True, enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=8, max_model_len=256, gpu_memory_utilization=0.3, enforce_eager=True) params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, prompt_logprobs=0, detokenize=False) for i, name in enumerate(CASES, start=1): try: outs = llm.generate([TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=p) for p in prompts], params, lora_request=LoRARequest(name, i, f"{tmp}/{name}"), use_tqdm=False) except Exception as e: print(f"{name:18s} {type(e).__name__}") sys.exit(0) lp = torch.tensor([[o.prompt_logprobs[j][t].logprob for j, t in enumerate(p) if j > 0] for p, o in zip(prompts, outs)]) print(f"{name:18s} mean |vLLM - PEFT|: {(lp - ref[name]).abs().mean():.4f} " f"adapter effect in PEFT: {(ref[name] - ref_base).abs().mean():.4f}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
Output: ```text plain mean |vLLM - PEFT|: 0.0022 adapter effect in PEFT: 0.2029 lora_bias mean |vLLM - PEFT|: 0.3311 adapter effect in PEFT: 0.3136 pissa mean |vLLM - PEFT|: 0.1019 adapter effect in PEFT: 0.2359 layer_replication mean |vLLM - PEFT|: 0.1652 adapter effect in PEFT: 0.2478 ``` The plain adapter matches PEFT within bf16 noise; the others don't, and nothing in the log mentions the dropped fields. What goes wrong for each field: - `lora_bias=True`: PEFT saves a `lora_B.bias` tensor. Since #53555 (which allowed `.bias` for the `score` / `classifier` heads of classification adapters), `parse_fine_tuned_lora_name` also accepts `lora_A.bias` / `lora_B.bias` and maps them to the same module as the weight, so whichever tensor is loaded last becomes `lora_b`. With safetensors the bias comes first in key order, so lora_B's weight survives and the bias is dropped; with a `.bin` adapter the ordering can differ and lora_B can end up as the 1-D bias. Before #53555, such adapters were rejected with `... is unsupported LoRA weight`. #53555 is in v0.31.0 but not in v0.30.0, so this is a regression in the v0.31.0 release. - `init_lora_weights` = `"pissa"` / `"pissa_niter_*"` / `"olora"` / `"corda"` / `"loftq"` / `"lora_ga"`: when PEFT loads such an adapter it rewrites the base layer weights (for example `pissa_init` and `corda_init` in `peft/tuners/lora/layer.py` assign `get_base_layer().weight.data`), so the adapter is only correct on the modified base. vLLM serves it on the unmodified base. PEFT's own `path_initial_model_for_weight_conversion` produces a regular adapter and resets the field to `true`, so converted adapters are unaffected. PiSSA was measured above; OLoRA was measured on CPU (similar gap); CorDA, LoftQ and LoRA-GA follow from the PEFT code, not measured. - `layer_replication`: PEFT builds extra layers by sharing base weights and gives each its own LoRA; vLLM's model has no such layers, so those LoRAs are skipped. - `alora_invocation_tokens` (Activated LoRA): PEFT applies the adapter only from the invocation tokens on; vLLM applies it to every token (support was proposed in #19710, closed unmerged). - `use_bdlora` (BD-LoRA) and `use_qalora`: the stored A or B matrices are narrower than the layer (block-diagonal / pooled input). `set_lora` copies them into the top-left corner of the zero-padded slot without a shape check, so they load as a different matrix. Measured for BD-LoRA (mean diff 0.44 on a tiny Llama); QALoRA follows from the same code path. This also affects published adapters. A search of the Hugging Face Hub finds about 100 PEFT adapters whose config still has `init_lora_weights` set to `"pissa"` / `"olora"` or uses aLoRA. For one of them, `AkameV6p5/qwen2.5-3b-agent-pissa-sft` on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B`, vLLM differs from PEFT by 3.44 in mean prompt logprob (PEFT's own run-to-run difference is 1.55, from its randomized SVD) and matches PEFT with `init_lora_weights` forced to `true` (0.06), so it is served as a plain LoRA on the unmodified base. Not affected (checked to match PEFT): `use_rslora`, `layers_to_transform`, `exclude_modules`, `init_lora_weights` = `true` / `"gaussian"` / `"eva"` / `"orthogonal"` / `"mica"`, embedding and `lm_head` LoRA. ## Proposed fix Reject these adapters with a clear error, the same way DoRA is rejected: read the fields in `PEFTHelper` and add them to `_validate_features`, and only accept `.weight` for `lora_A` / `lora_B` in `parse_fine_tuned_lora_name` (keeping `.bias` for `score` / `classifier`). Fields that open PRs are adding support for are left alone: `target_parameters` (#52198), `trainable_token_indices` (#55796), DoRA (#47395); if BD-LoRA support (#28136) lands first, its rejection can be dropped. I'm working on a PR for this. A generic shape check in `set_lora` would also catch the BD-LoRA / QALoRA case, but it runs at activation time where an error stops the engine, so I'd keep that for a follow-up next to the load-time validation in #59924. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: [KV Offload][P2P] After a peer's EngineCore stalls ~45 s, P2P transfers to and from it fail permanently, although the control session reconnects
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.30.0+g87ecf7d`, plus open PRs #56836 and #57139 and some local P2P hardening patches (see the note below).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2 (UCX backend).
- 8× H100 80GB HBM3 per node, driver 580.126.20, RoCE.
- Model: GLM-5.3, disaggregated prefill/decode. Prefill is DP4 × PCP8, one DP rank per node, with `TieringOffloadingSpec`: a 512 GiB CPU primary tier plus a `p2p` secondary tier over UCX.


The P2P tier config on each prefill rank:

```json
{"type": "p2p", "host": "<pod ip>", "port": 7777, "backends": ["UCX"], "num_threads": 4,
 "connect_timeout_s": 30, "heartbeat_interval_s": 2, "heartbeat_timeout_s": 10}
```

Note: this build is vLLM `87ecf7d` plus #56836, #57139 (`data/nixl.py` byte-identical to #57139's head `590a8d97`) and four local patches: unacked handshakes expire to MISS; reconnects that reuse a peer's identity are accepted (`ROUTER_HANDOVER`); configurable heartbeat and connect timeouts (the last three fields above); and control sends that never block the scheduler. We have not yet reproduced this on plain `main`. The relevant path does exist there: `manager.py` (around line 774) calls `self._data.remove_remote_peer(pid)` when a peer goes down, and the session re-registers the peer on reconnect.

### 🐛 Describe the bug


One prefill rank's EngineCore, which also serves its P2P port, was paused with `SIGSTOP` for 45 s and then resumed with `SIGCONT`. This was under steady multi-turn load, 32 concurrent sessions with ~90K-token contexts. The DP group stalled and recovered as expected: 45 s is under DeepEP's timeout, and no request failed.

After the resume, the **control plane recovered but the data plane did not**:

- Peers marked the paused rank `down` and later logged `created connected session` for it; heartbeats and lookups work again.
- Every P2P data transfer **to or from** that rank fails, with all 3 peers, in both directions. Errors: `check_xfer_state failed … NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, then `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND`, and `error handling message 'fetch' … NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT / NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` on the serving side.
- The first failures appeared 6 minutes after the resume, and transfers were still failing at our last check, 22 minutes after it. We saw no recovery in that time. Restarting the group (46 minutes after the resume) fixed it.
- Lookups keep succeeding: the source reports holding the prefix (219-221 of 219-221 chunk lookups hit), so the router and engine keep choosing pulls that cannot succeed. Each one then hits issue 1 (a 30 s wait, then recompute).
- Pulls between the other three ranks keep working throughout.

UCX (`UCX_LOG_LEVEL=diag`) logged exactly one error on the paused rank, at the moment of `SIGCONT`:

```
04:56:27 ucp_ep.c:1905 UCX ERROR ep 0x7fc41735c100 has already been closed
```

That suggests the peers closed their UCX endpoints to it during the freeze.

Directed pulls 20-22 minutes after the resume, each a ~113K-token prefix warmed on the source and requested on the target with the source named in `kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source`:

| Source → target | Bytes pulled | Tokens via P2P | Request time |
|---|---|---|---|
| healthy → healthy | 6.16 GB | 112,640 | 3.5 s |
| healthy → healthy | 6.16 GB | 112,640 | 3.3 s |
| healthy → **paused rank** | 0 | 0 | 37.1 s (recomputed) |
| **paused rank** → healthy | 0 | 0 | 37.3 s (recomputed) |

For contrast, blocking the P2P port on a rank with an iptables DROP for 3 minutes is handled correctly. Peers mark it down within 17 s, handshake retries are bounded (`no ConnectAckMsg within 30.0s`), and transfers work again after the block is lifted. The difference with `SIGSTOP` is that the paused process keeps its own NIXL/UCX state across the freeze, while its peers tear theirs down.

### Expected behavior

After a peer reconnects, P2P transfers to and from it work again. If the data path cannot be re-established, the peer should be treated as unavailable, so lookups MISS immediately instead of matching and then failing every fetch.

### Questions for maintainers

- On reconnect, are both sides expected to `remove_remote_agent` / `add_remote_agent` and rebuild the prepped descriptor lists? The paused rank was frozen while its peers declared it down, so its own view of them may never have been reset.
- Could NIXL be reusing a stale UCX endpoint when the remote agent of the same name is re-added? That would fit `ep … has already been closed` followed by `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` and then `NOT_FOUND`. If so, this may need a NIXL change or a fresh agent name or generation per registration.

### Reproduction

1. Two or more prefill ranks with the `p2p` secondary tier, under load that produces pulls.
2. `kill -STOP` one rank's EngineCore for longer than the peers' heartbeat timeout (10 s here; we used 45 s), then `kill -CONT`.
3. Wait for sessions to reconnect, then send a pull between the paused rank and a healthy one, in either direction.

We can provide full prefill logs, the UCX diag log of the paused rank, and py-spy stacks of all engine processes taken at the first failure.

Related: #60204 (why each failed pull costs the full timeout), #57139 (peer registration), #56836.

title: [Bug]: [KV Offload][P2P] A NIXL error raised by `write_blocks` during a fetch is never reported to the requesting peer, so it waits the full round timeout
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.30.0+g87ecf7d`, plus open PRs #56836 and #57139 and some local P2P hardening patches (see the note below).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2 (UCX backend).
- 8× H100 80GB HBM3 per node, driver 580.126.20, RoCE.
- Model: GLM-5.3, disaggregated prefill/decode. Prefill is DP4 × PCP8, one DP rank per node, with `TieringOffloadingSpec`: a 512 GiB CPU primary tier plus a `p2p` secondary tier over UCX.

The code path below is unchanged on `main` (checked against `e11962fc1c`): our build's `session/server.py` is byte-identical to `main`, and `data/nixl.py`'s `write_blocks` is identical too.


### 🐛 Describe the bug


When the source side of a P2P fetch calls `NixlTransport.write_blocks` and NIXL raises (we saw `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` and `nixlNotFoundError`), the exception escapes to the session's message dispatcher, which only logs it. The requesting peer is never told the fetch failed. It waits for its round timeout (30 s here), aborts, and only then falls back to recomputing the prefix.

Call chain, from our traceback (line numbers from our build, same code on `main`):

```
session.py   _on_message            -> _dispatch_message
server.py    on_fetch               (line 390) -> self._submit_transfer(...)
server.py    _submit_transfer       (line 1072) -> self._transport.write_blocks(...)
nixl.py      write_blocks           (line 294) -> self._agent.transfer(handle)
nixl_cu13/_api.py transfer          (line 632) raises nixlRemoteDisconnectError / nixlNotFoundError
```

`_submit_transfer` already has a fail-fast path, but only for `write_blocks` *returning* `None` (no remote descriptor list for the peer). That path marks the round finishing and calls `_finalize_outbound(kv_request_id, round_key, success=False)` so that "the peer and the local store jobs don't wait for finish_request or for `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` / `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S`". A raised exception skips it. The dispatcher in `session.py` (`main` lines ~319-333) logs `error handling message 'fetch'`, increments `_dispatch_error_count` and continues. Nothing finalizes the round.

Observed on the source and requesting ranks for one pull (`kv_request_id` shortened):

```
05:16:26 source     P2PSession <requester>:7777: error handling message 'fetch' (count=1): NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT
                      File ".../p2p/session/server.py", line 390, in on_fetch
05:16:56 requester  P2PSession <source>:7777: paircheck-5d88… round=0 timed out, sending abort
05:16:56 source     P2PSession <requester>:7777: store job 6883 timed out
05:16:57 requester  load request paircheck-5d88… (job_id=6864) completed with failure after abort
```

Impact: each affected request took 37 s, against about 6 s to recompute the ~113K-token prefix locally and about 3.4 s for a successful pull. With any persistent transfer failure (see issue 2), every pull touching the bad peer pays the full timeout, and there is no request error to surface it.

It also looks like the handle from `make_prepped_xfer` is not released when `transfer` raises, though we did not confirm this.

### Expected behavior

A NIXL error while submitting a fetch's write should be handled like the existing `write_blocks -> None` case: finalize the round with `success=False`, so the requester falls back to recompute immediately rather than after its timeout.

### Suggested fix

One of:

- catch NIXL errors in `NixlTransport.write_blocks` around `make_prepped_xfer` / `transfer`, release the handle, log, and return `None`, which reuses the existing fail-fast path; or
- in `P2PSession._submit_transfer`, wrap the `write_blocks` call and send exceptions to the same branch as `transfer_id is None`.

A unit test could make the transport's `write_blocks` raise and assert that the round is finalized with `success=False` and the peer is notified, without waiting for `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S`.

### Reproduction

Any condition that makes `agent.transfer` raise on the source while the control session stays up reproduces it. We hit it after issue 2: a peer whose NIXL path had gone stale. In that state, every directed pull to or from the peer showed the trace above, which we confirmed with requests carrying `kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source = {kv_request_id, remote_host, remote_port}`.

Related: #56836 (bounds unanswered *lookup* waits; does not cover this *fetch* failure), #57139.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: `vllm preload` daemon never matches a dense (non-MoE) engine with `--data-parallel-size > 1` (WeightCacheKey `dp_size` mismatch)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS : Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS (x86_64) Python : 3.12.14 PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA 13.0) transformers : 5.17.0 GPUs : 2x NVIDIA RTX A6000 Nvidia driver : 580.178.04 vLLM : main at 5f30fc7031 (2026-10-03), built from source ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug With a dense (non-MoE) model and `--data-parallel-size N` (N > 1), engines started with `--load-format ipc_cache` never use the daemon started by `vllm preload` with the same flags. The daemon fingerprints each rank with `dp_size=N, dp_rank=r`, but a dense engine fingerprints every rank with `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0`, so the `WeightCacheKey` check fails on every rank. - With the default `fallback=true`, each rank logs one warning and loads from disk. The server works, but Fast Start does nothing, and the daemon keeps holding its own copy of the weights on every GPU. - With `"fallback": false`, the engine fails to start. The preload docs list data parallelism as supported ([`docs/features/preload.md` L26-L28](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/docs/features/preload.md#L26-L28), [L167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/docs/features/preload.md#L167)) and do not restrict it to MoE models. #### Reproduction Two GPUs, public dense model. ```bash # Terminal 1 vllm preload --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size 2 ``` Wait for `Weight cache daemon READY`, then: ```bash # Terminal 2 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size 2 --load-format ipc_cache \ --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --max-model-len 2048 ``` `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.2` and `--max-model-len 2048` only keep the run small because the GPUs on my machine are shared. #### Results With the default `fallback=true`, the server starts and answers, but no rank logs `Mapped ... tensors from the weight cache daemon`. Instead: ```text (Worker pid=2698932) WARNING [ipc_loader.py:217] Weight cache unusable (WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size']); falling back to disk loading (Worker pid=2698929) WARNING [ipc_loader.py:217] Weight cache unusable (WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size', 'dp_rank']); falling back to disk loading ``` The daemon logs the same two mismatches and keeps serving. With `--model-loader-extra-config '{"fallback": false}'` added to `vllm serve`, `EngineCore failed to start`. Rank 0 raises `CacheConfigMismatchError: WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size']`, rank 1 the same with `['dp_size', 'dp_rank']`.
Traceback with fallback=false (rank 0) ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 915, in worker_main worker = WorkerProc(*args, **kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/tracing/otel.py", line 175, in sync_wrapper return func(*args, **kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 682, in __init__ self.worker.load_model() File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 574, in load_model self.model_runner.load_model(load_dummy_weights=load_dummy_weights) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 379, in load_model self.model = model_loader.load_model( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/tracing/otel.py", line 175, in sync_wrapper return func(*args, **kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 211, in load_model state = self._fetch_entries(model_config) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 359, in _fetch_entries return self._request_state_with_startup_wait(cache_config) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 365, in _request_state_with_startup_wait return self._with_startup_wait(lambda: self._request_state(cache_config)) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 373, in _with_startup_wait return op() ^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 365, in return self._with_startup_wait(lambda: self._request_state(cache_config)) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py", line 397, in _request_state raise CacheConfigMismatchError( vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.protocol.CacheConfigMismatchError: WeightCacheKey mismatch on fields: ['dp_size'] ```
Two controls on the same machine: - The same commands without `--data-parallel-size` on one GPU: the engine logs `Mapped 339 tensors from the weight cache daemon (zero_copy mode)`. - One `vllm preload` **without** `--data-parallel-size` per GPU (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1`), then the same `vllm serve ... --data-parallel-size 2 --load-format ipc_cache` with `fallback=false`: both ranks map 339 tensors from the daemon on their GPU and the server answers normally. So the daemons' weights are usable; only the advertised key differs. (This also works as a workaround.) #### Cause 1. For a non-MoE model, the engine runs every DP rank as an independent DP=1 engine: `run_engine_core` calls `parallel_config.reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` ([`core.py` L1388-L1397](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L1388-L1397)), which sets `data_parallel_size = 1` and `data_parallel_rank = 0` ([`parallel.py` L1158-L1167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/config/parallel.py#L1158-L1167)). The Ray actor path does the same ([`core.py` L2631](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L2631)). 2. The IPC loader builds its `WeightCacheKey` from `get_dp_group()`, so a dense engine sends `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` on every GPU ([`ipc_loader.py` L345-L357](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L345-L357)). 3. The daemon builds its key from the launcher's `data_parallel_size` and its own `dp_rank`, regardless of the model ([`daemon.py` L189](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L189), [L226-L237](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5f30fc7031cae49bf51073fc953d419b08f8887c/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L226-L237)). For `--data-parallel-size 2`: | GPU | daemon key | engine key | mismatched fields | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | `dp_size=2, dp_rank=0` | `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` | `dp_size` | | 1 | `dp_size=2, dp_rank=1` | `dp_size=1, dp_rank=0` | `dp_size`, `dp_rank` | MoE models are not affected: their engines keep the real DP placement (`DPEngineCoreProc`), which is what the daemon advertises. #### Scope - Reproduced on `main` at `5f30fc7031` (2026-10-03). All code links above point at that commit. - Only tested on one node with TP=1 and the multiprocessing backend. Not tested: TP > 1 with DP, multi-node DP, MoE with DP, the Ray DP path, and draft daemons (speculative decoding) with DP. - `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py` checks the daemon's rank placement and the key comparison, but nothing checks the key a dense DP engine actually sends. #### Related - #57386 added data parallelism to the daemon. Its description targets DP + EP decode fleets; the dense DP=1 rescoping in the engine is not accounted for. - #56949 (closed) is the same class of problem in the RL weight-transfer path: dense DP engines reset `data_parallel_rank` to 0. #56950 fixed that path by reading `data_parallel_index` instead. > AI disclosure: this issue was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). A human reviewed the issue before filing. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

At ≥128 concurrent requests, outputs get much worse (GSM8K, greedy decoding): - GSM8K accuracy drops from 96% to about 64%. - Many responses end after ≤5 tokens. - Many other responses run much longer than usual. Setting `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` (everything else unchanged) brings accuracy at c256 back to 96.7%. The bug is not caused by: - the attention backend; - the model runner (V1 or V2); - prefix caching; - the AITER FP8 linear kernel. Some AITER component other than those is involved. Custom all-reduce and RMSNorm were not tested separately (see "Not yet tested"). Greedy outputs should not depend on how many other requests share the batch. ## Launch command ```bash docker run -d --init --name qwen38-27b --network host --ipc host \ --group-add video --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri/renderD136 --device /dev/dri/renderD152 \ --device /dev/dri/renderD144 --device /dev/dri/renderD128 \ -v $HF_HOME:/hf -e HF_HOME=/hf -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 -e VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 \ vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-36768d1bfd39094681cdbc8cb37d4b31c0729c89 \ Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --language-model-only \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \ --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder ``` The defaults that apply are: - max_num_seqs 256; - max_num_batched_tokens 16384; - cudagraph_mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, capture sizes up to 512. The log shows: - `Using V2 Model Runner` - `GDN decode kernel: triton` - all-reduce backends `['AITER_CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']` - `fuse_allreduce_rms: True` - GPU KV cache of about 15.4M tokens (usage stays below 7%). ## Reproduction The eval runs GSM8K test (all 1319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions` with these settings: - temperature 0, max_tokens 8192. - Prompt: `"Solve the following math problem. Put the final answer, a number only, on the last line in the form 'Answer: '.\n\n{question}"` - Client-side concurrency is controlled by an asyncio semaphore, and the client does not cap connections (`aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=0)`). - The server log confirms that `Running:` reaches the target concurrency. ## Results All runs use a fresh server, one change at a time, and the full 1319 questions. | Config | Concurrency | Accuracy | Truncated (8192) | Mean completion tokens | Wrong w/ no parsable answer | Responses ≤5 tokens | Error rate: first 256 reqs / rest | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | baseline (prefix caching on) | 64 | **96.1%** | 15 | 457 | 24 | 9 | 4% / 4% | | baseline | 128 | **90.7%** | 24 | 538 | 73 | 49 | 10% / 9% | | baseline (prefix caching on) | 256 | **64.5%** | 60 | 806 | 312 | 243 | 13% / 41% | | baseline | 256 | **66.9%** | 56 | 780 | 291 | 229 | 7% / 39% | | `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | 256 | 62.1% | 50 | 710 | 335 | 277 | 8% / 45% | | `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` | 256 | 64.6% | 56 | 820 | 308 | 246 | 9% / 42% | | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0` (log: `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`) | 256 | 63.9% | 47 | 696 | 337 | 282 | 6% / 43% | | **`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0`** + `TRITON_ATTN` | 256 | **96.7%** | 11 | 481 | 11 | **0** | 3% / 3% | "Baseline" means the launch command above. "Responses ≤5 tokens" counts `completion_tokens` ≤5, which includes reasoning tokens. These requests stopped almost right away. ### Observations 1. **The bug depends on batch size, not on accumulated state.** I took 40 random questions that were wrong in the c256 run and resent them one at a time (concurrency 1) to the same server process. 34 of the 40 were then correct. The other 6 are about the same as the normal error rate at low concurrency. 2. **It is not progressive degradation over server lifetime.** On one server, c256 ran first on a fresh process and c128 ran after it. c256 was already broken (66.9%), and the later c128 run was better (90.7%). 3. **Errors are concentrated in requests that join an already-running batch.** In c256 runs, the first 256 requests start together. They have a 6–13% error rate. Requests admitted later, into a full running batch, have a 39–45% error rate. These later requests are likely scheduled into mixed prefill+decode steps (chunked prefill), but I have not verified this. 4. **Two failure modes appear:** responses that stop after ≤5 tokens, and long rambling responses. The rambling shows up as higher mean completion tokens and more truncations at 8192. 5. **A different model on the same image is not affected.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on the same image (BF16, MoE, TP2, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0`, all-reduce also `AITER_CUSTOM`, MTP k=1). On the same eval it stays at 97.4–97.9% for c64, c128 and c256 per replica, including both replicas at c256 at once. Differences from the 27B setup: TP2 vs TP4, BF16 vs block-FP8, MoE vs dense. ## Ruled out - **Prefix caching.** Results are the same with it on and off. - **Model Runner V2.** V1 is just as bad. - **The AITER unified-attention kernel**, including the new gfx950 Gluon path from ROCm/aiter#4614. `TRITON_ATTN` is just as bad. - **The AITER block-FP8 GEMM.** It is just as bad with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0`. - **Client-side effects.** The connection cap was removed, there are no HTTP errors, and failed prompts succeed when resent at c=1. - **KV cache pressure.** Usage stays below 7%, and there are no preemptions. ## Not yet tested (remaining suspects under `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`) - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` (AITER custom all-reduce at TP4), and the `fuse_allreduce_rms` fusion that comes with it. - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=0` - `--no-async-scheduling`, `-cc.cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, `--enforce-eager` - TP2 with the same model, to check whether TP4 matters. ## Possibly related - vllm#57562: async scheduling with hybrid GDN models emits spurious tokens. - vllm#57224: MRV2 stale UVA views cause garbage output. Ruled out here, since V1 is also affected. - vllm#35219: progressive NaN-type degradation. This does not match: there is no lifetime dependence here. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug][HiSparse] GLM-5.3 TP8 on B200: illegal memory access when admitting a new request wave
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `528772a4bf` (main, 2026-10-05), torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.7.0.post1
- 8× NVIDIA B200, driver 595.91.07
- Model `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, TP8, FlashInfer sparse MLA, default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs, MRv2

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With HiSparse enabled, the server crashes when a new wave of requests is admitted after an earlier wave has finished on the same server. Every GPU-memory-related error surfaces inside HiSparse's residency resolution during piecewise-graph replay (or as a segfault in `cudaGraphLaunch`). It reproduced in 3 of 3 attempts on main, and also with #60083 applied. The same workload without `--kv-transfer-config` doesn't crash.

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len 22528 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":128}}'

# passes: 4/4 requests
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 4
# crashes immediately: 0/8 requests, engine dead
vllm bench serve --model RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 20480 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed 42 --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 8
```

GPU KV usage is ~1% when it crashes, so everything is GPU-resident and no host spills are needed.

Error (Worker_TP4; asynchronous, so the faulting kernel may be earlier):

```
gpu/model_runner.py:2025 run_pw_graph -> breakable_cudagraph replay
-> models/deepseek_v32/attention.py:594 _sparse_indexer_and_attn
-> v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse.py:526 forward_mqa
-> v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py:253 convert_logical_to_physical_topk
-> v1/hisparse/runtime.py:1081 swap_in -> :1019 _resolve_and_stage_group
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Other occurrence:

```
!!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!!
  cuGraphLaunch <- cudaGraphLaunch <- at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay()
```

Notes:
- A single run at `--max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 128` with 16k inputs completed without crashing, so continuous admission inside one benchmark run doesn't seem sufficient by itself.
- Under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the c=4 phase was too slow to finish, so that run is inconclusive.
- Root-causing in progress; tracked in #60072.

cc @LucasWilkinson
label: bug

The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Chat tells the engine when to start enforcing structured outputs. The scale-out generate path doesn't, so the same rendered request can be constrained differently depending on which path serves it. `OpenAIServingChat` passes two things to `engine_client.generate` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py`): - `reasoning_ended=True` when `include_reasoning=false` or when the Mistral grammar came from the parser (`request._grammar_from_parser`). Otherwise it checks the prompt with the parser. - `reasoning_parser_kwargs={"chat_template_kwargs": ...}`, so the engine's reasoner knows about things like `enable_thinking`. `/inference/v1/generate` passes neither (`vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py`), and `GenerateRequest` has no fields for them. With `--reasoning-parser` set, the engine then defaults to `reasoning_ended=None`. It checks the prompt and if reasoning hasn't ended there it holds the grammar until the model ends reasoning (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`). Its reasoner is also built without the template kwargs. What that means in practice: - **`include_reasoning=false`**: chat constrains from the first token. Generate lets the model reason unconstrained first. - **Mistral grammar** (tool choice `required` / named, JSON): the grammar has its own optional `think?` rule and expects to start at token 0. On generate it only starts after `[/THINK]`, so if the model doesn't think, the constraint is never applied. - **Reasoners that read `chat_template_kwargs`**: the engine side reasoner can disagree with the frontend about whether thinking is on. #39130 looks like the same thing on the full path (Gemma4, `enable_thinking=false`) and generate never gets the kwargs. This affects any client of the render → generate path, including the new `output_mode="text"` from #58588. Suggested fix: have `/render` work out `reasoning_ended` and `reasoning_parser_kwargs` the same way main chat does, carry them on `GenerateRequest` and pass them through in generate. `_grammar_from_parser` is a private attr that never gets serialized, so it has to be resolved into `reasoning_ended` on the render side. Found during the `adjust_request` audit for #42729 / #56851. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: TRITON_MLA is not batch invariant under chunked prefill with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DeepSeek-V3.1)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `main` at `f590eb2448a51028f6044c6f60104ce0ef3189e9`, torch 2.13.0+cu130
- NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), driver 580.167.08, CUDA toolkit 13.1
- Models: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (TP=1) and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` (TP=4)
- Attention backend: `TRITON_MLA`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`

### 🐛 Describe the bug


With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the output of an MLA model changes when its prefill is split into chunks. Both DeepSeek models above fail the chunked-prefill test of the batch-invariance suite, while their needle tests and `bs1_vs_bsN` bitwise tests pass. Both are on the tested-models list in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`.

**Repro**

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  pytest -v -s "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill[TRITON_MLA]"
```

```text
AssertionError: Batch invariance violated under chunked prefill (max_num_batched_tokens=131):
prompt 1 (263 tokens): logprobs differ, max|delta|=8.945e-02; prompt 8 (248 tokens): tokens differ;
prompt 10 (97 tokens): tokens differ; ...
```

Three runs in fresh processes give the same failure and the same delta. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` fails the same test the same way.

**Isolation**

The difference does not need other requests in the batch. One prompt run alone, with only the token budget changed:

| `max_num_batched_tokens` | Prefill | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | one chunk | reference |
| 131 | several chunks | selected-token logprobs differ from the first step (about 1e-3), sampled tokens differ from decode step 9 |

Other observations:

- With `max_num_batched_tokens=4096` the batched test input shows no mismatch. With 512 one prompt still mismatches.
- `enforce_eager=True` still fails, so CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` are not needed to trigger it.
- Prefix caching is off (the test disables it, and it is disabled for `TRITON_MLA` in batch-invariant mode).

Since chunk boundaries depend on the scheduler's token budget, and so on the other requests in the step, this makes the output depend on batch composition.

**Suspected area (not proven)**

The MLA prefill path for a chunk that has cached context (`_compute_prefill_context` in `mla_attention.py`): cached context is gathered and up-projected per context chunk, attended separately, and combined with `merge_attn_states`. A single-chunk prefill does not go through that merge, and merging LSE-rescaled partial results is not bitwise associative. I have not instrumented it at layer level. #46592 discusses canonical chunk boundaries for a related reason (prefix caching).

**CI coverage**

The Batch Invariance jobs run the full `test_batch_invariance.py` only with the default model. For `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` they run only the needle test with `-k TRITON_MLA`, so the chunked-prefill test (added in #55612) is not exercised for `TRITON_MLA`.

I only ran this on GB300, but nothing in this path looks Blackwell-specific. Happy to run more experiments on this hardware.

title: [Bug]: NIXL pull: one wedged connection repeatedly strands decode KV blocks (production log analysis)
body:
### Your current environment

- Production: disaggregated P/D on a build based on v0.30.0, `nixl==1.4.1`, `NixlConnector` in pull mode, `kv_load_failure_policy: fail`, default `engine_ttl=3600`, mlx5 `rc` transport.
- Decode is TP2. Prefill is TP8/DCP8, so each decode request posts 16 READs (2 decode workers x 8 prefill ranks). About 40 prefill engines.
- The connector's NIXL agent is created without `sync_mode` (see #59870).

### Describe the bug

One decode engine leaked KV blocks in a staircase until it sat at ~97% utilization and stopped admitting anything but small requests. The decode pod's log shows the cause is **a single wedged connection**: one decode TP worker has a connection to one rank of one prefill engine on which no READ ever completes. Every request prefilled on that engine and routed to this decode engine loses the same READ, waits until the client gives up, is aborted, and leaves its blocks pinned.

This is the production case behind #59872. That issue describes what vLLM does once a READ stays in `PROC`. This issue adds what the log shows about how it gets there and why it repeats.

#### What each episode looks like

Stats lines normally report successful transfers in multiples of 16. Each episode starts with one that is one short, followed by ~45 minutes with no engine activity, after which the KV floor has risen:

```
08:08:38 Engine 012: Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, Deferred: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 5.5%
08:08:38 KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=15, ..., Num failed transfers=0
08:53:38 Engine 012: Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 5.5%
```

| Stuck at (UTC) | Transfers in that line | Silence after | KV floor after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 08:08:38 | 15 | 45m00s | 5.5% |
| 09:16:38 | 15 | 45m10s | 8.6% |
| 12:24:18 | 15 | 45m21s | 30.9% |
| 13:14:39 | 15 | 45m30s | 36.3% |
| 14:22:29 | 31 | 45m10s | 38.9% |
| 15:38:39 | 31 | 44m50s | 63.1% |
| 16:28:59 | 15 | 45m10s | 65.2% |
| 17:19:39 | 31 | 45m00s | 67.0% |
| 18:16:39 | 15 | 45m00s | 76.3% |
| 19:28:29 | 31 | 21m20s | 95.3% |

`Num failed transfers` stays 0 and nothing is logged. The ~2,700 s wait matches an upstream timeout; the request is aborted at that point (inferred, the log has no abort line). While it waits, the engine receives no other traffic.

#### It is one connection, not random loss

- **Only one of four engines in the pod is affected.** Same build, same prefill peers, same transfer latency and throughput.

  | Engine | Successful READs | Stat silences > 10 min | KV floor at end |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | affected | 11,597 | 56 | 83% |
  | sibling 1 | 220,033 | 0 | 0% |
  | sibling 2 | 221,404 | 0 | 0% |
  | sibling 3 | 219,944 | 0 | 0% |

- **One prefill engine is never evicted by TP0.** For every other live prefill engine, the affected engine's two workers evict in lockstep (for example 15 and 14 times). For one engine, TP1 evicted it 9 times and TP0 never did in 58 hours. `_evict_stale_engines` skips engines in `_engines_with_inflight_transfers`, so TP0 has had a READ outstanding to that engine the whole time.
- **TP1 re-handshakes alone, then a request sticks.** There are 8 handshake bursts where only TP1 handshook (8 log lines, not 16). Two of them are 2 to 5 s before a stuck request.
- **If READs were lost at random, about ten different prefill engines would be held.** Exactly one is.
- **The rate fits one engine's share of traffic.** A mean of 61 requests completed between stuck events, with ~40 prefill engines.
- **It was broken from first use.** The first stuck request came 4 s after a handshake burst, 19 minutes after the pod started and before any eviction. That this handshake was with the held engine is inferred; the handshake log lines carry no engine id.

#### Why it never recovers

1. NIXL reports `PROC` for as long as UCX reports the request in progress. In NIXL 1.4.1 `nixlUcxEngine::checkXfer` relays `ucp_request_check_status` and has no deadline. UCX only fails a request when the transport reports the endpoint failed.
2. The pull path has no deadline either (#59872), so the request waits until the client aborts.
3. On abort the scheduler delays the free until every worker reports `finished_recving`, which never happens.
4. The stuck READ keeps the engine in `_engines_with_inflight_transfers`, so that worker never evicts and re-handshakes it. The broken connection is used again for the next request from the same prefill engine.

#### Knock-on effect

The leaking engine served 1,079 requests against ~14,100 on each sibling, so its prefill pairings went idle and were evicted far more often (285 evictions per worker against 57 to 74). Each eviction and re-handshake leaks UCX endpoints (#59956), and about 31 hours after the KV leak plateaued the same workers started failing handshakes.

### What is not established

- **Why the connection wedged.** Nothing is logged on the decode side. The timing (broken from the first READ after a handshake) points at connection setup, and the unsynchronized agent access in #59870 is the leading candidate, but it is not proven.
- **Which of the 8 prefill ranks it is.** The prefill pod's lease-expiry warnings (`Releasing expired KV blocks ... retrieved by N remote worker(s)`) should show it.

### Reproduction

**Wedged connection to leak (reproduces, CPU only).** A script drives the real `Scheduler` and the real NIXL pull worker with the repo's `FakeNixlWrapper`, modified so READs to one of two remote engines never leave `PROC`, and aborts each stuck request after a timeout. Requests from the healthy engine keep completing; usage only steps up.

| Req | Prefill engine | Blocks | Outcome | KV in use after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | good | 60, 90 | completed | 0.0% |
| 3 | bad | 55 | aborted | 9.2% |
| 4 | good | 80 | completed | 9.2% |
| 5 | bad | 110 | aborted | 27.5% |
| 6-7 | good | 70, 50 | completed | 27.5% |
| 8 | bad | 85 | aborted | 41.7% |
| 9 | bad | 120 | aborted | 61.8% |
| 10 | good | 60 | completed | 61.8% |
| 11 | bad | 100 | aborted | 78.5% |
| 12 | good | 40 | completed | 78.5% |

470 blocks stay pinned, equal to the five requests from the bad engine, and the scheduler is left tracking five `FINISHED_ABORTED` requests.

**Handshake race to wedged connection (does not reproduce on TCP).** A standalone NIXL 1.4.1 harness (CPU memory, `UCX_TLS=tcp,self`, agent without `sync_mode`) runs a handshake thread loading new peers while a second thread polls notifications, sends heartbeats and posts READs, then tests the first READ on each new connection.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| New connections tested | 48,520 |
| First READ completed | 48,512 |
| First READ raised on status check | 8 |
| First READ stuck in `PROC` | 0 |
| `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` from other calls during the race | 119 |

The race is visible as errors, but none produced a silently stuck handle. This was not run on `rc` with GPU memory.

Separately, a standalone test confirms NIXL has no transfer deadline: a READ posted to a peer that is connected but not progressing (`SIGSTOP`) stayed `PROC` for 90 s with no error and completed within about a second of `SIGCONT`. A killed peer raised `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` immediately.

### Proposal

1. **Recover from a wedged connection, not only report it.** A pull-side deadline that fails the request (#59874 default) stops the 45-minute stalls but the next request from that prefill engine sticks again. After a deadline, the worker should drop and re-handshake that remote engine. This depends on NIXL closing the endpoint (#59956, ai-dynamo/nixl#2338) and on a guarantee that the stalled READ has stopped before its blocks are reused.
2. **Do not let a stuck READ pin an engine against eviction forever.** `_engines_with_inflight_transfers` currently guarantees a wedged connection is reused.
3. **Make it visible.** A gauge for KV pinned by transfers of finished requests (#58004), and an engine id on the handshake log lines.
4. **Close the agent race** (#59870, #59877) as the leading candidate for the trigger.

Operationally, restarting the decode pod is the only thing that clears it today.

### Related

- #59872 / #59874: aborted request whose READ never completes keeps its blocks; pull-side timeout.
- #59870 / #59877: one NIXL agent used from two threads without a sync mode.
- #59956: `remove_remote_agent` does not release UCX endpoints.
- #58004: gauges for KV cache pinned by pending KV transfers.

_AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to analyze the production log, write the reproducers and draft this issue. The numbers above are from that log and from runs of those reproducers._

title: [Bug]: NIXL: `remove_remote_agent` does not release UCX endpoints, so each `engine_ttl` eviction + re-handshake leaks until handshakes fail
body:
### Your current environment - vLLM `main` at `54020c3c3e`, `nixl==1.4.1` (`nixl-cu13` wheel, bundled UCX), Python 3.12. - Repro box: 8x H100, no RDMA NIC, so UCX uses `tcp` / `cuda_ipc` / `sm`. - Production deployment this came from: disaggregated P/D, `NixlConnector` (pull), decode TP2, each decode worker loads 8 remote agents per prefill engine, mlx5 `rc` transport, default `engine_ttl=3600`. ### Describe the bug `nixl_agent.remove_remote_agent()` (`invalidateRemoteMD`) returns success but does not destroy the UCX endpoints created by `add_remote_agent()` (`loadRemoteMD`). vLLM calls it for every agent in `_cleanup_remote_engine` (`nixl/base_worker.py:3525`) and assumes the transport resources come back. They do not, so every `engine_ttl` eviction followed by a re-handshake permanently leaks one UCX endpoint per UCX worker per remote rank in the decode worker process. **Production symptom.** After ~2,290 `add_remote_agent` calls (and ~280 evictions that had already removed ~2,250 of those agents), two decode workers hit a fixed ceiling two hours apart and every later handshake failed: ``` UCX madvise(DONTFORK, len=65536) failed: Resource temporarily unavailable (ib_mlx5.h, DEVX buffer alloc) -> UCX endpoint create failed -> loadRemoteMD NIXL_ERR_BACKEND -> handshake_setup_failed ``` That is consistent with per-QP DEVX buffers never being freed until the process reaches `vm.max_map_count`. Evictions after the wall freed nothing. The least-loaded decode rank failed first because idle pairings are the ones that get evicted and re-handshaken. **Standalone reproducer (no vLLM, no RDMA).** Two NIXL agents, UCX backend, `num_threads=4` as vLLM configures it. D loops `add_remote_agent -> prep_xfer_dlist -> READ -> release -> remove_remote_agent` and samples `/proc/self`: | mode | D-side growth per cycle | after 400 cycles | |---|---|---| | add + READ + remove | +5 fds, all TCP sockets in `ESTABLISHED` | 173 -> 2173 fds | | add + remove, no transfer | +4 fds | | | add + READ, never remove | 0 | | | 25 s idle after the loop, then one more READ | nothing is closed | | 5 = one endpoint per UCX worker (1 main + 4 progress threads); the main worker's endpoint is created lazily on first transfer. The P side stays flat. On mlx5 the same endpoints are QPs plus DEVX buffers, i.e. the VMA growth above. **Reproduced in vLLM.** DeepSeek-V2-Lite, P TP2/DCP2, D TP2 with `"kv_connector_extra_config": {"engine_ttl": 30}`. Each cycle = one P->D request, idle past the TTL, then a handshake to another engine so `_evict_stale_engines` runs. Sockets per decode worker: 85, 95, 105, 115, i.e. +10 per cycle (2 remote ranks x 5 endpoints), with "Evicted stale remote engine" logged each time. With 8 remote ranks that is 40 endpoints per re-handshake per worker.
nixl_add_remove_loop.py ```python """Standalone NIXL add_remote_agent / remove_remote_agent churn test. Mirrors what a vLLM decode worker does on every engine_ttl eviction + re-handshake: add_remote_agent -> prep_xfer_dlist(remote) -> READ -> release -> remove_remote_agent and samples per-process resources on the "D" side to see what remove does not return. .venv/bin/python nixl_add_remove_loop.py --iters 400 --every 50 [--no-xfer] """ import argparse import multiprocessing as mp import os import subprocess import time import torch BUF_BYTES = 256 << 20 BLOCK = 64 << 10 def sample(dgpu: int) -> dict: with open("/proc/self/maps") as f: maps = sum(1 for _ in f) with open("/proc/self/status") as f: st = dict(l.split(":", 1) for l in f.read().splitlines() if ":" in l) bar1 = subprocess.check_output( ["nvidia-smi", "-q", "-d", "MEMORY", f"--id={dgpu}"]).decode() bar1_used = [l for l in bar1.splitlines() if "Used" in l][1].split(":")[1].strip() kinds: dict[str, int] = {} for fd in os.listdir("/proc/self/fd"): try: tgt = os.readlink(f"/proc/self/fd/{fd}") except OSError: continue k = tgt.split(":")[0] if tgt.startswith(("socket", "anon_inode", "pipe")) else tgt.rsplit("/", 1)[0] kinds[k] = kinds.get(k, 0) + 1 inodes = set() for fd in os.listdir("/proc/self/fd"): try: t = os.readlink(f"/proc/self/fd/{fd}") except OSError: continue if t.startswith("socket:["): inodes.add(t[8:-1]) socks: dict[str, int] = {} for fam, path, icol, scol in (("tcp", "/proc/self/net/tcp", 9, 3), ("tcp6", "/proc/self/net/tcp6", 9, 3), ("unix", "/proc/self/net/unix", 6, None)): for line in open(path).read().splitlines()[1:]: cols = line.split() if cols[icol] in inodes: key = fam if scol is None else f"{fam}:{cols[scol]}" socks[key] = socks.get(key, 0) + 1 return dict(maps=maps, fds=sum(kinds.values()), fd_kinds=kinds, socks=socks, threads=int(st["Threads"]), rss=st["VmRSS"].strip(), bar1=bar1_used) def make_agent(name: str, num_threads: int): from nixl._api import nixl_agent, nixl_agent_config cfg = nixl_agent_config(num_threads=num_threads, capture_telemetry=True) return nixl_agent(name, cfg) def p_main(gpu: int, q_meta: mp.Queue, q_stop: mp.Queue): torch.cuda.set_device(gpu) agent = make_agent("P", 4) buf = torch.empty(BUF_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device=f"cuda:{gpu}") descs = agent.get_reg_descs([(buf.data_ptr(), BUF_BYTES, gpu, "")], "VRAM") agent.register_memory(descs, backends=["UCX"]) q_meta.put((agent.get_agent_metadata(), buf.data_ptr(), gpu)) q_stop.get() print(f"P side at end: fds={len(os.listdir('/proc/self/fd'))} " f"sockets={sum(1 for fd in os.listdir('/proc/self/fd') if 'socket' in (os.readlink(f'/proc/self/fd/{fd}') if os.path.exists(f'/proc/self/fd/{fd}') else ''))}", flush=True) agent.deregister_memory(descs) def d_main(args, meta, raddr, rgpu): torch.cuda.set_device(args.dgpu) agent = make_agent("D", 4) buf = torch.empty(BUF_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device=f"cuda:{args.dgpu}") reg = agent.get_reg_descs([(buf.data_ptr(), BUF_BYTES, args.dgpu, "")], "VRAM") agent.register_memory(reg, backends=["UCX"]) nblocks = BUF_BYTES // BLOCK local_h = agent.prep_xfer_dlist( "NIXL_INIT_AGENT", [(buf.data_ptr() + i * BLOCK, BLOCK, args.dgpu) for i in range(nblocks)], "VRAM") rdescs = [(raddr + i * BLOCK, BLOCK, rgpu) for i in range(nblocks)] ids = list(range(0, 64)) base = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"iter 0: {base}", flush=True) t0 = time.time() for it in range(1, args.iters + 1): name = agent.add_remote_agent(meta) rh = agent.prep_xfer_dlist(name, rdescs, "VRAM") if not args.no_xfer: xh = agent.make_prepped_xfer("READ", local_h, ids, rh, ids, b"n") agent.transfer(xh) while agent.check_xfer_state(xh) == "PROC": time.sleep(0.0005) agent.release_xfer_handle(xh) agent.release_dlist_handle(rh) if not args.no_remove: agent.remove_remote_agent(name) if it % args.every == 0: s = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"iter {it}: {s} (+{s['maps']-base['maps']} maps, " f"+{s['fds']-base['fds']} fds, {time.time()-t0:.1f}s)", flush=True) if args.settle: time.sleep(args.settle) s = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"after {args.settle}s idle: fds={s['fds']} sockets={s['fd_kinds'].get('socket')}", flush=True) name = agent.add_remote_agent(meta) rh = agent.prep_xfer_dlist(name, rdescs, "VRAM") xh = agent.make_prepped_xfer("READ", local_h, ids, rh, ids, b"n") agent.transfer(xh) while agent.check_xfer_state(xh) == "PROC": time.sleep(0.0005) agent.release_xfer_handle(xh) agent.release_dlist_handle(rh) agent.remove_remote_agent(name) time.sleep(2) s = sample(args.dgpu) print(f"after one more READ + 2s: fds={s['fds']} sockets={s['fd_kinds'].get('socket')}", flush=True) agent.release_dlist_handle(local_h) agent.deregister_memory(reg) if __name__ == "__main__": ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=400) ap.add_argument("--every", type=int, default=50) ap.add_argument("--pgpu", type=int, default=0) ap.add_argument("--dgpu", type=int, default=1) ap.add_argument("--no-xfer", action="store_true") ap.add_argument("--no-remove", action="store_true") ap.add_argument("--settle", type=float, default=0.0) args = ap.parse_args() mp.set_start_method("spawn") q_meta, q_stop = mp.Queue(), mp.Queue() p = mp.Process(target=p_main, args=(args.pgpu, q_meta, q_stop)) p.start() meta, raddr, rgpu = q_meta.get() try: d_main(args, meta, raddr, rgpu) finally: q_stop.put(1) p.join(10) ``` Run: `UCX_NET_DEVICES=all python nixl_add_remove_loop.py --iters 400 --every 50` (add `--no-xfer`, `--no-remove`, `--settle 25` for the other rows). On an RDMA node, also watch `wc -l /proc//maps` and `rdma resource show qp | grep -c "pid "`.
### What needs fixing **NIXL / UCX** - `invalidateRemoteMD` should actually close the UCX endpoints on every worker (and report failure if it cannot), so add/remove is resource-neutral. **vLLM** - Stop treating eviction as free. Until NIXL releases endpoints, `engine_ttl` churn is a per-process countdown; consider defaulting it off or making eviction much rarer. Workaround today: `engine_ttl: 0`. - Related leak on handshake failure: `add_remote_agent` (`base_worker.py:2119`) stores `dst_xfer_side_handles[engine_id][rank]` (`:2384`) and the NIXL remote agent per rank, but `_remote_agents[engine_id]` is only committed in `_ensure_handshake`'s `done_callback` after all ranks succeed. A handshake that fails at rank k leaves ranks 0..k-1 loaded with live dlist handles; the retry re-adds them and overwrites the handles without `release_dlist_handle`. Once a worker is at the wall, every retry pays this. - A metric for remote agents added/removed per worker would have made this visible days earlier. ### Related - #59871 heartbeats do not refresh `engine_ttl` (one trigger of the churn; it notes the buffers left behind as "a separate NIXL/UCX issue", which is this one) - #59872 / #59874 stuck READ strands decode KV blocks - #58063 / #57507 decoder keeps a dead prefill's KV cache mapped via `cuda_ipc` (also reproduced here: `remove_remote_agent` after TTL eviction did not release 23 GiB/GPU of a killed prefill; only decode exit did) - #59870 unsynchronized NIXL agent access This is not a duplicate of the above: none of them cover `remove_remote_agent` leaking endpoints or include a reproducer for it. _AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and to draft this issue; the reproducer was run and the numbers above are from those runs._
label: bug

title: [Bug]: Multimodal chat requests silently drop all images when request-level chat_template_kwargs is present (v0.30.0, Gemma-4-26B-A4B)
body: ### Your current environment vLLM version: 0.30.0 Model: Gemma-4-26B-A4B (NVFP4, ModelOpt quantization) GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (32 GiB), driver 610.57.04 Deployment: official image docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0, podman ### 🐛 Describe the bug Describe the bug On /v1/chat/completions, the presence of any request-level chat_template_kwargs causes all images in the request to be silently dropped. The rendered prompt contains only the text portion (usage.prompt_tokens ≈ 20 instead of ≈ 276 for one image), the server returns 200 OK, and the model correctly reports that no image was provided. No error or warning is logged. The identical payload without chat_template_kwargs processes images normally. To reproduce Server: vllm serve /models/gemma-4-26b \ --served-model-name gemma-4-26b \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --trust-remote-code \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":3,"audio":0,"video":0}' \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true}' Request A (control, works — images processed): { "model": "gemma-4-26b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,"}}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this scene in detail."} ]}], "temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 4096 } Result: usage.prompt_tokens: 276, image-grounded description. Request B (fails — identical, adds per-request kwargs): { "model": "gemma-4-26b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,"}}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this scene in detail."} ]}], "temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 4096, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true} } Result: usage.prompt_tokens: 22, response states no image was provided. Behavior is identical with {"enable_thinking": false} and with 1 or 3 images attached. Note the per-request value duplicates the server default, so it should be a no-op. Expected behavior Per the Reasoning Outputs documentation, request-level chat_template_kwargs merges with/overrides server defaults during template rendering — image inputs must still be bound into the prompt (prompt_tokens ≈ 276, grounded response). Additional context The failure is invisible in normal operation (200 OK, coherent reply); we detected it only by comparing usage.prompt_tokens across requests. At temperature 0.7 the model confabulates a fully detailed fictional scene for the image-less prompt rather than declining — silently degraded grounding for any pipeline combining per-request thinking control with images. Happy to attach minimal payload files / full server logs if useful. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Identified while working on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59107. With async scheduling, the V2 model runner snapshots each step's sampled tokens and counts with `async_copy_to_np()`. It reads the snapshot after the next step has started. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e006d761a526d0a69555a59f7c10c0c889babd98/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py#L264-L265 On GPU, `.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` copies into new memory. On CPU the tensor is already on the target device. PyTorch returns the same tensor and `.numpy()` shares its memory. If the buffer is reused, the next step overwrites the snapshot before it is read. DiffusionGemma reuses its sampled-token buffers on every step: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e006d761a526d0a69555a59f7c10c0c889babd98/vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py#L1203-L1213 The CPU platform forces sync scheduling for every model, and sync reads each output before the next step runs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e006d761a526d0a69555a59f7c10c0c889babd98/vllm/platforms/cpu.py#L312-L314 It appears as soon as async scheduling is enabled on CPU. I enabled it for DiffusionGemma only, with a local change to that hook, to test structured reads. ### To reproduce No model is needed. This runs on any CPU build: ```python import torch from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.async_utils import async_copy_to_np sampled = torch.zeros((2, 32), dtype=torch.int64) num_sampled = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int32) sampled_snapshot = async_copy_to_np(sampled[:, :1]) num_sampled_snapshot = async_copy_to_np(num_sampled) sampled.fill_(100) num_sampled.fill_(32) print(sampled_snapshot.tolist(), num_sampled_snapshot.tolist()) ``` we get: ``` [[100], [100]] [32, 32] ``` The expected output is `[[0], [0]] [0, 0]`. A snapshot should not change after it is taken. ### Impact on DiffusionGemma I sent the same seeded read 10 times with a batch of 1 and 10 times with a batch of 4. The read uses a 32-token canvas on a 64-token server, is read-only and runs one step. With async scheduling, every output is corrupted: ``` sync tokens[:8] [45518, 45518, 107, 148436, 148436, 236787, 11262, 1] logprob rows 32 async tokens[:8] [45518, 1, 1, 1, 1, 148436, 236787, 11262] logprob rows 31 ``` I logged each snapshot when it was taken and again when it was read. Two steps are overwritten: ```text counts=[0]->[32] tokens=[[0]]->[[45518]] counts=[32]->[32] tokens=[[45518, 45518, 107, 148436]]->[[1, 1, 1, 1]] ``` - The prefill snapshot has no tokens. It picks up the read step's count and first token, and returns a phantom token. - The read's own snapshot is overwritten by the next in-flight step. - The phantom token counts toward the read's 32-token limit. The read keeps 31 of its own positions and returns 31 logprob rows. ### Proposed fix Always copy in `async_copy_to_np()`. On GPU, this change has no impact. No open issue or PR covers this. I searched for `async_copy_to_np`, CPU async aliasing and overwritten sampled tokens. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58082 edits the code next to `async_copy_to_np()` but does not change it. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

"vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py", line 444, in __init__ raise ValueError(f"Duplicate layer name: {prefix}") ValueError: Duplicate layer name: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn ```
#### Cause 1. The IPC loader builds the model under `torch.device("meta")` ([`ipc_loader.py` L259-L264](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L259-L264)). 2. With EP on, `ExpertMapManager.__init__` logs the expert map ([`expert_map_manager.py` L248-L261](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/expert_map_manager.py#L248-L261)). `get_compressed_map_string()` calls `torch.where(self._expert_map != -1)` ([L409](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/expert_map_manager.py#L409)). `_expert_map` is a meta tensor here. `torch.where(cond)` is `torch.nonzero`, which cannot run on meta tensors, so it raises `NotImplementedError`. 3. With `fallback=true`, `load_model` catches the error and calls `_fallback_load` ([`ipc_loader.py` L225-L237](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/ipc_loader.py#L225-L237)), which builds the model a second time. The first, partial build already registered its first attention layer in `compilation_config.static_forward_context` ([`attention.py` L443-L445](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py#L443-L445)), so the second build raises `Duplicate layer name`. Step 3 does not look specific to EP: from the code, any exception raised inside `_build_model` after the first attention layer is constructed would leave the fallback unable to rebuild the model. I have only observed it through the path above. #### Scope - Tested at `863475eb9c`. The files linked above are unchanged on `main` at `0979892992` (2026-10-02). - Only tested with `tiny-random/qwen3-moe` at TP=2. #### Related PRs - #55490 (open, needs rebase) builds the expert map on the CPU (`_expert_map_cpu`). From reading the diff, this should fix step 2. I have not run it. - #43928 (draft) makes the same log line skip meta tensors, which should also avoid the crash in step 2. I have not run it either. - #58876 (closed, not merged) built the expert map on the host. - None of them changes the fallback path in step 3. #### Note for the fix #55490 also rejects `--enable-eplb` with `ipc_cache`. `main` has no such check, and the crash above is the only thing that stops that combination today, because EPLB requires EP. The check should land together with the fix. With step 2 worked around locally and EPLB on in `zero_copy` mode, EPLB's in-place rearrangement rewrote the daemon's cached expert weights, and the next engine attached to the same daemon produced different outputs with no error. I can share the details if useful. > AI disclosure: this issue was investigated and drafted with an AI assistant (Claude). A human reviewed the issue before filing. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
