### 🐛 Describe the bug `PEFTHelper` (`vllm/lora/peft_helper.py`) reads `r` and `lora_alpha` from `adapter_config.json` and applies one scaling, `lora_alpha / r`, to every LoRA module. PEFT also supports per-module rank and alpha through `rank_pattern` and `alpha_pattern`, and scales each module by its own `alpha_m / r_m`. vLLM ignores both fields, so every module whose pattern changes `alpha_m / r_m` is served with the wrong scaling. Nothing warns about it: `_validate_features` rejects DoRA and unsupported `modules_to_save`, but patterns are accepted and dropped. The relevant code is unchanged on main (0979892992). This matters most for MoE. PEFT's LoRA docs recommend `target_parameters` on the experts with `rank_pattern={"experts.gate_up_proj": r // num_experts, ...}` and point to vLLM for serving. The experts are then scaled `r / (r // num_experts)` times more in PEFT than in vLLM. With OLMoE-1B-7B (64 experts, `r=16`), a LoRA trained that way for 200 steps on wikitext-2 gives a held-out perplexity of 10.06 in PEFT and 11.28 in vLLM (base model: 13.09 / 13.08), so vLLM loses about 40% of the adapter's gain. Folding each module's scaling into `lora_B` and removing the patterns makes vLLM match PEFT again (10.06). Minimal repro with a tiny random dense model (vLLM 0.30.0, PEFT 0.21.2, RTX 3090; I set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` only because this machine has no `nvcc`): ```python import json import os import tempfile import torch from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, Qwen3Config from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest def main(): tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp() torch.manual_seed(0) cfg = Qwen3Config(vocab_size=1024, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=64, tie_word_embeddings=False) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg, dtype=torch.bfloat16) model.save_pretrained(f"{tmp}/base") # r=16, lora_alpha=32 everywhere, except q_proj at rank 4 -> PEFT scales q_proj by 32/4=8, the rest by 32/16=2 lora = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"], rank_pattern={"q_proj": 4}, init_lora_weights=False) model = get_peft_model(model.cuda(), lora) for n, p in model.named_parameters(): if "lora_B" in n: p.data.mul_(4) # make the adapter effect large compared to bf16 noise model.save_pretrained(f"{tmp}/lora") prompts = [torch.randint(10, 1024, (48,), generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(i)).tolist() for i in range(4)] with torch.no_grad(): peft_lp = [] for ids in prompts: x = torch.tensor([ids], device="cuda") logp = torch.log_softmax(model(input_ids=x).logits[0, :-1].float(), -1) peft_lp.append(logp.gather(-1, x[0, 1:, None])[:, 0].tolist()) del model # same adapter with the q_proj scaling folded into lora_B and the pattern removed sd = load_file(f"{tmp}/lora/adapter_model.safetensors") sd = {k: v * (8 / 2) if "q_proj.lora_B" in k else v for k, v in sd.items()} os.makedirs(f"{tmp}/lora_folded") save_file(sd, f"{tmp}/lora_folded/adapter_model.safetensors") ad_cfg = json.load(open(f"{tmp}/lora/adapter_config.json")) ad_cfg["rank_pattern"] = {} json.dump(ad_cfg, open(f"{tmp}/lora_folded/adapter_config.json", "w")) llm = LLM(f"{tmp}/base", skip_tokenizer_init=True, enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16, max_model_len=256, gpu_memory_utilization=0.3, enforce_eager=True) params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, prompt_logprobs=0, detokenize=False) for i, name in enumerate(["lora", "lora_folded"], start=1): outs = llm.generate([TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=p) for p in prompts], params, lora_request=LoRARequest(name, i, f"{tmp}/{name}")) vllm_lp = [[o.prompt_logprobs[j][t].logprob for j, t in enumerate(p) if j > 0] for p, o in zip(prompts, outs)] diff = torch.tensor(vllm_lp).sub(torch.tensor(peft_lp)).abs() print(f"{name:12s} mean |vLLM - PEFT| logprob diff: {diff.mean():.4f} max: {diff.max():.4f}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Output: ```text lora mean |vLLM - PEFT| logprob diff: 0.0176 max: 0.1231 lora_folded mean |vLLM - PEFT| logprob diff: 0.0018 max: 0.0079 ``` The folded adapter matches PEFT within bf16 noise; the original one doesn't. ## A second, smaller problem: bare `AssertionError` for 3D MoE adapters For MoE models that are not flagged `is_3d_moe_weight` (Qwen3-MoE, OLMoE, Mixtral, ...), a PEFT adapter that uses `target_parameters` on the experts kills the engine with a bare assertion. It works when the engine is started with `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=True` and the request sets `is_3d_lora_weight=True`, but the error gives no hint of that:
Repro ```python import sys import tempfile import torch from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, Qwen3MoeConfig from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest def main(mixed): tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp() torch.manual_seed(0) cfg = Qwen3MoeConfig(vocab_size=1024, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512, moe_intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=64, num_experts=8, num_experts_per_tok=2, tie_word_embeddings=False) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg, dtype=torch.bfloat16) model.save_pretrained(f"{tmp}/base") lora = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=[], target_parameters=["mlp.experts.gate_up_proj", "mlp.experts.down_proj"]) get_peft_model(model, lora).save_pretrained(f"{tmp}/lora") llm = LLM(f"{tmp}/base", skip_tokenizer_init=True, enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16, max_model_len=256, gpu_memory_utilization=0.3, enforce_eager=True, enable_mixed_moe_lora_format=mixed) out = llm.generate(TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=list(range(10, 40))), SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, detokenize=False), lora_request=LoRARequest("lora", 1, f"{tmp}/lora", is_3d_lora_weight=mixed)) print("generated", out[0].outputs[0].token_ids) if __name__ == "__main__": main(mixed=len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "mixed") ```
```text self._adapter_manager.activate_adapter(lora_request.lora_int_id) File "vllm/lora/model_manager.py", line 1231, in activate_adapter result = super().activate_adapter(lora_id) File "vllm/lora/model_manager.py", line 349, in activate_adapter module.set_lora( index, module_lora.lora_a, module_lora.lora_b, ) File "vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py", line 386, in set_lora assert isinstance(lora_a, list) AssertionError vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause. ``` With `python repro.py mixed` it loads and generates. ## Possible fixes 1. Support the patterns: compute the scaling per module when the adapter is loaded, using PEFT's key matching (a pattern key matches a module name if `re.match(rf"(.*\.)?({key})$", name)`; the first matching key wins). 2. If that's not wanted, reject adapters where a pattern changes `alpha_m / r_m` away from `lora_alpha / r`. A blanket rejection of non-empty patterns would break adapters that work today: PEFT's `convert_to_lora` / `save_as_lora` with a dynamic rank writes `r=1, lora_alpha=1` and sets `rank_pattern` and `alpha_pattern` to the same value per module, so every module's scaling is 1 and vLLM serves them correctly. 3. Check the largest rank in `rank_pattern` in `validate_legal`, not only `r`. Today an adapter with `r=8` and `rank_pattern={"q_proj": 32}` passes the `max_lora_rank=16` check and then kills the engine with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (16) must match the size of tensor b (32) at non-singleton dimension 0`. PEFT's own `save_as_lora` with a dynamic rank writes `r=1`, so its per-module ranks are never checked. 4. For the second problem, replace the assertion with an error that names `enable_mixed_moe_lora_format` and `is_3d_lora_weight`, or detect the 3D PEFT layout and handle it. I'll open a PR that implements 1 and 3 (per-module scaling, and the `max_lora_rank` check over the patterns) and leave 4 for a follow-up; happy to switch to 2 instead if you prefer rejecting these adapters. I'm also reporting the docs side to PEFT, since their MoE recipe is what sends users here. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next AutoRound/INC checkpoint fails because PLE rejects INCConfig even though PLE is unquantized
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `v0.30.0`
- Container: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0`
- Model: `Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound`
- GPUs: `2x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB`
- Compute capability: `SM80 / (8, 0)`
- Tensor parallel size: `2`
- Expert parallel: enabled
- Model dtype: `bfloat16`
- Quantization detected by vLLM: `inc`
- Max model length in the failing deployment: `262144`

The same checkpoint works with the dedicated Qwen3.8 preview image:

```text
vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next
vLLM: 0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198
```


### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound` fails during model initialization on stock vLLM `v0.30.0`.

The checkpoint uses AutoRound / INC quantization for the model body, but the Qwen3.8 PLE embedding is intentionally left unquantized.

vLLM passes the model-level `INCConfig` to `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()`. The PLE implementation does not recognize `INCConfig`, so initialization fails before weights are loaded:

```text
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py", line 695, in __init__
    embedding_quant_method = Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config(

File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py", line 187, in from_quant_config
    raise NotImplementedError(

NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config INCConfig
```

This happens on both TP workers.

The rest of the AutoRound path appears to initialize correctly before the failure. In particular, the checkpoint is recognized as INC and the expected W4A16 MoE backend is selected:

```text
Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend.
```

### Reproduction

A minimal reproduction should be possible with the public Intel checkpoint:

```bash
vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --enable-expert-parallel
```

My production configuration additionally uses long context, prefix caching, chunked prefill and MTP, but the exception occurs during model construction before those features are relevant.

### Expected behavior

The model should load successfully.

For an AutoRound/INC checkpoint where the PLE embedding itself is not quantized, the PLE layer should use the unquantized PLE embedding implementation rather than rejecting the model-level `INCConfig`.

Conceptually, this case seems equivalent to:

```python
if isinstance(quant_config, INCConfig):
    # PLE is excluded from AutoRound quantization in this checkpoint.
    return Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod()
```

The exact implementation should probably verify the per-layer/checkpoint quantization metadata rather than assuming that every INC checkpoint necessarily has an unquantized PLE.

### Why this seems to be a PLE quantization-dispatch issue

The checkpoint is a mixed layout:

- the main model uses AutoRound W4A16 / `INCConfig`;
- PLE is not quantized by the AutoRound recipe;
- nevertheless, PLE method selection receives the model-level `INCConfig`;
- `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()` interprets that config as if it described the PLE table itself and rejects it.

There are similar mixed-quantization PLE issues for Qwen4Exp where the body quantization config does not directly describe the PLE representation, e.g. #54765 and #56272.

### Workaround tested

As a diagnostic workaround, I patched `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config()` so that `INCConfig` selects the unquantized PLE method.

With that change, the model gets past the original exception and proceeds to initialize:

```text
Resolved Engram configuration:
EngramConfig(cpu_offload=True, embedding_across_dp=False, dp_shared_memory=False)

Using 'MARLIN' WNA16 MoE backend.
```

So the INC W4A16/MARLIN path itself is not the source of this particular exception.

I would prefer an upstream fix that determines the PLE representation correctly from the checkpoint/layer metadata rather than relying on this local workaround.

### Additional context

The older dedicated image `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` successfully serves this exact checkpoint on the same 2x A100 system.

That image uses the older separate PLE offload worker implementation, so this appears to be a compatibility regression/coverage gap in the newer Qwen4Exp PLE/Engram implementation rather than an unsupported AutoRound checkpoint in general.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Description

Serving `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B` using the documented sequence-classification override fails during weight loading.

The model is started with:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B \
  --runner pooling \
  --served-model-name qwen3-vl-reranker-8b \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --hf-overrides '{"architectures":["Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification"],"classifier_from_token":["no","yes"],"is_original_qwen3_reranker":true}' \
  --chat-template examples/pooling/score/template/qwen3_vl_reranker.jinja \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8002
```

### Error

The model fails while executing `load_weights_using_from_2_way_softmax`:

```text
File "vllm/model_executor/models/adapters.py", line 545,
in load_weights_using_from_2_way_softmax

    if text_config.tie_word_embeddings:

AttributeError:
'Qwen3VLTextConfig' object has no attribute 'tie_word_embeddings'
```

### Root cause

With the current Transformers configuration:

```python
from transformers import AutoConfig

config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B"
)

print(type(config))
print(type(config.text_config))
print(getattr(config, "tie_word_embeddings", "MISSING"))
print(getattr(config.text_config, "tie_word_embeddings", "MISSING"))
```

returns:

```text
<class 'transformers.models.qwen3_vl.configuration_qwen3_vl.Qwen3VLConfig'>
<class 'transformers.models.qwen3_vl.configuration_qwen3_vl.Qwen3VLTextConfig'>
False
MISSING
```

`Qwen3VLConfig` therefore defines `tie_word_embeddings=False`, but its `Qwen3VLTextConfig` does not expose the attribute.

`load_weights_using_from_2_way_softmax` currently accesses it directly:

```python
if text_config.tie_word_embeddings:
```

### Tested workaround

Changing this to:

```python
if getattr(text_config, "tie_word_embeddings", False):
```

fixes the issue.

After rebuilding vLLM with this change, `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B` starts successfully with the sequence-classification overrides and exposes the reranking endpoints:

```text
/v1/rerank
/v2/rerank
```

The fallback value `False` is also consistent with the value defined by the parent `Qwen3VLConfig`.

### Environment

```text
vLLM: 0.30.0
Python: 3.12
Model: Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B
Runner: pooling
Architecture override: Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification
```

The issue occurs during generic sequence-classification weight loading and does not appear to be backend-specific.

### Suggested fix

Use a defensive lookup in the sequence-classification adapter:

```diff
- if text_config.tie_word_embeddings:
+ if getattr(text_config, "tie_word_embeddings", False):
```

There appears to be another direct access to the same attribute in `adapters.py` that may need the same treatment.

title: [Bug]: Illegal memory access (Xid 13) with SimpleCPUOffloadConnector on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next while an async CPU→GPU prefix load is in flight / sm120
body:
### Your current environment

docker

### 🐛 Describe the bug

[vllm_tb.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32956928/vllm_tb.txt)

SimpleCPUOffloadConnector on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next while an async CPU→GPU prefix load is in flight

**Environment**
- Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19` (`0.29.1rc1.dev573+ge97573215`, includes #56810), Model Runner V2
- 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB), PCIe Gen3, driver 615.71.09
- Model: `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, TP1

**Config**
```
env:
  VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1
  TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0f
  PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

vllm serve Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4
  --max-model-len 262144 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --distributed-executor-backend mp
  --max-num-seqs 12 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv-cache-memory=15679970304
  --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":68719476736,"lazy_offload":true}}'
```

Workload: agentic, 4–8 concurrent long-context requests (80k–185k tokens each), GPU KV pool 880,600 tokens, CPU tier 64 GiB (1518 blocks of 3200 tokens).

**Symptom**
The engine dies with:
```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  at vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py:170 get_output -> self.copy_event.synchronize()
```
Kernel log at the same time:
```
NVRM: Xid 13, Graphics SM Warp Exception on (GPC 2, TPC 0, SM 0): Out Of Range Address
NVRM: Xid 13, Graphics SM Global Exception on (GPC 2, TPC 0, SM 0): Multiple Warp Errors
NVRM: Xid 43, pid=..., name=VLLM::Worker, channel 0x00000004
```

All crashes show the identical fault signature in dmesg: always GPC 2, TPC 0, SM 0, and byte-identical ESR values (`0x525730=0x101000e 0x525734=0x24 0x525728=0x1c81fb60 0x52572c=0x1174`) — i.e. the same instruction faulting deterministically. Always SM 0 suggests a single-CTA kernel (e.g. metadata/block-table preparation) rather than a large attention/MoE kernel.

Apart from that, offload works well: external prefix cache hit rate 80–90%, no output corruption observed, throughput roughly doubled compared to running without offload.

**Common signature across all 5 dumps** (from `dump_input.py`):

| UTC | kv_cache_usage | running / waiting / skipped_waiting | req with num_output_tokens=1 | connector_prefix_cache_stats hits / queries (GPU prefix hits = 0) | store in step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 09-27 18:34 | 0.979 | 5 / 1 / 1 | yes | 96000 / 107026 | yes |
| 09-27 19:21 | 0.918 | 5 / 0 / 1 | yes | 73600 / 81165 | no |
| 09-30 11:50 | 0.944 | 4 / 0 / 1 | yes | 124800 / 132176 | no |
| 10-02 09:08 | 0.973 | 5 / 2 / 1 | yes | 118400 / 124640 | no |
| 10-02 10:25 | 0.962 | 6 / 1 / 1 | yes | 140800 / 148333 | no |

The server was idle between these sessions; under sustained load (4–8 concurrent long-context requests) the crash recurs roughly every 45–80 minutes (e.g. 18:34 → 19:21 and 09:08 → 10:25 UTC), so it reproduces quickly.

In every case:
- exactly one waiting request is skipped (`num_skipped_waiting_reqs=1`, shown as `Deferred: 1 reqs` in the stats log), i.e. an async CPU→GPU load of a 74k–141k-token prefix is in flight;
- the batch contains a request in its first decode step after prefill (`num_output_tokens=1`), with MTP (4 tokens scheduled per request);
- the KV pool is at 92–98%;
- the step's own `kv_connector_metadata` has `load_event=-1` (the load was issued in an earlier step);
- a concurrent GPU→CPU store is present in only 1 of 5 cases, so the store path seems uninvolved.

Example scheduler output (10-02 10:25):
```
num_computed_tokens=[131090, 140280, 125803, 1553, 836, 119148]
num_output_tokens=[1974, 1099, 628, 16, 11, 1]
total_num_scheduled_tokens=24
kv_connector_metadata=SimpleCPUOffloadMetadata(load_event=-1, load_gpu_blocks=[], load_cpu_blocks=[], load_event_to_reqs={}, store_event=-1, store_gpu_blocks=[], store_cpu_blocks=[], need_flush=false)
SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=6, num_waiting_reqs=1, num_skipped_waiting_reqs=1, kv_cache_usage=0.9623, prefix_cache_stats=PrefixCacheStats(queries=148333, hits=0), connector_prefix_cache_stats=PrefixCacheStats(queries=148333, hits=140800))
```

**Hypothesis**
A race between the in-flight async load (possibly involving the non-prefix-cacheable QSA ring group, block size 8, or the GDN state of the loading request) and block reallocation for the running batch under high KV pressure. kv cache group sizes in this setup: `[3200, 3200, 3200, 3200, 8, 3200]`.

For reference: #56810 / #55033 were validated end-to-end only up to 24k tokens (GLM-5.3-Flash), with scheduler-level tests for the QSA ring; this setup is single-GPU SM120 with fp8 KV, MTP3 and 74k–185k-token restores.

**Possibly related**
- #53863 / #53860 — out-of-bounds `attrIdxs` in `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` (also in `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/cuda_mem_ops.py`); our restores are 74k–141k tokens, i.e. thousands of descriptors per load. Note though that the fault here is an SM exception (Xid 13), not a copy-engine MMU fault.
- #53505 — hybrid Mamba (align) + spec decode + KV connector corruption (closed); same combination of features as here.
- #51771 — MTP block drop + prefix caching untested for hybrid models with ≥3 attention groups (this model has 6 KV cache groups).

Full logs with all 5 dumps attached.
(docker-compose logs |grep -v GET |grep -v POST |grep -B50 -A500 Traceback)

Control experiment: removing --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 makes the same output arrive correctly (as regular content), and stream=false is also correct — so the issue is specific to the streaming reasoning path. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug # [Bug]: CUTLASS fp8 MoE corrupts valid tokens when CUDA-graph padding routes are `-1` (wrong `expert_first_token_offset` from `moe_permute`) ## Your current environment - vLLM **0.29.0** (tag), **0.30.0** (`ced6857afa0e`) and **`main` at `47de9d4d04`** (2026-10-01, precompiled kernels), identical results. - torch 2.13.0+cu130, H100 80GB HBM3 (SM 9.0), TP=1 and TP=2. - V2 model runner, default compilation (`VLLM_COMPILE`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs), `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1` (default). - MoE backend auto-selected as `VLLM_CUTLASS` (`CutlassExpertsFp8`) for a compressed-tensors `FP8_DYNAMIC` checkpoint (per-channel weight scales, per-token dynamic activation scales). ## 🐛 Describe the bug With the CUTLASS fp8 MoE backend, **valid tokens get the wrong MoE output whenever the batch contains padding tokens**. CUDA-graph replay pads small batches up to a capture size, and with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1` the router writes `topk_ids = -1` for those padding tokens. The CUTLASS path then computes wrong per-expert offsets and runs some real tokens through the wrong expert's weights. User-visible effect (a 128-expert, top-4, fp8 MoE model): with single-request serving the first generated token often collapses (e.g. bf16 `'Yes'` p=0.90 becomes `'\n'` p=0.997 in fp8), and sampled output drifts into unrelated text. The same checkpoint is correct with batched requests, with `--moe-backend triton` or `marlin`, with `--enforce-eager`, with CUDA graphs disabled, or with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0`. 56-expert and 224-expert fp8 models served the same way are also affected, less often. ### Minimal repro (no weights, a few seconds on one GPU) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Minimal repro: vLLM moe_permute computes wrong expert_first_token_offset when topk_ids contains -1 (the id the router writes for CUDA-graph padding tokens when VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1, the default). No weights needed. The CUTLASS fp8 MoE path (CutlassExpertsFp8) feeds these offsets to the grouped GEMM, so a wrong boundary runs some real tokens through the wrong expert. Run on any CUDA GPU with vLLM installed: python vllm_moe_permute_neg1_repro.py """ import torch from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_permute_unpermute import moe_permute E, TOPK, HIDDEN = 128, 4, 256 # 120B-class MoE: 128 experts, top-4 torch.manual_seed(0) bad_cases = bad_remapped = 0 for n_valid in range(1, 49): n_pad = 8 * ((n_valid + 7) // 8) - n_valid # pad to a CUDA-graph size valid = torch.stack([torch.randperm(E)[:TOPK] for _ in range(n_valid)]) topk_ids = torch.cat([valid, torch.full((n_pad, TOPK), -1)]).int().cuda() hidden = torch.randn(n_valid + n_pad, HIDDEN, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) _, _, offsets, _, _ = moe_permute(hidden, None, topk_ids, E, E, None) counts = torch.bincount(valid.reshape(-1).long(), minlength=E) expected = torch.cat([torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.long), counts.cumsum(0)]) wrong = (offsets.cpu() != expected).nonzero().reshape(-1).tolist() # same routing with padding routes remapped from -1 to E remapped = torch.where(topk_ids < 0, torch.full_like(topk_ids, E), topk_ids) _, _, offsets_r, _, _ = moe_permute(hidden, None, remapped, E, E, None) bad_remapped += bool((offsets_r.cpu() != expected).any()) if wrong: bad_cases += 1 e = wrong[0] print(f"n_valid={n_valid:2d} n_pad={n_pad}: {len(wrong)} wrong offsets, " f"first at expert {e}: got {offsets[e].item()}, expected {expected[e].item()}") print(f"\n{bad_cases} of 48 batch sizes have wrong expert offsets with -1 padding") print(f"{bad_remapped} of 48 with the padding routes remapped from -1 to E") ``` Output (identical on 0.29.0, 0.30.0 and `main`): ``` n_valid= 1 n_pad=7: 129 wrong offsets, first at expert 0: got 32, expected 0 n_valid= 2 n_pad=6: 129 wrong offsets, first at expert 0: got 32, expected 0 n_valid= 3 n_pad=5: 129 wrong offsets, first at expert 0: got 32, expected 0 n_valid= 4 n_pad=4: 9 wrong offsets, first at expert 120: got 32, expected 16 ... 42 of 48 batch sizes have wrong expert offsets with -1 padding 0 of 48 with the padding routes remapped from -1 to E ``` Every padded batch size is wrong; the 6 correct sizes are the multiples of 8, which have no padding. When padding outnumbers the valid tokens (e.g. `n_valid=1, n_pad=7`), every offset equals the total route count, so every expert segment is empty and the valid tokens' MoE output is silently zero. ### End-to-end op repro (`CutlassExpertsFp8`, random weights, E=128, top-4, K=3072, N=1536) Rows `[0, n)` of the CUTLASS MoE output, compared with the same call on the valid rows alone (relative error), for `n = 1..48` padded to the next vLLM CUDA-graph capture size (1, 2, 4, then multiples of 8): | padding rows | routing | valid-row error | |---|---|---| | 0 | — | 0 in all sizes | | > 0, `topk_ids = -1` | default | **wrong in 25 of 40 sizes** (rel. error 0.09 to 0.94) | | > 0, routed to real experts | `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` equivalent | 0 in all sizes | | > 0, `-1` remapped to `E` | proposed fix | 0 in all sizes | The same corruption appears with or without CUDA-graph capture, so the graph only matters because it is what produces the padding. The 25 corrupted sizes are exactly the sizes where at least one valid route lands in another expert's segment of the permuted buffer (25/25 corrupted, 0/23 clean). ### Why batched accuracy benchmarks miss it Padding rows only exist when a forward pass runs a CUDA graph whose capture size is larger than its token count. Single-request serving hits this on most prompt prefills: a 27-token prompt runs in the 32-token graph with 5 padding tokens (20 `-1` routes at top-4). Across 180 single-request prompts, sequences whose prefill had 0-3 padding tokens were never affected (0/100); 17/80 with 4-7 padding tokens were. Offline accuracy runs that queue thousands of requests mostly avoid that shape: prefill steps pack well over the 512-token largest capture size (no graph, so no padding), and decode batches are large, so the `-1` tail is a small fraction of the routes. The affected fp8 checkpoint scored within one standard error of its bf16 source on MMLU-Pro (77.8% vs 78.1%, 12,032 questions, sampled with thinking on), while the same checkpoint served one request at a time collapsed as described above. Comparing next-token distributions against the bf16 model with one request per engine call catches it directly: | 128-expert fp8 checkpoint, first 8 response tokens | foreign mass (mean / p99) | top-1 agreement with bf16 | |---|---|---| | one request at a time, greedy (`main`, unpatched) | 0.0081 / 0.39 | 0.951 | | all 180 requests in one batch, teacher-forced | 0.0000 / 0.0000 | 0.990 | "Foreign mass" is the probability the fp8 model puts on its top-10 tokens that are outside the bf16 model's top-100; it is exactly 0 for bf16 against itself. ## Root cause `moe_permute` → `sortAndScanExpert` (`csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/permute_unpermute_kernels/moe_permute_unpermute_kernel.cu`): 1. `CubKeyValueSorter` radix-sorts only the low `expertsToBits(E) = floor(log2(2E-1)) + 1` bits. `-1` is `0xFFFFFFFF`, so its low bits are all ones and padding routes sort **after** every real expert (keys `[0, 0, 1, ..., E-1, -1, -1, ...]`). 2. `computeExpertFirstTokenOffsetKernel` (on `main`: `computeExpertOffsetsAndInverseKernel`) gets each offset from `findTotalEltsLessThanTarget`, a binary search that assumes the keys are ascending as signed ints. The trailing `-1`s break that assumption: whenever a probe lands in the tail, `-1 >= target` is false, the search moves right, and the offset (including the final valid-row count) comes out too large. 3. `run_cutlass_moe_fp8` passes those offsets to `get_cutlass_moe_mm_problem_sizes_from_expert_offsets` / `cutlass_moe_mm`, so an expert's GEMM segment can extend over the next expert's rows. A Python emulation of steps 1 and 2 reproduces the kernel's offsets exactly in 48/48 cases. On `main`, `preprocessTopkIdKernel` already maps ids outside `[0, n_expert)` to `n_expert` (and accepts a null `expert_map`), but `moe_sort_routing` only launches it when `expert_map.has_value() || build_inverse`. `moe_permute` and `moe_permute_with_scratch`, the entry points `CutlassExpertsFp8` uses, pass `build_inverse=false` and no expert map on a single EP rank, so they skip the remap; only `moe_prepare_scatter` (`build_inverse=true`) gets it. The existing `test_moe_permute_ignores_invalid_expert_ids_with_scratch` always passes an `expert_map`, so this path is untested. #54747 ("Handle padded routes in CUTLASS MoE permutations") fixed sentinel handling in `get_cutlass_moe_mm_data` / `shuffle_rows`, but the fp8 path in `run_cutlass_moe_fp8` (non-batched) gets its offsets from `moe_permute`, which still has this problem. ## Workarounds - `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` (keeps CUTLASS and CUDA graphs; padding tokens get real routes) - `--moe-backend triton` or `marlin` - `--enforce-eager` / `cudagraph_mode=NONE` (slower) ## Proposed fix Always run the existing `preprocessTopkIdLauncher` remap in `moe_sort_routing` (not only with an `expert_map` or `build_inverse`), so invalid ids become the `n_expert` sentinel the sort and offset scan are designed around (`sortAndScanExpert` already notes that `n_expert` is the sentinel for disabled experts). Also make `preprocessTopkIdLauncher` return early for an empty batch, which the unconditional call would otherwise reach with `block = 0`. Tested on `main` `47de9d4d04` by rebuilding `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` (sm_90, CUDA 13.1) with this change: | check | unpatched | patched | |---|---|---| | minimal repro, batch sizes with wrong offsets | 42 / 48 | 0 / 48 | | `CutlassExpertsFp8` end-to-end, sizes with valid-row corruption | 25 / 48 | 0 / 48 | | new test `test_moe_permute_invalid_expert_ids_without_expert_map` (E ∈ {16, 128, 224}, top-k ∈ {4, 8}, 4 padding cases, with/without scratch) | 48 failed | 48 passed | | rest of `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py` | | 454 passed | I can open a PR with this change and the test. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues; closest are #56900 / #57823 (top-k softmax row stride, a different bug) and #54747 (sentinels in `moe_data.cu`, does not cover `moe_permute` offsets). - Related: other backends have received fixes for the same `-1` padding sentinel (AITER #57036, FlashInfer b12x #57946, XPU #55231, Triton under EP #54083); this is the CUTLASS fp8 / `moe_permute` instance. #58789 / #58790 handle empty routing in `moe_permute`, a separate (zero-row) case. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: cudagraph_mode=FULL crashes on prefill with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ `2a52715ef7`, 1× B200 (SM100), Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `cudagraph_mode=FULL` and the FlashInfer sparse MLA backend on SM100 (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`), the engine crashes as soon as a prefill chunk replays a FULL CUDA graph. `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the default, works.

`FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` declares `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` (added in #52783), so `FULL` mode captures FULL graphs for mixed/prefill batches too. Neither MLA prefill backend can replay those:

| MLA prefill backend | Result |
|---|---|
| FlashAttention (default for DeepSeek-V3.2) | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` during FULL-graph replay |
| TRTLLM ragged (default for larger MLA dims, e.g. GLM-5.3) | `ValueError: TRTLLM ragged prefill contains mixed active and empty query rows: query_lens=[512, 0, 0, 0]`: the FULL graph pads the batch with empty requests |
| FlashInfer | not valid for these MLA dimensions |

In both failing cases, a 512-token prefill chunk is dispatched to a request-padded FULL graph. The variable-length verification FULL graphs that adaptive DSpark (#52783) needs may be what `ALWAYS` was meant for. If so, a lower support level plus the varlen-decode hook might cover that without capturing prefill.

**Repro** (DeepSeek-V3.2 shrunk to 4 layers, dummy weights; no HiSparse or KV connector). Pass `TRTLLM_RAGGED` or `FLASH_ATTN` as the argument to pick the prefill backend:

```python
# cudagraph_mode=FULL with FlashInfer sparse MLA (SM100) crashes when a
# prefill chunk replays a FULL graph. Usage: python repro.py [MLA_PREFILL_BACKEND]
import os
import sys

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", "1")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

SHRINK = {"num_hidden_layers": 4, "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512,
          "moe_intermediate_size": 128, "num_attention_heads": 8,
          "num_key_value_heads": 1, "n_routed_experts": 8, "num_experts_per_tok": 2,
          "n_shared_experts": 1, "first_k_dense_replace": 1, "index_topk": 128}


def shrink(config):
    config.update(SHRINK)
    if hasattr(config, "quantization_config"):
        delattr(config, "quantization_config")
    return config


def main() -> None:
    attention_config = {"backend": "FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE"}
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        attention_config["mla_prefill_backend"] = sys.argv[1]
    llm = LLM(
        "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2",
        load_format="dummy",
        hf_overrides=shrink,
        max_model_len=8192,
        max_num_seqs=4,
        max_num_batched_tokens=512,
        attention_config=attention_config,
        compilation_config={
            "cudagraph_mode": "FULL",
            "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512],
        },
    )
    prompts = [{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1000, 3000))}]
    out = llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(max_tokens=16, ignore_eos=True))
    print("OK", len(out[0].outputs[0].token_ids))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

With `"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"` the same script prints `OK 16`.

This also blocks HiSparse users on `cudagraph_mode=FULL`. HiSparse has a separate hazard here: its prefill path branches on per-step page residency, which a FULL graph would freeze at capture. It is masked by this crash.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to reproduce and write up this issue.
label: bug

title: [Unconfirmed] Qwen2 key bias may degrade int4_per_token_head KV-cache accuracy
body:
### Status

This issue was filed prematurely. **No real vLLM run on an NVIDIA GPU has confirmed degraded Qwen2 output.** I am closing it pending that check.

### Evidence available so far

- vLLM's int4 Triton kernels were run through Triton's CPU interpreter on Qwen-like keys. Attention error was 1.36 with the current path and 0.12 with the proposed correction; 0.12 is comparable to the no-bias case.
- A CPU emulator matched those kernel results within 0.000003. The previously posted perplexity figures (13.80/137.6/14.26 for Qwen2.5-0.5B and 9.55/7,381/9.70 for Qwen2.5-1.5B) came from that emulation, **not from a GPU vLLM run**. Two emulator variants differed on the unpatched result.
- Real Qwen2.5 key-projection bias magnitudes reach roughly 400. The suspected mechanism is that a per-token-head 4-bit scale is dominated by that constant and loses the smaller key variation.

### Required confirmation before reopening

Run unpatched vLLM with Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on an NVIDIA GPU using TRITON_ATTN and `--kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head`; compare its output with the same model using the default KV-cache dtype. Then run the proposed fix on that same setup. Record the environment, commands, output/quality results, and latency.

The proposed correction removes key bias before cache quantization and restores its RoPE-dependent contribution in attention scores. Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and Qwen2-MoE are outside its scope. AI assistance was used in this investigation.

title: [Bug]: Fast Start WeightCacheKey hashes only safetensors headers, so an ipc_cache engine can silently map another checkpoint's weights
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text vLLM Version : 0.30.1rc1.dev426+g863475eb9 (git sha: 863475eb9) PyTorch : 2.13.0+cu130 Python : 3.12.14 OS : Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GPU : NVIDIA RTX A6000 (driver 580.178.04) ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug #### Summary `hash_checkpoint()` builds the `checkpoint` field of `WeightCacheKey` from each shard's file name and safetensors header only ([`protocol.py#L239-L272`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/protocol.py#L239-L272)). The header holds tensor names, dtypes, shapes and offsets, but no weight values. Two local checkpoints with the same architecture and file layout (a base model and its fine-tune, `step_0` and `step_100`) therefore get the same key. If a daemon preloaded from checkpoint A is still running and an engine starts on checkpoint B with `--load-format ipc_cache`, the daemon's check ([`daemon.py#L399-L403`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_cache/daemon.py#L399-L403)) finds no mismatched field and serves A's tensors. The engine never reads B from disk and logs no warning, while the CLI and the API `model` field both say B. The [docs](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/863475eb9cd78ae6a4a22f1b90df7fe85e0af438/docs/features/preload.md?plain=1#L21-L23) promise a "Safe fallback" when the daemon's cached weights don't match the engine, and say the fingerprint covers "checkpoint content". A user would therefore expect a daemon that still holds a different checkpoint to be rejected. #### Reproduction with `vllm preload` Make two checkpoints that differ only in weight values. `q` is `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`; `q_mod` is a copy with `model.norm.weight` zeroed and the safetensors header untouched. ```bash hf download Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --local-dir q cp -r q q_mod ``` ```python import json import struct with open("q_mod/model.safetensors", "r+b") as f: (n,) = struct.unpack("

The drafter keeps proposing at full rate; nothing is ever accepted. The same build accepts normally for two metric windows early in the run, so the drafter itself is functional. ## Environment - Model: `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (`qwen4_exp` architecture) - 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121), one prefill + one decode instance - `kv_connector: NixlConnector`, `kv_load_failure_policy: fail` - `speculative_config.method: mtp`, `num_speculative_tokens: 3` - `mamba_cache_mode: align`, `max_num_seqs: 1`, concurrency 1 - Synthetic acceptance disabled (`specdec_rejection_sample_method` not set), so these are real acceptance numbers ## Symptom Over a 1-hour run: 149 requests, 149 successful KV transfers (avg ~400-490 ms), 360 SpecDecoding metric windows. **358 of 360 windows report:** Mean acceptance length: 1.00, Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 333 tokens, Per-position acceptance rate: 0.000, 0.000, 0.000, Avg Draft acceptance rate: 0.0% Drafted throughput stays at ~33 tokens/s throughout, so the drafter is running and proposing; only acceptance is zero. **The 2 exceptions are consecutive, early, and healthy:** 19:13:33 Per-position acceptance rate: 0.204, 0.118, 0.054 (12.5%) 19:13:43 Per-position acceptance rate: 0.551, 0.326, 0.191 (35.6%) The second is a textbook MTP profile, decaying with position. After 19:13:53 it is `0.000, 0.000, 0.000` for 356 consecutive windows and never recovers, while KV transfers keep succeeding for every subsequent request. ## Why "exactly zero" is the interesting part With ~300 drafted tokens per window, a merely mis-conditioned drafter would still match the target by chance now and then, especially at position 0. Exactly `0.000` across all three positions, for 356 consecutive windows, looks like the acceptance test failing categorically rather than draft quality degrading. ## What has been ruled out **PR #58784** (placeholder draft tokens in the padded first step after a P/D remote KV load) is **not** the cause. The patched `rejection_sampler.py` was hot-copied into the running container and its application verified in the server log; the symptom was unchanged. ## Inconclusive Raising `kv_recompute_threshold` to 1e9 via `kv_connector_extra_config`, to force the decode instance to re-prefill locally instead of trusting transferred state, did not change the symptom. The parameter name and placement were verified correct (read through `get_from_extra_config` in `base_scheduler.py`, and `NixlPullConnector` confirmed in use), but `External prefix cache hit rate` stayed at 100%, so it is not clear the knob took effect. This experiment should be considered unperformed rather than negative. ## Leading hypothesis Qwen3-Next works in PD and it's a GDN MoE. The only difference is QSA. NIXL transfers the KV cache; if the decode instance resumes with KV but without — or with stale — recurrent and side state, the target's logits need not agree with what the drafter expects. The MTP drafter is itself a `full_attention` layer consuming hidden states, so it is sensitive to exactly that mismatch. This is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis. It has not been tested. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Xid 31 MMU fault under load in multi-node Expert-Parallel (EP16) CUDA-graph replay (fused-MoE FP8 reduce_scatterv) — --enforce-eager clean
body:

<details>
<summary>Environment (click to expand)</summary>

- **vLLM:** `v0.18.0+rhaiv.14` (Red Hat AI build; V1 engine)
- **Model:** `Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8` (MoE, FP8 **block quantization**, `block_n=128`)
- **GPUs:** 2 nodes × 8× **NVIDIA H200** (16 total); NVLink/NVSwitch intra-node, **RoCE** inter-node
- **Parallelism:** `tensor_parallel_size=8`, `data_parallel_size=2`, `enable_expert_parallel=True` (EP16), `data_parallel_size_local=1`
- **Quantization:** `fp8` (block quant); `kv_cache_dtype=auto`
- **all2all manager:** `AgRsAll2AllManager` (default `all2all_backend=allgather_reducescatter`)
- **Attention backend:** `FLASH_ATTN`
- **Compilation (default):** `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
- **custom all-reduce:** enabled by default (`disable_custom_all_reduce=False`); crash also occurs with it disabled
- **Serving:** OpenShift AI / KServe `LLMInferenceService` → `LeaderWorkerSet` with `RecreateGroupOnPodRestart` (any worker death tears down + recreates the whole 16-GPU group)

> **EP cannot be disabled for this model.** With `expert=false` the MoE FFN weights get TP8-sharded and the per-shard output size (160) isn't divisible by the FP8 block-quant block (128):
> `ValueError: output_size ... = 160 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128`.
> So EP is mandatory; the only test lever is the EP all-to-all **transport/execution**, not EP on/off.
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving **Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8** (MoE) across **2 nodes / 16× H200** (TP8 · DP2 · EP16, RoCE), the engine **crashes with a GPU Xid 31 MMU page fault** within tens of requests under moderate concurrent load.

The fault is **deterministically tied to CUDA-graph-captured execution of the expert-parallel collective path**:

- reproduces with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` **and** `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`
- **completely disappears with `--enforce-eager`** (cudagraphs off) — 400/400 clean, 16h+ healthy

We have ruled out **hardware**, the **custom all-reduce** kernel, and the **all2all backend choice**. This looks like a cudagraph capture/replay correctness bug in the fused-MoE FP8 + EP `reduce_scatterv` combine path.

#### Reproduction

1. Deploy the model multi-node 16-GPU: TP8 / DP2 / EP16, RoCE, **default** `allgather_reducescatter` backend, cudagraphs **ON** (default).
2. Drive load:
   ```bash
   vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
     --model <name> --dataset-name random \
     --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 0.5 --ignore-eos \
     --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 400 --request-rate inf
   ```
3. Within ~30 requests the engine dies; LWS recreates the 16-GPU group (~8 min outage). Also reproduced at `--max-concurrency 8` (crash at the tail of the run). **Halving concurrency does not prevent it** → not a simple capacity/concurrency limit.

Performance is **within SLA right up to the fault** (ITL p50 ~25 ms, TPOT p50 ~34 ms, TTFT p50 ~315 ms) — this is a stability crash, not a saturation/queueing failure.

#### The fault

**GPU driver (authoritative, survives pod recreate) — `dmesg`:**
```text
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:1b:00): 31, pid=..., name=VLLM::Worker, channel 0x0000000c,
  MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC1 GPCCLIENT_T1_x faulted @ 0x....
  Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ
```
Always on the **rank-0 / TP-0 / EP-0** worker's GPU. Same signature every time (Xid 31, GRAPHICS GPC1, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`).

**vLLM traceback (captured live before group recreate) — rank-0 worker (`Worker_DP0_TP0_EP0`).** The illegal access surfaces inside a **PIECEWISE CUDA-graph replay** of the Qwen3 MoE forward, in the **EP combine** collective (condensed; full trace in the collapsible block below):
```text

<eval_with_key>.280:813 forward (submod_70)
compilation/cuda_graph.py:251 __call__
compilation/piecewise_backend.py:377 __call__ (range_entry.runnable)

fused_moe/runner/default_moe_runner.py:85 _moe_forward -> :693 forward_impl

fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1581 apply -> :1381 apply -> :1256 _finalize

get_ep_group().combine(...)                     # parallel_state.py:1114

```
The illegal access then re-raises as `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, which the engine core reports as `EngineDeadError` across all API-server ranks.
On the other API-server/worker ranks the same corruption surfaces downstream as:
```text
Cuda error .../csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:621 'an illegal memory access was encountered'
-> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```
i.e. the MMU fault corrupts the CUDA context on rank-0 (in the EP `reduce_scatterv` combine during graph replay); NCCL then reports "unhandled cuda error" and the custom all-reduce on peers reports the illegal access. **The custom-all-reduce message is a downstream symptom, not the cause** (crash reproduces with custom all-reduce disabled).

#### What we ruled out, and how

| Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | `dcgmi diag -r 1/3/4` (memtest, pulse, nvbandwidth, pcie, targeted_stress), ECC aggregate, row-remap, NVLink counters on the faulting GPU | **All clean / Pass**, ECC all 0, no row-remap pending |
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | Run model **single-node 8-GPU (TP8/EP8)** pinned to each node under identical load | **Both nodes 400/400, 0 Xid** — the "always 1B:00" GPU handled the load cleanly |
| **Faulty GPU (silicon)** | **Leader-swap:** force rank-0 onto the *other* node's GPU0 (different UUID/serial), same load | **Xid 31 moved with rank-0** to the different physical card; old card (now worker) stayed clean → **fault follows the RANK, not the silicon** |
| **Custom all-reduce** | `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (`disable_custom_all_reduce=True` confirmed in engine) | **Still crashes**, identical Xid 31 |
| **EP all2all backend** | `--all2all-backend naive` | Non-viable: worker dies during FULL cudagraph capture (never reaches Ready) |
| **EP all2all backend** | `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` | Non-viable: **Xid 43** (kernel launch fail) on all 16 GPUs at KV-cache profiling |
| **CUDA-graph FULL decode graph** | `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` (drop FULL pass) | **Still crashes**, identical Xid 31 |
| **CUDA graphs at all** | `--enforce-eager` (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`) | **400/400 SUCCESS, 0 failed, 0 Xid, engine healthy 16h+** |

**Decisive evidence**

- **Hardware excluded:** fault follows rank-0 across *different physical GPUs* (leader-swap); single-node runs on the "suspect" GPU are 400/400 clean; DCGM / ECC / NVLink all clean.
- **CUDA graphs are the trigger:** the *only* configuration change that eliminates the crash is turning cudagraphs off (`--enforce-eager`). `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` crashes, `PIECEWISE` crashes, `NONE` is clean.
- **Not the custom all-reduce** (crashes on and off) and **not backend math** (eager uses the same kernels and is clean).

#### Suspected root cause

A CUDA-graph capture/replay correctness bug in the **multi-node expert-parallel path** — specifically the fused-MoE FP8 modular kernel combine that performs a variable-size `reduce_scatterv` (`AgRsAll2AllManager.combine` → pynccl `ncclReduce`) inside a piecewise graph. Under concurrent/variable-shape load the replayed graph appears to issue a GPU memory access with a stale/invalid address (MMU `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ` in the GRAPHICS engine), corrupting the context; NCCL and the custom all-reduce then report secondary errors.

Candidate areas: captured buffers/pointers in the EP combine for dynamic `sizes=`; interaction of `reduce_scatterv` with graph capture; or the FP8 grouped-GEMM MoE path under piecewise inductor partitioning (NCCL collective not honored by `splitting_ops`).

#### Workaround

`--enforce-eager` eliminates the crash but costs throughput/latency:

- eager: **TPOT ~80 ms, ITL ~80 ms, TTFT ~272 ms, ~583 tok/s** @ conc 16 (400/400 clean)
- vs cudagraph single-node: TPOT ~16 ms, ITL ~15 ms

Eager misses our 30–50 ms TPOT target, so it's a functional stopgap, not a performance-acceptable fix. `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` is **not** a usable middle ground (still crashes).

#### Related issues

Not an exact duplicate of any of these, but they form a clear cluster — each matches one axis of this crash:

- **#46253** — *Cross-node piecewise-cudagraph capture → illegal memory access; NCCL collective captured, `splitting_ops` not honored; `--enforce-eager` fixes.* **Closest root-cause thesis.** Differs: theirs faults at **capture** (GB-class, host-staged NCCL); ours faults at **replay** under load on H200 with working RoCE.
- **#58850** — *Intermittent Xid 31 MMU fault in pynccl collective during CUDA graph.* **Closest fault signature** (identical Xid 31 / GRAPHICS GPC / pynccl / CUDA graph). Differs: theirs is intermittent at capture on a TP all-reduce (dense); ours is deterministic at replay in the EP MoE combine.
- **#59189** — *EP serving crashes in NCCL reduce-scatter (EP combine → `reduce_scatterv` → NCCL "unhandled cuda error") under high concurrency.* **Closest stack surface.** Differs: theirs requires `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1` (symmetric-memory scratch regression, bisected to #48247) and is **not** cudagraph-triggered; ours is plain pynccl `ncclReduce` and **is** cudagraph-triggered.

**How this report is distinct:** deterministic at **replay under load** (not capture); EP MoE combine via plain pynccl `reduce_scatterv` (not symm-mem); **Xid 31**; `--enforce-eager` clean; on **H200 / RoCE**; both `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` and `PIECEWISE` crash.

#### Questions / asks for triage

- [ ] Is the EP `reduce_scatterv`/all2all combine (`AgRsAll2AllManager`) expected to be CUDA-graph-safe for **variable `sizes=`** across replays? If not, should it be added to `splitting_ops` / excluded from capture for EP?
- [ ] Any known fixes post-`v0.18.0+rhaiv.14` touching fused-MoE modular kernel + cudagraph + EP combine?
- [ ] We can collect `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, `compute-sanitizer` (memcheck) on rank-0, and a reduced-`cudagraph_capture_sizes` run if helpful — let us know what's most useful.

title: [Bug][HiSparse] Engine crash: "Cannot get N free blocks" allocating the hot region at admission under GPU-pool pressure
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ `93dd80f636`, 1× B200, Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Also reproduces on #55398 before and after merging main.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Under HiSparse GPU-pool pressure, admitting a new request can crash the engine in `HiSparseHotManager.allocate_new_blocks`: admission does not count the request's hot region (4 blocks here), then allocation fails.

```
  File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1209, in schedule          # waiting-queue admission
    new_blocks = self.kv_cache_manager.allocate_slots(
  File "vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py", line 585, in allocate_slots
    new_blocks = self.coordinator.allocate_new_blocks(
  File "vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py", line 300, in <genexpr>
    manager.allocate_new_blocks(
  File "vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py", line 2461, in allocate_new_blocks   # HiSparseHotManager
    new_blocks = self.block_pool.get_new_blocks(num_new_blocks)
  File "vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py", line 682, in get_new_blocks
    raise ValueError(f"Cannot get {num_blocks} free blocks from the pool")
ValueError: Cannot get 4 free blocks from the pool
```

The engine is dead afterwards (`EngineDeadError`).

**Repro** (shrunk GLM-5.3 config with dummy weights: 8 layers, hidden 256, 8 heads, 8 experts, `index_topk=128`, quantization removed):

- `AsyncLLM`, `enforce_eager=True`, `block_size=64`, `max_model_len=8192`, `max_num_seqs=2`, `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`, `num_gpu_blocks_override=160`
- attention backend `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla`, `hisparse_config={"eager_host_mirror": true}`
- `MultiConnector` kv_consumer: `HiSparseConnector` (`host_pool_gib=4`) + `NixlConnector`

Steps:
1. Submit two concurrent ~6k-token prompts; neither gets admitted. Abort them after 20 s.
2. Submit a 4k-token prompt that shares a prefix with an aborted one; it is never admitted either. Abort it after 20 s.
3. Submit a tiny prompt with `max_tokens=3000`. The engine crashes with the traceback above.

Found while investigating a different report on #55398; that report's crash (`HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative decode capacity`) did not reproduce, but this one reproduces on every build tried. #59282 does not touch this path.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B merged SFT BF16 intermittently produces NaN logits and exclamation-only output on H20 (v0.19.1; HF control finite)
body:
### Your current environment

Privacy-reviewed, targeted environment collection (not a full collect_env.py dump):

```text
GPU used by the reproduction: 1 x NVIDIA H20-3e
GPU memory reported by nvidia-smi: 143771 MiB
Compute capability: 9.0
NVIDIA driver: 580.159.03
OS: Linux x86_64, kernel 5.4.119-19-0009.56
Python: 3.12.13
vLLM: 0.19.1
PyTorch: 2.10.0+cu128
PyTorch CUDA: 12.8
cuDNN reported by torch: 91002
Triton: 3.6.0
Transformers: 5.7.0
flash-linear-attention: 0.4.0
causal-conv1d: 1.6.0
```

Model: a private, merged SFT checkpoint based on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, loaded as BF16 with quantization=None. This report does not claim reproduction on the public unmodified base checkpoint. Both backends loaded the same verified checkpoint files. No runtime LoRA, training, sleep/wake, or speculative decoding was involved.

The vLLM package was not upgraded for this comparison. A newer release / current main and candidate patches have not yet been tested on these exact frozen inputs.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

On a standalone vLLM 0.19.1 server, a frozen 11,686-token input produced exactly 2,500 exclamation marks (token ID 0), while `vllm:corrupted_requests_total` increased from 0 to 1 with `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1`. This happened during a **serial** request. A later identical request in the same server completed without a NaN-counter increment.

Using **the same merged BF16 weights and exactly the same frozen input token array**, Transformers generated 122 tokens and terminated normally on both replays; the two output token arrays were identical and every observed raw-logits tensor was finite.

Expected: finite logits and non-corrupted generation. I am not expecting bitwise equality between different backends. This report provides evidence of an intermittent numerical failure in the current vLLM execution stack, not a confirmed attribution to a particular kernel or cache bug.

## Observed sequence and results

Two inputs were selected because they had failed previously. A normal input was used as a control. Original generation budgets were retained; the tests were not shortened to a few output tokens.

| Input | Input tokens | Output budget | Historical failure | Transformers replay | vLLM replay |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 752 | 3200 | 3198 consecutive copies of one token | 187 output tokens; finite logits | 163 / 174 / 161 / 169 tokens; no NaN increment |
| B | 11686 | 2500 | 2500 copies of token 0 | 122 / 122 tokens; identical output arrays; finite logits | First serial request: 2500 copies of token 0 and NaN-counter +1. Later requests: 437 / 442 / 717 tokens without NaN increments |
| C (normal control) | 332 | 2500 | Normal | 177 tokens; finite logits | 171 tokens; no NaN increment |

Transformers order: A, B, C, B, all serial. Total: **4 requests, 608 forward/raw-logits checks, 0 nonfinite results**.

vLLM order on one fresh server: A, B, A, B serial; then A, B, A, B concurrently (4 requests); then C serial. Total: **9 requests, 1 NaN-corrupted request**. The failure was the second serial request, before the concurrent phase. There was no restart between the failed B request and its successful retries. These selected cases are not a representative failure-rate estimate.

Sanitized measurements around the failed serial request:

```text
corrupted_requests_total before: 0
corrupted_requests_total after:  1
usage.prompt_tokens:             11686
usage.completion_tokens:         2500
finish_reason:                  length
unique output token IDs:        [0]
longest identical-token run:    2500
returned text:                  "!" repeated exactly 2500 times
```

In the installed `vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py`, corruption is marked when `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` is enabled and `output.num_nans_in_logits > 0`. Therefore this is not just a guess based on repetitive text. The request returned successfully at the HTTP level; the server remained alive. No CUDA exception, OOM, or resource-guard violation occurred during this replay.

## vLLM configuration

Normalized launch command (private path, device index, served name, and port replaced with placeholders/local defaults):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 MKL_NUM_THREADS=8 \
VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1 \
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name qwen35-debug \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.60 \
  --max-model-len 40960 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 40960 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gdn-prefill-backend triton \
  --language-model-only \
  --seed 20260912 \
  --generation-config auto \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":8}'
```

The server log confirms `enable_chunked_prefill=True`, `kv_cache_dtype=auto`, `quantization=None`, `enforce_eager=False`, and `speculative_config=None`. No MTP, prefix caching, adapter hot-loading, weight synchronization, or sleep/wake occurred. The server used fresh task-local compilation caches.

Requests used `/v1/completions` with pre-tokenized integer arrays, not server-side chat templating:

```python
payload = {
    "model": "qwen35-debug",
    "prompt": frozen_input_ids,  # same array used by Transformers
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_tokens": original_budget,  # 3200 for A; 2500 for B/C
    "seed": 20260912,
    "stop_token_ids": [248046, 248044],
    "skip_special_tokens": False,
    "return_token_ids": True,
}
```

`/metrics` was sampled before/after each serial request and before/after the concurrent group. Complete native output-token arrays, input hashes, request order, and metrics were retained locally.

## Transformers control

Transformers used the checkpoint tokenizer with `enable_thinking=True` to rebuild the saved full conversation, including prior tool-result context. The original incident did not log input token arrays: reconstructed lengths were checked against the original events, and the **same newly frozen arrays** were then passed to both backends. No external tools were executed during either replay.

Core generation code, with paths normalized:

```python
import torch
from transformers import (
    AutoTokenizer, Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, StoppingCriteria
)

torch.set_num_threads(8)
torch.manual_seed(20260912)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL, local_files_only=True)
model = Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    MODEL, dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation="sdpa",
    device_map={"": 0}, local_files_only=True,
).eval()
model.requires_grad_(False)
observer = {"calls": 0, "nonfinite": False}

def observe_logits(module, args, output):
    observer["calls"] += 1
    if not bool(torch.isfinite(output.logits).all()):
        observer["nonfinite"] = True

class StopOnNonFinite(StoppingCriteria):
    def __call__(self, input_ids, scores, **kwargs):
        return observer["nonfinite"]

hook = model.register_forward_hook(observe_logits)
# Repeated for A, B, C, B; reset observer before each call.
ids = torch.tensor([frozen_input_ids], device="cuda")
with torch.inference_mode(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    output = model.generate(
        input_ids=ids, attention_mask=torch.ones_like(ids),
        do_sample=False, num_beams=1, max_new_tokens=original_budget,
        use_cache=True, eos_token_id=[248046, 248044],
        pad_token_id=tokenizer.pad_token_id,
        stopping_criteria=[StopOnNonFinite()],
    )
hook.remove()
```

CUDA-visible Transformers module inspection reported its FLA fast path available (`chunk_gated_delta_rule`, `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule`, and causal-conv1d). This is an independent Transformers `generate()` control, not vLLM eager mode. The hook synchronizes each forward, and both instrumentation and backend differences can alter timing; this comparison does not identify the first bad operator.

## Reproduction limitations and related reports

**The SFT checkpoint and original full conversations are private, so this is not yet a self-contained public reproducer.** The snippets above describe the executed method but require those local assets. I have not tested the public unmodified base model, newer vLLM releases/current main, or a candidate patch with this exact sequence, and am not claiming that upgrading is a verified fix.

I searched related issues and consulted the documentation chatbot before filing. Possible related reports: #51562 / #51565 (stateless first-chunk GDN classification), #38527 (FP8 exclamation-only output), and #55291 (a different FP8 model with persistent corruption). Our case is **BF16, TP1, prefix cache off, no speculation, and later requests recover without restarting**. I have not captured metadata proving the first-one-token-chunk trigger in #51562, so I cannot establish that this is the same root cause or a duplicate.

Which fixed revision or targeted diagnostic would you recommend to distinguish GDN state initialization/reuse from a prefill/decode kernel or graph-related numerical failure? I understand that a public-checkpoint or shareable minimized-input reproduction may be needed for further triage.

Disclosure: the investigation and this report were AI-assisted. The request counts, raw-logits checks, NaN-counter transition, and token statistics above come from actually executed replays, not hypothetical results. Private paths, prompt/tool content, credentials, and host identifiers are omitted.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description On H100 (SM90) vLLM v0.30.0's FA4 forward kernel ignores `num_splits`, so decode attention always runs as a single KV split. Models with few KV heads lose most of their decode attention parallelism. For [google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it) at ~6k context, a decode step is **48% slower** than on v0.26.0 at batch 1 and **36% slower** at batch 4. Results stay correct (the empty splits are weighted at zero) so nothing fails but it's just slow. The one-line fix was merged in the fork on 2026-09-28 as [vllm-project/flash-attention#198](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/198) (`6d11b3c`) but vLLM hasn't picked it up yet. The regression came in with the pin move in #54819: | vLLM | `vllm_flash_attn` pin | Has the fix? | |---|---|---| | v0.26.0 to v0.29.0 | `caaa4eb` ... `06bdd47` | Not needed, bug not present | | v0.30.0 | `506341a` (#54819) | **No** | | main | `9cd61de` | **No** (one commit behind `6d11b3c`) | **Ask:** bump the `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake` to `6d11b3c` or later, and backport it to a v0.30.x patch release if there is one. The fix was validated at the kernel level and this issue adds end-to-end numbers on v0.30.0 below. ## Root Cause Analysis We isolated it one component at a time on v0.30.0, starting from the end-to-end decode slowdown: | Step | What we changed | Result | Conclusion | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Split time to first token from per-token decode | Decode +48% per token, TTFT flat (61 ms on both) | Decode only | | 2 | Batch 4 → 1 | Gap *grows* (+36% → +48%) | Not batching or scheduler contention | | 3 | V1 v/s V2 model runner, text-only prompts, same MoE configs | V1 runner: +49% (bs 1), +34% (bs 4) | Not the runner, multimodal or MoE | | 4 | Context ~260 → ~5.9k tokens | v0.26 flat (4.34 → 4.38 ms), v0.30 +8% → +48% | Scales with KV length: attention | | 5 | `attention_backend=TRITON_ATTN` on v0.30 | Recovers ~70% of the gap | The problem is in FA4 | | 6 | torch.profiler per-kernel diff, bs 1, ~5.9k context | Attention 0.53 → 2.51 ms/step; GEMM, MoE, norms flat | One kernel | | 7 | Kernel alone, sweep `num_splits` | v0.26: 374 → 20 µs with more splits. v0.30: flat 348-364 µs | `num_splits` is ignored | In step 6 the global-layer FA4 kernel goes from 18.5 µs to 311 µs per launch with an **identical** launch configuration (grid `[2, 66, 1]`, 384 threads, 205,824 B shared memory). The same CTAs launch, but only one split per head has work, which is why this doesn't show up in a launch-config diff. ### Mechanism The fork sync that v0.30.0 pins (`506341a`) moved the split count into a `BlockInfo` field. `BlockInfo.get_n_block_min_max` in `vllm_flash_attn/cute/block_info.py` still takes `num_splits` as an argument but overwrites it on the non-packed path: ```python if cutlass.const_expr(self.is_split_kv): if const_expr(self.pack_split_idx): num_splits = split_idx >> 16 # SM100: packed into split_idx else: num_splits = self.num_splits # SM90: the constructor value, default Int32(1) ``` `flash_fwd_sm100.py` constructs `BlockInfo(..., num_splits=num_splits)` but `flash_fwd_sm90.py` doesn't, so on SM90 split 0 covers the whole KV range and splits 1..N-1 get `n_block_min == n_block_max`. The combine kernel weights the empty splits at zero so results are correct. Gemma-4's global layers are the worst case: 1 query token and 2 KV heads per sequence, so without splits only 2 of the H100's 132 SMs have work. The fix ([vllm-project/flash-attention#198](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/198)): ```diff --- a/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py +++ b/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py @@ -686,6 +686,7 @@ def kernel( window_size_left, window_size_right, qhead_per_kvhead_packgqa=self.qhead_per_kvhead if const_expr(self.pack_gqa) else 1, + num_splits=num_splits, ) ``` ## Reproduction
Environment * vLLM: 0.30.0 (bug), 0.26.0 (reference), official `vllm/vllm-openai` images, CUDA 13.0 * PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 (v0.30.0), 2.11.0+cu130 (v0.26.0) * CuTe DSL (`nvidia-cutlass-dsl`): 4.7.1 (v0.30.0), 4.6.0 (v0.26.0) * GPU: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (p5.48xlarge)
Model * [google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it): 30 layers, 25 sliding-window (head dim 256, 8 KV heads, window 1024) and 5 global (head dim 512, 2 KV heads) with 16 query heads.
Configuration Same engine arguments on both versions, via `vllm.LLM(...)` (the text-only decode numbers below): ```python tensor_parallel_size=1, quantization="fp8", attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN", # v0.30.0; v0.26.0 selects FLASH_ATTN on its own max_model_len=8192, max_num_seqs=8, max_num_batched_tokens=14000, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, enforce_eager=False, # cudagraph_mode resolves to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (the default) on both versions trust_remote_code=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"video": 0, "audio": 0}, mm_processor_cache_gb=8, disable_custom_all_reduce=True, # no-op at TP=1 ``` Prefix caching, chunked prefill and async scheduling are at their defaults. v0.30.0 uses the V2 model runner (its default) but the V1 runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) shows the same slowdown.
Minimum Script to Reproduce Kernel only, no model needed. Paged decode at Gemma-4 global-layer shapes, sweeping `num_splits`: ```python import torch from vllm.vllm_flash_attn import flash_attn_varlen_func SEQK, PAGE, HD, NQ, NKV, BS = 7040, 32, 512, 16, 2, 1 nblk = (SEQK + PAGE - 1) // PAGE k = torch.randn(BS * nblk, PAGE, NKV, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") v = torch.randn_like(k) q = torch.randn(BS, NQ, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") bt = torch.arange(BS * nblk, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").view(BS, nblk) cu_q = torch.arange(BS + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") sk = torch.full((BS,), SEQK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") for ns in (1, 4, 16, 64): f = lambda: flash_attn_varlen_func(q=q, k=k, v=v, max_seqlen_q=1, cu_seqlens_q=cu_q, max_seqlen_k=SEQK, seqused_k=sk, block_table=bt, causal=True, softmax_scale=1.0, num_splits=ns, fa_version=4) for _ in range(3): f() g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() with torch.cuda.graph(g): for _ in range(20): f() s, e = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) s.record(); [g.replay() for _ in range(10)]; e.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize() print(f"num_splits={ns}: {s.elapsed_time(e) / 200 * 1e3:.1f} us") ``` Output on one H100 (µs per call), each column run in the `vllm/vllm-openai` image for that version, with the fix mounted over `flash_fwd_sm90.py` for the last one: | `num_splits` | v0.26.0 | v0.30.0 | v0.30.0 + fix | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 385.4 | 360.1 | 358.6 | | 4 | 104.7 | 360.2 | 101.1 | | 16 | 33.0 | 356.5 | 32.7 | | 64 | 20.3 | 363.0 | 20.2 | The CuTe DSL `UserWarning` about `aux_data` that all three versions print on the first compile is unrelated.
Results Kernel µs per call (CUDA-graph replay, includes the combine kernel) with 7040 KV tokens and 32 page size are shown below. Max error v/s an fp32 reference is identical across all three columns: | Shape | `num_splits` | v0.26.0 | v0.30.0 | v0.30.0 + fix | |---|---|---|---|---| | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 0 (heuristic) | 19.8 | 364.0 | 20.7 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 1 | 374.3 | 356.8 | 351.6 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 16 | 32.8 | 348.5 | 32.8 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 1 | 64 | 20.3 | 362.4 | 20.3 | | hd 512, 2 KV heads, bs 4 | 0 (heuristic) | 53.3 | 387.6 | 51.7 | | hd 256, 8 KV heads, window 1024, bs 1 | 0 (heuristic) | 12.3 | 34.5 | 12.2 | End to end: google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, text-only greedy decode, ms per step (median of 3): | Context | Batch | v0.26.0 | v0.30.0 | v0.30.0 + fix | |---|---|---|---|---| | ~260 tokens | 1 | 4.335 | 4.691 (+8.2%) | 4.349 (+0.3%) | | ~260 tokens | 4 | 5.179 | 5.558 (+7.3%) | 5.382 (+3.9%) | | ~5.9k tokens | 1 | 4.378 | 6.460 (+47.5%) | 4.440 (+1.4%) | | ~5.9k tokens | 4 | 5.462 | 7.455 (+36.5%) | 5.568 (+1.9%) |
What Works * v0.30.0 + fix (mounted over `vllm_flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py`, no rebuild as it's a JIT kernel): decode within 0.3-3.9% of v0.26.0, of which ~1.5% is the unrelated QK-norm + RoPE change below. * `attention_backend=TRITON_ATTN` on v0.30.0: recovers ~70% of the gap.
What Doesn't Work * Passing `num_splits` explicitly: ignored on SM90 (flat timings above). * V1 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`): same slowdown.
What Was Ruled Out | Hypothesis | How tested | Result | |---|---|---| | V2 model runner | V1 runner on v0.30.0 | Same slowdown | | Multimodal / structured output | Text-only prompts, no schema | Same slowdown | | MoE kernel / tuning configs | Per-kernel profile; config files diffed | MoE flat, configs identical | | Scheduler / async scheduling | Batch 4 → 1 | Gap grows | | Launch configuration | Grid, threads, smem from the profile | Identical across versions | | torch 2.13 fused QK-norm + RoPE | Per-kernel profile | Real but small (~1.5% of a step), unrelated |
## Related Issues * [vllm-project/flash-attention#198](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/198): the fix, merged 2026-09-28. * #54819: the pin move (`06bdd47` → `506341a`, fork sync vllm-project/flash-attention#188) that introduced it. * #57680: a different 0.26 → 0.29 decode drop, root-caused to the V2 model runner on Confidential Computing VMs. Not this bug (v0.29.0 doesn't have `506341a`, and our V1-runner control is just as slow). * The same fork sync also kept the pre-[Dao-AILab#2624](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2624) `seqlen_k_loaded` expression in `flash_attn/cute/interface.py` (`window_size_right or max_seqlen_k` treats a causal window's right bound of 0 as unbounded, so the split heuristic sizes sliding-window layers by the full KV length). No measurable cost at Gemma-4's shapes; worth cherry-picking while bumping the pin. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `method="draft_model"` speculative decoding cannot start when the drafter and the target both run on the Transformers modeling backend. OLMo-2 is one example: since v0.26.0, vLLM serves `Olmo2ForCausalLM` through `TransformersForCausalLM`. Engine start-up fails with: ```text ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn ``` **Minimal reproduction** ```python from vllm import LLM LLM( model="allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct", speculative_config={ "method": "draft_model", "model": "allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, }, ) ``` On `main` (model runner V2, the default). Abridged: ```text (EngineCore) INFO [base.py:121] Using Transformers modeling backend. # target (EngineCore) INFO [base.py:121] Using Transformers modeling backend. # drafter File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 397, in load_model self.speculator.load_model(self.model) File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/draft_model/speculator.py", line 112, in load_draft_model return get_model( File "vllm/model_executor/model_loader/utils.py", line 95, in initialize_model model = model_class(vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=prefix) File "vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py", line 186, in __init__ self._create_attention_instances() File "vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py", line 668, in _create_attention_instances attn_instance = attn_cls(**kwargs) File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py", line 444, in __init__ raise ValueError(f"Duplicate layer name: {prefix}") ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn ``` The V1 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) fails the same way, through `vllm/v1/spec_decode/draft_model.py`. The failure does not depend on the drafter being the same model as the target. `allenai/OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct` as the target with `allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct` as the drafter fails with the same `ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn`. (For comparison, the existing test suite runs `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` as both target and drafter, and that works.) This is not #18503. That issue was a single-model OLMo-2 load failure from May 2025, fixed at the time, and it involved no speculative decoding. **Root cause** `Base._create_attention_instances` (`vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py`) names every attention layer `f"{i}.attn"`. It ignores the `prefix` that `Base.__init__` receives. The `draft_model` proposer builds the drafter in the same engine with `prefix="draft_model"`. That applies to both `vllm/v1/spec_decode/draft_model.py` and the model runner V2 `draft_model/speculator.py`. As a result, target and drafter both register `0.attn`, `1.attn`, and so on, and `Attention.__init__` raises on the duplicate. Native models are not affected, because their attention names carry the full module path (`draft_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.attn`). **Affected** Any architecture that is served only through the Transformers backend (the `_TRANSFORMERS_SUPPORTED_MODELS` entries in the registry: OLMo, OLMo-2, OLMo-3, SmolLM3, Starcoder2, GPTBigCode, and others), when it is used as the drafter for a Transformers-backend target. I have a small fix and a regression test ready and will open a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
