title: [Bug]: ThinkingBudgetStateHolder.sync_batch leaks stale state on unidirectional moves
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary On a `MoveDirectionality.UNIDIRECTIONAL` move `i1 -> i2`, `sync_batch` only clears the source index `i2`'s entry when the source index `i1` actually has state. If the request moving into `i2` has no `thinking_token_budget` but the slot `i2` still holds the state of the request that previously lived there, the stale entry survives. The new occupant of `i2` is then charged against the departed request's thinking budget and has `` tokens forcibly injected into its output, even though it never requested a thinking budget. Reproducing the Bug ```python import torch from vllm.v1.sample.logits_processor.interface import BatchUpdate, MoveDirectionality from vllm.v1.sample.thinking_budget_state import ThinkingBudgetStateHolder START, END, FILLER, VOCAB = 100, 200, 7, 300 class Cfg: reasoning_start_token_ids = [START] reasoning_end_token_ids = [END] class Params: def __init__(self, b): self.thinking_token_budget = b holder = ThinkingBudgetStateHolder(Cfg(), 8, 0, torch.device("cpu"), False) a_out, b_out = [], [] holder.sync_batch( BatchUpdate( 2, [], [(0, Params(2), [], a_out), (1, Params(None), [], b_out)], [] ) ) holder.sync_batch(BatchUpdate(1, [], [], [(1, 0, MoveDirectionality.UNIDIRECTIONAL)])) for _ in range(6): holder.update_state([b_out], None) logits = torch.zeros(1, VOCAB) logits[0, START if not b_out else FILLER] = 1.0 holder.apply_to_logits(logits, False, None) b_out.append(int(logits.argmax())) print("B's output:", b_out) assert END not in b_out, "B set no thinking_token_budget but was forced to " ``` Output: ``` B's output: [100, 7, 7, 200, 7, 7] AssertionError: B set no thinking_token_budget but was forced to ``` Fix Pop both endpoints unconditionally, matching `process_dict_updates`. This collapses the `SWAP` and `UNIDIRECTIONAL` branches: ```diff --- a/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py +++ b/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py @@ for i1, i2, direction in batch_update.moved: - if direction == MoveDirectionality.SWAP: - state1 = self._state.pop(i1, None) - state2 = self._state.pop(i2, None) - if state1 is not None: - self._state[i2] = state1 - if state2 is not None: - self._state[i1] = state2 - else: - state = self._state.pop(i1, None) - if state is not None: - self._state[i2] = state + state1 = self._state.pop(i1, None) + state2 = self._state.pop(i2, None) + if state1 is not None: + self._state[i2] = state1 + if state2 is not None and direction == MoveDirectionality.SWAP: + self._state[i1] = state2 ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: ThinkingBudgetStateHolder maps every request to logits row 0 when spec decoding is on but a step has no drafts
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `_apply_forcing_to_logits` derives each request's first logits row (`cu_num_tokens`) from `len(spec_token_ids[i])` whenever `in_spec_mode` is true and `predict_bonus_token` is false. On a step where no draft tokens were proposed, every `len(spec_token_ids[i])` is 0, so `cu_num_tokens[i] == 0` for *all* requests: the forced `` tokens for every budgeted request are written into row 0. Request 0 gets other requests' end tokens injected into its output, and requests 1..n-1 have their thinking budget silently not enforced at all. Reproducing the Bug ```python import torch from vllm.v1.sample.logits_processor.interface import BatchUpdate from vllm.v1.sample.thinking_budget_state import ThinkingBudgetStateHolder START, END, FILLER, VOCAB = 100, 200, 7, 300 class Cfg: reasoning_start_token_ids = [START] reasoning_end_token_ids = [END] class Params: def __init__(self, b): self.thinking_token_budget = b def run(num_spec_tokens): holder = ThinkingBudgetStateHolder( Cfg(), 8, num_spec_tokens, torch.device("cpu"), False ) outs = [[], []] holder.sync_batch( BatchUpdate(2, [], [(i, Params(2), [], outs[i]) for i in range(2)], []) ) for step in range(6): holder.update_state(outs, None) logits = torch.zeros(2, VOCAB) for i in range(2): logits[i, START if step == 0 else FILLER] = 1.0 holder.apply_to_logits(logits, False, [[], []]) for i in range(2): outs[i].append(int(logits[i].argmax())) return outs print("num_spec_tokens=0:", run(0)) print("num_spec_tokens=3:", run(3)) ``` Output: ``` num_spec_tokens=0: [[100, 7, 7, 200, 7, 7], [100, 7, 7, 200, 7, 7]] num_spec_tokens=3: [[100, 7, 7, 200, 200, 200], [100, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7]] ``` Fix Only use the draft-token row layout when the step actually has drafts, and give no row to requests that own none (`_apply_forcing_to_logits` already skips `seq_idx not in self.cu_num_tokens`). ```diff --- a/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py +++ b/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py @@ n_layout = len(spec_token_ids_for_layout) if self._state: n_layout = max(n_layout, max(self._state.keys()) + 1) - for index in range(n_layout): - self.cu_num_tokens[index] = cumulative_total - spec_tokens = ( - spec_token_ids_for_layout[index] - if index < len(spec_token_ids_for_layout) - else [] - ) - if self.in_spec_mode: - cumulative_total += len(spec_tokens) if not predict_bonus_token else 1 - else: - cumulative_total += 1 + # The draft-token row layout only applies to the rejection sampler's + # target logits. A step with no drafts goes through the plain Sampler + # (``spec_decode_metadata is None``), whose logits have one row per + # request, as does the bonus-token pass. + use_spec_layout = ( + self.in_spec_mode + and not predict_bonus_token + and any(spec_token_ids_for_layout) + ) + + for index in range(n_layout): + spec_tokens = ( + spec_token_ids_for_layout[index] + if index < len(spec_token_ids_for_layout) + else [] + ) + if not use_spec_layout: + self.cu_num_tokens[index] = cumulative_total + cumulative_total += 1 + elif spec_tokens: + self.cu_num_tokens[index] = cumulative_total + cumulative_total += len(spec_tokens) + # else: this request owns no target-logits rows this step. ``` With this patch both reproductions above behave correctly (`num_spec_tokens=3` matches `num_spec_tokens=0`; `cu_num_tokens == {1: 0}` with nothing boosted in the mixed case) and the property tests pass. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4 VL dummy image is not the worst case for multimodal profiling
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `get_image_size_with_most_features` returns a square `756x756` image, but a square does *not* maximize the features within the token budget: real images produce up to **378 placeholder tokens vs. 346** and **3312 ViT patches vs. 2916** for the dummy. Memory profiling therefore runs on an input ~9% short on decoder multimodal tokens and ~14% short on ViT patches. Reproducing the Bug ```python from PIL import Image from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.common.mm_preprocess import ( DeepseekV4VLProcessingInfo, DeepseekV4VLProcessor, build_image_block_pad_free, ) from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4Config config = DeepseekV4Config(vision_n_layers=24) class Ctx: def get_hf_config(self, *args, **kwargs): return config info = DeepseekV4VLProcessingInfo(Ctx()) processor = DeepseekV4VLProcessor(config) def features(width, height): out = processor(images=[Image.new("RGB", (width, height))]) n_llm_h, n_llm_w = out["llm_grid"][0].tolist() types, _ = build_image_block_pad_free(n_llm_h, n_llm_w) return len(types), out["patches"].shape[0] dummy = info.get_image_size_with_most_features() print("dummy", dummy, features(dummy.width, dummy.height)) print("1932x336", features(1932, 336)) assert features(1932, 336) <= features(dummy.width, dummy.height) ``` ``` dummy ImageSize(width=756, height=756) (346, 2916) 1932x336 (378, 3312) AssertionError ``` Fix Search the LLM grids that fit the token budget instead of assuming a square. The loop runs once at startup and returns `1932x336` for the shipped config, matching the sweep maxima for both patches and tokens. ```diff --- a/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/mm_preprocess.py +++ b/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/mm_preprocess.py @@ def get_image_size_with_most_features(self) -> ImageSize: hf_config = self.get_hf_config() patch_size = hf_config.vision_patch_size downsample_ratio = hf_config.vision_downsample_ratio - # A square maximizes the ViT patch count (area) within the token - # budget; solve the budget-derived size directly to keep the dummy - # image small. - budget = hf_config.vision_max_n_token - (COMPRESS_PAD_TO - 1) - side = budget * patch_size * downsample_ratio - _, _, best_h, best_w, _ = solve_resize_ratio( - side, side, patch_size, downsample_ratio, budget - ) - return ImageSize(width=best_w, height=best_h) + max_wh_ratio = hf_config.vision_max_wh_ratio + # Every aligner row costs an extra IMAGE_NEW_LINE token, so height is + # more expensive than width and a square is *not* optimal: search the + # LLM grids that fit the budget for the one with the most ViT patches + # (ties broken by the longer sentinel block). + budget = hf_config.vision_max_n_token - (COMPRESS_PAD_TO - 1) + step = patch_size * downsample_ratio + best_grid = (1, 1) + best_key = (0, 0) + for n_llm_h in range(1, budget): + if ( + grid_tokens(n_llm_h * step, step, patch_size, downsample_ratio)[2] + > budget + ): + break + for n_llm_w in range(1, budget): + if max_wh_ratio is not None and n_llm_w > n_llm_h * max_wh_ratio: + break + num_tokens = grid_tokens( + n_llm_h * step, n_llm_w * step, patch_size, downsample_ratio + )[2] + if num_tokens > budget: + break + key = (n_llm_h * n_llm_w, num_tokens) + if key > best_key: + best_key, best_grid = key, (n_llm_h, n_llm_w) + n_llm_h, n_llm_w = best_grid + return ImageSize(width=n_llm_w * step, height=n_llm_h * step) ``` The `max_wh_ratio` guard keeps the returned size from being clamped back down by `load_image`; the selected grid also maximizes area, so it comfortably clears `vision_min_pixels` (649k pixels vs. the 147k minimum) and is not rescaled either. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: FilesystemResolver loads adapters outside VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR (path traversal via LoRA name)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `FilesystemResolver.resolve_lora` builds the adapter path with a bare `os.path.join(self.lora_cache_dir, lora_name)` and never checks that the result stays inside the cache directory. A `lora_name` containing `..`, or an absolute path (which makes `os.path.join` discard the cache dir entirely), resolves to a directory anywhere on the server filesystem. `lora_name` is the client-supplied `model` field of an OpenAI API request (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/models/serving.py:304`), so the `VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR` confinement is trivially bypassable. Reproducing the Bug ```python import asyncio import json import os import tempfile from vllm.lora.resolver import LoRAResolverRegistry from vllm.plugins.lora_resolvers.filesystem_resolver import register_filesystem_resolver root = tempfile.mkdtemp() cache_dir = os.path.join(root, "lora_cache") outside = os.path.join(root, "private_adapter") os.makedirs(cache_dir) os.makedirs(outside) with open(os.path.join(outside, "adapter_config.json"), "w") as f: json.dump( {"peft_type": "LORA", "base_model_name_or_path": "meta-llama/Llama-3-8B"}, f ) os.environ["VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR"] = cache_dir register_filesystem_resolver() resolver = LoRAResolverRegistry.get_resolver("Filesystem Resolver") for name in ["../private_adapter", outside]: req = asyncio.run(resolver.resolve_lora("meta-llama/Llama-3-8B", name)) print(name, "->", req.lora_path if req else None) ``` ``` ../private_adapter -> /tmp/tmpXXXX/lora_cache/../private_adapter /tmp/tmpXXXX/private_adapter -> /tmp/tmpXXXX/private_adapter ``` Fix Normalize the joined path and reject anything that does not remain under the cache directory. ```diff --- a/vllm/plugins/lora_resolvers/filesystem_resolver.py +++ b/vllm/plugins/lora_resolvers/filesystem_resolver.py @@ async def resolve_lora( self, base_model_name: str, lora_name: str ) -> LoRARequest | None: - lora_path = os.path.join(self.lora_cache_dir, lora_name) + cache_root = os.path.realpath(self.lora_cache_dir) + lora_path = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(cache_root, lora_name)) + if os.path.commonpath([cache_root, lora_path]) != cache_root or ( + lora_path == cache_root + ): + return None maybe_lora_request = await self._get_lora_req_from_path( lora_name, lora_path, base_model_name ) return maybe_lora_request ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - title: [Bug]: vllm.utils.system_utils.suppress_stdout silently suppresses stderr when sys.stdout is bound to fd 2
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary The docstring states "Only suppresses stdout, not stderr, to preserve error messages", but the implementation redirects whatever fd `sys.stdout` happens to point at. Under the common `sys.stdout = sys.stderr` idiom, that fd is 2, so `suppress_stdout()` sends **stderr** to `/dev/null` — silently discarding error messages and tracebacks emitted by C libraries during `torch.distributed` group creation. Reproducing the Bug Run as `python repro.py 2> err.txt`; `err.txt` is empty. ```python import os import sys from vllm.utils.system_utils import suppress_stdout sys.stdout = sys.stderr with suppress_stdout(): os.write(2, b"CRITICAL ERROR MESSAGE\n") sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__ ``` ## Fix Target `STDOUT_FILENO` explicitly, so stderr is never a candidate. ```diff --- a/vllm/utils/system_utils.py +++ b/vllm/utils/system_utils.py @@ -76,7 +76,9 @@ def suppress_stdout(): if envs.VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL == "DEBUG": yield return - stdout_fd = sys.stdout.fileno() + # C libraries write to STDOUT_FILENO regardless of what `sys.stdout` is + # bound to; deriving the fd from `sys.stdout` can wrongly target stderr. + stdout_fd = 1 stdout_dup = os.dup(stdout_fd) devnull_fd = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: vllm.utils.system_utils.suppress_stdout crashes when sys.stdout has no file descriptor
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `suppress_stdout()` calls `sys.stdout.fileno()` unguarded, so it raises `io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno` whenever the application has replaced `sys.stdout` with a stream that has no underlying file descriptor — e.g. inside `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())` or in a Jupyter/IPython kernel (`ipykernel.iostream.OutStream`). Because `suppress_stdout()` sits on the core distributed-init path (`vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py:505`, `vllm/distributed/utils.py:556`), this aborts engine startup. Reproducing the Bug ```python import contextlib import io from vllm.utils.system_utils import suppress_stdout with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): with suppress_stdout(): pass ``` ``` io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno File ".../vllm/utils/system_utils.py", line 79, in suppress_stdout stdout_fd = sys.stdout.fileno() ``` Fix Suppress `STDOUT_FILENO` directly instead of asking `sys.stdout` for an fd. ```diff --- a/vllm/utils/system_utils.py +++ b/vllm/utils/system_utils.py @@ -76,7 +76,9 @@ def suppress_stdout(): if envs.VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL == "DEBUG": yield return - stdout_fd = sys.stdout.fileno() + # C libraries write to STDOUT_FILENO regardless of what `sys.stdout` is + # bound to, and `sys.stdout` may not have an fd at all (Jupyter, StringIO). + stdout_fd = 1 stdout_dup = os.dup(stdout_fd) devnull_fd = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: AudioSpec(target_channels=1) does not produce 1D mono output for single-channel 2D audio
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `normalize_audio` documents that "For mono output (target_channels=1), returns 1D array/tensor", but single-channel 2D input — `(1, time)` from torchaudio/pyav, or `(time, 1)` from soundfile, both explicitly listed as supported input layouts — is returned as a 2D `(1, time)` array. Multi-channel input is correctly reduced to 1D, so the output rank silently depends on the input channel count. Downstream, `AudioProcessorItems.get_audio_length` (which uses `len(audio)`) then reports an audio length of `1` instead of the number of samples. Reproducing the Bug ```python import numpy as np from vllm.multimodal.audio import MONO_AUDIO_SPEC, normalize_audio from vllm.multimodal.parse import MultiModalDataParser assert normalize_audio(np.zeros((2, 16000), np.float32), MONO_AUDIO_SPEC).ndim == 1 assert normalize_audio(np.zeros((1, 16000), np.float32), MONO_AUDIO_SPEC).ndim == 1 parser = MultiModalDataParser(target_sr=16000.0, target_channels=1) for shape in [(16000,), (1, 16000), (16000, 1), (2, 16000)]: items = parser._parse_audio_data((np.zeros(shape, np.float32), 16000.0)) print(shape, np.asarray(items.get(0)).shape, items.get_audio_length(0)) ``` Output: ``` AssertionError # on the (1, 16000) assertion (16000,) (16000,) 16000 (1, 16000) (1, 16000) 1 # wrong: 2D, length 1 (16000, 1) (1, 16000) 1 # wrong: 2D, length 1 (2, 16000) (16000,) 16000 ``` Fix Squeeze the singleton channel axis when the target is mono and no reduction is needed. ```diff --- a/vllm/multimodal/audio.py +++ b/vllm/multimodal/audio.py @@ -142,9 +142,11 @@ def normalize_audio( num_channels = audio.shape[0] - # No reduction needed if already at target + # No reduction needed if already at target. Mono output is documented to be + # 1D, so drop the singleton channel axis for single-channel input. if num_channels == spec.target_channels: - return audio + return audio[0] if spec.target_channels == 1 else audio # Cannot expand channels if num_channels < spec.target_channels: ``` With this patch all shapes in the reproducer above return `(16000,)` / length `16000`, for both numpy arrays and torch tensors, and the multi-channel behaviour is unchanged. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: /derender logprob token strings drop SentencePiece leading space
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
Tokenizer only, so platform agnostic. Reporduced on `main` (741edeebeec3cedbe938d831b6d87641ed6191ef) with tokenizers 0.22. ### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Describe the bug Logprob token strings from the derender endpoints lose the SentencePiece leading space. The engine path restores it (#48674) but derender doesn't. `resolve_token_id_placeholder` (`vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py`) does `convert_ids_to_tokens` → `convert_tokens_to_string([tok])` which strips the Metaspace `▁`. The engine uses `convert_ids_list_to_tokens` (`vllm/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py`) which puts it back. ### Reproduction ```python from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer from vllm.tokenizers.detokenizer_utils import convert_ids_list_to_tokens from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.serving import resolve_token_id_placeholder tok = get_tokenizer("hf-internal-testing/llama-tokenizer") ids = tok.encode("x true", add_special_tokens=False) for tid, eng in zip(ids, convert_ids_list_to_tokens(tok, ids)): der, _ = resolve_token_id_placeholder(f"token_id:{tid}", tok) print(tid, repr(tok.convert_ids_to_tokens([tid])[0]), repr(eng), repr(der)) ``` ``` 921 '▁x' engine=' x' derender='x' 1565 '▁true' engine=' true' derender='true' ``` Same result with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`. ### Impact - `/v1/completions/derender`: `top_logprobs` is `dict[str, float]`, so `▁true` and `true` collide and one alternative is silently dropped (the #48674 symptom). - `text_offset` is built from `len(token)`, so it drifts by one per leading space token. - Chat derender `token` / `bytes` don't match the coupled `/v1/chat/completions` output for the same token IDs. ### Proposed fix Resolve through `convert_ids_list_to_tokens(tokenizer, [token_id])[0]` so derender uses the same code as the engine. #58181 renames this function to `decode_token_id` and keeps the current body, so the fix fits best there or right after it merges. Related: #48674, #59046 (raised by @noooop), #58181, #47161. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Description `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` cannot start with `HiSparseConnector` on vLLM v0.30.0 because there is no KV cache layout accepted by all involved backends. The same model starts successfully when HiSparse is disabled. There appear to be conflicting layout requirements: - `HiSparseConnector` requires `BLHNC`. - `KpoolTailBackend`, used by GLM-5.3-Flash's IndexPool tail cache, only advertises `LBHNC`. - `LBHNC` cannot represent the mixed page sizes produced by the model and HiSparse. - Explicitly selecting `BLHNC` is rejected because the common supported-layout intersection only contains `LBHNC`. This concerns `GLM-5.3-Flash` (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`), not the non-Flash `zai-org/GLM-5.3` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) used in the earlier HiSparse blog reproduction. ### Environment - Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0-cu129` - vLLM: `0.30.0` - Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` - Architecture: `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` - Tensor parallel size: 8 - CUDA driver: `580.126.09` - Current PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130` - `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` imports successfully Full `python -m vllm.collect_env` output is attached. ### Minimal reproducer ```bash VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG \ VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC \ vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --language-model-only \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --max-model-len 16640 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 4 \ --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \ --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}' ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug] ExampleHiddenStatesConnector does not support Hybrid KV Cache Manager
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Current environment I am running vLLM on an NVIDIA A100 environment. Relevant environment: * OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS * GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB × 8 * CPU: Intel Xeon Platinum 8458P * NVIDIA driver: 580.178.04 * CUDA runtime: 13.0.88 * PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 * Python: 3.12.13 * Transformers: 5.8.1 * Triton: 3.6.0 * vLLM: 0.21.0 * FlashInfer: 0.6.8.post1 The target model is a hybrid-attention model and I am using `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` for online EAGLE3 draft-model training. Full `collect_env.py` output is included below. ## 🐛 Describe the bug I am trying to use `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` for online EAGLE3 draft-model training. The target model is a hybrid-attention model where different layers use different attention/KV-cache configurations. Therefore, the Hybrid KV Cache Manager (HMA) is required. However, `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` currently does not support HMA, so there is no working configuration for online hidden-state extraction. There are two cases. ### 1. HMA enabled When running with HMA enabled: ```bash --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager ``` the server fails with: ```text ExampleHiddenStatesConnector does not support HMA but HMA is enabled ``` ### 2. HMA disabled When running with: ```bash --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager ``` vLLM attempts to convert the heterogeneous KV-cache specifications into a single unified KV-cache type, but this is not possible for the hybrid-attention model: ```text Hybrid KV cache manager is disabled but failed to convert the KV cache specs to one unified type. ``` Therefore, there is currently no working configuration for using `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` with this hybrid-attention model. The situation can be summarized as: ```text Hybrid-attention model | v Hybrid KV Cache Manager required | +---- HMA enabled | | | v | ExampleHiddenStatesConnector | | | X HMA is not supported | +---- HMA disabled | v KV specs must be unified | X heterogeneous KV specs cannot be unified ``` ## Minimal reproduction I am using the target model with vLLM V1 and the hidden-state extraction path required by online EAGLE3 training. With HMA enabled: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python3 \ /home/speculators-main/scripts/launch_vllm.py \ /home/Qwen3.8-27B \ -- \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --port 8099 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \ --renderer-num-workers 1 \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --enforce-eager ``` This fails with: ```text ExampleHiddenStatesConnector does not support HMA but HMA is enabled ``` If HMA is disabled: ```bash --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager ``` initialization instead fails with: ```text Hybrid KV cache manager is disabled but failed to convert the KV cache specs to one unified type. ``` ## Expected behavior `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector` should support models using the Hybrid KV Cache Manager. For a hybrid-attention model, the expected execution path is: ```text Hybrid-attention model | v Hybrid KV Cache Manager | v ExampleHiddenStatesConnector | v Extract target hidden states | v Online EAGLE3 training ``` The heterogeneous KV-cache configuration should be preserved instead of requiring all KV-cache groups to be converted into a single unified KV-cache type. ## Additional investigation While implementing HMA support, I also found that the current hidden-state extraction path cannot safely reconstruct KV-cache slots using a single global block size/block ID. With HMA, different KV-cache groups can have different metadata and layouts. Reconstructing a slot using logic equivalent to: ```python slot = block_id * block_size + offset ``` can therefore produce an invalid KV-cache index. The execution-time attention metadata already contains the actual slot mapping: ```python attn_metadata.slot_mapping ``` Therefore, the HMA implementation should use the execution-time slot mapping and handle KV metadata per cache group. In particular, the implementation needs to: 1. Support HMA / `CacheOnlyAttention`. 2. Handle KV metadata separately for different KV-cache groups. 3. Use the execution-time `attn_metadata.slot_mapping` instead of reconstructing slots from a single global block size. 4. Preserve the actual KV-cache layout. 5. Correctly align extracted hidden states and token IDs with the execution tokens. 6. Continue to provide the hidden states required by the online EAGLE3 training pipeline. ## Relevant code The main component involved is: ```text vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/example_hidden_states_connector.py ``` The hidden-state extraction path also involves: ```text vllm/model_executor/models/extract_hidden_states.py vllm/v1/spec_decode/extract_hidden_states.py ``` ## Why this is a vLLM issue The target model can be initialized without `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`. The failure is specifically caused by the interaction between: * hybrid-attention KV-cache configuration, * Hybrid KV Cache Manager, * `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`. Disabling HMA is not a workaround for this model because its heterogeneous KV-cache specifications cannot be represented by a single unified KV-cache type. ## Error traces ### HMA enabled ```text ExampleHiddenStatesConnector does not support HMA but HMA is enabled ``` ### HMA disabled ```text Hybrid KV cache manager is disabled but failed to convert the KV cache specs to one unified type. ``` ## Debug logging The issue was reproduced with debug logging enabled: ```bash export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG ``` ## Environment information ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : Could not collect Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-138-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPU 1: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPU 2: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPU 3: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPU 4: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPU 5: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPU 6: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPU 7: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB Nvidia driver version : 580.178.04 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 176 Vendor ID: GenuineIntel Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8458P Core(s) per socket: 44 Socket(s): 2 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 [pip3] numpy==2.2.6 [pip3] torch==2.11.0+cu130 [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0+cu130 [pip3] torchvision==0.26.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.8.1 [pip3] triton==3.6.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.21.0 ``` ## title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash illegal memory access on long-context chucked prefill still reproduces on v 0.30.0 (B200, TP4+EP, MTP)
body:
### Your current environment

## Still reproduces on the v0.30.0 release (4x B200, MTP enabled)

Adding a data point from a different config: official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` image, and **with MTP speculative decoding** (the reports above run without spec decode).

### Environment
- 4x NVIDIA B200 (SM100), TP=4 + EP, Docker, air-gapped
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` (no custom patches)
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8 checkpoint)
- Driver / CUDA: `v13.0`

### Serve args
```
--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
--max-num-batched-tokens 16500 --max-num-seqs 32
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45
```
Prefix caching left at the default (on). `max_model_len` left at the default (1048576). Resolved config: `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, compilation mode NONE, Model Runner V2 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Crash
`CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` on all 4 ranks, followed by `EngineDeadError`.

Where it surfaced:
- All ranks: `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` in the MLA `q_proj` GEMM (`glm5next/nvidia/attention.py:590` → `layers/mla.py:221` → `default_unquantized_gemm`).
- TP0 also: `kv_block_zeroer.zero_block_ids` (`model_runner.py:1206` → `async_tensor_h2d`).

As noted above, these are async reporting sites, not the origin.

### Batch at the time of the crash (from `dump_input`)
```
req A: num_computed_tokens=100513, 6 tokens scheduled (MTP decode, 5 spec tokens)
req B: num_computed_tokens=490752, 16128 tokens scheduled (chunked prefill)
total_num_scheduled_tokens=16134
new_block_ids_to_zero=[1084, 1083, 1082, 1134, 1135, 1136, 1137]
```
So the batch was a mixed step: a ~490K-position chunked prefill combined with an MTP decode. The prefix cache hit rate was ~80% just before the crash. Draft acceptance fell from 95.7% to 45.7% to 28.5% across the last three 10-second intervals before the crash. That may or may not be related.

### Takeaways
- The v0.30.0 release (2026-09-22) is still affected. This is consistent with the 2026-09-16 nightly repro above.
- MTP does not avoid it, and MTP adds spec-decode state paths to the mix.
- We have not yet isolated the cause by varying one setting at a time (prefix caching off, MTP off, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, a smaller `--max-num-batched-tokens`). We will report back.

We have the full worker tracebacks and the scheduler dump, and can share them.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

When a generation stops in the middle of a multi-byte character, which `max_tokens` does routinely, the rebuilt response is not the same string: ``` ordinary : 'Output:\n```\n🌈' derendered : 'Output:\n```\n🌈�' ``` Same request, same token ids, same `finish_reason`. The ordinary route holds the incomplete bytes back (they belong to a character the next token would have finished, and the generation ended first); the **non-streaming** derender decodes the whole id list in one call and gets a replacement character. The **streaming** derender in the same file does it correctly, it carries `prefix_offset`/`read_offset` through `detokenize_incrementally`, which is exactly the mechanism that holds a partial character across a boundary (as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161 describes). So this is not a judgement call about what to do with trailing incomplete bytes; one half of the feature already makes the other choice. At short lengths the difference is the whole answer: for `/v1/completions` at `max_tokens=1`, the ordinary route returns `''` and the derender returns `' �'`. **Versions** Reproduced identically on **0.27.1** and **0.29.0**. Stock wheels, one GPU, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, no special flags. **Reproduction** `repro_derender_replacement_char.py` go thru `max_tokens` 1…24 over three prompts, through three legs, and compares only rows where both paths emitted the **same token ids**, so batch numerics (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40896) cannot produce a false positive, seems like that one still in progress :) [repro_derender_replacement_char.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/5a260da5349fe424591f5b3c31c7733b#file-repro_derender_replacement_char-py) ``` $ python repro_derender_replacement_char.py --base-url http://localhost:8000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B ``` | arm | 0.27.1 | 0.29.0 | |---|---|---| | `/v1/chat/completions/derender`, non-streaming | **6 differing / 70 compared** | **6 / 70** | | `/v1/completions/derender`, non-streaming | **8 differing / 69 compared** | **8 / 69** | | `/v1/chat/completions/derender`, streaming | 0 differing / 70 compared | 0 / 70 | Every differing row adds exactly one `U+FFFD` that the ordinary answer does not contain. Sample (0.27.1, identical on 0.29.0): ``` chat max_tokens= 6 ordinary='Output:\n```\n🌈' derendered='Output:\n```\n🌈�' chat max_tokens=10 ordinary='Output:\n```\n🌈‍🌈🧑' derendered='Output:\n```\n🌈‍🌈🧑�' completions max_tokens= 1 ordinary='' derendered=' �' completions max_tokens= 4 ordinary=' 🌈' derendered=' 🌈�' ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py` attaches the elastic-EP router inside `if "generate" in supported_tasks:` with **no condition on `--enable-elastic-ep`**. So `/scale_elastic_ep` and `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` are reachable on every ordinary vLLM deployment, including a plain single-GPU `vllm serve`. So there are few issues here ## Bug 1: the route is a state-changing endpoint outside the API-key guard With the server started as `--api-key SECRET-KEY-123` and **no** `Authorization` header sent: | route | status | |---|---| | `/v1/models` | **401** | | `/v1/completions` | **401** | | `/tokenize` | 200 | | **`/scale_elastic_ep`** | **200** | | `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` | 200 | The api-key middleware guards by path prefix (`entrypoints/serve/utils/server_utils.py:42`): ```python GUARDED_PREFIX = ("/v1", "/v2", "/inference", "/cohere") ``` `/scale_elastic_ep` is mounted at the root, so it is never checked. It is the only **state-changing** route in that position: `/health`, `/version`, `/metrics` and `/tokenize` are reads, while this one changes the serving topology and, while it runs, makes `ScalingMiddleware` answer **every** request on the server with 503. That is the part of this finding that matters. An operator who sets `--api-key` reasonably believes the server is closed; for this route the guarantee does not hold, and the impact is availability rather than one bad response. The two bugs below are what makes it reachable by accident as well as on purpose. ## Bug 2: a boolean passes validation and is used as the engine count ```python if not isinstance(new_data_parallel_size, int) or new_data_parallel_size <= 0: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, ...) ``` In Python `bool` is a subclass of `int`, so `isinstance(True, int)` is `True` and `True <= 0` is `False`. The value passes, reaches `client.scale_elastic_ep(...)`, and the server answers: ``` POST /scale_elastic_ep {"new_data_parallel_size": true} 200 {"message": "Scaled to True data parallel engines"} ``` The request was **accepted and executed** on the same server, the same route, the same second, `{"new_data_parallel_size": 2}` returned 500. And the confirmation message renders the Python `bool` (`"Scaled to True data parallel engines"`), `True == 1`, so what was requested is "scale to a single engine". On a deployment running more than one, a JSON encoder that emits `true` where a count was meant asks for every other engine to be torn down, and is told it succeeded. Every neighbouring value is rejected correctly, making this clearly cleary a bug: | body | status | |---|---| | `{}` (missing) | 400 | | `{"new_data_parallel_size": 0}` | 400 | | `{"new_data_parallel_size": -1}` | 400 | | `{"new_data_parallel_size": "2"}` | 400 | | `{"new_data_parallel_size": 2.5}` | 400 | | **`{"new_data_parallel_size": true}`** | **200** | | `{"drain_timeout": 0, ...}` | 400 | | `{"drain_timeout": "60", ...}` | 400 | `drain_timeout` has the identical guard and therefore the identical hole. ## Bug 3, a request the server structurally cannot honor is a 500 On the same plain server, `{"new_data_parallel_size": 2}` returns: ``` 500 {"error": {"message": "Scale failed", "type": "Internal Server Error", "code": 500}} ``` The engine is healthy: `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` answers 200 `false` immediately afterwards and a `/v1/completions` right after that returns 200. Nothing failed on the server side, the server simply was not started with `--enable-elastic-ep` (and `--enable-eplb`, which vLLM's own config requires with it), so this request can never succeed on this process. So this should be a 4xx? A 5xx makes clients retry with backoff and makes monitoring page, for a request that is permanently impossible. It is the same shape as the `/v1/messages` context-overflow 500 filed separately, on a different route. **The operator gets nothing either.** The handler logs `logger.error("Scale failed: %s", e)` and the underlying exception carries no message, so the server log reads, verbatim: ``` ERROR 09-21 16:23:53 [api_router.py:79] Scale failed: ``` Neither the client nor the log says the engine lacks elastic EP. **Reproduce** [repro_scale_elastic_ep.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/79b4dbf5d0a6993c7f85cdbb6a557638#file-repro_scale_elastic_ep-py) `python3 repro_scale_elastic_ep.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000` Any `vllm serve ` will do; no parallelism flags, one GPU. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: `--tool-call-parser mistral` on a non-Mistral tokenizer can start but then answers EVERY chat request with 500
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Very interesting issue, the Mistral tool-call parser needs the tokenizer's `[TOOL_CALLS]` token. A tokenizer that does not have one is accepted at startup: the server boots, logs no error, and `/health` returns 200. Every subsequent chat request then fails: ``` HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"Mistral parser could not locate the tool call token in the tokenizer!", "type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}} ``` Below are some Claude blob describing the experiemnts: **Including requests that have nothing to do with tools.** A plain `{"messages":[{"role":"user", "content":"Say hi."}]}` with no `tools` field is answered with the same 500, because the parser is constructed for every chat completion once `--enable-auto-tool-choice` is on. Measured 2026-09-19 with a 17-shape sweep (plain chat, tools, two tools, `tool_choice` none/required/named, truncated variants, JSON schema, stop, logprobs, n=2, long prompt), each in non-streaming, repeated non-streaming and streaming form: | requests | status | |---|---| | 51 of 51 | **500** `Mistral parser could not locate the tool call token in the tokenizer!` | | of which `plain` (no `tools` in the body) | 3 of 3 also 500 | The same sweep against `hermes`, `granite`, `pythonic`, `xlam` and `kimi_k2` on the same model returns 200 throughout (their parsers degrade to "no tool call found" instead of raising). Re-run on **0.29.0** the same evening with the same 17-shape sweep on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`: **51 of 51 requests 500 again**, byte-identical complaint. Whatever 0.29 changed in the structured-output validators, it did not touch this. Re-checked 2026-09-20 on a second model, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, with the repro below: | request | status | |---|---| | `GET /health` | **200** -- the server reports healthy | | chat, no `tools` in the body | **500** | | chat with one tool | **500** | | `/v1/completions` (the parser is not in that path) | **200** | But def somethings we want to fix, either 1. **fail at startup** -- the parser's requirement on the tokenizer is knowable at launch, so `vllm serve` should refuse the combination rather than serve a dead endpoint; or 2. **fail the tool requests only, with a 4xx** -- a request that carries no `tools` does not need the parser at all, and a request that does is a client/server configuration error, not an internal one. **Reproduction** [repro_mistral_parser_foreign_tokenizer_500.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/13223f4891c2725d3f137ed24f69f1f9#file-repro_mistral_parser_foreign_tokenizer_500-py) ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral ``` Just point it the script at a server launched with the flags above and it sends three requests -- plain chat, a chat with a tool, and a `/v1/completions` control (which does not touch the parser). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Reproducer (`repro_bi_awq_compile.py`, attached): request A (1610 tokens) alone, alone again, then started 5 ms after a 3227-token request B so its prefill/decode steps are batched with B. 48 greedy tokens with per-token log-probs, three rounds. **Repro** [repro_bi_awq_compile.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/6a17ff82eff9648323330616bc479c50#file-repro_bi_awq_compile-py) ``` VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000 python3 repro_bi_awq_compile.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ ``` | serve flags | A alone vs A alone | A batched with B vs A alone | |---|---|---| | default (compile + CUDA graphs) | identical, 3/3 | **greedy token differs at position 4, max abs log-prob gap 0.0135, 3/3 rounds** | | `--enforce-eager` | identical, 3/3 | identical, 3/3 | | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` bf16, default | identical | identical, 3/3 | | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8`, default and `--enforce-eager` | identical | identical, 3/3 each | The same shows up with prefix caching on, as cold-vs-warm: the same prompt served from the prefix cache (only its tail computed, in a 1-16-token batch) vs. computed in one full prefill differs on the AWQ model at every length tried (36 / 120 / 395 / 981 / 2977 tokens; log-prob gaps 0.004-0.028, a greedy flip at 981), identical on bf16, identical on AWQ with `--enforce-eager`, and exactly the same five numbers with `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'` as with the default. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 MXFP4: flashinfer_trtllm selects unsupported BF16/SiTU MoE backend
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment captured from the failing job logs</summary>

```text
- Base image: vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7f1a5398e9610d96c473931a26c0e12bbe0d0423 (vLLM 0.30.1rc1.dev48+g7f1a5398e)
- vLLM builds tested: the image as shipped (7f1a5398e), plus per-commit wheels from https://wheels.vllm.ai/<sha>/cu130 installed on that image with --no-deps:
  - 0.26.1rc1.dev135+gaeeb36b1f
  - 0.30.1rc1.dev52+g44bf011f4
- Also observed on a container built from vLLM 0.29.1rc1.dev513+g0961bbae2 with FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 (TP=16, DP=1 case below)
- FlashInfer: flashinfer-python / flashinfer-cubin / flashinfer-jit-cache (+cu130), versions 0.6.18.post1 and 0.7.0 (0.6.15.post1 also tried, see below)
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, NVIDIA driver 580.178.04, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, Python 3.12
- Hardware: 4 x GB200 NVL nodes (aarch64), 4 GPUs each (16 GPUs)
- Model: moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (revision f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06); vLLM reports quantization=mxfp4, dtype=bfloat16
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug


Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 MoE weights, SITU activation) served with `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm` fails during engine start-up (`profile_run`). vLLM logs `Using 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16' Mxfp4 MoE backend.`, and then every worker fails inside FlashInfer:

```
RuntimeError: Error in function 'TrtllmGenBatchedGemmRunner' at .../flashinfer/data/csrc/trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu:239: No kernel found for the given options: mDtypeA: MxE2m1, mDtypeB: Bfloat16, mDtypeC: Bfloat16, mUseDeepSeekFp8: 0, mActType: 2, mEltwiseActType: 0, mTransposeMmaOutput: 1, mRouteAct: 1, mFusedAct: 1, mIsStaticBatch: 0, mTileSize: 32, mBiasType: 0, mFusedBiasShuffleMode: 0, mBiasDtype: Bfloat16, mUsePerTokenScaling: 0, mPerTokenSfDtype: Void, mUsePerChannelScaling: 0
```

`mActType: 2` is `ActType::SiTuGlu` (`include/flashinfer/trtllm/batched_gemm/KernelRunner.h`: `SwiGlu = 0, GeGlu = 1, SiTuGlu = 2, None = 3`). The API server never becomes ready.

Both TRTLLM MXFP4 expert implementations are affected:

- **Data parallel > 1 / expert parallel** uses `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` → `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`.
- **Tensor parallel only (TP=16, DP=1)** uses `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic` → `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`.

**Reproduction 1: DP=4 / EP, modular path.** A Ray cluster spans 4 GB200 nodes; the command runs on the head node:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=1
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 1 --data-parallel-backend ray \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-model-len 3840 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --load-format safetensors
```

Traceback (abridged; vLLM 44bf011f4 + FlashInfer 0.7.0; identical on every rank):

```
vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:612 determine_available_memory
 -> vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:949 profile_run -> :836 _dummy_run -> :1992 execute_model
 -> vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py (2110, 1626, 1338, 1096, 841)
 -> vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py:314 forward
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:734 / 165 / 921 / 633
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py:1248 forward_modular
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:866 apply
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1708 / 1481 / 1321
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py:436 apply -> :361 _invoke_kernel
 -> flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py:6673 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe -> :3633 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op -> :3559 run_selected_tactic
RuntimeError: ... No kernel found ... mDtypeA: MxE2m1, mDtypeB: Bfloat16 ... mActType: 2 ... mTileSize: 32 ...
```

**Reproduction 2: TP=16, DP=1, monolithic path.** Same 4-node GB200 Ray cluster, vLLM 0961bbae2 + FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. The relevant flags are:

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

vLLM logs `Using 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16' Mxfp4 MoE backend.` and `Using TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, then fails with the same error. Traceback (abridged):

```
-> vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py:311 forward -> :356 _fused_forward
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py:165 / 917 / 619
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/routed_experts.py:1282 forward_monolithic
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py:889 apply_monolithic
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py:1678 apply_monolithic -> :1550 apply
 -> vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py:243 apply
 -> flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py:6217 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe -> :3885 trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe_op -> :3813 run_selected_tactic
RuntimeError: Error in function 'TrtllmGenBatchedGemmRunner' at .../trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu:242: No kernel found ... mDtypeA: MxE2m1, mDtypeB: Bfloat16, mDtypeC: Bfloat16 ... mActType: 2 ...
```

**Expected.** vLLM either selects a backend variant that has SITU kernels (MXFP4 × MXFP8), or rejects the configuration with a clear error at backend-selection time.

**Actual.** A runtime kernel-lookup failure occurs in `profile_run`.

**Results (reproduction 1).** Base image, hardware, model and flags are the same in every row; only the vLLM wheel and the FlashInfer version change.

| vLLM | FlashInfer | Selected MoE backend | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| aeeb36b1f (#50000, Kimi-K3 support) | 0.6.15.post1 | none | `ValueError: Mxfp4 MoE backend 'FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support MoEActivation.SITU activation.` (this FlashInfer has no `ActivationType.Situ`) |
| aeeb36b1f | 0.6.18.post1 | FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16 | `No kernel found` (above) |
| 7f1a5398e (nightly image as shipped) | 0.6.18.post1 | (same error signature) | `No kernel found` |
| 44bf011f4 | 0.7.0 | FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16 | `No kernel found` |

This configuration has not worked on any public vLLM and FlashInfer combination we tried. On an earlier nightly (0961bbae2, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1) with the DP=4 parallelism but `--moe-backend` left on auto, vLLM selected `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` and got past MoE profiling. That run later failed because the requested 1M context exceeded the available KV-cache memory, so it is evidence that the MXFP8 SiTU path gets past profiling, not an end-to-end serving pass.

### Root cause and source recheck (2026-09-28)

The latest GPU reproduction above is **vLLM `44bf011f4` with FlashInfer `0.7.0`**. The September 28 update is a source and issue/PR review; the newer revisions below were not rerun on GPUs.

The relevant capability mismatch remains in vLLM `cd63bf9996d3fdbe24a3228f970b84310600612f`:

- [`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsBase`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd63bf9996d3fdbe24a3228f970b84310600612f/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py#L129-L147) accepts both `(kMxfp4Static, None)` and `(kMxfp4Static, kMxfp8Dynamic)`. For `MoEActivation.SITU`, `_supports_activation()` independently returns `has_flashinfer_situ_activation()`. This tests the presence of the FlashInfer activation enum rather than support for the specific weight/activation-format pair, so the BF16 variant also claims SiTU support.
- [The MXFP4 backend mapping](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/cd63bf9996d3fdbe24a3228f970b84310600612f/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py#L307-L311) still tries `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` before `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` for `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm`.
- Both `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic` (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`) and `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` (`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`) inherit the same capability checks. The tested TP16/DP1 and DP4/EP configurations therefore pass `ActivationType.Situ` with BF16 hidden states into FlashInfer.

FlashInfer's current source corroborates the unsupported combination:

- [FlashInfer #4180](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4180), merged July 29, added TRTLLM-Gen SiTU for **MXFP4 × MXFP8** and **NVFP4 × NVFP4**.
- At FlashInfer `85bfa5e4b599a9c616f073e2c06d3b9a1cdadee4`, the [TRT-LLM FP4 activation matrix](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/85bfa5e4b599a9c616f073e2c06d3b9a1cdadee4/docs/design_docs/flashinfer_moe_api.md#L823-L825) lists **only SwiGLU for MXFP4 × BF16**, while MXFP4 × MXFP8 includes SiTU.
- The [runner capability declaration](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/85bfa5e4b599a9c616f073e2c06d3b9a1cdadee4/flashinfer/fused_moe/runners.py#L5253-L5265) expresses that same restriction per quantization pair. vLLM's direct calls above do not use this unified-runner capability validation.

This supports retaining the report as a vLLM backend-selection/capability-validation bug. The observed `mTileSize: 32` is part of the failure signature; the evidence does not establish that merely choosing another tile makes BF16/SiTU supported.

### Suggested fix

1. **vLLM:** validate the activation type and quantization pair together for both TRTLLM MXFP4 expert implementations. Reject SiTU with `activation_key=None` while that combination is unsupported, allowing selection to continue to `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` when supported on the target device, or fail early with a clear configuration error.
2. **FlashInfer:** alternatively or additionally, add TRTLLM-Gen MXFP4 × BF16 SiTuGlu kernels. vLLM could also consume a capability check covering the quantization pair, activation and target device instead of relying only on the enum's presence.

A possible user-side workaround on the tested GB200 platform is `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm_afp8`, which maps only to `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`. **This explicit flag was not tested in either exact reproduction configuration**, and the auto-selection result above is not an end-to-end validation.

The smallest model-level configuration tested here used 16 GB200 GPUs; the repro was not reduced further. A direct `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` or `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` call with MXFP4 weights, BF16 hidden states and `ActivationType.Situ` is a candidate single-Blackwell-GPU reproducer, but has not been run.

### Related upstream work, checked 2026-09-28

A renewed search of vLLM and FlashInfer issues and PRs found no matching report or fix for this exact TRTLLM MXFP4 × BF16/SiTU kernel-lookup failure. Related activity includes:

| Reference | Status as of 2026-09-28 | Relation to this report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [vLLM #58635](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58635) | Merged September 25 | Adds deferred finalization to modular TRTLLM-Gen experts. The SiTU/quantization capability mismatch remains in current source. |
| [FlashInfer #5430](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5430) | Merged September 27 | Adds a separate CuTe DSL W4A8 MXFP4/SiTU routed-MoE backend for SM100/SM103. It does not add the missing TRTLLM MXFP4 × BF16 support. |
| [FlashInfer #5639](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5639) | Open; created September 28 | Performance follow-up to #5430 for the same CuTe DSL W4A8 backend. |
| [FlashInfer #5518](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5518) | Open | Another CuTe DSL W4A8 MXFP4/SiTU implementation for B300, not the failing TRTLLM BF16 path. |
| [vLLM #58827](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58827) | Closed without merge | Targets unquantized BF16 Kimi-K3 dense/shared MLP projections, not the MXFP4 routed experts. |

Other references considered in the original investigation:

- [vLLM #50001](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50001): Kimi-K3 tracking.
- [vLLM #54723](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54723): FP8 DP/EP hang.
- [vLLM #52240](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52240): MXFP4 W13 layout.
- [vLLM #56770](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56770): compressed-tensors W4A16.
- [vLLM #52308](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52308): NVFP4 ReLU².
- [FlashInfer #5053](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5053): NVFP4 SiTU output scale factors.
- [FlashInfer #5337](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5337): MXFP8/MXFP4 SiTU routed-MoE performance.
- [FlashInfer #5296](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5296): blockwise FP8 SiTU.
- [FlashInfer #5462](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5462): SM107 CuTe DSL activation support.
- [FlashInfer #5183](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5183) and [#5455](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5455): NVFP4 SiTU paths.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug][ROCm] v0.30.0: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot boot on gfx942 — Engram pinned-host CPU offload lost on the AMD path (+47 GiB/rank GPU), OOM in profile_run
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM Version                 : 0.30.0
Image                        : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0 (official, digest sha256:2e7da1ad1c66…, no custom layers)
PyTorch version              : 2.12.0+git6bbd260
ROCm Version (image)         : 7.2.3 (/opt/rocm-7.2.3, bundled); host user space: ROCm 7.2.4
GPU                          : 8x AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942, 191.98 GiB each), TP=4 (DeepSeek on GPUs 0-3)
Orchestrator                 : GPUStack v2.2.3 (docker backend)
Model                        : deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — DeepseekV41ForCausalLM,
                               FP8 (ue8m0) attention + MXFP4 experts, 48 shards / 475.25 GiB,
                               engram_num_embeddings=[384006168, 384016682], head_dim=256
Working image (baseline)     : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-eed1f3d0c6043bd494424a22443ee198dd56f657
                               (vLLM 0.1.1.dev50+geed1f3d0c, 0.29.x nightly, ~2026-09-12)
<!-- run `vllm collect-env` in the serving container and paste the full output here -->
```

Serve command (production):

```
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer-mode=deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size=4 --gpu-memory-utilization=0.94 \
  --moe-backend=aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 --tool-call-parser=deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser=deepseek_v41 --mm-encoder-tp-mode=data \
  --max-model-len 819200 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_MXFP8_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD=1
VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Every startup on v0.30.0 dies in `profile_run` (~2.5 min into init) on all TP workers, and the server never becomes healthy:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 955, in profile_run
...
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py", line 309, in forward
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py", line 1077, in forward
File ".../vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py", line 1045, in rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer
  workspace_manager.get_simultaneous(((decode_rows, max_model_len), torch.float32))
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/workspace.py", line 207, in _ensure_workspace_size
  self._current_workspaces[workspace_id] = torch.empty(...)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 50.00 GiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 191.98 GiB of which 37.10 GiB is free.
Of the allocated memory 150.30 GiB is allocated by PyTorch ...
```

(The same model + same args start fine on the 0.29.x nightly image above the same GPUs.)

### Root cause (code-level, both images inspected)

Two facts combine:

1. **0.30.0 lost the Engram pinned-host CPU offload on the AMD/common path.**
   On the 0.29 nightly, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py:914` wired
   `cpu_offload=engram_config.cpu_offload if engram_config else True` into the
   `ParallelEngramEmbedding`, so the two DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Engram tables
   (94.4 GiB each; 23.60 GiB per rank at TP4) lived in pinned host memory and were
   read via UVA — each rank's log shows
   `Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory: 9600xxxx rows x 256, 23.60 GiB per rank`,
   and `Model loading took 100.09 GiB` per rank.

   In v0.30.0 the tree was renamed `deepseek_v4_1` → `deepseek_v41`. The NVIDIA path
   still reads the config (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py:358-365`,
   `get_current_vllm_config().engram_config`), but the AMD model instantiates the
   common `Engram` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py:64`), whose
   `ParallelEngramEmbedding._allocate_weights()` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:695`)
   now allocates unconditionally on the current (CUDA) device — the `cpu_offload`
   wiring is gone from this path entirely. `EngramConfig.cpu_offload` still defaults
   to `envs.VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` = `True` in 0.30.0, and
   `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config()` even auto-creates the config for
   models with Engram layers — the AMD path just never consults it.

   Result: `Model loading took 147.3 GiB` per rank (+47.2 GiB = exactly 2 x 23.60 GiB),
   no offload log lines.

2. **The profile-time sparse-indexer workspace reservation is unchanged and large.**
   `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` (profiling early-exit branch) reserves a decode-logits
   workspace of `(decode_rows, max_model_len)` fp32. `_max_decode_logits_rows()` would
   bound it to `max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` = 192 rows (592 MiB), but
   that bound requires `get_current_vllm_config()`, which is not set during `profile_run`
   in either version — so both images fall back to `num_batched_tokens` = 16384 rows:
   16384 x 819200 x 4 B = **50.00 GiB**.

   On the nightly this 50 GiB reservation succeeds (weights 100.09 GiB → ~80 GiB free)
   and the engine starts (`Available KV cache memory: 11.29 GiB`). On 0.30.0 with
   GPU-resident Engram tables only 37.10 GiB is free → the allocation OOMs and the
   engine core dies.

### Fix

Restore the nightly default on the common/AMD path — one small patch to
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py::_allocate_weights()`:

```python
cpu_offload = True
try:
    engram_config = get_current_vllm_config().engram_config
    if engram_config is not None:
        cpu_offload = engram_config.cpu_offload
except Exception:
    pass
kwargs = {"device": "cpu", "pin_memory": True} if cpu_offload else {}
```

(also guarding with `is_uva_available()` like the NVIDIA path, and re-adding the
`Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory` log line).

With only this change, v0.30.0 boots identically to the 0.29 nightly on the same rig:

| | 0.29 nightly | v0.30.0 + engram patch |
|---|---|---|
| Engram offload log | 23.60 GiB per rank x8 | 23.60 GiB per rank x8 |
| Model loading | 100.09 GiB/rank | 100.09 GiB/rank |
| Available KV cache | 11.29 GiB (4,031,384 tokens, 4.92x concurrency) | 11.33 GiB (4,045,600 tokens, 4.94x) |
| init engine | 286.43 s | 280.38 s |
| Short request (17*23) | — | `391` correct |
| 30,060-token needle (chunked prefill) | — | exact recall |

### Suggested upstream fix

Make `ParallelEngramEmbedding._allocate_weights()` in
`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` honor
`vllm_config.engram_config.cpu_offload` (with the `EngramConfig` default, i.e.
`envs.VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` / `True`), matching the NVIDIA variant
(`deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py`) and the pre-refactor behavior
(`deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py:914`). Otherwise every ROCm deployment of
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 on 192 GB GPUs cannot boot on 0.30.0.

Side note: the profile-time fallback in `_max_decode_logits_rows()` means the 50 GiB
decode-logits workspace is reserved and locked even on healthy boots, which is why
TP4 MI308X ends up with only ~11 GiB of KV cache at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.94`.
The config-based tight bound (192 rows) would presumably be used if
`get_current_vllm_config()` were reachable during profiling — worth a look, though it
is orthogonal to this regression.

Related: #58310 (documents that `cpu_offload=True` is the intended default for these
tables; sizes match our measurements), #58808 (notes `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` churn),
#58782 (unrelated ROCm DSv4.1 Quark-checkpoint fixes).

title: [Bug]: Derender drops the leading space on SentencePiece tokenizers
body:
### Your current environment

Tokenizer only, so it's not platform specific. Reproduced on `main` (a2be4d3cc7) with `tokenizers` 0.22.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On SentencePiece/Metaspace tokenizers, `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` drop the first output token's leading space. `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` keep it. Thank you to @hyeongyun0916 for reporting it in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42729#issuecomment-5857086699.

The engine seeds its incremental detokenizer with the prompt (`DecodeStream(ids=prompt_token_ids)` for fast tokenizers, `convert_prompt_ids_to_tokens` for slow ones). Derender decodes the output IDs cold in every path in `vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py`. The batch paths call `tokenizer.decode` and streaming starts from an empty `DerenderStreamState`. The parser streaming path does this too, even though it already requires `prompt_token_ids`. A Metaspace decoder strips the `▁` from whatever token comes first, so without the prompt in front, the first output token loses its space.

Tokenizer level repro (the same decode each path does):

```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from tokenizers.decoders import DecodeStream

for name in ["microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"]:
    tok = Tokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
    prompt = tok.encode("<|user|>\nHi<|end|>\n<|assistant|>\n",
                        add_special_tokens=False).ids
    out = tok.encode("Hello there, output", add_special_tokens=False).ids

    derender = tok.decode(out, skip_special_tokens=True)
    ds = DecodeStream(ids=prompt, skip_special_tokens=True)
    coupled = "".join(s for t in out if (s := ds.step(tok, t)) is not None)
    print(f"{name}: derender={derender!r} coupled={coupled!r}")
```

```text
microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct: derender='Hello there, output' coupled=' Hello there, output'
Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct:       derender='Hello there, output' coupled='Hello there, output'
```

Against the render server:

```bash
vllm launch render microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions/derender \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "generate_response": {
      "choices": [{"index": 0, "token_ids": [15043, 727, 29892, 1962],
                   "finish_reason": "stop"}]
    },
    "prompt_tokens": 8
  }' | jq '.choices[0].message.content'
# "Hello there, output"   (/v1/chat/completions returns " Hello there, output")
```

Derender should match the main path for the same prompt and output IDs (RFC #42729 / #47161).

This hits Metaspace tokenizers with a dummy prefix: Llama-2, Phi-3/3.5 and older HF-format Mistral. Byte-level BPE (Llama-3, Qwen, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Phi-4) is fine which is why the parity test in #48617 doesn't catch it because it only runs `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B`. I haven't checked `mistral-common` tokenizers. Parsers on the derender path also get slightly different input text than chat serving gives them.

**Proposed fix:** seed derender's detok state from the prompt tail the same way the engine does and route the batch paths through `_detokenize_delta` so batch and streaming share one decode (related to #57593). Prompt IDs come from an optional `prompt_token_ids` on each derender request, then from `GenerateResponse.prompt_token_ids`. If neither is present it falls back to the current behaviour, so nothing breaks.

Related: #42729, #47161, #43606, #47301, #48617, #57593

cc @hyeongyun0916  @DarkLight1337

title: [Bug][ROCm] v0.30.0: GLM-5.3-Flash cannot boot on gfx942 — ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl missing record_logical_topk_ready (#57252 not in the release)
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM Version                 : 0.30.0
Image                        : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0 (official, digest sha256:2e7da1ad1c66…, no custom layers)
PyTorch version              : 2.12.0+git6bbd260
ROCm Version (image)         : 7.2.3 (/opt/rocm-7.2.3, bundled); host user space: ROCm 7.2.4
GPU                          : 8x AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942), TP=4
Orchestrator                 : GPUStack v2.2.3 (docker backend)
Model                        : ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3-Flash — Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration,
                               native FP8 (weight_block_size [128,128]), 62 shards / 305.79 GiB
<!-- run `vllm collect-env` in the serving container and paste the full output here -->
```

Serve command (production):

```
vllm serve /models/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup": false}'
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug


Every startup on v0.30.0 dies in `profile_run` (~2 min into init) on all TP workers, and the server never becomes healthy:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
  self.model_runner.profile_run()
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 955, in profile_run
...
File ".../vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/attention.py", line 590, in forward
File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py", line 235, in forward
  self.mla_attn.impl.record_logical_topk_ready()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'

RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no
attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'', ... Engine core initialization failed.
```

Root cause: `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper.forward` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`) calls
`impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on **every** sparse MLA layer. On ROCm the only sparse MLA backend is
`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`, whose impl `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` extends `MLAAttentionImpl` +
`SharedTopkIndicesBuffer`. In the `v0.30.0` tag neither base provides the method — the only definition lives on
`SparseMLACommonImpl` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py:717`), which the ROCm impl
does not extend. The method was added on `main` by #57252 (merged 2026-09-17; present in tag `v0.30.1rc0`,
verified against `main`'s `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`), but it did not make it into `v0.30.0`.

This is the same regression as #58575 (GLM-5.3 `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` on MI325X) and regression 1 of #57248.
This report adds an independent reproduction for `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (GLM-5.3-Flash) on MI308X
(gfx942) at TP=4, plus long-context findings below. Since the call site runs on every sparse MLA layer and ROCm
has no alternative sparse backend, no flag combination avoids it on ROCm.

Additional gfx942 data point: in the `v0.30.0` tag, `fwht128_quant_fp8`
(`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py`) still hardcodes `torch.float8_e4m3fn` and the 448 clamp
(verified by exact-source match against #56607's diff anchors), so the >16K-token chunked-prefill indexer path on
gfx942 is expected to hit the flydsl compile failure documented in #56607. We validated long context **with**
#56607 applied (see below); we did not run the >16K case on stock v0.30.0.


### Workaround (validated on 8x MI308X, TP=4)

1. Add the no-op from #57252 to `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl`
   (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) — equivalent to the base-class default proposed in #56604:

   ```python
   def record_logical_topk_ready(self) -> None:
       pass
   ```

2. Keep `--kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup": false}'` — the jit-warmup subsystem otherwise crashes on this
   path (`'function' object has no attribute 'compile'`, #57248 regression 2 / #57192).

With (1) alone the engine boots and serves short requests. With (1) + (2) + the still-open gfx942 GLM patches
(#56607, #56469, #56381, #56584), a 28,842-token chunked-prefill needle-in-a-haystack request completes with
exact recall (prefix cache hit 27,648 tokens), and the server has been running in production since.

### Request

- Backport #57252 into a `v0.30.x` patch release (same ask as #58575), or add a known-issues note for
  GLM-5.3 / sparse-MLA models on ROCm to the v0.30.0 release notes.
- Before pointing AMD ROCm users at `vllm-openai-rocm:latest` (= v0.30.0 today) for GLM-5.3-Flash, note that
  boot needs #57252 and gfx942 long context additionally needs the open PRs #56607 (and, for production
  correctness on MI308X, #56469/#56381/#56584 from the 0.29-based stacks).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

*Search results: #58575 (same root cause, different model arch / GPU), #57248, #57252, #56604, #56607. This
report does not duplicate their content; it adds the MI308X/gfx942 + Glm5Next TP4 reproduction and the
long-context status on v0.30.0.*
