### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description `Qwen2VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample()` raises an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError` when a video contains exactly one decoded frame. Through the OpenAI-compatible API, this becomes an HTTP 500 response. The sampler rounds the available frame count down to a multiple of the default `temporal_patch_size=2`. For a one-frame video, that calculation produces `n=0`, but the function then uses `n` as a divisor. This report is specifically about the unhandled division by zero. Regardless of whether a one-frame video should be padded or rejected, it should not reach an internal arithmetic error. ## Reproduction Start vLLM: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct \ --max-model-len 2048 \ --enforce-eager ``` Run the self-contained reproducer with [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32563254/repro_qwen2vl.py): ```bash python repro.py ``` Observed output: ```text {"case": "one_frame", "status": 500, "body": "{\"error\":{\"message\":\"division by zero\"...}}"} {"case": "two_frame_control", "status": 200, ...} ``` `repro.py` sends two otherwise identical requests using embedded H.264 MP4 fixtures. The one-frame input fails, while the two-frame control succeeds. The server traceback ends at the frame-index calculation: ```text ZeroDivisionError: division by zero ``` Full log is here: [server_qwen2vl.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32563277/server_qwen2vl.log) ## Expected behavior The sampler should either: - produce a valid nonzero frame count, for example by repeating the single frame to satisfy the temporal patch size; or - reject the input with a clear validation error. It should not return HTTP 500 because of an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError`. ## Root cause For the failing input: ```text total_frames_num = 1 temporal_patch_size = 2 ``` `compute_frames_index_to_sample()` first rounds `max_frames` down to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size`: ```python max_frames = ( floor(min(max_frames, total_frames_num) / temporal_patch_size) * temporal_patch_size ) ``` This makes `max_frames` zero. The subsequent clamp and alignment also produce `n=0`. The function does not validate that result before evaluating: ```python torch.arange(0, total_frames_num, total_frames_num / n) ``` The final expression therefore evaluates `1 / 0`. ## Related PRs [#33746](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33746) discussed frame-count alignment for preprocessed Qwen3-VL inputs with `do_sample_frames=False`. The discussion favored an informative validation error when the caller supplies an unaligned frame count. That PR was closed without being merged and does not handle the one-frame `video_url` sampling path in `Qwen2VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample()`. [#33956](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33956) addressed a related zero-frame condition in Qwen3-VL's generic short-duration sampler. It was also closed without being merged and does not change this Qwen2-VL backend. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

 ### Summary

  With `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` on the Realtime API (`/v1/realtime`), the time
  per engine step grows
  linearly with the age of the session, with no plateau at the model's 8192-token sliding window.
  On our machine the
  median step goes from 26 ms to 59 ms over 12 minutes of audio, and p99 crosses the 80 ms
  real-time budget (one token
  per 80 ms of audio) at about 8 minutes, after which a single stream can no longer keep up. GPU
  utilisation *falls*
  while this happens.

  A py-spy profile of the EngineCore late in a session puts **~55 % of wall time in the
  scheduler**, in:

  ```
  schedule (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py)
   └ NewRequestData.from_request (vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py)
      └ strip_covered_mm_data (vllm/multimodal/utils.py)      ← [maybe_strip(f) for f in
  mm_features]
         └ dataclasses.replace
  ```
 A realtime session appends one multimodal feature per 80 ms audio chunk (750 per minute) and is
  re-submitted to the
  worker on every step, so `strip_covered_mm_data` walks **all** accumulated features on
  **every** step and builds a
  fresh `dataclasses.replace` copy of each one already covered, without keeping the result. ~4 µs
  × 750 features ≈
  3 ms of pure Python per step per minute of session age, which matches the measured slope (2.99
  ms/min). Total work
  over a session is quadratic.

  `strip_covered_mm_data` came in with #52041. The decay reported in #39996 (0.19.x) suggests an
  older O(n) component
  existed as well; in 0.29.0 this function is the dominant one.

  ### Environment

  - vLLM 0.29.0 (PyPI wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu132, transformers 5.17.0, mistral-common 1.11.7,
  Python 3.12
  - RTX 3090, 4 vCPU of a Ryzen 7 2700 (Zen+). A slow core makes the effect large, but it is
  CPU-bound Python, so
    every host has it in proportion.

  ```
  VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 vllm serve <model dir> --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format
  mistral --load-format mistral \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}' --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4
  \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.60 --mm-processor-cache-gb 0
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
  ```
 ### Reproduction

  One realtime session, all audio sent at once, so the spacing of `transcription.delta` events is
  the per-step cost
  (a ~60-line script using only `websockets`; happy to share it). Nothing else attached to the
  server.

  | session age (min of audio) | 0–1 | 2–3 | 4–5 | 5–6 | 6–7 | 7–8 | 8–9 | 9–10 | 10–11 | 11–12 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | step p50 (ms) | 26.4 | 31.7 | 37.2 | 40.0 | 43.2 | 46.0 | 48.9 | 52.1 | 55.1 | 58.9 |
  | step p95 (ms) | 28.4 | 34.0 | 41.9 | 45.8 | 52.8 | 69.5 | 76.9 | 83.9 | 90.9 | 100.7 |
  | step p99 (ms) | 29.9 | 39.8 | 55.0 | 61.7 | 69.8 | 78.1 | 82.1 | 88.5 | 95.7 | 107.6 |

  - Linear fit of p50 from minute 2: 23.8 ms + 2.99 ms/min.
  - No change of slope at 8192 tokens (≈ 10.9 min), while GPU KV cache usage plateaus at ~31 %,
  so it is neither
    attention nor KV growth.
  - GPU utilisation went 66 % → 48 % → 41 % (by thirds of the run) while the EngineCore process
  held ~75 % of one core.
  - `usage.completion_tokens` equals the number of deltas in every run (8970/8970), so no output
  merging is involved.

  ### Profile (py-spy `--nonblocking`, 200 Hz, 20 s each, EngineCore; the SAME session early and
  late)

  Same process, same request, same sampling; the only variable is how much audio the session has
  accumulated. Shares
  are inclusive (the three scheduler rows are one call chain).

  | share of EngineCore samples | early (~1 min of audio) | late (~9 min of audio) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Scheduler.schedule()` | 16.9 % | **55.9 %** |
  | → `NewRequestData.from_request` | 16.9 % | 55.9 % |
  | → `strip_covered_mm_data` | 16.9 % | 55.9 % |
  | → → `dataclasses.replace` | 3.0 % | 11.4 % |
  | `execute_model` (the GPU forward) | 71.1 % | 37.8 % |
  | samples | 2391 | 2718 |

  The per-step time of that same session: p50 25 ms in its first minute, 50 ms in its ninth, 61
  ms in its thirteenth
  (p99 116 ms, beyond the 80 ms real-time budget). An independent earlier capture of a late
  session gave the same
  picture (`schedule()` 53 %, `execute_model` 41 %).

  At real-time pace (not burst), the same growth shows as +2.9 ms per minute of session age with
  one stream, +7.7 with
  two and +24 with four concurrent streams (7-minute sessions): concurrency multiplies how often
  the O(n) work runs.
 ### Suggested fix

  The set of covered features only ever grows, so the stripped form of a feature never changes
  once computed:

  - memoise it: keep the stripped copy next to the feature (or strip in place on the scheduler
  side for
    streaming-input requests, which never need the payload again), so a step touches only the
  *new* features; or
  - since features are ordered by `mm_position.offset`, remember the index of the first uncovered
  feature per request
    and only examine features from there on.

  Either makes the per-step cost O(new features) instead of O(all features).

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## 🐛 Describe the bug Multi-node TP=8 (2 nodes × 4 H200) serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash hangs indefinitely during engine startup, inside `ncclCommInitRank` graph/connection phase — before weight loading begins. The hang is deterministic and reproducible across 8+ restarts with different NCCL env configurations. Launch commands (per official multiprocessing multi-node docs) Head node: ```bash vllm serve /.cache/deepseek-v41-flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enable-chunked-prefill \ --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \ --master-addr \ --trust-remote-code --disable-custom-all-reduce ``` Worker node: same + `--headless --node-rank 1`. Observed behavior (NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE) Both nodes bootstrap fine (TCP bootstrap OK, `commId` shared, 2 nodes detected). Then, with IB enabled: Even local_ranks (0, 2 / 4, 6) complete `Init COMPLETE`, log their `Trees`, and establish cross-node GDRDMA channels: `Channel 00/0 : 0[0] -> 4[0] [send] via NET/IB/4/GDRDMA`, `Channel 01/0 : 2[2] -> 6[2] [send] via NET/IB/5/GDRDMA` Odd local_ranks (1, 3 / 5, 7) stop after `comm 0x... rank N nRanks 8 nNodes 2 localRanks 4 localRank N MNNVL 0` + one `Trees` line — no Channel lines, no Init COMPLETE, indefinitely The APIServer loops forever on: `Waiting for 1 local, 0 remote core engine proc(s) to start.` Weight loading (`Loading safetensors`) never starts All worker threads sleep (futex / socket / ib_uverbs_event_read) — no spinning, no watchdog timeout, no error With `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport): the same hang, but now all 8 ranks block at the `MNNVL 0` boundary with zero Channel lines. The even/odd localRank asymmetry (the most distinctive part) On both nodes, exactly cudaDev 0 and cudaDev 2 (even local_ranks) complete init and own the cross-node GDRDMA channel pairs (0↔4 on one rail, 2↔6 on another). Odd local_ranks never establish their cross-node connections (1↔5, 3↔7). The pattern is stable across restarts and independent of: Variable tested Result `NCCL_IB_QPS_PER_CONNECTION=8` vs default ❌ no change `NCCL_CROSS_NIC=0` vs `1` ❌ no change `NCCL_NCHANNELS_PER_NET_PEER=4` vs `8` vs unset ❌ no change (worse: all ranks block) `NCCL_MAX/MIN_NCHANNELS=16/8` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=SYS` + `NCCL_NET_GDR_READ=1` vs unset ❌ no change `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (Socket transport) ❌ all 8 ranks block (earlier) `--disable-custom-all-reduce` ❌ no change Worker `--headless` (was missing initially — fixed) ❌ no change to the even/odd pattern env propagation ✅ verified — every NCCL_* var logged as "set by environment" on both nodes Ruled out TCP connectivity: bootstrap + `distributed_init_method=tcp://...:29501` reachable from both nodes (tested live) `/dev/shm`, UID, permissions: identical on both nodes GPU-NIC topology: NV6 intra-node, NICs PIX-adjacent to their NUMA-local GPUs, GDR works (GDRDMA channels DO form for even ranks) Env propagation: NCCL TRACE confirms every var read on both nodes Same model + same topology works on SGLang (NCCL 2.28.3) with identical k8s/network setup — 4 rails, GDRDMA, TP8/EP8 Hypothesis The rank-pair channel assignment during `ncclCommInitRank` graph-connect deadlocks when ranks need to establish cross-node QP connections in an order that requires the odd-rank pair's initiator to be a rank that is itself still initializing. ## Additional context Related: #53894 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro 2-node hang — `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fixed their case, not ours), #46097 (MiniMax multi-node collective deadlock — "ranks not in the same collective instance" hypothesis), #57423 (FlashInfer autotune rank-0-only cache — ours hangs earlier, at comm init) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4 chat template puts `tools` into a synthetic leading system message instead of on the existing system message (diverges from the reference encoder)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collected with `python -m vllm.collect_env` in the serving conda environment on a CPU dev box (the template rendering reported below does not involve a GPU; the same environment serves on 4x B300 with TP=4). OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 CMake version : version 3.31.6 Libc version : glibc-2.39 PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 Python version : 3.12.14 (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-5.10.25-nvidia-gpu-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 Is CUDA available : False (CPU dev box; serving nodes: 4x NVIDIA B300, driver from the same image) [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.18 [pip3] nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7 [pip3] torch==2.13.0 [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0 [pip3] transformers==5.12.1 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 [pip3] tokenspeed-triton==3.8.10.post20260906 vLLM Version : 0.28.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled The same code path (vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py, apply_chat_template) is present in 0.24.1 builds we also run. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary With `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`, `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` renders the request `tools` by inserting a **new** system message at index 0 that carries only `tools`, even when the conversation already starts with a `system` message. The DeepSeek reference encoder (`encoding/encoding_dsv4.py` shipped in the model repo, and its `test_encoding_dsv4.py`) attaches `tools` to the existing system message instead. As a result every tool-calling request served by vLLM renders as ``` [effort prefix] ## Tools ...tool schema block... ...to invoke tool calls. <｜User｜>... ``` whereas the reference renders ``` [effort prefix] ## Tools ...tool schema block... <｜User｜>... ``` Same tokens, different order: the tools block moves in front of the system prompt, and the system prompt ends up glued to the last line of the tools block with a single `\n` and immediately followed by `<｜User｜>`. The rendering is otherwise identical (same length, same tokens), so this is easy to miss. ## Environment - vLLM 0.28.0 (`vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py`, `apply_chat_template`); the same code is present in 0.24.x. - Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (`--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). - Reference: `encoding/encoding_dsv4.py` and `encoding/test_encoding_dsv4.py` from the model repository. ## Reproduction ```python import copy, importlib.util from vllm.tokenizers.deepseek_v4 import DeepseekV4Tokenizer MODEL = "/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" # local checkout with encoding/encoding_dsv4.py spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("enc", f"{MODEL}/encoding/encoding_dsv4.py") enc = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(enc) tool = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "bash", "description": "Execute a bash command", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["command"]}}} messages = [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "List /tmp."}] tok = DeepseekV4Tokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL) served = tok.apply_chat_template(copy.deepcopy(messages), tools=[tool], enable_thinking=True, reasoning_effort="high", tokenize=False) ref_messages = copy.deepcopy(messages); ref_messages[0]["tools"] = [tool] # how the reference tests attach tools reference = enc.encode_messages(ref_messages, thinking_mode="thinking", reasoning_effort="high") print(len(served), len(reference)) # 1681 1681 print(served.find("## Tools"), served.find("You are a helpful assistant.")) # 499 1615 -> tools first print(reference.find("You are a helpful assistant."), reference.find("## Tools")) # 497 527 -> system first print(served == reference) # False ``` Served text around the system prompt: ``` ...defined tool name and parameter schemas to invoke tool calls.\nYou are a helpful assistant.<｜User｜>List /tmp. ``` Reference text around the system prompt: ``` ...no assumption is left unchecked.\n\nYou are a helpful assistant.\n\n## Tools\n\nYou have access to a set of tools... ``` ## Where it comes from `vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py` (0.28.0, lines 37-41; identical in 0.24): ```python conversation = kwargs.get("conversation", messages) messages = conversation.copy() if tools is not None and len(tools) > 0: messages.insert(0, {"role": "system"}) messages[0]["tools"] = tools ``` The encoder renders a system message as `content + "\n\n" + render_tools(tools)` and puts no separator between two consecutive system messages, so the synthetic tools-only message becomes `"" + "\n\n## Tools ..."` followed directly by the caller's system text. The reference encoder's README states: "Tools are defined on the `system` or `developer` message via the `tools` field (OpenAI-compatible format)", and `test_encoding_dsv4.py` does `messages[0]["tools"] = td["tools"]` on the existing system message; its golden output `tests/test_output_1.txt` starts with `<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>You are a helpful assistant.\n\n## Tools`. ## Why it matters - Fine-tuning pipelines that pack data with the reference encoder put the tools block after the system prompt. Serving the same model through vLLM shows it the tools block before the system prompt on 100% of tool requests, a systematic train/serve prefix mismatch that no length or token-count check catches. - The caller's system prompt loses its blank-line separation on both sides (`...invoke tool calls.\nSYSTEM<｜User｜>`), which is not a layout the reference ever produces. - Anyone comparing vLLM prompts against the reference encoder (or against another serving stack) gets a mismatch that looks like a template bug elsewhere. ## Proposed fix In `apply_chat_template`, attach `tools` to the first message when it is a `system` (or `developer`) message without its own `tools`, and only insert a synthetic system message when the conversation has no leading system/developer message: ```python if tools: if messages and messages[0].get("role") in ("system", "developer") and not messages[0].get("tools"): messages[0] = {**messages[0], "tools": tools} else: messages.insert(0, {"role": "system", "tools": tools}) ``` Both the bundled `deepseek_v4_encoding.py` and the reference encoder already support `tools` on system/developer messages, so no encoder change is needed. If backward compatibility with the current layout is a concern, a `chat_template_kwargs` switch would let users pick, but the reference layout should be the default. ## Related (separate, smaller) - The DeepSeek-V4 tool parser keeps the trailing `\n\n` of visible text before a `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` block in `message.content`, and the encoder appends its own `\n\n` when re-rendering that history turn, so text-then-call turns round-trip with four newlines instead of two. - Tool messages whose `content` is a list of text parts are joined with `\n` by `chat_utils` (content_format="string") but with `\n\n` by the reference encoder. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: CPU W4A16 Whisper fails: cpu_gemm_wna16 rejects 3-D encoder activations; packed k_proj bias is synthesized incorrectly

### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : version 3.28.3 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cpu Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.15 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Aug 10 2026, 13:05:01) [GCC 14.4.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 384 Vendor ID: AuthenticAMD Model name: AMD EPYC 9654 96-Core Processor Thread(s) per core: 2 Core(s) per socket: 96 Socket(s): 2 NUMA node(s): 2 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] numpy==2.4.6 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cpu [pip3] torchao==0.17.0+cpu [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0+cpu [pip3] torchvision==0.28.0+cpu [pip3] transformers==5.15.1 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 [pip3] compressed-tensors==0.17.0 [pip3] vllm==0.27.1+cpu [pip3] zentorch==2.13.0.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : Could not collect vLLM Version : 0.27.1 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: Could not collect ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary Loading a compressed-tensors **W4A16 Whisper** checkpoint on **CPU** (`CPUWNA16LinearKernel` / `cpu_gemm_wna16`) fails at runtime. The Whisper encoder feeds **3-D** activations `[B, T, D]` into quantized Linear layers, but the C++ kernel treats the input as 2-D `[M, K]` and reads `K` from `input.size(1)`. For encoder time `T=28` that is not a multiple of 32, so the kernel aborts. Separately, packed checkpoints expose `.k_proj.weight_packed` and omit `.k_proj.bias`. `_create_fake_bias_for_k_proj` only matches `.k_proj.weight` and sizes the fake bias from `weight.size(0)`, which is wrong for packed AWQ/Marlin layouts (`d_model` is required). After the crash is avoided, that produces garbage transcripts (WER 100 on LibriSpeech in our runs). ### Repro Model: https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w4a16 ```python from vllm import LLM from vllm.assets.audio import AudioAsset llm = LLM( model="RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w4a16", device="cpu", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=448, enforce_eager=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1}, ) prompt = "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>" audio, sr = AudioAsset("mary_had_lamb").audio_and_sample_rate outputs = llm.generate( { "prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio, sr)}, } ) print(outputs[0].outputs[0].text) ``` ### Expected The request completes. BF16 openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo on the same CPU path is around 2.x WER on LibriSpeech; W4A16 should be in the same ballpark, not crash. ### Actual ```RuntimeError: Check failed: a_k_size % 32 == 0 (28 vs. 0)``` ### Root cause - 3-D activations. ops.cpu_gemm_wna16 does not flatten leading dims the way int4_scaled_mm_cpu already does (x.reshape(-1, x_shape[-1]), then reshape the output back). Whisper encoder Linear layers therefore pass [B, T, D] straight into the C++ op. - Packed k_proj bias. WhisperForConditionalGeneration.load_weights only walks .k_proj.weight. Compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoints use .k_proj.weight_packed and have no real .k_proj.bias. The fused qkv_proj/kv_proj path still needs a d_model-sized zeros bias; using packed dim0 is wrong. ### Suggested fix (native vLLM) - Flatten/reshape in cpu_gemm_wna16 to match int4_scaled_mm_cpu. - In _create_fake_bias_for_k_proj, also match .k_proj.weight_packed, size the fake bias from config.d_model, and do not override a real .k_proj.bias. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: An Anthropic messages test is not compatible with Anthropic SDK 1.x
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py vllm 0.28.0, 0.29.0 ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py::test_anthropic_streaming_cache_usage` passes `temperature=0.0` as a keyword argument to `AsyncMessages.create()`. That works on Anthropic Python SDK 0.x, but breaks on 1.x: ```text TypeError: AsyncMessages.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'temperature' ``` This is a client-side SDK change, not a vLLM serving bug. Anthropic SDK 1.0 removed temperature / top_p / top_k from messages.create(), messages.stream(), and messages.parse(). Official migration notes: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/MIGRATION.md#removed-deprecated-request-parameters Those sampling fields are gone from the method signature, not from the HTTP API. For older models that still honor them (including this test's served name claude-3-7-sonnet-latest), the documented replacement is extra_body: ```python # before client.messages.create(..., temperature=0.2) # after client.messages.create(..., extra_body={"temperature": 0.2}) ``` extra_body is merged into the JSON body by the SDK. vLLM already declares temperature on AnthropicMessagesRequest, so the server keeps parsing it as a normal field. No serving-side extra_body handling is required. vLLM depends on anthropic >= 0.71.0 (requirements/common.txt) with no <1 cap, so CI / downstream installs can resolve either 0.x or 1.x. extra_body exists on both generations, so this keeps the test working for both, but temperature= would get TypeError on 1.x. This test only asserts streaming prefix-cache usage (cache_read / cache_creation on message_delta). It does not inspect generated text, so it is indifferent to greedy vs default sampling. Dropping temperature entirely would also fix the TypeError This PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57780 keeps greedy via extra_body to stay closest to the original request. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8 excludes SM89 (Ada Lovelace) despite native FP8 tensor core support
body:
### Your current environment

**Environment:**
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (SM 8.9)
- vLLM: 0.29.0
- CUDA: 13.4
- Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (block-quantized FP8, 128×128 blocks)

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Description:**
cutlass_block_fp8_supported() returns False on Ada Lovelace (SM89), causing block-quantized FP8 checkpoints to fall through the kernel priority list in _POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS all the way to MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel — bypassing CUTLASS entirely, even though:

Non-block FP8 CUTLASS is supported on this card: cutlass_fp8_supported() == True
Ada Lovelace has native FP8 tensor core hardware, and vLLM's own docs state FP8 W8A8 is officially supported on "Hopper and Ada Lovelace" (https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/quantization/fp8/)

Bisecting ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8() directly shows a hard floor at SM90:
- 80 -> False
- 86 -> False
- 89 -> False
- 90 -> True
- 100 -> True

**Question:** Is this a genuine CUTLASS-library-level limitation (e.g. block-scaled grouped GEMM requiring Hopper-specific TMA multicast at the collective-builder level, similar to the SM_120/SM_121 CUTLASS MoE gap in #43507), or is SM89 support for block-scaled CUTLASS GEMM simply not yet wired up in vLLM's compiled extension?

If it's the latter, this is a meaningful gap for anyone running block-quantized FP8 checkpoints (increasingly common — DeepSeek-style 128×128 block scales) on Ada workstation cards (RTX 6000 Ada, L40S, RTX 4090), since it silently falls back to Marlin's weight-only dequant path rather than using the card's native FP8 compute.

**Repro:**
```
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
for cap in [80, 86, 89, 90, 100]:
    print(cap, ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8(cap))
```

This new feature allows per-request opt-out even when the server operator configured `--watermark-config`. A user can send `"watermarking": false` in a request, and the server disables the watermark for that request without any warning or log. This appears to be a gap in the initial implementation of the v0.30.0 watermarking feature. RFC #53916 states watermarking "is a modification of the sampling process, which cannot be modified by downstream consumers." The current implementation contradicts this — any API caller can modify the watermark behavior per-request. **Root cause:** `gpu_sampler.py` L41 reads `sampling_params.watermarking` directly. No code path checks the server's `--watermark-config` to override the per-request value. ```python # v1/watermarking/gpu_sampler.py:41 def add_request(self, req_idx, sampling_params): self.watermarking.np[req_idx] = sampling_params.watermarking # ← uses per-request value, no server-level enforcement ``` The `watermarking` field is exposed on all API endpoints: - `ChatCompletionRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L270) - `CompletionRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L78) - `ResponsesRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L217) **Steps to reproduce:** ```bash # Start server with watermark enforced python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model facebook/opt-125m \ --max-model-len 512 \ --watermark-config '{"key": 12345}' \ --port 8000 ``` ```python import requests MODEL = "facebook/opt-125m" URL = "http://localhost:8000" r1 = requests.post(URL + "/v1/completions", json={ "model": MODEL, "prompt": "Once upon a time", "max_tokens": 50, "temperature": 0.7, "seed": 42, "watermarking": True }) r2 = requests.post(URL + "/v1/completions", json={ "model": MODEL, "prompt": "Once upon a time", "max_tokens": 50, "temperature": 0.7, "seed": 42, "watermarking": False }) t1 = r1.json()["choices"][0]["text"] t2 = r2.json()["choices"][0]["text"] print(f"watermarking=True: {t1[:100]!r}") print(f"watermarking=False: {t2[:100]!r}") ``` ``` watermarking=True: ' for a great nation, it was the world’s greatest country, with a population of approximately 4 milli' watermarking=False: ', I fell in love with a girl.\nBut when I came to the realization that I had no idea what kind of a g' ``` The outputs differ because watermarking changes the sampling distribution (Gumbel-max). The server accepted `watermarking=False` (HTTP 200) without error, even though `--watermark-config` was set. **Expected behavior:** When `--watermark-config` is active, one of: 1. Ignore the per-request `watermarking` field and always watermark 2. Reject `watermarking=False` with HTTP 400 3. Add a `--watermark-enforce` flag that prevents per-request opt-out **Why this matters:** The v0.30.0 watermarking feature was built for regulatory compliance (EU AI Act Article 50(2), California SB 942 — see RFC #53916). Without server-level enforcement, operators who deploy `--watermark-config` for compliance cannot guarantee all outputs are watermarked. Any API user can silently bypass the policy. The server logs no warning when watermarking is disabled per-request. Since this feature just shipped in v0.30.0, fixing the enforcement gap now avoids breaking changes later. Related: RFC #53916, PR #54053, PR #56338 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: vLLM does not ignore temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty for DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, unlike the official DeepSeek API
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary According to the official DeepSeek API documentation, the DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode does not support the temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty parameters. For backward compatibility, passing these parameters does not raise an error, but they have no effect. However, vLLM does not behave consistently with the DeepSeek API. When serving DeepSeek V4 series models in thinking mode, these parameters are still applied to sampling instead of being ignored. Expected behavior For DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, vLLM should accept temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty without raising an error, but silently ignore them — matching the official DeepSeek API behavior. Actual behavior These parameters are still honored by the sampler, which can lead to different (and unexpected) outputs compared to the official API. Impact Users migrating from the official DeepSeek API to vLLM may get inconsistent results. Clients that rely on the documented "accepted but ignored" behavior may unintentionally change model output. Reproducibility across the official API and vLLM is broken for these models. Steps to reproduce Serve a DeepSeek V4 series model in thinking mode with vLLM. Send a request with different values of temperature (or presence_penalty / frequency_penalty). Observe that the output changes, whereas the official DeepSeek API would produce identical sampling behavior regardless of these values. Suggested fix Detect DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode and skip applying temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty in the sampling path, while still accepting them in the request schema for compatibility. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_vllm ```
### The bug For Mistral models served with `--tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice`, every chat completion request — including plain-text ones with `tool_choice="none"` and no `tools`— triggers a full rebuild of `MistralToolParser` → `ParserEngine` → `StreamingParserEngine`, which compiles `regex` patterns over the tokenizer's entire special-token vocabulary (`_build_drop_info` in `vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py`). This runs **synchronously on the main asyncio event loop**, not inside the renderer's `ThreadPoolExecutor` (unlike tokenization itself, which is offloaded via `make_async`). Under concurrent load this becomes a bottleneck: the event loop can't advance anything else while blocked on it, so requests back up long before ever reaching the scheduler. Model: `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603`, served with `--tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral --tensor-parallel-size 2` on 2×H200. Confirmed present, unchanged, in both v0.29.0 and v0.30.0 (checked directly against source). Root cause is `online_renderer.py`'s `preprocess_chat`: ```python is_mistral_grammar_eligible = ( tool_parser is not None and is_mistral_tool_parser(tool_parser) and is_mistral_tokenizer(tokenizer) and tokenizer.supports_grammar ) should_adjust_request = ( parser.reasoning_parser_cls is not None or tool_choice != "none" or is_mistral_grammar_eligible # forces adjust_request unconditionally for Mistral ) ``` The comment above it explains this is intentional ("so that the grammar factory can prevent special-token leakage"), but the expensive part (`_build_drop_info`) depends only on the fixed tokenizer vocabulary/parser config — not on per-request `tools` or content — so it looks memoizable rather than needing reconstruction on every request. **Reproduction:** 1. Serve a Mistral model: `vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603 --tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral --tensor-parallel-size 2 ...` 2. Send concurrent `tool_choice="none"` requests (no `tools`), e.g. `vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 200 --request-rate 16`. 3. Observe TTFT balloon and engine `Running` (from the periodic `Engine 000: ...` log line) stay near-flat despite high offered load, while GPU/KV-cache usage stays near-idle. 4. Remove `--tool-call-parser`/`--enable-auto-tool-choice`/`--reasoning-parser` and rerun — throughput and TTFT return to normal. **Results observed vs. expected**, same benchmark (200 requests, request-rate=16, random 512-token prompts): | | With the three flags | Without (diagnostic) | |---|---|---| | Mean TTFT | 39,013 ms | 101 ms | | Output throughput | 604 tok/s | 3,213 tok/s | | Engine `Running` (concurrent) | capped ~3-6 | 45-84 | | GPU KV cache usage | ~0.1% | ~1.8% | Expected: `Running` should scale with offered load regardless of these flags being set, the same way it does without them. Confirmed via `py-spy dump --pid ` mid-load that the `MainThread` (not a worker thread) is caught inside this exact construction path, with locals directly showing `tool_choice: "none"`, `is_mistral_grammar_eligible: True`, `should_adjust_request: True` for a request with no tools: ``` _create_chat_completion (vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py:275) render_chat_request (serving.py:240) render_chat (vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py:192) preprocess_chat (online_renderer.py:718) [tool_choice: "none", is_mistral_grammar_eligible: True, should_adjust_request: True] MistralToolParser.__init__ (vllm/parser/engine/adapters.py:167) MistralParser.__init__ (vllm/parser/mistral.py:279) ParserEngine.__init__ (vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py:107) StreamingParserEngine.__init__ (vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py:133) _build_drop_info (streaming_parser_engine.py:73) regex.compile(...) # compiling patterns over hundreds of special tokens, per request ``` **Suggested fix:** cache `_build_drop_info`'s result (or the constructed `StreamingParserEngine`'s tokenizer-dependent state) keyed on tokenizer identity + parser config, separate from the genuinely per-request-stateful parts of the streaming parser — so `adjust_request` doesn't redo vocabulary-wide regex compilation on every request. - [x] Searched existing issues (closest match found: #57571, which covers a related but distinct cost — output-side streaming derender replay — not this input-side per-request construction) and checked the docs chatbot. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

### 🐛 Describe the bug A server started with `--api-key` refuses unauthenticated requests on `/v1/*`, as documented. The same requests are **served** when posted to `/invocations`, which dispatches to the same handlers and is not covered by the guard. Measured with `--api-key SECRET-KEY-123` and **no** `Authorization` header: | request | 0.27.1 | 0.29.0 | |---|---|---| | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | 401 | 401 | | `POST /v1/completions` | 401 | 401 | | **`POST /invocations`** (chat body) | **200, full completion** | **200, full completion** | | **`POST /invocations`** (completions body) | **200, full completion** | **200, full completion** | No special flags: a plain `vllm serve --api-key ` on one GPU. **Related to but distinct from CVE-2026-22778. That CVE was the video-processing RCE reachable via this route (fixed in 0.14.1).** _The api-key bypass property of /invocations itself was not the subject of that fix and still holds on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0; the SageMaker router is mounted unconditionally (no SageMaker flag, no dev-mode gate), so every --api-key operator gets an unauthenticated inference path they did not opt into._ **Cause** The guard is a path-prefix test (0.27.1 `entrypoints/serve/utils/server_utils.py:42`, 0.29.0 `entrypoints/serve/middleware/authenticate.py:11`): ```python GUARDED_PREFIX = ("/v1", "/v2", "/inference", "/cohere") ... if url_path.startswith(GUARDED_PREFIX) and not self.verify_token(headers): return JSONResponse(content={"error": "Unauthorized"}, status_code=401) ``` `/invocations` is mounted at the root, and **unconditionally** — there is no SageMaker flag and no dev-mode gate: ```python register_sagemaker_api_router(app, supported_tasks, model_config) # api_server.py ``` So on every vLLM deployment the SageMaker entrypoint is present, it forwards a request body to the ordinary chat/completions handlers, and the prefix test never sees it. ### Reproduction Use this: [repro_api_key_bypass.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/99df19c52a4383e5e328be02baaceddc#file-repro_api_key_bypass-py) `python3 repro_api_key_bypass.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model --api-key ` Start any model with `--api-key `. The script sends the *same* body to `/v1/chat/completions` and to `/invocations` with no credentials and prints both statuses; it exits non-zero when the guarded route refuses and the unguarded one serves. An operator who sets `--api-key` has exactly one authentication mechanism, and it does not hold. Anyone who can reach the port gets unrestricted inference: * compute is consumed without authorisation; * anything the deployment attaches server-side — a system prompt, a chat template's instructions, retrieved context, tools — is reachable by an unauthenticated caller; * rate limiting or accounting keyed on the API key does not see this traffic at all. The vLLM security guide's firewall advice is to "block all incoming connections except to the TCP port the API server is [on]", i.e. that port is the intended exposed surface, which is where this route lives. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description For a BERT-style cross encoder, `padding="max_length"` pads `input_ids` correctly but assigns every padding token the last real token's `token_type_id`. In a query/document pair that value is normally 1, so padding is incorrectly treated as part of the document segment instead of using the tokenizer's `pad_token_type_id` of 0. BERT consumes token-type embeddings, so accepted `/score` and `/rerank` requests can run on different segment IDs from the tokenizer's intended input. This can change scores, rank order, and threshold decisions. ## Reproduction Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32512913/repro_cross_encoder.py), run: ```bash python repro.py 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The reproducer uses vLLM's released rerank request, tokenization parameters, post-tokenization logic, and worker-side token-type compression. An in-memory BERT tokenizer provides the Transformers reference result, so no model download or GPU is required. The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. ## Actual result Both paths produce the same padded input IDs: ```text [2, 5, 3, 6, 3, 0, 0, 0] ``` vLLM produces: ```text token_type_ids = [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1] ``` ## Expected result Transformers uses the tokenizer's padding token type: ```text token_type_ids = [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0] ``` Full log is here: [reproducer_cross_encoder.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32512950/reproducer_cross_encoder.log). ## Root cause `_apply_post_tokenization_to_token_type_ids()` pads with `token_type_ids[-1]` instead of `tokenizer.pad_token_type_id`. The following compression step stores only one zero-to-one boundary. That representation can encode `0*1*`, but not the correct right-padded shape `0*1*0*`, so the worker also reconstructs all padded positions as type 1. ## Related PR [PR #47772](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47772) fixes a different boundary problem after truncation. It does not change max-length padding or the single-boundary representation, so this case remains reproducible in vLLM 0.29.0. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

This happens with ordinary CJK text and emoji ZWJ sequences. The request succeeds with HTTP 200, so this is not an unsupported configuration or a validation error. Callers cannot reliably enforce the documented per-query or per-document token budgets for multilingual input. Extra tokens consume context and compute and can change scores or downstream overlength behavior. ## Reproduction Start the server: ```bash MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \ --served-model-name qwen3-embed \ --runner pooling \ --convert embed \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8036 \ --max-model-len 512 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log ``` In another terminal, use the script [repro_unicode.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32511832/repro_unicode.py): ```bash python repro.py --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. ## Actual result | Limited input | Text | Limit | Character slice | Retokenized count | Prompt tokens | Expected upper bound | |---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | document | `中 文 测试` | 3 | `中 文 测` | 4 | 8 | 7 | | document | `😵‍💫x` | 2 | `😵‍` | 3 | 7 | 6 | | document control | `one two three four` | 3 | `one two three` | 3 | 7 | 7 | | query | `中 文 测试` | 3 | `中 文 测` | 4 | 8 | 7 | | query control | `one two three four` | 3 | `one two three` | 3 | 7 | 7 | For the CJK case, the original document has four tokens. After requesting a limit of three, vLLM still reports the same eight prompt tokens as the unlimited request. The same result occurs when that text is the query and the request uses `max_tokens_per_query=3`. Full log is here: [server_unicode.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32511885/server_unicode.log). ## Expected result After `max_tokens_per_doc=N` is applied, the document passed to the model should contain at most `N` content tokens. The same invariant should hold for `max_tokens_per_query`. ## Root cause `truncate_text_to_tokens()` tokenizes the full string, takes the end character offset of token `N`, and returns `text[:char_end]`. The scoring path then tokenizes that character slice again. Token offsets are not guaranteed to form safe retokenization boundaries. Multiple byte-fallback tokens can share or overlap a character span, and BPE merges can change at the new end of the string. The returned substring can therefore tokenize to more than `N` tokens. ## Related issues [#38651](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38651) introduced the token-limit feature and specified tokenizing each document, truncating the token list to `max_tokens_per_doc`, and applying that truncation before prompt or template assembly. This report is not a duplicate of that RFC. It concerns an implementation defect where character slicing followed by retokenization violates the token-list invariant. The same helper is used for `max_tokens_per_query`, and the reproducer demonstrates both fields directly. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description The `hunyuan_a13b` reasoning parser returns different content for streaming and non-streaming Chat Completions when given the same well-formed model output: ```text ink answer ``` Non-streaming returns `reasoning="ink"` and `content="answer"`. Streaming returns the same reasoning but aggregates to `content="answer\n"`, exposing Hunyuan's closing framing marker to the client. Both requests succeed with HTTP 200 and contain exactly the same generated token IDs. Streaming clients receive model protocol syntax in the user-visible answer, while non-streaming clients receive clean content for the same tokens. Applications that render, persist, compare, or parse streamed answers can therefore expose the marker or produce mode-dependent results. ## Reproduction The Hunyuan-A13B checkpoint is over 150 GiB and is not needed to reproduce a frontend parsing bug. The included debug logits processor forces the exact token sequence documented by `HunyuanA13BReasoningParser`, while the official Hunyuan tokenizer supplies the corresponding text. The requests still go through a real vLLM engine, HTTP server, Chat Completions serving code, and the production `hunyuan_a13b` parser. Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32508930/repro_hunyuan.py), first download only the Hunyuan tokenizer files: ```bash python repro.py --prepare-tokenizer ./hunyuan_tokenizer ``` Start vLLM 0.29.0: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \ VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --tokenizer ./hunyuan_tokenizer \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --reasoning-parser hunyuan_a13b \ --logits-processors repro:HunyuanTraceLogitsProcessor \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8033 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \ --max-model-len 256 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log ``` Run the client: ```bash python repro.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8033 \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script sends the same forced output once with `stream=false` and once with `stream=true, stream_interval=1`. It exits with status 1 when the marker leak is reproduced. ## Actual result The server returns the following identical token sequence for both requests: ```text [14023, 771, 397, 771, 198, 524, 27963, 397, 27, 9399, 397, 9399, 198, 524, 9399, 29] ``` The Hunyuan tokenizer decodes it as: ```text ink answer ``` The parsed responses differ: | Mode | HTTP | `reasoning` | Aggregated `content` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Non-streaming | 200 | `"ink"` | `"answer"` | | Streaming | 200 | `"ink"` | `"answer\n"` | The complete SSE chunks and non-streaming response are in [reproducer_hunyuan.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32508958/reproducer_hunyuan.log). The server startup and both successful requests are in [server_hunyuan.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32508963/server_hunyuan.log). ## Expected result Streaming and non-streaming parsing of the same generated token sequence should agree: ```text reasoning = "ink" content = "answer" ``` The closing `\n` frame should be consumed by the parser and must not appear in user-visible content. ## Root cause The Hunyuan streaming parser is a three-state envelope parser: `idle -> think -> response -> idle`. It is designed to keep receiving tokens in the `response` state until it recognizes [`response_end_ids`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/reasoning/hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py#L59-L64) and suppresses the closing marker. The outer `DelegatingParser` interprets the intermediate `response` state as a permanent end of reasoning: 1. After parsing `\n\n\n`, the Hunyuan parser changes its state to `response` and starts waiting for `\n` ([state transitions](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/reasoning/hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py#L177-L203)). 2. Its [`is_reasoning_end()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/reasoning/hunyuan_a13b_reasoning_parser.py#L81-L82) returns `True` in that state. 3. `DelegatingParser.parse_delta()` therefore sets [`state.reasoning_ended = True`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py#L835-L857). 4. With no tool parser configured, later deltas take the outer [content passthrough branch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py#L917-L927) and are emitted verbatim. The inner Hunyuan state machine never receives the later `response_end_ids`, so it cannot consume `\n`. The non-streaming regex sees the complete frame and removes the marker correctly. ## Related issues The unified `DelegatingParser.parse_delta()` flow was introduced by [#39446](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39446). The bug is an interface mismatch between that outer binary reasoning/content handoff and Hunyuan's three-state envelope parser. [#52658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52658) is an open Rust frontend port of the Hunyuan A13B parser. Its implementation suppresses the closing answer marker, but it does not modify or fix the Python frontend path reproduced here. [#54499](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54499) fixes a separate `IndexError` when a partial Hunyuan response-start sequence diverges. It does not change the response-state handoff or closing-marker handling. The same Python parser behavior remains on the current `main` branch at the time of writing. Searches for Hunyuan with ``, `response_end_ids`, and streaming found no dedicated issue or fix for this leak. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: Partial cache events can reference unreported parent hashes
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : macOS 26.3.2 (arm64) GCC version : Could not collect Clang version : 21.0.0 (clang-2100.0.123.102) CMake version : version 4.3.2 Libc version : N/A ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : None ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.14.7 (v3.14.7:823f0323ee6, Aug 5 2026, 07:07:01) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : macOS-26.3.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O ============================== CPU Info ============================== Apple M5 Pro ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] numpy==2.4.6 [pip3] pyzmq==27.2.0 [pip3] torch==2.11.0 [pip3] torchaudio==2.11.0 [pip3] torchcodec==0.16.0 [pip3] torchvision==0.26.0 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [conda] Could not collect ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : Could not collect vLLM Version : 0.25.1.dev26+g08dfd6861 (git sha: 08dfd6861) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: Could not collect ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Hi, I believe I found a case where a BlockStored event for a partial block references a parent_block_hash that was never emitted. This prevents an external consumer from reconstructing the prefix chain. Consider a request having 1,800 tokens (so 1,536 + 128 + 128 + 8), and its tokens to be stored in a contiguous array `tokens`, and a Hashing function `H` (to simplify notation): The relevant chain is: `H1536 -> H1664 -> H1792` The problem is, we don’t emit a KV cache event for `H1664`. That is, an event is emitted only for the full block `H1536`, and for the final partial block hash `H1792`. However, we never received `H1664`, and we cannot decipher H1792’s position in the prefix chain without `H1664`. Our KV cache chain is thus irremediably broken. Code for full reproduction: ```python import json from collections.abc import Callable import vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils as kv_cache_utils from vllm.distributed.kv_events import BlockStored from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256 from vllm.v1.core.block_pool import BlockPool from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import ( BlockHash, get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash, ) from vllm.v1.request import Request def make_request( request_id: str, prompt_token_ids: list[int], hash_block_size: int, hash_fn: Callable, ) -> Request: sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=17) sampling_params.update_from_generation_config({}, eos_token_id=100) return Request( request_id=request_id, prompt_token_ids=prompt_token_ids, sampling_params=sampling_params, pooling_params=None, block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(hash_block_size, hash_fn), ) def boundary_hash( request: Request, hash_block_size: int, num_tokens: int, ) -> BlockHash: return request.block_hashes[num_tokens // hash_block_size - 1] init_none_hash(sha256) hash_block_size = 128 block_size = 1536 partial_boundary = 1792 token_ids = list(range(1800)) request = make_request( "partial-parent-reproducer", token_ids, hash_block_size, sha256, ) pool = BlockPool( num_gpu_blocks=3, enable_caching=True, hash_block_size=hash_block_size, enable_kv_cache_events=True, ) blocks = pool.get_new_blocks(2) pool.cache_full_blocks( request=request, blocks=blocks, num_cached_blocks=0, num_full_blocks=1, block_size=block_size, kv_cache_group_id=0, ) pool.cache_partial_block( request=request, block=blocks[1], num_tokens=partial_boundary, kv_cache_group_id=0, block_size=block_size, ) events = [ event for event in pool.take_events() if isinstance(event, BlockStored) ] def external_hash(num_tokens: int): return kv_cache_utils.maybe_convert_block_hash( boundary_hash(request, hash_block_size, num_tokens) ) h1536 = external_hash(1536) h1664 = external_hash(1664) h1792 = external_hash(1792) names = { h1536: "H1536", h1664: "H1664", h1792: "H1792", None: None, } for event in events: print( json.dumps( { "block_hashes": [ names.get(block_hash, repr(block_hash)) for block_hash in event.block_hashes ], "parent_block_hash": names.get( event.parent_block_hash, repr(event.parent_block_hash), ), "token_range": [ event.token_ids[0], event.token_ids[-1] + 1, ], "token_count": len(event.token_ids), "block_size": event.block_size, }, separators=(",", ":"), ) ) assert events[0].block_hashes == [h1536] assert events[0].parent_block_hash is None assert events[1].block_hashes == [h1792] assert events[1].parent_block_hash == h1664 assert events[1].token_ids == token_ids[1664:1792] emitted_hashes = { block_hash for event in events for block_hash in event.block_hashes } skipped_context_reconstructs_parent = ( getattr(events[1], "skipped_parent_block_hash", None) == h1536 and getattr(events[1], "skipped_token_ids", None) == token_ids[1536:1664] ) assert h1664 in emitted_hashes or skipped_context_reconstructs_parent, ( "H1792 references H1664, but H1664 was not emitted and the event " "contains no skipped ancestry from H1536" ) ``` Which produces: ``` {"block_hashes":["H1536"],"parent_block_hash":null,"token_range":[0,1536],"token_count":1536,"block_size":1536} {"block_hashes":["H1792"],"parent_block_hash":"H1664","token_range":[1664,1792],"token_count":128,"block_size":128} ``` i.e., we get `H1792`, but its parent `H1664` was never emitted. PR #44488 provides a hint on fixing the issue, by introducing the `skipped_parent_block_hash` param in `BlockStored` events. I have an initial attempt [here](https://github.com/Lucas-Fernandes-Martins/vllm/compare/efc443a645f4986bc2f458d74ebf841e158a4813...1b2e19ed69) to use `skipped_parent_block_hash` to solve the issue, adding those fields to `cache_partial_block` by producing instead: ```json { "block_hashes": ["H1536"], "parent_block_hash": null, "token_ids": "tokens[0:1536]", "block_size": 1536 } { "block_hashes": ["H1792"], "parent_block_hash": "H1664", "token_ids": "tokens[1664:1792]", "block_size": 128, "skipped_parent_block_hash": "H1536", "skipped_token_ids": "tokens[1536:1664]", "skipped_extra_keys": [null] } ``` Thank you very much and let me know if I can tackle this issue! ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Only a correctness issue, doesn't affect performance, might just confuse people. `POST /v1/responses/{id}/cancel` refuses every response that is not `queued` or `in_progress` with one message, and that message names the wrong reason. A response created with `background: true` is asynchronous by construction, yet once it reaches a terminal state the API says it is synchronous: | response | `background` | status when cancelled | result | |---|---|---|---| | finished on its own | **true** | `completed` | 400 `"Cannot cancel a synchronous response."` | | cancelled a moment earlier (that cancel returned 200 and `status: "cancelled"`) | **true** | `cancelled` | 400 `"Cannot cancel a synchronous response."` | | control: an ordinary stored response | false | `incomplete` | 400 `"Cannot cancel a synchronous response."` — here the message is true | The second row is the funniest: the same endpoint cancelled that response successfully one call earlier, so the server itself already treated it as cancellable. ### Reproduction `repro_responses_cancel_wrong_reason.py` (attached; stdlib only) runs the three cases above and exits 1 when a `background: true` response is refused as synchronous. It exits 2 if the store is not enabled, so a misconfigured server cannot look like this bug. ### For whomever wanting to fix, this likely comes from `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py`, `cancel_responses`, one branch serves every non-cancellable state: ```python prev_status = response.status if prev_status not in ("queued", "in_progress"): return self.create_error_response( err_type="invalid_request_error", message="Cannot cancel a synchronous response.", param="response_id", ) ``` `completed`, `failed`, `incomplete` and `cancelled` all land there, and so does the genuinely synchronous case. The message was written for the last one and inherited by the rest. ### Reproducer inlined
repro_responses_cancel_wrong_reason.py — standard library only; save and run against a running server ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """vLLM: cancelling a BACKGROUND /v1/responses that already reached a terminal state is refused with "Cannot cancel a synchronous response." Self-contained (stdlib only). Needs the Responses store: VLLM_ENABLE_RESPONSES_API_STORE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 python3 repro_responses_cancel_wrong_reason.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Three cancels are attempted. Two of them are on responses created with `background: true` -- one that finished on its own and one that was successfully cancelled a moment earlier -- and both are told they are synchronous. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import json import sys import time import urllib.error import urllib.request def call(base, method, path, body=None, timeout=180): req = urllib.request.Request(base.rstrip("/") + path, method=method, data=(json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None), headers={"content-type": "application/json"}) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r: return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode() or "{}") except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: raw = e.read().decode() try: return e.code, json.loads(raw) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return e.code, {"raw": raw[:300]} def wait_terminal(base, rid, limit=60): for _ in range(limit): time.sleep(0.5) sc, g = call(base, "GET", f"/v1/responses/{rid}") if sc != 200: return f"retrieve {sc}" if g.get("status") in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled", "incomplete"): return g["status"] return "timeout" def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") ap.add_argument("--model", required=True) a = ap.parse_args() sc, probe = call(a.base_url, "POST", "/v1/responses", {"model": a.model, "input": "hi", "max_output_tokens": 8, "store": True}) if sc != 200 or not probe.get("id"): print(f"the Responses store is not enabled here (create -> {sc}); " "start the server with VLLM_ENABLE_RESPONSES_API_STORE=1") return 2 rows, bad = [], 0 # 1. a background response that finished on its own sc, r = call(a.base_url, "POST", "/v1/responses", {"model": a.model, "input": "Say OK.", "max_output_tokens": 400, "background": True, "store": True}) st = wait_terminal(a.base_url, r["id"]) sc_c, c = call(a.base_url, "POST", f"/v1/responses/{r['id']}/cancel") rows.append(("background, finished on its own", True, st, sc_c, (c.get("error") or {}).get("message"))) # 2. a background response cancelled, then cancelled again sc, r2 = call(a.base_url, "POST", "/v1/responses", {"model": a.model, "input": "Write a long essay.", "max_output_tokens": 500, "background": True, "store": True}) time.sleep(0.4) sc_first, first = call(a.base_url, "POST", f"/v1/responses/{r2['id']}/cancel") sc_c2, c2 = call(a.base_url, "POST", f"/v1/responses/{r2['id']}/cancel") rows.append((f"background, already cancelled (first cancel {sc_first} -> {first.get('status')!r})", True, "cancelled", sc_c2, (c2.get("error") or {}).get("message"))) # 3. the control: a genuinely synchronous response sc_c3, c3 = call(a.base_url, "POST", f"/v1/responses/{probe['id']}/cancel") rows.append(("synchronous (the message is true here)", False, probe.get("status"), sc_c3, (c3.get("error") or {}).get("message"))) for label, is_background, status, code, msg in rows: flag = "" if is_background and msg and "synchronous" in msg: flag = " <-- this response is NOT synchronous" bad += 1 print(f" {label:52s} status={str(status):11s} cancel -> {code} {str(msg)[:44]!r}{flag}") print() if bad: print(f"REPRODUCED: {bad} background response(s) refused with \"Cannot cancel a synchronous " "response.\" The refusal is about reaching a terminal state, not about being synchronous.") return 1 print("not reproduced") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```

title: [Bug]: `/v1/responses` output items are always `status: "completed"`, even inside an incomplete response
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Correctness issue, env shouldn't matter, let me know if you need one ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug A Responses API request cut off by `max_output_tokens` reports itself as incomplete at the top level and as **completed** in the very item that was cut: ```json { "status": "incomplete", "incomplete_details": {"reason": "max_output_tokens"}, "output": [{"type": "message", "status": "completed", ...}], "usage": {"output_tokens": 16} } ``` The control, the same request with a budget it can meet, returns `"status": "completed"` with the same `"completed"` item, so the item status carries no information at all: it is the same string either way. Both item types behave this way; on a server with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, `max_output_tokens: 32` with `tool_choice: "required"` gives: ```json {"status": "incomplete", "incomplete_details": {"reason": "max_output_tokens"}, "output": [{"type": "function_call", "status": "completed", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Paris\", \"unit\": \"celsius\", \"days\": 1}"}]} ``` (in that run the arguments happened to be complete; the point is the status, which is the same literal for a cut response as for a finished one). ### Reproduction Go lower to look for `python3 repro_responses_item_status.py`, I pasted it in the end. `repro_responses_item_status.py` (attached; stdlib only): ``` python3 repro_responses_item_status.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B ``` It asks once with `max_output_tokens: 16` and once with `400`, and exits 1 when an item says `completed` inside a response that says `incomplete` (and 2 if the control misbehaves, so a strange engine cannot be mistaken for this bug). ### Where it comes from, and vLLM's own counter-example `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/utils.py` builds the non-harmony output items with the status as a literal: ```python # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/utils.py outputs.append( ResponseOutputMessage( ..., role="assistant", status="completed", # <- always, whatever finish reason produced this type="message", ) ) ... outputs.append( ResponseFunctionToolCall( ..., type="function_call", status="completed", # <- same, for a tool call that may be cut mid-arguments ... ) ) ``` The harmony path in the same feature does it correctly, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a decision: ```python # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/harmony.py (three places: 323, 363, 407) status="incomplete" if incomplete else "completed", ``` So a gpt-oss/harmony deployment reports item status truthfully and every other model does not. ### Reproducer, inline
repro_responses_item_status.py — standard library only; save and run against a running server ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """vLLM: /v1/responses output items are always `status: "completed"`, even when the response was cut off. Self-contained (stdlib only): python3 repro_responses_item_status.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B The same question is asked twice: once with room to finish, once with a `max_output_tokens` budget it cannot meet. In the truncated case the response's own top-level `status` is "incomplete" with `incomplete_details.reason == "max_output_tokens"`, while the message item inside `output` still says `"completed"`. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import json import sys import urllib.error import urllib.request def post(base, path, body, timeout=180): req = urllib.request.Request(base.rstrip("/") + path, method="POST", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"content-type": "application/json"}) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r: return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode()) except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: raw = e.read().decode() try: return e.code, json.loads(raw) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return e.code, {"raw": raw[:300]} def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") ap.add_argument("--model", required=True) ap.add_argument("--small", type=int, default=16, help="a budget the answer cannot fit in") ap.add_argument("--large", type=int, default=400, help="a budget it can") a = ap.parse_args() rows, bad = [], 0 for label, budget in (("truncated", a.small), ("complete (control)", a.large)): sc, d = post(a.base_url, "/v1/responses", {"model": a.model, "input": "Name one colour and explain why you picked it.", "max_output_tokens": budget}) if sc != 200: print(json.dumps({"case": label, "error": f"{sc}: {json.dumps(d)[:200]}"}, indent=1)) return 2 items = [{"type": o.get("type"), "status": o.get("status")} for o in (d.get("output") or [])] row = {"case": label, "max_output_tokens": budget, "response_status": d.get("status"), "incomplete_details": d.get("incomplete_details"), "output_items": items, "output_tokens": (d.get("usage") or {}).get("output_tokens")} rows.append(row) print(json.dumps(row, indent=1)) if d.get("status") == "incomplete": for it in items: if it["status"] == "completed": bad += 1 else: for it in items: if it["status"] != "completed": print(" !! the control's item is not 'completed' -- this engine does " "something else entirely, the result above is not evidence") return 2 print() if bad: print(f"REPRODUCED: {bad} output item(s) report status 'completed' inside a response whose " "own status is 'incomplete'.") return 1 print("not reproduced: the item status followed the response status") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
### Before submitting a new issue... (By claude, take it with a grain of salt, it's prob right here tho) - [x] Searched for existing issues (responses api, output item status, incomplete_details, max_output_tokens). #24184 (v0.10.1.1, closed) asked for a *top-level* signal that a Responses call hit `max_output_tokens`; that top-level `status`/`incomplete_details` now works. This report is the *per-item* `output[i].status`, a literal `"completed"` on the non-harmony path while `harmony.py` derives it from the finish reason — a distinct field, still wrong on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0. - [x] Reproduced with the public HTTP API only, on released 0.27.1 and 0.29.0, with a passing control, for both `message` and `function_call` items. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug This is a simple correctness issue I believe, so I won't provide my enviroment above, should be reproducible across. The Anthropic-compatible endpoint answers errors in two different shapes depending on where the error was raised. **Raised inside the handler**, the documented Anthropic envelope: ```json POST /v1/messages {"model": "no/such-model", "max_tokens": 8, "messages": [...]} 404 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"NotFoundError","message":"The model `no/such-model` does not exist."}} ``` **Raised by request validation** -- the OpenAI envelope, and the message is a Python `repr`: ```json POST /v1/messages {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "max_tokens": 0, "messages": [...]} 400 {"error":{"message":"1 validation error:\n {'type': 'value_error', 'loc': ('body', 'max_tokens'), 'msg': 'Value error, max_tokens must be positive', 'input': 0, 'ctx': {'error': ValueError('max_tokens must be positive')}}", "type":"Bad Request","param":"body.max_tokens","code":400}} ``` Same endpoint, same client, two envelopes. A client written against the Anthropic API reads `body["error"]["type"]` and `body["type"] == "error"`; on a validation error neither is there. And the human-readable part is a Python dict repr, not JSON, so the detail cannot be parsed either, `'ctx': {'error': ValueError(...)}` is not machine-readable in any language. **_Reproduced on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0_** with three validation cases (`max_tokens: 0`, an unknown role, a missing `messages`); all three take the OpenAI shape on both versions. **If you want to try fix this, here is where you should look** `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` has the translation and uses it for everything the handler raises: ```python def translate_error_response(response: ErrorResponse) -> JSONResponse: anthropic_error = AnthropicErrorResponse( error=AnthropicError(type=response.error.type, message=response.error.message)) return JSONResponse(status_code=response.error.code, content=anthropic_error.model_dump()) ``` Request validation never reaches that function: FastAPI raises `RequestValidationError` before `create_messages` runs, and the app-wide validation handler answers in the OpenAI envelope for every route. ### Expected `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` answer validation failures in the Anthropic envelope too, a path-scoped validation handler, or a dependency that validates and translates. `count_tokens` behaves exactly like `/v1/messages`, measured on the same 0.29.0 engine: an unknown model is a 404 in the Anthropic envelope, while a bad role and a missing `messages` field are 400s in the OpenAI one. So the fix belongs to both routes. Smaller, in the same area: even the translated errors carry the Python exception class name as `error.type` (`"NotFoundError"`), where the Anthropic API uses `not_found_error`, `invalid_request_error`, and so on -- the field SDKs switch on. ### Reproducer inlined
repro_anthropic_validation_error_envelope.py — standard library only; save and run against a running server ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone repro: /v1/messages answers validation errors in the OpenAI envelope. vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000 python3 repro_anthropic_validation_error_envelope.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Anthropic's envelope is {"type": "error", "error": {"type": ..., "message": ...}}. Measured on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0: the handler's own errors use it, request-validation errors use {"error": {"message": ..., "type": ..., "param": ..., "code": ...}} with a Python repr inside the message. Standard library only. """ import argparse import json import urllib.error import urllib.request def post(base_url, body): req = urllib.request.Request(base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1/messages", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp: return resp.status, resp.read().decode() except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc: return exc.code, exc.read().decode() def anthropic_shaped(body_text): try: b = json.loads(body_text) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return False return b.get("type") == "error" and isinstance(b.get("error"), dict) and "type" in b["error"] def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") ap.add_argument("--model", default="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") a = ap.parse_args() msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}] cases = [ ("handler error: unknown model", {"model": "no/such-model", "max_tokens": 8, "messages": msgs}), ("validation: max_tokens 0", {"model": a.model, "max_tokens": 0, "messages": msgs}), ("validation: unknown role", {"model": a.model, "max_tokens": 8, "messages": [{"role": "wizard", "content": "hi"}]}), ("validation: no messages", {"model": a.model, "max_tokens": 8}), ] print(f"{'case':<32} {'status':>6} {'anthropic shape':>15} body") for name, body in cases: status, text = post(a.base_url, body) print(f"{name:<32} {status:>6} {str(anthropic_shaped(text)):>15} {text[:110]}") print("\nexpected: every row True. Measured on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0: only the handler error is.") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```

`echo` is the OpenAI completions field that asks the server to put the prompt back in front of the completion. vLLM's own extension `return_token_ids` asks for the engine's token ids.
