The capital of France' post({**base, "return_token_ids": True}) # text: ' Paris. The capital of France' post({**base, "echo": False, "return_token_ids": True}) # text: ' Paris. The capital of France' <- identical ``` The second and third answers are the same string: with `return_token_ids` on, `echo: true` and `echo: false` are indistinguishable in the response text. ### Where it comes from `vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py` (line 270 in 0.29.0, the same line in 0.27.1): ```python needs_detokenization=bool(self.echo and not self.return_token_ids), ``` The prompt is only detokenized when `echo` is set AND `return_token_ids` is not. The reasoning is presumably "the caller can detokenize `prompt_token_ids` themselves", and the response does carry `prompt_token_ids` -- but the field the caller set is `echo`, whose documented effect is on `text`, and nothing tells them it was dropped. ### Reproducer
repro_echo_dropped_by_return_token_ids.py, standard library only; save and run against a running server ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone repro: `echo: true` stops echoing when `return_token_ids: true` is also set. vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000 python3 repro_echo_dropped_by_return_token_ids.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \ --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B Measured on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0: the answer with both flags is byte-identical to the answer with echo turned off, so the prompt the caller asked to have echoed is silently missing. Standard library only. """ import argparse import json import urllib.request PROMPT = "The capital of France is" def post(base_url, body): req = urllib.request.Request(base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as resp: return json.loads(resp.read().decode())["choices"][0] def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") ap.add_argument("--model", default="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") a = ap.parse_args() base = {"model": a.model, "prompt": PROMPT, "max_tokens": 6, "temperature": 0.0, "echo": True} echo_only = post(a.base_url, base)["text"] echo_ids = post(a.base_url, {**base, "return_token_ids": True})["text"] no_echo = post(a.base_url, {**base, "echo": False, "return_token_ids": True})["text"] print(f"echo only {echo_only!r}") print(f"echo + return_token_ids {echo_ids!r}") print(f"no echo + return_token_ids {no_echo!r}") print() print("echo honoured without the extension:", echo_only.startswith(PROMPT)) print("echo honoured WITH the extension: ", echo_ids.startswith(PROMPT)) print("with the extension, echo=true and echo=false are the same answer:", echo_ids == no_echo) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description Combining two supported sampling constraints can leave no valid next token and silently break the allowlist. With Qwen3-0.6B, the text `" a"` is token 264. This request allows only token 264 and also bans `" a"`: ```json { "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "prompt": "Return a short answer.", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 4, "return_token_ids": true, "allowed_token_ids": [264], "bad_words": [" a"] } ``` vLLM accepts the request and returns HTTP 200, but generates token 0 four times. Token 0 is not in `allowed_token_ids`. This is not an empty `allowed_token_ids=[]` request. Both fields are non-empty, each constraint works on its own, and vLLM does not report the combination as unsupported. Applications use `allowed_token_ids` to force outputs into a fixed vocabulary, for example label IDs, routing choices, or constrained decoding. This bug can return an arbitrary out-of-domain token in a successful response, so clients that trust the allowlist can accept an invalid result without seeing an error. ## Reproduction Start the server: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8032 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \ --max-model-len 256 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log ``` Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32479783/repro_empty_sampler.py), run: ```bash python repro.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8032 \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script obtains the token IDs from the model tokenizer and sends four requests: each constraint alone, the empty intersection, and a non-empty intersection control. It exits with status 1 when the out-of-allowlist result is reproduced. ## Actual result All four requests return HTTP 200: | Case | Constraints | Returned token IDs | Text | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Allowlist only | allow `[264]` | `[264, 264, 264, 264]` | `" a a a a"` | | Bad word only | ban token 264 | `[4710, 785, 2701, 374]` | `" \n\nThe following is"` | | Empty intersection | allow `[264]`, ban token 264 | `[0, 0, 0, 0]` | `"!!!!"` | | Non-empty control | allow `[264, 279]`, ban token 264 | `[279, 279, 279, 279]` | `" the the the the"` | The controls show that the individual processors work. Only the contradictory combination returns tokens outside the allowlist. The complete client and server output is in [server.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32479792/server_empty_sampler.log). ## Expected result If the active constraints leave no valid next token, vLLM should reject the request or stop it with a clear no-valid-token error. A successful response must never contain a token outside `allowed_token_ids`. ## Root cause The V2 sampler applies the two masks sequentially: 1. The [`allowed_token_ids` kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logit_bias.py#L193-L226) sets every logit to `-inf`, then restores token 264. 2. [`bad_words` runs afterward](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py#L224-L245) and [sets token 264 back to `-inf`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/bad_words.py#L148-L166). 3. There is no check for an all-`-inf` row. At temperature 0, the [Gumbel sampler performs a plain argmax](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py#L102-L130), and the all-tied row falls through to token 0. Request validation rejects a literal empty allowlist and out-of-vocabulary IDs, but [does not validate the intersection with `bad_words`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/sampling_params.py#L981-L1010). ## Related issues [#53665](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53665) reports a different way to create an all-masked row: a terminal structured-output grammar combined with `min_tokens`. [#54218](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54218) fixes that specific `min_tokens + structured output` case. Its description mentions that semantic masks such as `allowed_token_ids` and `bad_words` can cause the same broader all-`-inf` problem, but explicitly leaves the general fix for future work. The implementation only enables stop-token restoration when both `min_tokens` and structured output are active; it does not detect the intersection reproduced here. This report was reproduced on vLLM 0.29.0, which already contains that PR. The same processor ordering and lack of cross-constraint validation are still present on the current `main` branch at the time of writing. No dedicated issue for the `allowed_token_ids + bad_words` intersection was found in searches of existing vLLM issues and PRs. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_xxx ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description In vLLM 0.29.0's V1 model runner, a completed request can leave its `prompt_embeds` tensor referenced by `InputBatch.req_prompt_embeds`. After all requests have been removed and the persistent batch is empty, the dictionary still contains one tensor for every slot that previously handled a prompt-embedding request. Reusing those slots with ordinary token-ID requests does not release or overwrite the old tensors. They remain alive until another prompt-embedding request overwrites the same slot, the dictionary is cleared, or the worker exits. The retention is bounded by persistent-batch capacity, but a worker can keep the peak prompt-embedding footprint of a previous burst even after ordinary text requests replace that workload. The reproducer retains 256 MiB across eight reused slots and releases it only when the stale dictionary is cleared. At a `max_num_seqs` of 256, the same `(4096, 4096)` BF16 shape can retain up to 8 GiB of host memory. This can increase host-memory pressure, swapping, allocation failures, or container eviction risk. Stale entries can also cause unnecessary prompt-embedding staging work for replacement requests. ## Reproduction Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32476544/repro_slot_retention.py), with vLLM 0.29.0 installed, run: ```bash python repro.py 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script reproduces a prompt-embedding burst followed by ordinary text traffic: 1. fills eight slots with `(4096, 4096)` BF16 prompt-embedding tensors, totaling 256 MiB; 2. completes all eight requests and forces garbage collection; 3. reuses every slot with an unrelated token-ID request; 4. verifies that every old tensor is still attached to the reused slot; and 5. clears only `req_prompt_embeds` as a control while the text requests remain active. The script records both weak-reference liveness and process RSS. It calls `malloc_trim()` only after clearing the dictionary so that the RSS control is visible; the weak references establish tensor lifetime independently of the allocator. ## Actual result ```text After the embedding requests finish: active request IDs: [] req_prompt_embeds keys: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] live old tensors: 8 live old tensor bytes: 268435456 process RSS bytes: 1166053376 After text requests reuse the same slots: active request IDs: [text-request-0, ..., text-request-7] req_prompt_embeds keys: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] live old tensors: 8 live old tensor bytes: 268435456 stale entries still reference the old tensors: true process RSS bytes: 1166053376 After clearing only req_prompt_embeds: active request IDs: [text-request-0, ..., text-request-7] req_prompt_embeds keys: [] live old tensors: 0 live old tensor bytes: 0 process RSS bytes: 896708608 RSS drop bytes: 269344768 ``` The weak-reference control shows that the stale dictionary entries are the remaining owners of the tensors. The text requests remain active when the old tensors are released, so the tensors are not needed by the replacement requests. The complete output is in [reproducer_slot_retention.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32476576/reproducer_slot_retention.log). ## Expected result Once a request is removed, its slot must no longer own the request's prompt-embedding tensor. With an empty batch, `req_prompt_embeds` should be empty. Reusing the slots with token-ID requests should not keep any tensor from the completed requests alive. ## Root cause [`InputBatch.add_request()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L350-L386) stores the tensor by slot index: ```python if request.prompt_embeds is not None: self.req_prompt_embeds[req_index] = request.prompt_embeds ``` [`InputBatch.remove_request()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L528-L582) clears the other request-scoped state but never removes this entry. The empty-batch branch of [`condense()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py#L706-L727) also leaves the dictionary unchanged. The missing cleanup can be performed as soon as the request index is known: ```python self.req_prompt_embeds.pop(req_index, None) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description The `functiongemma` tool parser handles the same valid model output differently depending on whether Chat Completions is streamed. For a declared function named `get-weather`, streaming returns a structured tool call. Non-streaming returns no tool call and exposes the complete FunctionGemma control frame as assistant content: ```text call:get-weather{city:Paris} ``` Applications can silently receive ordinary content instead of a tool call when they switch from streaming to non-streaming responses. The leaked content also contains model-specific control tokens that should have been consumed by the parser. Changing only the name to `get_weather` makes both modes work. ## Reproduction Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32470722/repro_get_weather.py), with vLLM 0.29.0 installed, run: ```bash python repro.py 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` If the tokenizer is already cached, the run can be kept fully offline: ```bash python repro.py --local-files-only 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The script feeds one real tokenizer token per streaming delta and compares it with a non-streaming parse of the identical output. It also runs `get_weather` as a control. ## Actual result ```text get_weather, non-streaming: content: null tool call: get_weather({"city": "Paris"}) get_weather, streaming: content: null tool call: get_weather({"city": "Paris"}) get-weather, non-streaming: content: call:get-weather{city:Paris} tool calls: [] get-weather, streaming: content: null tool call: get-weather({"city": "Paris"}) ``` ## Expected result Both response modes should return one structured call named `get-weather` with `{"city": "Paris"}` as its arguments and no assistant content. Hyphens are valid in OpenAI function names, and the official FunctionGemma chat template preserves the declared name in both the function declaration and assistant tool-call history. ## Root cause The non-streaming parser uses `\w+` for the function name: ```python r"call:(\w+)\{(.*?)\}" ``` That expression stops at the hyphen, so `extract_tool_calls()` finds no match and returns the raw model output as content. The streaming path uses all text between `call:` and `{`: ```python func_name = func_part.split("{")[0] ``` It therefore accepts the same name. The two paths implement different grammars for the same field. Relevant source: - [non-streaming regex](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/tool_parsers/functiongemma_tool_parser.py#L41-L46) - [streaming name extraction](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/tool_parsers/functiongemma_tool_parser.py#L203-L222) ## Related issues [#56263](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56263) and [#55199](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55199) concern non-streaming parsers dropping ordinary text after an already successfully parsed tool call. [#57120](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57120) addresses that trailing-content problem in FunctionGemma and leaves tool-call extraction unchanged. This issue occurs earlier in parsing: `get-weather` does not match the non-streaming function-name regex, so no tool call is extracted and the raw control frame is returned as content. None of the changes above modifies that function-name grammar. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

The batch runner does not recognize that response type and replaces the successful result with a 400 error saying the request was sent in stream mode. ## Reproduction Install vLLM 0.29.0 and run this script [probe_vllm_0290_batch_diarized_response_union.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32465739/probe_vllm_0290_batch_diarized_response_union.py): python probe_vllm_0290_batch_diarized_response_union.py \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log For a full GPU reproduction through the standalone batch runner, first create the self-contained JSONL input from any speech WAV with the script [make_batch_input.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32465755/make_batch_input.py): python make_batch_input.py \ --audio /path/to/speech.wav \ --output batch_input.jsonl Then run: vllm run-batch \ -i batch_input.jsonl \ -o batch_output.jsonl \ --model OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize \ --revision 704aa4a9c304e8520be88901e0d1960158ef5b15 \ --served-model-name OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize \ --trust-remote-code \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log This requires the audio dependencies provided by **vllm[audio]**. The included **batch_input.jsonl** already contains the tested WAV as a data URL, so it can also be used directly. The batch input is: { "custom_id": "diarized-probe", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/audio/transcriptions", "body": { "model": "openmoss-transcribe-diarize", "file_url": "data:audio/wav;base64,UklGRg==", "response_format": "diarized_json", "stream": false } } The probe supplies a valid successful handler response and runs it through the released **run_batch.run_request** classifier. The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. The end-to-end run used the official model revision above on an NVIDIA L40S. The batch runner reported vLLM 0.29.0, loaded the model, advertised **Supported tasks: ['transcription']**, completed the request, and exited 0. The model handler produced a valid 9.04225-second diarized transcription with one **S01** speaker segment before the batch classifier replaced it with the error below. ## Actual result The normal transcription response union recognizes the response, but the batch union does not. The batch runner returns: { "response": { "status_code": 400 }, "error": "Request must not be sent in stream mode" } This happens even though the validated request has **stream=false**. Full log is here: [server_batch_diarized.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32465842/server_batch_diarized.log) ## Expected result The batch runner should serialize the successful diarized response: { "task": "transcribe", "duration": 1.25, "text": "Hello.", "segments": [ { "id": "seg_0", "start": 0.0, "end": 1.25, "text": "Hello.", "speaker": "A" } ] } ## Root cause The normal transcription response union includes **TranscriptionResponseDiarized**, while **run_batch.AllResponse** includes only the plain and verbose transcription response types. The diarized response therefore fails the batch runner's successful-response type check and falls into a generic branch that assumes every unrecognized result is a stream. Relevant code: - [batch response classification](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/entrypoints/launchers/run_batch.py#L564-L605) - [normal transcription response union](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/protocol.py#L413-L420) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `--kv-cache-memory` value that vLLM prints at startup double-counts CUDA-graph memory whenever `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1` (the default). For models with a large CUDA-graph pool the suggested value comes out **negative**, so it cannot be used and, since #47374, it also silently defeats `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1`.

#### Background: what the `--kv-cache-memory` recommendation is

`--kv-cache-memory` (config `kv_cache_memory_bytes`) lets the operator hard-code the KV cache size in bytes. When set, vLLM skips the memory-profiling measurement and the CUDA-graph memory estimation pass, and reserves exactly that amount instead of deriving it from `--gpu-memory-utilization` (a short `profile_run()` for compilation still happens). The value is only meaningful if it reproduces the current allocation: too optimistic and the engine OOMs at graph capture, too conservative and batch concurrency (hence throughput) is capped. It is valid only on the same GPU with the same initial free memory.

Because the profiled value is deterministic for a fixed (model, config, hardware, library) combination, `gpu_worker.py` recomputes the exact `--kv-cache-memory` that reproduces the current allocation on every boot and logs it at INFO (promoted from DEBUG in #47374, "Surface the --kv-cache-memory suggestion at INFO and document fast-startup knobs"). The message offers two numbers:

```
Replace gpu_memory_utilization config with `--kv-cache-memory=<X>` (<X> GiB) to fit into
requested memory, or `--kv-cache-memory=<Y>` (<Y> GiB) to fully utilize gpu memory.
```

`X` fills up to the `--gpu-memory-utilization` target; `Y` uses all free device memory. Both are meant to be copied back verbatim, and `X` is also what the opt-in `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` feature (same PR, #47374) persists under `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/startup_plan/` to skip profiling on subsequent boots. That feature's guard rejects non-positive recorded values, so a negative `X` makes the whole fast-startup mechanism inert for exactly the models that would benefit most.

#### Impact

- The copy-paste `--kv-cache-memory` suggestion is unusable (negative) on large-graph models.
- `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` records the negative value and its guard rejects it, so fast startup is a silent no-op.
- No OOM: the double count only affects the reported recommendation, not the live allocation (`Current kv cache memory in use` is still correct).

### Reproduction

Serve any model whose CUDA-graph pool is large relative to the device — e.g. a DeepSeek-class MoE with dspark/MTP speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens=5`, 85 + 81 capture sizes) — and read the startup memory-profiler line. Here `--gpu-memory-utilization` was left at its 0.92 default, TP=8:

```
Free memory on device (175.81/178.35 GiB) on startup. Desired GPU memory utilization is
(0.92, 164.08 GiB). Actual usage is 58.44 GiB for consumed memory (weights + non-torch),
62.33 GiB for peak activation, and 63.99 GiB for CUDAGraph memory. Replace
gpu_memory_utilization config with `--kv-cache-memory=-22362854379` (-20.83 GiB) to fit
into requested memory, or `--kv-cache-memory=-9766683136` (-9.1 GiB) to fully utilize gpu
memory. Current kv cache memory in use is 43.31 GiB.
```

The engine runs fine with 43.31 GiB of KV cache, yet both suggested values are negative. The same run also logs:

```
CUDA graph pool memory: 63.99 GiB (actual), 57.45 GiB (estimated), difference: 6.55 GiB (10.2%).
```

### Root cause

The allocation path counts CUDA-graph memory once; the suggestion path counts it twice.

Allocation path — `determine_available_memory` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`):

```python
self.peak_activation_memory = (
    profile_result.transient_peak_headroom + cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
)
...
self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes = (
    self.requested_memory
    - profile_result.non_kv_cache_memory          # = total_consumed + transient_peak_headroom
    - cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
)
```

Suggestion path — `compile_or_warm_up_model` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`):

```python
non_kv_cache_memory = (
    self.total_consumed
    + self.peak_activation_memory          # already contains cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
    + cuda_graph_memory_bytes              # actual captured pool, added again
)
```

With the numbers above:

| Term | Value |
|---|---|
| `total_consumed` (weights + non-torch) | 58.44 GiB |
| `transient_peak_headroom` | 4.88 GiB |
| `cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied` | 57.45 GiB |
| `cuda_graph_memory_bytes` (actual) | 63.99 GiB |
| `self.peak_activation_memory` (= transient + estimate) | 62.33 GiB |

```
non_kv (current) = 58.44 + 62.33 + 63.99  = 184.76 GiB   # estimate counted twice
fit              = 164.08 − 184.76 − 0.15 = −20.83 GiB

non_kv (correct) = 58.44 +  4.88 + 63.99  = 127.31 GiB
fit              = 164.08 − 127.31 − 0.15 = +36.62 GiB
full             = 175.81 − 127.31 − 0.15 = +48.35 GiB
```

For small graph pools (a few GiB) the error keeps the suggestion positive but still under-reports the achievable KV cache; for large pools it goes negative.

### Regression history

- Introduced by #30515; fixed by **#37426** ("fix CUDAGraph memory being counted twice", merged 2026-03-20), which removed `+ cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied` from `peak_activation_memory`.
- Reintroduced by **#49208** "[copy of #45208] CuMem slept-L1 fragmentation accounting" (commit `58b2012aa2`, merged 2026-07-20), which rewrote the accounting (`torch_peak_increase`/`non_torch_increase` → `total_consumed`/`transient_peak_headroom`) and restored the estimate term.
- Still present on `main` as of this report.

### Suggested fix

Restore #37426: use the transient headroom (not `peak_activation_memory`) when computing `non_kv_cache_memory`, so CUDA-graph memory is counted once:

```diff
             non_kv_cache_memory = (
                 self.total_consumed
-                + self.peak_activation_memory
+                + profile_result.transient_peak_headroom
                 + cuda_graph_memory_bytes
             )
```

or equivalently keep `self.peak_activation_memory = profile_result.transient_peak_headroom` as it was before #49208. This also makes the #47374 startup-plan feature effective for large-graph models.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Description When **/v1/chat/completions/batch** is called with **include_reasoning=false**, the response removes **message.reasoning** but still returns metadata for the complete raw generation. The hidden `...` span can be recovered from either the logprob token strings or **choice.token_ids**. ## Reproduction Install vLLM 0.29.0, download Qwen3-0.6B locally, and run with [probe_vllm_0290_batch_reasoning_metadata_leak.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32464286/probe_vllm_0290_batch_reasoning_metadata_leak.py): python probe_vllm_0290_batch_reasoning_metadata_leak.py \ --tokenizer /path/to/Qwen3-0.6B \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log The probe uses the released batch response assembler, Qwen3 tokenizer and Qwen3 reasoning parser with this deterministic engine output: PRIVATE_CHAIN_7f3aPUBLIC_ANSWER The relevant request is: { "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "messages": [[{"role": "user", "content": "Answer the probe."}]], "include_reasoning": false, "logprobs": true, "top_logprobs": 0, "return_token_ids": true } The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. Full log is here: [metadate_leakage_reproducer.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32464477/metadate_leakage_reproducer.log) ## Actual result message.content: PUBLIC_ANSWER message.reasoning: absent concat(choice.logprobs.content[].token): PRIVATE_CHAIN_7f3aPUBLIC_ANSWER decode(choice.token_ids): PRIVATE_CHAIN_7f3aPUBLIC_ANSWER ## Expected result With **include_reasoning=false**, the response must not expose the hidden reasoning through another field. **choice.logprobs** and **choice.token_ids** should therefore be absent or null. ## Root cause The batch response assembler builds logprobs from all raw output token IDs, then clears only the parsed reasoning field. It still emits the previously built logprobs and the raw token IDs. The normal non-batch chat path has a metadata-suppression guard for this case, but **chat_completion_full_generator_batch** does not. Relevant code: - [batch response assembler](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/batch_serving.py#L199-L332) - [non-batch metadata suppression](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py#L969-L981) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug The non-streaming scale-out completions pipeline drops prompt log probabilities at the final derender step. The generated text and usage are otherwise correct, so the missing data can go unnoticed. ## Environment - vLLM: `0.29.0` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` - GPU: NVIDIA L40S - Request mode: non-streaming The issue is also present in the current `main` implementation of `OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion`. ## Reproduction Start a vLLM server with the scale-out endpoints enabled: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \ --port 8029 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \ --max-model-len 1024 \ --enforce-eager \ 2>&1 | tee server.log ``` Run the reproducer [probe_vllm_0290_derender_prompt_logprobs.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32463597/probe_vllm_0290_derender_prompt_logprobs.py): ```bash python probe_vllm_0290_derender_prompt_logprobs.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8029 \ 2>&1 | tee reproducer.log ``` The reproducer sends this request both through `/v1/completions` and through the split render/generate/derender pipeline: ```json { "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "prompt": "The capital of France is", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 1 } ``` The split request flow is: ```text /v1/completions/render -> /inference/v1/generate -> /v1/completions/derender ``` ## Actual result All requests return HTTP 200 and generate the same text, `" Paris"`. ```text /v1/completions: choices[0].prompt_logprobs: 5 entries /inference/v1/generate: prompt_logprobs: 5 entries /v1/completions/derender: choices[0].prompt_logprobs: null ``` The prompt-logprob arrays returned by the direct endpoint and the generate endpoint are identical. Only the final derendered response loses them. Full log are here: [logprobs_server.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32463567/logprobs_server.log) [reproducer.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32463572/reproducer.log) ## Expected result The derendered response should preserve the prompt log probabilities already present in each `GenerateResponse`: ```text direct choice.prompt_logprobs == generate_response.prompt_logprobs == derendered choice.prompt_logprobs ``` ## Root cause `OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion()` builds each `CompletionResponseChoice` with `index`, `text`, `finish_reason`, and generated token `logprobs`, but it never copies `gen.prompt_logprobs` into the choice. The field therefore falls back to its default value of `null`, even though the engine has already computed and returned it. Clients using the scale-out pipeline for scoring, evaluation, ranking, or perplexity calculations silently receive an incomplete response. The engine still pays the cost of computing and serializing the requested prompt log probabilities. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

This affects more than the reported vector norm. It changes dot-product scores, threshold decisions, and comparisons between short and long inputs. Using embeddings returned by the API, an exact long-text self-match produces a dot product of only `0.61587080`. The same vector has cosine similarity `1.0`, and its dot product becomes `1.0` after L2 normalization. For example, a dot-product threshold of `0.8` rejects an exact match: ```text same 128-token text used as query and document raw vLLM dot product: 0.61587080 -> rejected dot after L2 normalization: 1.00000000 -> accepted threshold: 0.8 ``` All vectors in this comparison come directly from `POST /v1/embeddings`. ## Environment - vLLM: `0.29.0` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` - GPU: NVIDIA L40S - Endpoint: `POST /v1/embeddings` - Runner: pooling Pooler configuration: ```json { "enable_chunked_processing": true, "max_embed_len": 512, "use_activation": true } ``` ## Reproduction Start the server with `max_model_len=64` so a 128-token input is split into two chunks: ```bash MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \ --served-model-name chunk-embed \ --runner pooling \ --convert embed \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8134 \ --max-model-len 64 \ --pooler-config \ '{"enable_chunked_processing":true,"max_embed_len":512,"use_activation":true}' \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.20 \ --max-num-seqs 8 \ --enforce-eager ``` Use the script: [probe_vllm_chunked_embedding_normalization.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32462928/probe_vllm_chunked_embedding_normalization.py) Run: ```bash python scripts/probe_vllm_chunked_embedding_normalization.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8134 \ --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" \ --out /tmp/chunked_embedding_result.json ``` The reproducer builds two different 64-token sequences: - `A`: repetitions of `apple orchard harvest fruit trees sunshine agriculture`; - `B`: repetitions of `quantum mechanics particle wavefunction entanglement laboratory`. It requests embeddings for: 1. `A` and `B` as ordinary 64-token inputs; 2. `A + B` as one 128-token long input; 3. the same returned vectors under representative dot-product scoring and threshold rules. Every embedding request uses: ```json { "model": "chunk-embed", "encoding_format": "float", "add_special_tokens": false, "use_activation": true } ``` ## Actual result ### 1. Exact long-text match fails a dot-product threshold ```text query: embedding(A + B) document: embedding(A + B) raw dot product: 0.61587080 dot after L2 normalization: 1.00000000 cosine similarity: 1.00000000 threshold: 0.8 raw decision: reject normalized decision: accept ``` Every threshold in `(0.61587080, 1.0]` changes this decision. ### 2. A short query can fail against a long document containing it ```text query: embedding(A) document: embedding(A + B) raw dot product: 0.61584421 dot after L2 normalization: 0.78474047 threshold: 0.7 raw decision: reject normalized decision: accept ``` Every threshold in `(0.61584421, 0.78474047]` changes this decision. ### 3. Exact-match ranking margin nearly disappears Using `embedding(A + B)` as the query: | Candidate | Raw dot product | Dot after normalization | |---|---:|---:| | Exact long document `A + B` | `0.61587080` | `1.00000000` | | Short half-document `A` | `0.61584421` | `0.78474047` | The exact-match margin is only `0.00002658` with the raw vLLM outputs. After normalization it is `0.21525953`. ### 4. Long and short outputs have different norms ```text ordinary A norm: 1.00000003 ordinary B norm: 1.00000004 chunked A+B norm: 0.78477436 explicitly normalized: 1.00000000 ``` A magnitude threshold of `0.9` therefore accepts the ordinary embeddings but rejects the chunked long embedding. ## Expected result With `use_activation=true`, both ordinary and chunked embedding outputs should be L2-normalized. The exact long-text self dot product should therefore be approximately `1.0`. The final aggregation should be equivalent to: ```python final_embedding = F.normalize( weighted_sum / total_weight, p=2, dim=-1, ) ``` ## Root cause Each chunk passes through the normal embedding pooler and is L2-normalized before aggregation. `EmbedIOProcessor._post_process_chunked()` then computes a token-count-weighted mean: ```python final_embedding = weighted_sum / total_weight ``` That mean is returned directly. There is no final activation or `F.normalize()` call after the chunks have been combined. The mean of different unit vectors generally has a norm below 1. In this reproduction, a dot product involving one affected long vector is scaled by approximately `0.7848`; a long-vector self dot product is scaled by its square, approximately `0.6159`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: HunYuan Dense V1 fails CUDA graph capture on v0.29 — HF dynamic RoPE does a host-side sync during capture
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.29.0 (official image), 2× L40S (also reproduces TP=1), transformers 5.16
- Model: hy-mt2-7b HunYuanDenseV1ForCausalLM checkpoint, `rope_scaling = {"type": "dynamic", "alpha": 1000.0, "factor": 1.0, ...}`, `max_position_embeddings=262144`


### 🐛 Describe the bug


### Reproduce
`vllm serve  hy-mt2-7b --tensor-parallel-size 2` (default `cudagraph_mode=FULL`).
vLLM downgrades to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (FlashAttentionBackend, UNIFORM_BATCH), then dies during capture:

torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing
  transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py:100  `if seq_len > max_seq_len_cached:`
  called from modeling_hunyuan_v1_dense.py:436 `position_embeddings = self.rotary_emb(...)`

### Root cause
Since #53615 the model runs on the Transformers backend. Dynamic-rope checkpoints go through
`@dynamic_rope_update`, where `dynamic_frequency_update` does
`seq_len = torch.max(position_ids) + 1; if seq_len > max_seq_len_cached:` — `Tensor.__bool__`
forces a D2H sync, which is illegal inside CUDA graph capture → capture invalidated
(cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated at capture_end) → startup fails. Every cudagraph mode except
NONE fails (PIECEWISE capture passes 19/19 with torch.compile on, but the FULL phase /
profile_cudagraph_memory still runs the raw forward and dies).

Note: in vLLM `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings`, so for these checkpoints the whole
dynamic update is a no-op — but the check itself still syncs.

### Regression
≤0.28 native `hunyuan_v1.py` computed the NTK-alpha inv_freq statically in `__init__`; CUDA graphs worked.

### Workaround
`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}'` (starts, decode perf hit).

### Possible fixes
- In `vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py`: bypass `dynamic_rope_update` when
  `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings` (update is a no-op then), or
- warn + force `cudagraph_mode=NONE` for dynamic-rope models, or
- (upstream transformers) make `dynamic_frequency_update` capture-safe.

cc @hmellor (author of #53615)

title: [Bug]: DecodeBenchConnector repeats KV cache fills for shared state tensors at large batch sizes
body:
### Your current environment

<details>

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
- Python: 3.12.3
- vLLM: 0.25.1
- PyTorch: 2.12.1
- Engine: vLLM V1
- KV connector: DecodeBenchConnector
- Execution backend: Multiprocessing
- Workload: Long-context decode benchmark with a large batch size (256 requests)
- KV cache layout: Hybrid KV cache with shared state tensors


</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Bug Description

`DecodeBenchConnectorWorker.start_fill_kv()` currently processes requests one by one and fills the KV cache separately for each request.

For hybrid KV cache layouts, multiple requests may reference the same state tensor. The current implementation fills the same state tensor repeatedly for every request.

Block-indexed KV cache entries are also filled per request, even when block IDs overlap across requests.

As the batch size increases, the repeated fill operations introduce significant overhead before the first decode step.

In our vLLM-MLU testing environment, this behavior was observed during large-batch, long-context decode benchmarks and was associated with worker RPC timeouts.

The repeated-fill behavior can be identified in the upstream `DecodeBenchConnector` implementation. However, the runtime timeout has so far been reproduced on the MLU backend.

## Reproduction

The issue was observed with the following configuration:

- Engine: vLLM V1
- KV connector: `DecodeBenchConnector`
- KV cache layout: Hybrid KV cache containing shared state tensors
- Batch size: 256
- Execution backend: Multiprocessing
- Workload: Long-context decode benchmark

The issue occurs during the initial KV cache fill before the first decode step.

Instrumentation of `start_fill_kv()` shows that shared state tensors are filled repeatedly across requests within a single invocation.

As the number of requests increases, the repeated fill operations can significantly increase the initialization time.

## Actual Behavior

The initial KV cache fill becomes increasingly expensive at large batch sizes.

In our testing environment, the excessive delay was associated with the following errors:

```text
TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out No available shared memory broadcast block found
```

A subsequent error while querying worker memory usage may occur after the worker RPC has already timed out.

The repeated state-tensor fills occur before the first decode step.

## Expected Behavior

`start_fill_kv()` should avoid filling the same shared state tensor more than once within a single invocation.

Block IDs should be merged and deduplicated per KV cache group before the fill operation.

The implementation should also avoid creating a full-batch temporary value tensor when filling a large number of blocks.

These changes should reduce redundant KV cache initialization work without changing the intended cache contents.

## Related Pull Request

This issue is related to PR #56473:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56473

That PR discusses reducing temporary tensor allocation and fill overhead in `DecodeBenchConnector`.

## Temporary Workaround

A backend-specific workaround currently:

- Merges block IDs by KV cache group.
- Deduplicates block IDs.
- Deduplicates shared state tensors by object identity.
- Fills contiguous block ranges in place.
- Uses indexed writes for sparse blocks.

The workaround reduces redundant operations during the initial KV cache fill.

It can be removed once an equivalent upstream fix is merged and included in the dependency version.

title: [Bug] [watermarking]: reference detection server does not support dual_key_gumbel; detector alpha default disagrees with generation default
body:
### Your current environment

N/A — code-level report against current `main` (17e50b9b761023d5f2499f062507df1ff49092a4); no runtime environment involved.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two related gaps after #56122.

### 1. Reference detection server cannot detect `dual_key_gumbel` output

`examples/basic/online_serving/watermark_detection_server.py` always constructs `GumbelWatermarkDetector` (line 60). Its argparse takes only `--tokenizer / --key / --prf / --context-width / --p-value-threshold`. There is no `--algorithm` or `--alpha`, so text generated with `algorithm="dual_key_gumbel"` cannot be detected with the reference server. `docs/features/watermarking.md` points users at this server as the deployment pattern (line 228). It should accept `--algorithm dual_key_gumbel --alpha <value>` and build `DualKeyGumbelWatermarkDetector`.

### 2. Detector `alpha` default disagrees with generation default

- `DualKeyGumbelWatermarkDetector.__init__` defaults `alpha=0.2` (`vllm/v1/watermarking/gumbel.py:220`)
- `WatermarkConfig.alpha` defaults to `0.1` (`vllm/config/watermarking.py:35`), as does `DualKeyGumbelWatermarker` (`gumbel.py:107`)

The detector uses `alpha` in the variance normalization (`gumbel.py:252`: `variance = (1 - self.alpha) ** 2 + self.alpha ** 2`), so a silent default mismatch changes p-values. Suggest aligning the detector default to 0.1, or dropping the default and requiring `alpha` explicitly.

### Docs nit

Worth a one-line note in the constraints section that `deduplicate_contexts` and speculative decoding are mutually exclusive in effect today. It is stated at `docs/features/watermarking.md:80-82`, but under the spec-decode heading where it is easy to miss.

The output of python collect_env.py(run inside the vLLM nightly container; the host driver is 535.183.01) ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.2026) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : Could not collect Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jul 15 2026, 23:46:41) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-4.19.90-0.240102.openeuler.x86_64-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU 0..7 : NVIDIA L20 x8 (PCIe, no NVLink) Nvidia driver version : 535.183.01 ``` vLLM version: `0.2.1.dev58+g9854b580dfe518171eed3a6ad76cbd402ca2bdfa` (nightly wheel, 2026-09-17)
### 🐛 Describe the bug With `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}'` (pinned-host PLE / UVA lookup, #54371) and `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'`, engine startup **fails intermittently** during `profile_cudagraph_memory()`: all 4 TP workers raise `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted` at FULL-graph `capture_end()`. The failure is load-dependent: it succeeds on an idle host and fails under host load (load average 15–21), which matches a capture race rather than a deterministic incompatibility. ``` docker run ... \ /Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' \ ``` Observed runs (same image, same args, 4x L20): | Run | Host load | Result | |---|---|---| | 2026-09-17 13:08 | idle | startup OK | | 2026-09-17 18:17 | load 15–21, 64-min slow weight load, `shm_broadcast` 60s stall warning beforehand | PIECEWISE 11/11 OK → FULL failed at 1/2, all 4 workers | | 2026-09-18 10:14 | moderate | startup OK | Full traceback (identical on all 4 TP workers): ``` (Worker_TP1 pid=711) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1053] Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1045, in _execute_worker_rpc File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 586, in determine_available_memory cudagraph_memory_estimate = self.model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory() File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 922, in profile_cudagraph_memory measured = int(runner.capture_model(profile_only=True)) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 748, in capture File ".../torch/cuda/graphs.py", line 477, in __exit__ self.cuda_graph.capture_end() File ".../torch/cuda/graphs.py", line 169, in capture_end torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted Search for `cudaErrorNotPermitted` in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information. ``` I could not attach `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1` logs for the failing run yet because the failure is intermittent and each reproduction costs ~1 hour of weight loading; happy to add them on the next recurrence. The crash is fully reproducible *in probability* under synthetic load (see below). ### Root-cause analysis The pinned-host PLE backend decorates `start_prefetch` with `eager_break_during_capture` (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py`), launching the UVA lookup on a **side CUDA stream** and returning immediately. Under breakable capture the eager break runs between two capture segments, and the side-stream work is never joined: if it is still in flight when a later segment's `capture_end()` runs, the capture is invalidated and surfaces as `cudaErrorNotPermitted`. Host load slows the PCIe UVA reads, widening the race window (related: #40742, #36587, #54646). ### Suggested fix Join all device work in the legal window — at the top of `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture._begin_segment()` (`vllm/compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`), after the previous segment has ended and before the next `capture_begin()`: ```python def _begin_segment(self) -> None: assert not self._capturing torch.cuda.synchronize() # join side-stream work (e.g. PLE UVA prefetch) ... ``` ### Workaround `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}'` starts reliably (the PLE segment stays eager by construction), at the cost of TPOT regression at low concurrency (measured 22.2 ms vs 12.3 ms at C1; gap closes to ~7% at C16). Thanks for reporting 🙏 (and thanks for #54371 — the offload path itself has been rock-solid in production apart from this capture race). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

Version : 0.29.1rc1.dev128+gcd10ed6f9 (git sha: cd10ed6f9) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X N/A ============================== Environment Variables ============================== PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_xyf ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug # Summary vLLM’s generic multimodal `PromptReplacement` pipeline binds media items to placeholder occurrences after chat rendering and tokenization. The binding is based on token-value matching, not placeholder provenance. In the confirmed Qwen2.5-VL case, a literal `<|image_pad|>` in user text tokenizes to the same special-token id (`151655`) as the template-generated image placeholder. If the user-text occurrence appears first, it consumes the queued image update; the image feature span is inserted into user text, while the real `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>` image slot remains with one raw, unexpanded pad token. Token-level reproduction on the full chat path, using one 448x448 image (256 image tokens), gives: ```text control [image, text quoting <|image_pad|>]: total 292 tokens, pad runs [(15, 256), (278, 1)] -> 256-token image span inside the real <|vision_start|> slot attack [text quoting <|image_pad|>, image]: total 292 tokens, pad runs [(20, 256), (285, 1)] -> 256-token image span inside user text ("User asked: what does ...") -> real <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> slot keeps 1 raw token ``` The layouts have the same length and token multiset; the processor trace shows that the media binding moved from the template-generated slot into user text. End-to-end tests on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 7B then changed visual-safety verdicts from YES/UNSAFE to NO/SAFE and downstream decisions from BLOCK to ALLOW in the reported cells. A describe probe on the same allowed request still identified the depicted weapon, confirming that the image remained perceptible but was no longer structurally grounded at its intended slot. # Affected component Component: vLLM multimodal prompt processing — generic `PromptReplacement` matching and placeholder validation. Files: ```text vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py (confirmed adapter: placeholder construction and replacement target) vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py (generic matching, update planning, replacement, validation) vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py (chat-part assembly; no equivalent image/video placeholder reservation) ``` Confirmed affected adapter: ```text Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct ``` Source-level candidate adapters: ```text Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL, Keye, Mimo-V2-Omni, LLaVA-OneVision2, Bagel, and multiple -placeholder adapters such as LLaVA, InternVL, Idefics3, DeepSeek-VL2, LFM2-VL, and related adapters. ``` # Details The root cause is in vLLM’s generic multimodal prompt-update pipeline. Chat rendering produces a flat token sequence, and `PromptReplacement` later searches that sequence by token value. The pipeline does not retain whether a matched token originated from the chat template’s media placeholder or from user text. Therefore, any adapter that exposes a user-spellable placeholder string and uses token-value `PromptReplacement` can be susceptible. This report confirms the behavior on Qwen2.5-VL. Source references below are immutable links to the vLLM `v0.29.0` release tag commit [`98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206). ## 1. Qwen2.5-VL emits a user-spellable media placeholder Qwen2.5-VL renders an image part as: ```text <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> ``` Relevant source: [`qwen2_5_vl.py#L1334-L1338`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py#L1334-L1338). The important logic is: ```python if modality.startswith("image"): return "<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" ``` A literal `<|image_pad|>` in user text is preserved and tokenizes to the same special id (`151655`) as the middle token of the generated slot. After chat rendering and tokenization, both occurrences are just equal token ids in one flat prompt; no origin metadata remains. ## 2. The adapter registers only the pad token as the replacement target The Qwen2.5-VL processor builds replacement targets from the tokenizer vocabulary. For images, the target is the image pad token itself, not the surrounding vision wrapper. Relevant source: - [`qwen2_5_vl.py#L1162-L1178`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py#L1162-L1178) - [`qwen2_5_vl.py#L1208-L1214`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py#L1208-L1214) Condensed logic: ```python placeholder = { "image": vocab[hf_processor.image_token], "video": vocab[hf_processor.video_token], } PromptReplacement( modality=modality, target=[placeholder[modality]], replacement=... ) ``` The replacement callback expands the matched token to the number of visual feature tokens: ```python num_tokens = int(grid_thw.prod()) // merge_length return [placeholder[modality]] * num_tokens ``` For the 448x448 test image, this produces 256 image tokens. This creates the key condition: the real template slot and the user-text literal are indistinguishable to the generic replacement logic because both contain the same target token. ## 3. The generic processor searches by token value and uses first match The shared vLLM processor compiles per-item updates into ordered queues, then scans the already-tokenized prompt for matching token sequences. Relevant source: - queue construction: [`processor.py#L641-L665`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py#L641-L665) - left-to-right token matching: [`processor.py#L519-L557`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py#L519-L557) - first queue match: [`processor.py#L674-L691`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py#L674-L691) - planner selection: [`processor.py#L750-L788`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py#L750-L788) Condensed logic: ```python start_idx = token_ids.index(first_id, start_idx, ...) if token_ids[start_idx:end_idx] == match_ids: yield _TokenMatch(start_idx, end_idx) ``` And: ```python match = next(iter_matches(update, start_idx), None) ``` The planner then chooses the earliest non-empty replacement and pops the queued media item. Therefore, in this prompt: ```text ... user text ... <|image_pad|> ... <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> ... ^ selected ^ intended slot ``` the user-text occurrence is selected first and consumes image item 0. ## 4. Replacement records a valid span at the wrong location Once the earlier user-text token is selected, `_apply_token_matches_with_placeholders()` writes the expanded visual span at that location and records it as the placeholder span for the image. Relevant source: [`processor.py#L860-L909`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py#L860-L909). Condensed logic: ```python start_idx = len(new_token_ids) placeholders[update.modality].append(...) new_token_ids.extend(tokens) ``` Because the match came from user text, the recorded span is structurally outside the vision wrapper. The later genuine template token is copied through unchanged. This yields the measured attack layout: ```text [(20,256),(285,1)] ``` Meaning: ```text offset 20: 256-token image feature span inside user text offset 285: raw unexpanded <|image_pad|> inside the real vision wrapper ``` ## 5. Count-only validation accepts the wrong binding After replacement, `_validate_mm_placeholders()` only checks whether the number of recorded spans equals the number of media items. Relevant source: [`processor.py#L1667-L1701`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py#L1667-L1701). Condensed logic: ```python if len(placeholders) != item_count: raise RuntimeError(...) ``` In the attack layout, there is still exactly one recorded image span for exactly one image item, so validation passes. The path does not verify: ```text - whether the span came from a template-generated media placeholder, - whether the span is inside <|vision_start|> / <|vision_end|>, - whether the genuine media slot still contains a raw unexpanded pad token, - whether user text supplied a reserved media placeholder token. ``` This is a provenance-validation failure, not just a tokenizer quirk: provenance is discarded before matching, the earliest equal token receives the binding, and validation has no invariant capable of detecting the swap. ## 6. Chat parsing already protects prompt_embeds, but not image/video placeholders vLLM already has a boundary check for the internal `prompt_embeds` sentinel because user-supplied text could otherwise be mistaken for a splice point. Relevant source: [`chat_utils.py#L1822-L1838`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/98dff2a81d747d1dba01a47f939f48c3526d4206/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py#L1822-L1838). Condensed logic: ```python if model_config.enable_prompt_embeds and PROMPT_EMBEDS_PLACEHOLDER_TOKEN in text: raise VLLMValidationError(...) ``` There is no equivalent rejection or escaping for image/video placeholder strings such as `<|image_pad|>` or `<|video_pad|>`. As a result, user text can introduce token sequences that collide with template-generated media placeholders. ## 7. Scope beyond Qwen2.5-VL The OpenAI chat path and offline `LLM.generate` / `TextPrompt` + `multi_modal_data` path both reach `BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates()`, so the confirmed Qwen2.5-VL behavior is not tied to the OpenAI server only. Source review also shows that several other adapters expose user-spellable placeholders and use the same generic `PromptReplacement` token-value path. Examples include: ```text qwen2_vl.py -> <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> qwen3_vl.py -> <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> keye.py -> <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|> mimo_v2_omni.py -> image/video/audio pad placeholders llava_onevision2.py -> Qwen-style vision wrapper bagel.py -> <|image_pad|> llava.py -> internvl.py -> /
label: bug

### 🐛 Describe the bug With a KV connector configured (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`), `POST /reset_prefix_cache` reports `{"success":true}` and clears the GPU prefix cache, but leaves the connector's CPU tier populated. The very next request for the same prompt is served from that tier: the GPU prefix-cache hit counter stays at zero while `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` jumps by the whole prompt. The endpoint's name and its success response suggest the engine is back to a cold prefix state. It is not, and nothing in the response or the logs says so. Any measurement that uses "reset, then send" as a cold baseline is silently measuring a warm path instead. ### Reproduction Send a 1,024-token prompt, send it again, reset, send it a third time, then send it once more under a fresh `cache_salt`, reading `/metrics` between each step (`repro_reset_prefix_cache_offload_tier.py`, attached, is the same sequence in stdlib-only form and exits 1 when the tier serves the post-reset request). ```python import httpx B = "http://127.0.0.1:8000" IDS = [1000 + (i * 7919) % 90000 for i in range(1024)] def counters(): out = {} for line in httpx.get(B + "/metrics", timeout=30).text.splitlines(): if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip(): continue name = line.split("{")[0].split(" ")[0] if "prefix_cache" in name: out[name] = out.get(name, 0.0) + float(line.rsplit(" ", 1)[1]) return out def ask(salt=None): body = {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B", "prompt": IDS, "max_tokens": 4, "temperature": 0.0} if salt: body["cache_salt"] = salt httpx.post(B + "/v1/completions", json=body, timeout=300).raise_for_status() a = counters(); ask(); b = counters() # cold ask(); c = counters() # warm print(httpx.post(B + "/reset_prefix_cache", timeout=60).json()) ask(); d = counters() # after the reset ask(salt="fresh"); e = counters() # nothing can serve this for name, (x, y) in {"cold": (a, b), "warm": (b, c), "after reset": (c, d), "salted": (d, e)}.items(): print(name, {k: round(y[k] - x.get(k, 0), 1) for k in y if y[k] - x.get(k, 0)}) ``` ### What happens ``` cold {'external_prefix_cache_queries_total': 1024, 'prefix_cache_queries_total': 1024} warm {'external_prefix_cache_queries_total': 16, 'prefix_cache_hits_total': 1008, 'prefix_cache_queries_total': 1024} POST /reset_prefix_cache -> {"success": true} after reset {'external_prefix_cache_hits_total': 1008, 'external_prefix_cache_queries_total': 1024, 'prefix_cache_queries_total': 1024} salted {'external_prefix_cache_queries_total': 1024, 'prefix_cache_queries_total': 1024} ``` The reset does clear the GPU prefix cache: after it, `prefix_cache_hits_total` does not move. But `external_prefix_cache_hits_total` moves by 1,008 of the 1,024 prompt tokens, so the request was served from the CPU tier the reset left behind. Only a fresh `cache_salt` produces a genuinely cold path (last line: 1,024 external queries, zero hits). _Importance:_ Beyond the naming, the practical consequence is that "reset, then measure" is not a cold baseline on a connector arm, and there is no signal that it isn't. In our own testing this silently invalidated a four-way comparison: two byte-identical requests sent after a reset answered differently depending on which request had run *before* the reset, because each was served whatever the tier happened to hold. It took a dedicated probe to notice, because the endpoint reports success and the served-from-tier path is not visible in the response. _Expected behavior should prob be:_ One of: 1. `reset_prefix_cache` also drops the connector's cached blocks, or 2. it reports what it did and did not clear (for example `{"success": true, "connector_cache_cleared": false}`), or 3. the documentation for the endpoint states that connector tiers are out of scope and names `cache_salt` as the way to force a cold path. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

The same request on the same model without `--reasoning-parser` is constrained. ```bash SCHEMA='{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["name","age"],"additionalProperties":false}' curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{ \"model\":\"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B\",\"prompt\":\"Give me a person as JSON:\",\"max_tokens\":40,\"temperature\":0, \"structured_outputs\":{\"json\":$SCHEMA}}" ``` | server | `text` | |---|---| | no reasoning parser | `{"name": "John Doe", "age": 30}` (finish `stop`) | | `--reasoning-parser qwen3` | ` { "name": "John Doe", "age": 30, "city": "New York", "email": "john@example.com", "address": "123 Main St,` (finish `length`) | | `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, prompt suffixed with `\n\n\n\n` | `{\n "name": "John Doe",\n "age": 30\n}` (finish `stop`) | `additionalProperties: false` is violated and the object never closes. The other constraint kinds behave the same way on the reasoning-parser server: | constraint | `text` | |---|---| | `{"choice": ["yes", "no"]}`, prompt `Is the sky blue? Answer:` | ` Yes\nOkay, let's see. The question` | | `{"regex": "[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}"}`, prompt `A date:` | ` 2023-10-10\n\nI need to find the number of possible` | | `guided_json` (legacy field), Qwen3-8B | ` name, age, gender, and occupation. Also, include a list of hobbies. ...` | `/v1/chat/completions` on the same server is fine, with `enable_thinking` on (the grammar starts after ``) and off (the template's empty think block ends reasoning in the prompt). ### Why `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`: when a reasoner is configured, `should_fill_bitmask` / `should_advance` gate the grammar on `reasoning_ended`, which is initialised from `reasoner.is_reasoning_end(request.prompt_token_ids)` and then only flips when the model emits the reasoning end token. A raw completion prompt contains neither `` nor ``, so `is_reasoning_end` is False, the bitmask is never applied, and the model is free for the whole completion unless it happens to emit `` by itself. The same logic is on `main` today (`if reasoner.is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids): return 0; structured_req.reasoning_ended = False`). The reasoning parser is a chat-completions concept (it splits the assistant turn), but its grammar gate applies to every request of the engine, including completions that never render a chat template. _Expected behavior:_ Either of: - a prompt that contains no reasoning *start* token is treated as "reasoning already over" (the grammar applies from the first generated token, as it does for the empty think block), or - a completions request with a structured-output constraint under a reasoning parser is rejected with a 400 that names the workaround. Silently returning an unconstrained completion is the one outcome a caller cannot detect. ### Workarounds - append `\n\n\n\n` to the completion prompt (verified above), or - start the server with `--structured-outputs-config '{"enable_in_reasoning": true}'` (constrains the whole output, so chat requests lose free-form reasoning). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

### 🐛 Describe the bug In brief, there are actually 2 problems, both reachable by any caller with one request. **1. A client mistake in a JSON schema, a regex or a grammar is answered with `500 InternalServerError` and an empty `message`.** The validator itself produces a good message. Calling it in process: ```python from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams, StructuredOutputsParams p = SamplingParams(structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json={"type": "not-a-type"})) p._validate_structured_outputs(model_config, structured_outputs_config, tokenizer) # ValueError: Grammar error: Invalid type: not-a-type ``` Over HTTP the caller gets neither the status nor the text: ```json {"error": {"message": "", "type": "InternalServerError", "param": null, "code": 500}} ``` Nine different malformed specifications behave this way, on both `/v1/chat/completions` (`response_format: json_schema`) and `/v1/completions` (`structured_outputs.json`): | specification | in-process validator message | HTTP status | HTTP message | |---|---|---|---| | `{"type": "not-a-type"}` | `Grammar error: Invalid type: not-a-type` | 500 | empty | | `{"type": "object", "properties": {"a": {"type": "nope"}}}` | same class | 500 | empty | | `{"$ref": "#/$defs/missing"}` (dangling) | `Failed to transform json schema into a grammar: ...` | 500 | empty | | `{"enum": []}` | `Grammar error: Unsatisfiable schema: anyOf is empty` | 500 | empty | | `{"type": "string", "pattern": "("}` | `Grammar error: regex parse error: unclosed group` | 500 | empty | | `{"type": "integer", "minimum": "x"}` | grammar error | 500 | empty | | `{"type": "object", "properties": []}` | grammar error | 500 | empty | | `structured_outputs.grammar = "root ::= unclosed"` | grammar error | 500 | empty | | `structured_outputs.regex = "([a-z"` | regex error | 500 | empty | Four more one-request cases behave the same way (Qwen3-0.6B, same server shape): `structured_outputs.regex = "[a-"` (500, message `""`), an unterminated EBNF `structured_outputs.grammar = 'root ::= "a" | '` (500, message `"Internal server error"`), `response_format.json_schema.schema = {"type": "objekt"}` (500, `""`), and a schema with `"uniqueItems": true`, which xgrammar does not support (500, `""`). **The failure is backend-independent:** the same cases against `--structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"guidance"}'` return the empty-message 500 for 7 of the 9 rows above (`schema_invalid`, `schema_bad_nested_type`, `schema_dangling_ref`, `schema_empty_enum`, `schema_bad_pattern`, `so_grammar_undefined_rule`, `so_regex_unbalanced`), so it is the request-validation layer, not xgrammar. For comparison, neighbouring mistakes are handled correctly and show what the rest should look like: `structured_outputs.choice: []` gives `400 Choice '[]' cannot be an empty list`, `structured_outputs.grammar: ""` gives `400 structured_outputs.grammar cannot be an empty string`, a null schema gives `400 You must use one kind of structured output`, and a `structured_outputs.structural_tag` with a bad schema or two constraints at once are each a 400 that names the problem. **2. A self-referential `$ref` passes validation and then fails during generation.** ```json {"$ref": "#/$defs/n", "$defs": {"n": {"$ref": "#/$defs/n"}}} ``` `_validate_structured_outputs` accepts it (backend resolves to `xgrammar`). The request is admitted, scheduled, and then dies on its first token: ``` ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request for tokens 0. Please file an issue. ERROR [scheduler.py:1841] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [0] for request . Terminating request. ERROR [serving.py:173] Request failed with an internal error during generation POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error ``` The engine's own log asks for this report. The request occupies a slot and is terminated; the server stays healthy and later requests are served normally, so this is a correctness and diagnosability problem rather than an availability one. ### Reproduction ```python import httpx BASE, MODEL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000", "Qwen/Qwen3-8B" CASES = { "type is not a type": {"type": "not-a-type"}, "self-referential": {"$ref": "#/$defs/n", "$defs": {"n": {"$ref": "#/$defs/n"}}}, "dangling $ref": {"$ref": "#/$defs/missing"}, "empty enum": {"enum": []}, "pattern is not regex":{"type": "string", "pattern": "("}, } for name, schema in CASES.items(): r = httpx.post(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", timeout=120, json={ "model": MODEL, "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0.0, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "x", "schema": schema}}}) print(f"{name:22s} {r.status_code} {r.text[:120]}") ``` Every line prints 500. Expected: 400 with the validator's message. `repro_structured_output_malformed_schema_500.py` (attached, stdlib only) runs the malformed cases on both endpoints plus the self-referential `$ref` and the three well-handled controls,and exits 1 when any malformed request is answered with a 5xx. ### Expected behaviour 1. A structured-output specification the backend cannot compile is a client error: `400`, with the `ValueError` text the validator already produces, and `param` naming the field. 2. A schema that compiles into a grammar that rejects every token should be refused at validation time rather than terminating the request during generation. ### Where it comes from (By Claude) `validate_xgrammar_grammar` (`vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py`, the `raise ValueError(f"Failed to transform json schema into a grammar: {err}")` path) and the `auto` dispatch in `SamplingParams._validate_structured_outputs` (`vllm/sampling_params.py`) raise plain `ValueError`. The server registers `app.exception_handler(ValueError)(exception_handler)` as a fallback (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py`, "TODO: remove these fallback handlers after migration to VLLMError"), and that fallback is what produces the 500 with an empty message; `VLLMValidationError`, which the same file's handlers map to 400, is not used on this path. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Terminating request. ``` 151645 is `<|im_end|>`, the model's EOS. The same happens for a regex (`[0-9]{5}`) and a JSON schema, and on granite-4.0-h-tiny with its own EOS (`grammar rejected tokens [100257]`). In a 180-second run of 38,589 mixed structured requests on Qwen2.5-0.5B, **25,425 returned 500**: every `choice` (5,324 + 5,505 of as many), every `regex` that finished (5,547; 3,506 + 2,074 that hit `max_tokens` first), and 26 schemas that finished early (5,418 more ran into `max_tokens` and survived — a long output never emits EOS, which is how this hides). Unconstrained requests on the same server: 0 errors. The `guidance` backend on the same server configuration: 39,532 requests, 0 errors. The default `xgrammar`: 0 errors on 2026-09-18. ### Cause Reproducible without a GPU by driving vLLM's own `OutlinesGrammar` the way the engine does (`repro_outlines_backend_rejects_eos.py`, attached): ``` accept_tokens('yes') : True guide.is_finished(): True bitmask now allows : [151645] (eos allowed: True ) accept_tokens([eos]) : False <-- the engine reads False as 'grammar rejected tokens' and answers 500 ``` After the regex is matched, `outlines_core`'s `Guide` is finished; `fill_bitmask` then allows exactly one token, EOS, so the sampler emits EOS; and `OutlinesGrammar.accept_tokens([eos])` calls `Guide.accepts_tokens([eos])`, which returns False because the guide refuses any token once finished. `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_outlines.py` already carries a workaround for half of this — `is_terminated()` delays the finished flag by one step "so EOS can still be emitted" — but `accept_tokens` gets no such tolerance, and the scheduler treats its False as a rejection (`scheduler.py:1841`). A fix that matches the existing workaround: in `OutlinesGrammar.accept_tokens`, when the guide is already finished and the tokens are exactly `[eos]`, return True without advancing (the mask allowed nothing else, so nothing else can arrive). **_A related issue in `json_object`_** `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` under the outlines backend is accepted by the server and then fails inside the engine at `compile_grammar`,`ValueError: Invalid request type for Outlines backend (StructuredOutputOptions.JSON_OBJECT)`, which the client sees as a 500 (5,518 of 5,518 such requests in the same run). The backend does not support that request type; the request should be refused with a 400 at validation (`validate_structured_output_request_outlines`), not fail after admission. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
