Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks NIC Legend: NIC0: mlx5_0 ============================== Environment Variables ============================== PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_user ((vllm-27) ) gpu-a6-7:~$ ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Any Mamba-hybrid model whose `get_mamba_state_shape_from_config` does not pass `num_spec` fails to start when speculative decoding is enabled with `num_speculative_tokens >= 2`. The engine dies during startup with an `AssertionError` and no actionable message: ``` File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6540, in _init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling kv_cache_groups = get_kv_cache_groups(self.vllm_config, kv_cache_spec) File "vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py", line 1835, in get_kv_cache_groups filtered_spec = unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size(filtered_spec) File "vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py", line 1091, in unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size page_sizes = {layer.page_size_bytes for layer in kv_cache_spec.values()} File "vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py", line 725, in page_size_bytes assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size AssertionError RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. ``` Reproduce with the server: ```bash vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny --max-model-len 4096 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":2,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}' ``` or offline, which is the smaller reproducer: ```python from vllm import LLM LLM(model="ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny", max_model_len=4096, speculative_config={"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 2, "prompt_lookup_max": 4, "prompt_lookup_min": 2}) ``` `num_speculative_tokens=1` starts and generates correctly; `2` and above do not. Nothing about ngram is special, simply the method that needs no draft model. `repro_hybrid_spec_mamba_page_padding.py` (attached) is the offline form with `-k` and `--block-size` switches, so the three arms below (`-k 1` starts, `-k 2` asserts, `-k 2 --block-size 800` starts) are one script. ### Cause The padded mamba page size is planned from a state shape that does not carry the speculative widening, while the layer's own state shape does. * `Platform.check_and_update_config` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`) sizes `cache_config.mamba_page_size_padded` from `model_cls.get_mamba_state_shape_from_config(vllm_config)`. * For the affected models that classmethod calls `MambaStateShapeCalculator.mamba2_state_shape(...)` **without** `num_spec`, so the conv state is planned as `conv_kernel - 1` columns. * `MambaMixer2.get_state_shape()` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py`) passes `num_spec=self.num_spec`, so the real conv state is `conv_kernel - 1 + num_spec` columns. The real page is therefore wider than the planned one by `conv_dim * num_spec * itemsize`, and `MambaSpec.page_size_bytes` asserts. Whether it fires depends only on how much slack the padding happened to leave, which is why `num_speculative_tokens=1` slips through. On granite-4.0-h-tiny (bf16, TP=1): | | bytes | |---|---| | attention page (400 tokens × 2048 B) = planned padded mamba page | 819,200 | | mamba page at `num_spec=0` (conv 19,968 + ssm 786,432) | 806,400 | | incidental slack | 12,800 (1.59 %) | | added per speculative token (`conv_dim` 3,328 × 2 B) | 6,656 | | `num_spec=1` needs | 813,056 — fits | | `num_spec=2` needs | 819,712 — does not fit | Enlarging the attention page makes the same configuration start and generate correctly (`--block-size 800`, `num_speculative_tokens=2`, output identical to the `num_spec=1` run), which confirms that only the planned page size is wrong and the rest of the path is sound. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

So it is the *full* CUDA-graph capture (the Mamba / attention kernels inside the graph) at the one-token prefill shape; the piecewise graph and eager mode are both correct and are the workarounds. Independent of the mamba cache mode and of prefix caching. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Quick env recap: ``` vLLM 0.27.1, PyTorch 2.13+cu130, one NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GB), TP=1 Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, bf16 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-prompt-embeds --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 ``` On a server started with `--enable-prompt-embeds`, a batch of `prompt_embeds` completions that carry a **penalty** (`repetition_penalty`, `presence_penalty` or `frequency_penalty`) kills `EngineCore` with a CUDA device-side assert. Every in-flight and subsequent request gets `500 InternalServerError` and the server never recovers; the process must be restarted. ``` /__w/pytorch/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ScatterGatherKernel.cu:203: operator(): block: [2,0,0], thread: [25,0,0] Assertion `idx_dim >= 0 && idx_dim < index_size && "scatter gather kernel index out of bounds"' failed. ... File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 315, in get_output self.async_copy_ready_event.synchronize() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (EngineCore ...) EngineCore encountered a fatal error. vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. ``` Any client of a server whose operator enabled `--enable-prompt-embeds` can do this with one burst of ordinary requests, so it is a denial of service against the whole server, not one request. ### Reproduction Use this: [repro_prompt_embeds_penalties_engine_crash.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/5c70a3bb328eaf6d646b9d31e879dc4a#file-repro_prompt_embeds_penalties_engine_crash-py) `repro_prompt_embeds_penalties_engine_crash.py` (attached; `torch` + `safetensors` to build the embeddings, stdlib for HTTP) does this; the shape is small enough to state directly. Send ~16 concurrent `/v1/completions` requests whose prompt is an embedding tensor (`prompt_embeds` = base64 of `torch.save` of rows of the model's own `model.embed_tokens.weight`), **of two different lengths** (e.g. 900 and 300 tokens), each with ```json {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0.8, "repetition_penalty": 1.1, "presence_penalty": 0.4, "frequency_penalty": 0.3, "seed": 1} ``` The engine dies in the first round, every time (10 of 10 attempts across the runs below). **_Some ablation done by Claude:_** | arm | result | |---|---| | embeds requests + penalties, lengths 900 and 300, 16 concurrent | **dead in round 0** | | embeds + token requests mixed, penalties, varied lengths | **dead in round 0** | | embeds requests, `repetition_penalty` only | **dead in round 0** | | embeds requests, `presence_penalty` + `frequency_penalty` only | **dead in round 0** | | embeds 900 tokens, plain token prompts 300 tokens, penalties | **dead in round 0** | | embeds 300 tokens, plain token prompts 900 tokens, penalties | survived 6 rounds | | same load, greedy (no penalties, no log-probs, no `n`) | survived 6 rounds | | same load, penalties, **one** prompt length (all 300) | survived 6 rounds | | **token** prompts only (no `prompt_embeds`), penalties, varied lengths, same engine | survived 8 rounds | | token prompts only, penalties, engine without `--enable-prompt-embeds` | survived 8 rounds | | one request at a time (17 shapes: penalties, log-probs, `n=2`, stop, `min_tokens`, `bad_words`, `logit_bias`) | survived | | with and without `--enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 256` | dies either way | So it needs: `prompt_embeds` requests, a penalty, and a batch in which the **longest** prompt is an embeds one (that is the prompt that sets the batch's padding length). It does not need chunked prefill, does not need mixed token traffic, and never happens one request at a time. ### Where it looks like it comes from The only scatter over token ids in the sampler is the penalty bin count (`vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py`): ```python bin_counts = torch.zeros((num_seqs, vocab_size + 1), dtype=torch.long, device=tokens.device) bin_counts.scatter_add_(1, tokens, torch.ones_like(tokens)) ``` `tokens` comes from `InputBatch._make_prompt_token_ids_cpu_tensor()`, which reads `token_ids_cpu[:num_reqs, :max_prompt_len]` and pads each row past its own prompt length with `vocab_size`. For a `prompt_embeds` request, `InputBatch.add_request` never writes the prompt positions of that row (0.27.1 and `main` alike): ```python if request.prompt_token_ids is not None: self.token_ids_cpu[req_index, :num_prompt_tokens] = request.prompt_token_ids ... else: self.is_token_ids[req_index, :num_prompt_tokens] = False # nothing written to token_ids_cpu ``` `is_token_ids` records that those positions are not token ids, and the model-input path honours it (`safe_input_ids = torch.where(is_token_ids, input_ids, 0)` in `gpu_model_runner`), but the penalty tensor builder does not: it hands those positions to `scatter_add_` as if they were token ids. Whatever a previous occupant of that row left there (rows are reused as requests finish) is then used as an index, and the batch shape that decides how much of the row is read is `max_prompt_len` -- which is why the crash needs the embeds request to be the longest one in the batch, and why a single request never triggers it. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

### 🐛 Describe the bug On gfx1151, `torch.ops._rocm_C.paged_attention` accepts two configurations and returns incorrect results without an error: - With `alibi_slopes` supplied, the output matches attention **without ALiBi**. - With `block_size=32`, the output differs substantially from the reference for sequence lengths starting at 17 in the tested sweep. The same comparison passes with `block_size=16`. The gfx1x backend selection in `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention()` already excludes both configurations: it requires `alibi_slopes is None` and `block_size == 16`. This report concerns direct calls to the op; the normal backend path does not select these configurations. Testing was limited to gfx1151. **Expected:** Either compute the requested attention correctly or reject the unsupported configuration with a clear error. #### Reproduction and observed results Save the script below as `F2_F5_repro_navi_contract.py` and run it with `python F2_F5_repro_navi_contract.py` in a ROCm-enabled vLLM environment on gfx1151. It requires only PyTorch and vLLM; no model, test helpers, or external data are needed. The script uses bf16, one sequence, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, and head size 128. For the block-size comparison, valid Q/K/V values are identical across block sizes and unused cache slots are zero. Errors are maximum absolute differences from the attention reference; `reference_scale` is the maximum absolute reference output. Actual output on `main` (`39e33db7f3`): ```text ALiBi: block_size=16, seq_len=32 error vs ALiBi=0.075806, vs no ALiBi=0.000061, reference scale=0.078613 Block size comparison (no ALiBi) seq_len error_bs16 error_bs32 reference_scale 15 0.000122 0.000122 0.050537 16 0.000000 0.000000 0.052490 17 0.000000 0.010010 0.051514 28 0.000000 0.029053 0.028320 32 0.000061 0.028259 0.029785 33 0.000122 0.021820 0.028198 64 0.000061 0.025238 0.021118 100 0.000061 0.014587 0.017334 ``` With ALiBi supplied, the kernel matches the no-ALiBi reference within rounding. With block size 32, the first failing length in this sweep is 17, still within the first 32-token block. Its errors are comparable to the output magnitude, while block size 16 matches within rounding.
Standalone reproduction script ```python """Run with: python F2_F5_repro_navi_contract.py (ROCm vLLM on gfx1151).""" import torch import vllm from vllm import _custom_ops as ops from vllm.platforms import current_platform assert current_platform.is_rocm() and torch.cuda.is_available() assert hasattr(torch.ops._rocm_C, "paged_attention") print(f"vLLM={vllm.__version__}, torch={torch.__version__}") print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)) def run(block_size, seq_len, use_alibi=False): torch.manual_seed(1) device, dtype = "cuda", torch.bfloat16 nq, nkv, hs = 32, 8, 128 scale = hs ** -0.5 blocks = (seq_len + block_size - 1) // block_size # Generate logical tokens first, then pack them into the op's cache layout. # This keeps valid Q/K/V identical across block sizes; padding is zero. q = torch.empty((1, nq, hs), device=device, dtype=dtype).uniform_(-scale, scale) k = torch.empty((seq_len, nkv, hs), device=device, dtype=dtype).uniform_(-scale, scale) v = torch.empty_like(k).uniform_(-scale, scale) x = 16 // q.element_size() kc = torch.zeros((blocks, nkv, hs // x, block_size, x), device=device, dtype=dtype) vc = torch.zeros((blocks, nkv, hs, block_size), device=device, dtype=dtype) for t in range(seq_len): kc[t // block_size, :, :, t % block_size, :] = k[t].reshape(nkv, hs // x, x) vc[t // block_size, :, :, t % block_size] = v[t] bt = torch.arange(blocks, device=device, dtype=torch.int32).view(1, -1) lens = torch.tensor([seq_len], device=device, dtype=torch.int32) slopes = torch.linspace(0.1, 1.0, nq, device=device) if use_alibi else None partitions = (seq_len + 255) // 256 tmp = torch.empty((1, nq, partitions, hs), device=device, dtype=dtype) sums = torch.empty((1, nq, partitions), device=device, dtype=torch.float32) maxima = torch.empty_like(sums) one = torch.tensor(1.0, device=device) out = torch.empty_like(q) ops.paged_attention_rocm( out, sums, maxima, tmp, q, kc, vc, nkv, scale, bt, lens, None, block_size, seq_len, slopes, "auto", one, one, ) # Same attention math as the upstream reference, with no test-module imports. keys = k.repeat_interleave(nq // nkv, dim=1) values = v.repeat_interleave(nq // nkv, dim=1) logits = torch.einsum("qhd,khd->hqk", q, keys).float() * scale def reference(alibi): scores = logits if alibi is not None: positions = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device) - seq_len + 1 scores = scores + alibi[:, None, None] * positions[None, None, :] weights = scores.softmax(dim=-1).to(dtype) return torch.einsum("hqk,khd->qhd", weights, values) ref = reference(slopes) err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item() no_alibi_err = (out.float() - reference(None).float()).abs().max().item() return err, no_alibi_err, ref.abs().max().item() print("\nALiBi: block_size=16, seq_len=32") err, no_alibi_err, scale = run(16, 32, True) print(f"error vs ALiBi={err:.6f}, vs no ALiBi={no_alibi_err:.6f}, reference scale={scale:.6f}") print("\nBlock size comparison (no ALiBi)") print("seq_len error_bs16 error_bs32 reference_scale") for length in (15, 16, 17, 28, 32, 33, 64, 100): err16, _, scale = run(16, length) err32, _, _ = run(32, length) print(f"{length:7d} {err16:.6f} {err32:.6f} {scale:.6f}") ```
#### Relevant code and suggested fix In `csrc/rocm/attention.cu`, `CALL_CUSTOM_LAUNCHER` forwards `alibi_slopes` to `paged_attention_custom_launcher_navi`, but that launcher sets `alibi_slopes_ptr = nullptr`, with the comment `NOTE: Navi does not support alibi_slopes`. The Navi path also accepts block size 32. If these configurations are unsupported, add checks in the Navi launcher matching the backend's existing restrictions: ```cpp TORCH_CHECK(!alibi_slopes.has_value(), "paged_attention_rocm: alibi_slopes is not implemented for gfx11/gfx12"); TORCH_CHECK(BLOCK_SIZE == 16, "paged_attention_rocm: only block_size 16 is implemented for gfx11/gfx12"); ``` If block size 32 is intended to be supported, its numerical results need a fix instead. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : AOSC OS (x86_64) GCC version : (GCC) 15.3.0 20260612 (AOSC OS) Clang version : 23.0.0git CMake version : version 3.31.10 Libc version : glibc-2.42 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0a20260424 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : N/A ROCM used to build PyTorch : 7.13.26162 XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.15 (main, Sep 1 2026, 14:18:08) [Clang 22.1.3 ] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.1.7-aosc-main-x86_64-with-glibc2.42 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : Could not collect CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to : GPU models and configuration : Radeon 8060S Graphics (gfx1151) Nvidia driver version : Could not collect cuDNN version : Could not collect HIP runtime version : 7.13.26162 MIOpen runtime version : 3.5.1 Is XNNPACK available : True ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 32 Model name: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S Thread(s) per core: 2 Core(s) per socket: 16 (remaining lscpu lines omitted) ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] numpy==2.5.3 [pip3] pyzmq==27.2.0 [pip3] torch==2.11.0+rocm7.13.0a20260424 [pip3] torchvision==0.26.0+rocm7.13.0a20260424 [pip3] transformers==5.17.0 [pip3] triton==3.6.0+rocm7.13.0a20260424 [conda] Could not collect ============================== vLLM Info ============================== ROCM Version : 7.13.26162-1140233ffe vLLM Version : 0.26.1.dev0+g568afb3a1.d20260917 (git sha: 568afb3a1, date: 20260917) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Enabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: (single GPU) ============================== Environment Variables ============================== NVCC_THREADS=1 PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151 MAX_JOBS=32 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_canarypwn ```
Additional context on the environment: - vLLM is tag `v0.26.0` (`568afb3a1`) built from source with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151`, against the TheRock per-arch wheels from `https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx1151/` (torch / triton / `rocm-sdk-*` 7.13.0a20260424, all inside the venv; no system ROCm involved). - One local source change was needed to make the build link: a ROCm `atomicAdd(__half2*)` / `atomicAdd(__half*)` shim in `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/gptq/q_gemm.cu` (separate issue). GPTQ kernels are never executed in this bf16 run, so it cannot influence anything below. - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, bf16 safetensors (head_dim 128, 32 query heads / 8 KV heads, no sliding window). ### 🐛 Describe the bug On gfx1151, repeatedly sending the same greedy request after filler requests of varying lengths produces different text and token logprobs with `ROCM_ATTN`, the automatically selected backend. This happens with `max_num_seqs=1`, `enforce_eager=True`, and prefix caching disabled. With `attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN"`, the same script produces identical text and checked logprobs in all 20 trials. The difference shows up during decode: `logprob[5]` varies, while the first generated token's logprob, computed during prefill, is identical in every trial on both backends. Where the text diverges, the top two candidates (`' Germany'` and `' Spain'`) both have a reported logprob of −0.7841 when rounded to four decimal places. A small numerical difference can therefore change which token greedy decoding selects. ### Minimal reproduction ```python """Fails with AssertionError on ROCM_ATTN, passes with TRITON_ATTN. usage: python repro.py [ATTENTION_BACKEND]""" import collections, random, sys from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams model = sys.argv[1] kw = {"attention_backend": sys.argv[2]} if len(sys.argv) > 2 else {} # default = ROCM_ATTN on gfx1151 llm = LLM(model=model, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=8192, max_num_seqs=1, gpu_memory_utilization=0.45, enforce_eager=True, enable_prefix_caching=False, **kw) greedy = dict(temperature=0.0, top_k=1, seed=7) probe = SamplingParams(max_tokens=16, logprobs=2, **greedy) filler = SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, **greedy) random.seed(11) lp0, lp5, texts = [], [], [] for _ in range(20): # a "filler" request of varying length, then the fixed probe request llm.generate(["filler " * random.choice([1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, 64, 128])], filler, use_tqdm=False) out = llm.generate(["The capital of France is"], probe, use_tqdm=False)[0].outputs[0] lp0.append(out.logprobs[0][out.token_ids[0]].logprob) # first generated token: prefill-driven lp5.append(out.logprobs[5][out.token_ids[5]].logprob) # decode step 5 texts.append(out.text) def show(name, xs): print(f"distinct {name}: {len(set(xs))}") for v, c in collections.Counter(xs).most_common(): print(f" {c:>3}x {v!r}") show("logprob[0] (prefill-driven)", lp0) show("logprob[5] (decode step 5)", lp5) show("completions", texts) assert len(set(lp0)) == 1, "prefill unstable too - different bug" assert len(set(lp5)) == 1 and len(set(texts)) == 1, ( f"decode output of an identical greedy request depends on the previous request: " f"{len(set(lp5))} distinct logprob[5], {len(set(texts))} distinct completions " f"(max_num_seqs=1, enforce_eager, prefix caching off)") print("OK: 20/20 identical") ``` ### Observed `python repro.py Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (default backend) → exit code 1: ``` INFO [rocm.py:615] Found incompatible backend(s) [TURBOQUANT] with AttentionType.DECODER. Overriding with ROCM_ATTN out of potential backends: ['ROCM_ATTN', 'TRITON_ATTN']. ... distinct logprob[0] (prefill-driven): 1 20x -0.6213843822479248 distinct logprob[5] (decode step 5): 4 16x -1.3890184164047241 2x -1.381217360496521 1x -1.3818659782409668 1x -1.3905384540557861 distinct completions: 2 14x ' Paris. The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of Germany is Berlin.' 6x ' Paris. The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of Spain is Madrid.' Traceback (most recent call last): File "repro.py", line 36, in assert len(set(lp5)) == 1 and len(set(texts)) == 1, ( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ AssertionError: decode output of an identical greedy request depends on the previous request: 4 distinct logprob[5], 2 distinct completions (max_num_seqs=1, enforce_eager, prefix caching off) ``` `python repro.py Qwen/Qwen3-8B TRITON_ATTN` → exit code 0: ``` INFO [rocm.py:570] Using TRITON_ATTN backend (selected via --attention-backend). ... distinct logprob[0] (prefill-driven): 1 20x -0.6213843822479248 distinct logprob[5] (decode step 5): 1 20x -1.388966679573059 distinct completions: 1 20x ' Paris. The capital of Italy is Rome. The capital of Germany is Berlin.' OK: 20/20 identical ``` Results from the 20-trial runs: | | distinct `logprob[0]` (prefill) | distinct `logprob[5]` (decode) | distinct completions | |-----------------------------------------|---|---|---| | **`ROCM_ATTN`** (auto-selected default) | 1 | **4** | **2** (14× / 6×) | | **`TRITON_ATTN`** | 1 | **1** (20/20) | **1** (20/20) | ### Expected With this configuration, I expect repeating the same greedy request to return the same text and token logprobs, regardless of the preceding request. That is what I observe with `TRITON_ATTN`. ### Additional checks - **Offline and HTTP APIs:** Runs through `/v1/completions` on 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-18 produced the same four `logprob[5]` values and two completions with `ROCM_ATTN`. All 20 trials matched with `TRITON_ATTN`, as in the offline results above. - **Streaming:** In a separate run of eight non-streamed requests followed by eight streamed requests, all streamed outputs matched; one non-streamed output differed. The issue also occurs without streaming. - **First generated token:** `logprob[0]` was identical in every trial on both backends. This check does not establish that all prefill results are identical. - **Execution settings:** All runs used `enforce_eager=True`, `max_num_seqs=1`, and `enable_prefix_caching=False`. - **Logprobs:** The difference is measurable even when the text matches: `logprob[5]` takes four distinct values across the two completions. ### Decode code path For this configuration (`block_size=16`, `head_dim=128`, GQA ratio 4, bf16, `kv_cache_dtype="auto"`), `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention()` in `vllm/platforms/rocm.py` returns True on gfx1x. The logs contain no `"Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation"` message. Based on that selection logic, decode uses `ops.paged_attention_rocm` from `_rocm_C`, through `paged_attention_custom_launcher_navi` in `csrc/rocm/attention.cu`. `_rocm_C` is built only when `VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "HIP"` (`CMakeLists.txt:1360`). I have not investigated the kernel implementation or identified the cause. In an HTTP run on 2026-09-17, I sent the same probe after each filler request listed below. The results suggest an effect from prior requests, though filler length alone does not consistently predict the output: | preceding request | completion's 3rd clause | `logprob[0]` | `logprob[5]` | |---|---|---|---| | none (fresh server) | …Germany is Berlin | `-0.6213843822479248` | `-1.3890184164047241` | | 1-word filler | …Germany is Berlin | `-0.6213843822479248` | `-1.3890184164047241` | | **8-word filler** | **…Spain is Madrid** | `-0.6213843822479248` | **`-1.3905384540557861`** | | 64-word filler | …Germany is Berlin | `-0.6213843822479248` | `-1.3890184164047241` | | 8-word filler | …Spain is Madrid | `-0.6213843822479248` | `-1.3905384540557861` | | 1-word filler | …Germany is Berlin | `-0.6213843822479248` | `-1.3890184164047241` | | 8-word filler | …Spain is Madrid | `-0.6213843822479248` | `-1.3905384540557861` | After restarting the server, the same sequence produced four distinct logprob values instead of two. After 512- and 2000-word fillers, the first probe changed completion; subsequent probes then returned a stable completion. ### Not tested I have only tested gfx1151 with the configuration above. I have not tested CDNA (gfx9), `max_num_seqs > 1`, graph capture or compiled execution, other models or head sizes, or fp8 KV cache. ### Selecting the Triton backend Use `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` or `LLM(attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN")` to run the comparison. `VLLM_USE_TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` was removed in #27611 and has no effect in v0.26. Setting it logs `WARNING [envs.py:2096] Unknown vLLM environment variable detected: VLLM_USE_TRITON_FLASH_ATTN`; the engine still selects `ROCM_ATTN` on this machine. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug When `<|action_start|>` is split across streaming chunks, the `internlm` parser emits part of the marker as content and never returns the tool call. Non-streaming parsing of the same text succeeds. **Expected:** Return the same tool call regardless of chunk boundaries, without exposing the marker as content. #### Observed result | Input | Tool call | Content | |---|---|---| | 8-character chunks | None | `'<|action'` | | 1-character chunks | None | `'<|action_start|'` | | Non-streaming | `get_weather` with `{"city": "Paris"}` | `''` | #### Related reports [#48347](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48347) and its proposed fix [#48348](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48348) cover missing arguments when the whole call arrives in one delta. This report is limited to the split-marker case, where the entire call is lost. The reproducer below tests only 8- and 1-character chunks. #### Reproduce Runs without a server or model weights. Downloads the Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer. Save the script as `internlm-token-deltas-lose-tool-call.py` and run with `vllm==0.29.0` installed. ```bash python internlm-token-deltas-lose-tool-call.py ```
Reproducer script ```python import sys, warnings from unittest.mock import MagicMock warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager TOK = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") # any tokenizer; parser is text-based TEXT = '<|action_start|><|plugin|>{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}<|action_end|>' Parser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("internlm") request = MagicMock(); request.tools = None def stream(step): """Feed TEXT in fixed-size deltas and reassemble what a client would see.""" p = Parser(TOK) names, args, content, prev = {}, {}, "", "" for i in range(0, len(TEXT), step): cur = TEXT[: i + step] d = p.extract_tool_calls_streaming(prev, cur, TEXT[i : i + step], [], [], [], request) prev = cur if d is None: continue content += d.content or "" for tc in d.tool_calls or []: if tc.function.name: names[tc.index] = tc.function.name if tc.function.arguments: args[tc.index] = args.get(tc.index, "") + tc.function.arguments return names, args, content one_shot = Parser(TOK).extract_tool_calls(TEXT, request) print("non-streaming:", [(c.function.name, c.function.arguments) for c in one_shot.tool_calls]) bad = False for step in (8, 1): names, args, content = stream(step) ok = names == {0: "get_weather"} and args.get(0) == '{"city": "Paris"}' and content == "" bad |= not ok print(f"delta = {step:>2} chars: names={names} arguments={args} content={content!r} {'ok' if ok else '<-- WRONG'}") sys.exit(1 if bad else 0) ```
#### Cause In `internlm2_tool_parser.py:67–76`, `self.position` advances while the opening marker is incomplete. With one-character chunks, it reaches position 15, inside the marker. Subsequent searches start there and never find the full `<|action_start|><|plugin|>` prefix. Buffer partial marker prefixes instead of emitting them and advancing past them. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Weight-loading/repacking memory is not reclaimed on discrete GPUs, forcing lower max-num-seqs / max-num-batched-tokens (Kimi K3, B200, fastsafetensors + DeepEP v2)
body:
### Your current environment



- vLLM `v0.28.0`, `vllm/vllm-openai` container image
- 2–4 nodes x 8x NVIDIA **B200 SXM** (discrete GPU, 180 GB), GKE + LeaderWorkerSet
- Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (`mxfp4`), `--load-format fastsafetensors`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`
- Parallelism: TP4/TP8 + DP + `--enable-expert-parallel` (EP16 / EP32)
- All-to-all backends tested: **DeepEP v2** and NCCL (gIB RoCE)
- `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`
- Also reproduced with speculative decoding (draft model `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`)



### 🐛 Describe the bug


On discrete GPUs, memory used during weight loading and `process_weights_after_loading` is retained inside PyTorch's caching allocator pool (`reserved - allocated`) rather than returned to the CUDA driver before the engine initializes communication buffers, profiles KV cache, or loads secondary models. In practice this causes startup OOM or forces significantly lower batch capacity.

**Observed behavior (reproducible):**

1. **2-node DeepEP v2 (`TP8_DP2_EP16`)** — with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`, `--max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192` OOMs during startup. Without a patch, we have to clamp parameters down to `--max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80`, which severely limits throughput.
2. **Speculative decoding (target `Kimi-K3` + draft `Kimi-K3-DSpark`, both via `fastsafetensors`)** — exhibits the same startup memory exhaustion pressure.
3. **With a 4-line memory cleanup patch injected into `process_weights_after_loading`, both workloads start cleanly and allow raising `--max-num-seqs` / `--max-num-batched-tokens` back up to `256 / 8192`:**

```python
def process_weights_after_loading(
    model: nn.Module, model_config: ModelConfig, target_device: torch.device
) -> None:
    import gc
    gc.collect()
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    ...
```

### Empirical VRAM Measurements (2x 8×B200 nodes, `TP8_DP2_EP16`, `v0.28.0`)

We instrumented `BaseModelLoader.load_model()` (`vllm/model_executor/model_loader/base_loader.py`) on 2x 8×B200 hosts (`178.351 GiB` total HBM per GPU) running `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (`mxfp4`) + `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` with `--load-format fastsafetensors`:

| Model / Boundary | Arm A: Unpatched (`reserved_GiB` / `resv - alloc`) | Arm A: **`driver_free_GiB`** (`cudaMemGetInfo`) | Arm B: With `gc.collect() + empty_cache()` (`EMPTYCACHE_RETURNED`) | Arm B: **`driver_free_GiB`** (`cudaMemGetInfo`) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **`Kimi-K3`: `05_before_load_weights`** | `129.352 GiB` (`0.286 GiB`) | `46.338 GiB` | `129.352 GiB` (`0.000 GiB`) | `46.338 GiB` |
| **`Kimi-K3`: `10_immediately_after_load_weights`** | `169.691 GiB` (**`40.626 GiB`**) | **`5.537 GiB`** | `129.352 GiB` (**`+40.342 GiB` freed**) | **`45.879 GiB`** |
| **`Kimi-K3`: `30_after_repack` (`mxfp4`)** | `174.734 GiB` (**`45.611 GiB`**) | **`0.494 GiB (494 MB!)`** | `129.365 GiB` (**`+5.141 GiB` freed**) | **`45.865 GiB`** |
| **`DSpark`: `10_immediately_after_load_weights`** | `141.395 GiB` (`10.335 GiB`) | `33.834 GiB` | `131.305 GiB` (**`+10.039 GiB` freed**) | **`43.925 GiB`** |

Key empirical findings on Rank 0 (`dev=0`):
- Immediately after `Kimi-K3` `load_weights()`, **`40.626 GiB`** of unallocated HBM is stranded in PyTorch's caching allocator pool (`reserved - allocated`), dropping CUDA driver free memory (`driver_free_GiB`) from `46.338 GiB` to **`5.537 GiB`**.
- After `process_weights_after_loading()` (`mxfp4` weight repacking), `reserved - allocated` grows to **`45.611 GiB`**, leaving **only `0.494 GiB` (494 MB)** of free CUDA driver memory on a 180 GB B200 GPU. Calling `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` at these boundaries returns **`40.342 GiB + 5.141 GiB = 45.483 GiB`** directly to the CUDA driver, restoring `driver_free_GiB` to **`45.865 GiB`**.

### Hypotheses on why this causes OOM in DeepEP v2 & Speculative Decoding

1. **Driver-level allocations cannot use PyTorch's cache pool (`reserved - allocated`).** While subsequent *PyTorch* tensor allocations (`torch.empty`) can reuse cached blocks or trigger PyTorch's internal slow-path `release_cached_blocks()` on `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation`, raw CUDA driver allocations (`cuMemCreate` / DMA-BUF registration used by **DeepEP v2** `_C.ElasticBuffer`, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`, or C++/CUDA extensions) query the CUDA driver directly. When `driver_free_GiB` is **494 MB (`0.494 GiB`)** after `30_after_repack`, any raw driver allocation larger than 494 MB fails with `OutOfMemoryError` even though **45.61 GiB** is sitting idle in PyTorch's cache.
2. **`release_device_memory_under_pressure()` is a no-op on discrete GPUs.** PR #45179 added this helper inside `process_weights_after_loading()` to flush repacking transients, but `vllm/utils/mem_utils.py` guards it with `not current_platform.is_integrated_gpu(device.index)`, so it returns `False` immediately on discrete GPUs (H100/B200).
3. **Interaction with PR #55985.** PR #55985 derives the `fastsafetensors` staging budget from `current_platform.mem_get_info()` (`cudaMemGetInfo`). If `_fastsafetensors_memory_budget()` is called while tens of GiBs are trapped in `reserved - allocated` (e.g., when loading a second/draft model or after prior allocations), `mem_get_info()` understates available HBM and could cause the fit planner to raise `BudgetInfeasibleError` prematurely.

### Proposed direction

Add deterministic reclamation at the two lifecycle boundaries in `BaseModelLoader.load_model()` (`vllm/model_executor/model_loader/base_loader.py`):
- After `self.load_weights(...)`, before `process_weights_after_loading(...)`
- After `process_weights_after_loading(...)`, before KV cache profiling / CUDA graph capture / secondary model loading

```python
gc.collect()
if current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
```

`load_model()` runs once per engine startup (~ms overhead) and reclaims **45.5 GiB** of raw driver headroom per B200 GPU.

title: [Bug]: --fingerprint-mode=none still emits "system_fingerprint": null in non-streaming responses
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `--fingerprint-mode=none`, the `system_fingerprint` value is correctly suppressed, but the key itself is still present in non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` responses, serialized as an explicit `null`:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --fingerprint-mode none

curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "<model>", "stream": false, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]}'
```

Response contains:

```json
{
  "id": "chatcmpl-...",
  "system_fingerprint": null,
  ...
}
```

Expected behavior: with `--fingerprint-mode=none`, the `system_fingerprint` key should be omitted entirely from the response body, matching what "the field is omitted" suggests in the `--fingerprint-mode` help text.

Root cause: `none` mode makes `get_system_fingerprint()` return `None`, but non-streaming responses are serialized with `generator.model_dump()` in
`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/api_router.py`
without `exclude_none=True`, so the `None` value is emitted as an explicit JSON `null`. (Streaming paths use `exclude_unset=True`/`exclude_none=True` and are not affected.)

This matters for clients doing strict schema conformance checks against the OpenAI spec, and for deployments that want minimal response surface. Note that unconditional omission would be a breaking change for the OpenAI Python SDK (`extra="allow"` turns absent keys into `AttributeError`), as discussed in #53349 — so any fix should either be opt-in (e.g. extending the approach of #53832 to cover `system_fingerprint`) or scoped to `none` mode only, where the user has explicitly asked for the field to be disabled.

title: [Performance]: Streaming derender bypasses renderer thread pool and blocks the event loop
body:
### Your current environment

- vllm version: v0.28.0
- Architecture: AArch64
- Deployment: vLLM Render as a sidecar
- Request type: streaming Chat Completions
- Concurrent requests: 20
- Output length: up to 2048 tokens
- `--renderer-num-workers`: tested with both `4` and `8`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Streaming Derender appears to perform CPU-bound detokenization directly on the FastAPI event loop instead of using the renderer thread pool.

Under concurrent streaming workloads, this serializes Derender processing, increases per-chunk latency, delays tokenization requests, and propagates backpressure to the inference engine.

This looks related to, but not fully covered by, [#49396](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49396), which offloaded existing Derender CPU work to the renderer thread pool.

## Observed implementation

The non-streaming Derender paths use asynchronous wrappers backed by the renderer executor.

However, the streaming paths call synchronous detokenization directly from async code:

- `OnlineDerenderer.derender_chat_stream()`
- `OnlineDerenderer.derender_completion_stream()`
- `_detokenize_delta()`

As a result, increasing `--renderer-num-workers` does not improve streaming Derender throughput.

## Benchmark results

| Metric | 4 workers | 8 workers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate throughput | 889.1 tok/s | 899.5 tok/s |
| Per-stream throughput p50 | 46.3 tok/s | 46.0 tok/s |
| Derender RPC latency p50 | 21.35 ms | 21.52 ms |
| Chunk cadence p50 | 21.49 ms | 21.66 ms |
| Tokenize latency p50 | 153.8 ms | 155.4 ms |

Compared with the Render-disabled baseline:

| Metric | Render disabled | Streaming Render |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Aggregate throughput | 1011.6 tok/s | 889.1 tok/s |
| Per-stream throughput p50 | 53.1 tok/s | 46.3 tok/s |
| TTFT p50 | 166 ms | 167 ms |
| TTOT p50 | 18.70 ms | 21.26 ms |

The workload completed successfully without request errors.

## Additional timing evidence

For the streaming Derender consumer:

| Measurement | p50 |
| --- | ---: |
| Derender RPC time | 21.35 ms |
| RPC plus local processing | 21.40 ms |
| Chunk consumption cadence | 21.49 ms |
| Queue wait time | 0.15 ms |

The timing approximately satisfies:

```text
chunk cadence
~= queue wait + Derender processing
~= Derender RPC latency
```

This indicates that the streaming consumption loop is paced almost entirely by the synchronous Derender request.

The same RPC takes approximately 3.2 ms under light load but approximately 21.4 ms at concurrency 20, indicating event-loop saturation and queuing.

## Additional context: token-only Generate does not provide batch streaming

The token-only `/inference/v1/generate` endpoint currently handles one prompt or sequence per request. Therefore, a multi-prompt Completion request must be fanned out into multiple independent Generate streams.

Each generated stream maintains its own Derender `stream_state` and invokes the streaming Derender endpoint for every chunk:

```text
multi-prompt request
  -> N Generate streams
  -> N independent Derender states
  -> one Derender request per generated chunk
```

This is not the direct cause of the event-loop blocking issue, which is also reproducible with concurrent single-prompt requests. However, the lack of a batch Generate interface amplifies the problem because the number of concurrent per-chunk Derender calls grows with the number of generated sequences.

It may be useful to clarify whether batch token-only Generate is planned. Regardless of that direction, streaming Derender should avoid performing CPU-bound work directly on the shared event loop.

## Expected behavior

Streaming Derender CPU work should use the renderer's shared executor, consistent with the approach introduced by [#49396](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49396).

Increasing `--renderer-num-workers` should provide additional concurrency for streaming Derender and prevent Derender work from blocking Tokenize requests on the same event loop.

## Suggested direction

Consider offloading the CPU-bound part of streaming Derender to the existing renderer executor, while preserving the current async streaming API and client-carried `stream_state`.

Conceptually:

```python
result = await make_async(
    streaming_derender_cpu_work,
    executor=renderer._executor,
)(generate_chunk, stream_state)
```

The exact executor boundary may need to include parser replay and incremental detokenization so that all CPU-bound work is removed from the event loop.

Batch token-only Generate could reduce the number of independent RPC streams, but it should be treated as a separate enhancement rather than a prerequisite for fixing the event-loop blocking issue.

## Related work

- [#49396: Offload Derender CPU work to the renderer thread pool](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49396)
- [#47161: Streaming Derender RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161)

Could you confirm whether streaming Derender is expected to use the renderer executor, or whether another concurrency mechanism is planned for this path?

title: [Bug]: TieringOffloadingSpec leaks /dev/shm mmap files on non-graceful shutdown (barrier-unlink fix from #52596 not applied)
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Description PR #52596 fixed `SharedOffloadRegion` so the backing `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_{engine_id}.mmap` file is unlinked immediately after all workers have mapped it (via a `barrier` callback), so the kernel reclaims the memory on process exit regardless of how the process exits (including `SIGKILL` or a non-graceful container restart). However, this fix was only wired up in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py` (`CPUOffloadingSpec.create_worker`), which passes `barrier=_all_workers_barrier`. The `TieringOffloadingSpec` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/spec.py`) creates **two** `SharedOffloadRegion` instances — the scheduler-side region (`get_manager`) and the worker-side region (`create_worker`) — **neither passes a `barrier`**. As a result, these regions still rely solely on the old `cleanup()`-on-graceful-shutdown path, and the `.mmap` file is leaked in `/dev/shm` whenever the engine process is killed non-gracefully (e.g. `SIGKILL`, OOM-kill, or a container restart that doesn't fully drain the graceful-shutdown signal chain). ### Impact In a Kubernetes deployment using `medium: Memory` `emptyDir` for `/dev/shm` (shared at the Pod level, not the container level), restarting just the model container (without recreating the Pod) leaves the old engine's offload region file behind. The next engine startup generates a new `engine_id`/mmap file and needs the *full* configured offload size again, so `/dev/shm` free space is effectively halved (or exhausted) after every non-graceful restart, causing: RuntimeError: Insufficient space in /dev/shm: 131072 MiB required, 32768 MiB free. ### Reproduction - `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":137438953472,"offload_prompt_only":false}}'` - Send `SIGKILL` (or `kill -9`) to the EngineCore process (or otherwise bypass the graceful shutdown path). - Observe `/dev/shm/vllm_offload_.mmap` still present after the process exits. ``` ls -lh total 128G -rw------- 1 root root 128G Sep 17 05:00 vllm_offload_a2d4948b-0aab-4fec-8e44-8de823cd614d.mmap ``` - Restart the engine; it fails or has drastically reduced `/dev/shm` headroom due to the leaked file. ### Suggested fix Wire up a `barrier` callback (similar to `_all_workers_barrier` in `cpu/spec.py`) for both `SharedOffloadRegion` instantiations in `tiering/spec.py` (`get_manager`'s `scheduler_mmap` and `create_worker`'s `worker_mmap`), so the eager-unlink-after-barrier behavior from #52596 applies uniformly to `TieringOffloadingSpec` as well. ### Environment - vLLM version: v0.29.0 (also reproduced against latest `main` @ `0bfc7a15d0`) - Deployment: Kubernetes, `/dev/shm` backed by Pod-level `emptyDir(medium: Memory) ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug _Env:_ - vLLM 0.27.1 (pip wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Linux 5.15. - One RTX 4090 (sm_89); also seen on H100 (sm_90). - Models: `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` (hybrid Mamba2 + MoE) and `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct` (`FalconH1ForCausalLM`, 90M, **dense**), both bf16. The second shows the identical three-way pattern, so MoE routing is not involved. - Offline API, no server involved. One `LLM`, one `generate()` over the same eight prompts in the same order, repeated four times, with the prefix cache reset between calls so every call does the same work rather than reading back the previous one's. The outputs are not the same: ``` call 0 vs 1, prompt 1: first differs at token 5: 16 vs 24 call 0 vs 2, prompt 2: first differs at token 5: 24 vs 16 call 0 vs 3, prompt 1: first differs at token 5: 16 vs 24 ``` Same process, same weights, same batch members in the same order, greedy sampling (`temperature=0.0`). Reproducer attached as `repro_mamba_cache_mode_nondeterminism.py`; it takes about twenty seconds. Root cause should be `mamba_cache_mode`, not the rounding, see below: | configuration | prefills split? | four calls of the same batch | |---|---|---| | default (prefix caching on, so `mamba_cache_mode="all"`), budget 1,024 | yes | **differ** | | same, budget 4,096 | yes | **differ** | | same, budget 32,768 | **no** | identical every call | | `enable_prefix_caching=False` (so `mamba_cache_mode="none"`) | yes | identical every call | | `mamba_cache_mode="align"` | yes | identical every call | | `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype="float32"` | yes | **differ** | Two conditions are needed together: a prefill **split across scheduler steps**, and `mamba_cache_mode="all"`. Removing either makes the batch reproducible. (At a 32,768 budget nothing is split and the outputs are stable, so this needs chunked prefill, on by default, and prompts long enough to be chunked.) ### Also visible at the server level Found originally by a workload fuzzer replaying the same trace against a server several times and comparing runs whose scheduling matched exactly. Over 1,500 iterations the plain configuration produced 20 pairs of runs that shared the scheduler's whole step-by-step composition — same batch members, same scheduled token counts, same chunk boundaries — and produced different tokens. `--mamba-cache-mode align` produced 0 in 700 iterations; `--max-num-seqs 1` produced 0 in 1,103 and `--max-num-seqs 2` produced 0 in 470, so it needs more than two sequences in flight. The same runs also agreed on every per-layer field the worker records (attention backend, cascade path and shared-prefix length, split count, sequence lengths, `cu_seqlens`, layout, dtype) across 1,525 compared steps, so it is not a different kernel being selected. The server-level observation above was repeated as a two-arm experiment in which the cache mode is the only difference. Two `granite-4.0-h-tiny` engines on two RTX 4090s of one machine, same 4,096-token context, same workload and seed, same `--max-num-seqs 16` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, prefix caching and the hybrid KV manager on both, 45 minutes each: | | default (`"all"`) | `--mamba-cache-mode align` | |---|---|---| | iterations | 430 | 415 | | runs that differed under a **matched** scheduler composition | **108** | **0** | | probes where every request was identical across replays | 1 | **56** | **One caveat for anyone reproducing this: the two modes do not get the same KV pool at the same `--gpu-memory-utilization`.** `"align"` pads the mamba page by 1.59% where `"all"` pads by 30.03%, and the attention page differs (400 vs 512 tokens), so on the same card `"align"` was allocated **286,013 tokens against 80,998** — 3.5x more. Since a roomier pool means less eviction pressure, that difference flatters `"align"` on its own. The arms above were therefore pinned with `--num-gpu-blocks-override` to 81,049 and 81,072 tokens, 0.03% apart, both reporting a maximum concurrency of 19.79x. Comparing these modes by equalising memory rather than tokens measures the pool as much as the mode. ### Reproduce ``` python repro_mamba_cache_mode_nondeterminism.py ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny 8 4 out.json 1024 on # differs python repro_mamba_cache_mode_nondeterminism.py ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny 8 4 out.json 1024 off # identical python repro_mamba_cache_mode_nondeterminism.py ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny 8 4 out.json 1024 on align # identical ``` repro_mamba_cache_mode_nondeterminism.py is showed below: ```python """The same batch twice in one process -- in the configuration that DIVERGES. `scripts/probe_kernel_determinism.py` answered "the kernels are deterministic for a fixed batch" with `enable_prefix_caching=False`. On a Mamba model that is not a detail: `config/cache.py` sets `mamba_cache_mode="none"` when prefix caching is off, and the cells that file DIFFERS run the DEFAULT `"all"`, which caches the mamba state of all tokens at `i * block_size`. The earlier result therefore measured a different code path from the one under investigation. This runs the trigger shape instead: prefix caching ON, a token budget small enough that every prompt's prefill is SPLIT, several sequences in flight, and enough decode steps to carry a difference out to the tokens. The prefix cache is reset between calls so the second call does the same work as the first rather than being served from it. Same members, same order, same weights, same work -- different tokens would mean the kernels do not give the same answer for the same batch, in the configuration where the fuzzer sees it. """ import hashlib, json, os, sys from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams def _build_prompt(prompt_len: int, tag: str) -> str: """`prompt_len` marker words `u{h}_{p}` -- h hashes `tag`, p hashes (h, position). Self-contained (stdlib hashlib only), and each marker tokenises to several tokens so the prompt is long enough that its prefill is CHUNKED across scheduler steps, which the bug needs (a shorter builder whose markers were ~1 token did NOT reproduce -- L40S job 7559058).""" h = int(hashlib.md5(tag.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % 10000 def p(i: int) -> int: return int(hashlib.md5(f"{h}:{i}".encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % 10000 return " ".join(f"u{h}_{p(i)}" for i in range(prompt_len)) MODEL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny" K = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 8 CALLS = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 4 OUT = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "/tmp/chunked_same_batch.json" BUDGET = int(sys.argv[5]) if len(sys.argv) > 5 else 1024 PREFIX = (sys.argv[6].lower() not in ("0", "off", "false")) if len(sys.argv) > 6 else True CACHE_MODE = sys.argv[7] if len(sys.argv) > 7 and sys.argv[7] != '-' else None SSM_DTYPE = sys.argv[8] if len(sys.argv) > 8 and sys.argv[8] != '-' else None # prompts of mixed length, each well over the per-step budget so its prefill # must be split across steps -- the one property every DIFFERS request had prompts = [_build_prompt(200 + 40 * i, f"c{i}") for i in range(K)] llm = LLM(model=MODEL, max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.75, enable_prefix_caching=PREFIX, max_num_seqs=16, max_num_batched_tokens=BUDGET, enforce_eager=False, **({"mamba_cache_mode": CACHE_MODE} if CACHE_MODE else {}), **({"mamba_ssm_cache_dtype": SSM_DTYPE} if SSM_DTYPE else {})) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=64) def reset_cache(): """Make the next call do the work again instead of reading it back.""" for owner in (llm, getattr(llm, "llm_engine", None)): fn = getattr(owner, "reset_prefix_cache", None) if callable(fn): fn() return True return False reset_ok = reset_cache() print(f"model={MODEL} K={K} calls={CALLS} budget={BUDGET} " f"prefix_caching={'ON' if PREFIX else 'OFF'} " f"mamba_cache_mode={CACHE_MODE or '(default)'} " f"ssm_dtype={SSM_DTYPE or '(default)'} " f"reset_between_calls={reset_ok}", flush=True) runs = [] for c in range(CALLS): outs = llm.generate(prompts, sp) runs.append([tuple(o.outputs[0].token_ids) for o in outs]) print(f"call {c}: {[list(x)[:5] for x in runs[-1][:3]]}", flush=True) reset_cache() same = all(r == runs[0] for r in runs) print("\nSAME every call -> deterministic for this batch even with a split " "prefill and mamba_cache_mode=all" if same else "\nDIFFERS between calls -> the same batch does not give the same answer " "in the configuration the fuzzer flags") diffs = [] for c, r in enumerate(runs[1:], 1): for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(runs[0], r)): if a != b: d = next((k for k in range(min(len(a), len(b))) if a[k] != b[k]), None) diffs.append({"call": c, "prompt": i, "first_differing_token": d}) print(f" call 0 vs {c}, prompt {i}: first differs at token {d}: " f"{a[d]} vs {b[d]}") break json.dump({"model": MODEL, "k": K, "calls": CALLS, "budget": BUDGET, "prefix_caching": PREFIX, "mamba_cache_mode": CACHE_MODE, "reset_between_calls": reset_ok, "same_every_call": same, "diffs": diffs}, open(OUT, "w"), indent=1) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **My env** - vLLM 0.27.1 (pip wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Linux 5.15. - Reproduced on one RTX 4090 (sm_89) and on an H100 (sm_90) — not device-specific. - Models: `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` and `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct`. both hybrid Mamba2 + attention, bf16. The second is a different vendor and architecture (`FalconH1ForCausalLM`), 90M parameters and **dense**, neither MoE nor model size is involved. - Server setup: ``` vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \ --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \ --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-block-size 32 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 16 ``` Default scheduler, no speculative decoding, no LoRA, no quantization. Eight concurrent plain `/v1/completions` requests with long prompts (~2,500–3,900 tokens under a 4,096 `max_model_len`) and different shared-prefix lengths kill the engine on the first round: ``` File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py", line 963, in conv_ssm_forward ssm_state[cache_blocks_to_fill] = from_where RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [0, 48, 64, 128] cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [N, 48, 64, 128] ``` `N` has been 1, 2, 4 and 6. It raises inside EngineCore, so the engine does not recover: every later request — including a one-token `"hello"` — returns HTTP 500 `EngineDeadError`. On a shared server that is every tenant, not just the one that sent the request. ### Two unrelated models, so it is `MambaMixer2` and not a checkpoint | model | architecture | failing shapes | |---|---|---| | `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` | `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM` | `[0, 48, 64, 128]` vs `[N, 48, 64, 128]` | | `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct` | `FalconH1ForCausalLM` | `[0, 24, 32, 64]` vs `[13, 24, 32, 64]` | Same file, same line, each with its own head configuration. Both go through `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py`, so the fault is in the shared `MambaMixer2`. ### Where it comes from `conv_ssm_forward` writes the SSM state blocks a prefill filled ( with `num_computed_tokens_p_cpu` in place of`num_computed_tokens_p`): ```python first_aligned_chunk = first_chunk + chunk_stride - 1 num_unaligned_computed_tokens = num_computed_tokens_p[seq_idx] % mamba_block_size if num_unaligned_computed_tokens > 0: # If the number of computed tokens is not block aligned, # then we need to shift the index accordingly first_aligned_chunk -= num_unaligned_computed_tokens // chunk_size from_where = varlen_states[ first_aligned_chunk : first_aligned_chunk + n_blocks_to_fill * chunk_stride : chunk_stride ] ssm_state[cache_blocks_to_fill] = from_where # line 963 ``` `cache_blocks_to_fill` names `n_blocks_to_fill` state blocks, but `from_where` is a **strided slice**, and a slice whose range falls outside `varlen_states` is empty rather than an error. The mismatch surfaces at the assignment, one step after the arithmetic that produced it. `num_computed_tokens % mamba_block_size` is nonzero exactly when a request resumes at a position that is not a multiple of the mamba block: a prefix-cache hit of a length that is not a block multiple, or a chunked prefill that stopped mid-block. Concurrency supplies the chunking; a batch of mixed prefix lengths supplies the misalignment. Below are some Claudish describing the crash: ### What it takes — each varied on its own, fresh engine per row | configuration | result | |---|---| | `--mamba-block-size 32` (as above) | **EngineCore dead, round 0** | | `--mamba-block-size 16` | EngineCore dead | | **default** mamba block size | alive, 12 rounds × 8 concurrent | | no `--enable-prefix-caching` | alive, 12 rounds × 8 (vLLM also refuses `--mamba-block-size` without it) | | one request at a time | alive, **40 rounds** | | `--mamba-cache-mode align` | alive, 12 rounds × 8 | Prompt length also matters, the run whose longest prompt was ~1,700 tokens never crashed, while every shape in the reproducer is from 2,500 to 3,900 tokens. **`--mamba-cache-mode align` is a workaround.** That looks consistent with the cause: `"all"` — the default once prefix caching is on — caches "the mamba state of all tokens at position `i * block_size`", while `"align"` caches "only the mamba state of the last token of each scheduler step **and** when the token is at position `i * block_size`" (`config/cache.py`). `"all"` is the mode that writes state at positions no scheduler step ended on, which is the path taking the `num_unaligned_computed_tokens` correction above. ### Reproducer it sends eight concurrent completions per round with shared-prefix lengths of 0–900 markers, and reports a crash only when a trivial follow-up request also fails (so an over-length prompt returning 400 is not mistaken for one). The full reproducer ( Should be self-contained, needs only `vllm`): ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Reproduce the mamba_mixer2 conv_ssm_forward shape mismatch. Seen on the cluster (job 22378983, granite-4.0-h-tiny, vLLM 0.27.1) nine iterations into a run with ``--mamba-block-size 32`` beside the model's own 512-token attention blocks: ssm_state[cache_blocks_to_fill] = from_where RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [0, 48, 64, 128] cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [6, 48, 64, 128] It kills EngineCore, so every request in flight gets a 500 and the server never recovers -- EngineDeadError from then on. "value tensor of shape [0, ...]" against an index selecting six blocks reads as a prefix-cache hit that left nothing to copy while six state blocks were still expected to be filled, so this drives concurrent requests over SHARED prefixes of several block lengths. """ import argparse, asyncio, json, sys, time import httpx #: (shared prefix markers, total markers). A marker is ~3.8 tokens shared and #: ~9.9 novel, so every shape here lands between about 2,500 and 3,900 tokens: #: LONG, because the crash needs a prompt that spans many mamba blocks, and #: still inside a 4,096 max_model_len, because a prompt over it comes back 400 #: and a 400 is not a crash. Both halves were learned the hard way -- the #: first probe mixed over-length prompts in and its minimizer called four #: configurations crashes that were HTTP 400s; the second stayed so far under #: the limit that nothing crashed at all. SHAPES = [(600, 700), (800, 850), (400, 500), (900, 950), (200, 400), (100, 350), (0, 380), (700, 780)] def prompt(prefix_markers: int, total_markers: int, tag: str) -> str: shared = " ".join(f"pre{i}" for i in range(prefix_markers)) uniq = " ".join(f"{tag}u{i}" for i in range(max(0, total_markers - prefix_markers))) return (shared + " " + uniq).strip() async def one(client, base, model, p, n, rid): try: r = await client.post(base + "/v1/completions", json={ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-hf` fails to load. vLLM resolves it to the Transformers backend, which then crashes during engine startup when it calls the model's audio encoder. Affects all three AF-Next checkpoints — `audio-flamingo-next-hf`, `audio-flamingo-next-think-hf`, `audio-flamingo-next-captioner-hf` (identical configs, different weights). ### Reproduction ```python from vllm import LLM llm = LLM(model="nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-hf") ``` ### Result ``` INFO Resolved architecture: TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM WARNING TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM has no vLLM implementation, falling back to Transformers implementation. Some features may not be supported and performance may not be optimal. ... EngineCore failed to start. Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 864, in profile_run self.model_state.encoder_runner.profile_encoder_cache( File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py", line 139, in profile_encoder_cache dummy_encoder_outputs = self.execute_mm_encoder(dummy_mm_inputs) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py", line 168, in execute_mm_encoder else self.model.embed_multimodal(**mm_kwargs_batch) File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py", line 1208, in embed_multimodal embeddings.extend(process_input(**kwargs) or []) File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/multimodal.py", line 1109, in _process_audio_input audio_output = self.model.get_audio_features( File ".../transformers/utils/generic.py", line 939, in wrapper output = func(self, *args, **kwargs) TypeError: MusicFlamingoModel.get_audio_features() missing 1 required positional argument: 'input_ids' RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {} ``` ### Why the Transformers backend cannot work for this architecture HF's `MusicFlamingoModel.get_audio_features` takes `input_ids` as a required argument. It uses it to recover, for each 30-second audio chunk, that chunk's index within the audio it came from — which drives the model's rotary *time* embedding. vLLM encodes audio separately from the text tokens, so `_process_audio_input` has no `input_ids` to pass. This is not a tuning issue; the fallback is structurally unable to satisfy the signature. ### transformers alone works correctly ```python import torch, librosa from transformers import AutoProcessor, MusicFlamingoForConditionalGeneration MODEL = "nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-hf" proc = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL) model = MusicFlamingoForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained( MODEL, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda").eval() wav = librosa.load("clip.wav", sr=16000, mono=True)[0] messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio"}, {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this audio."}]}] prompt = proc.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False) inputs = proc(text=[prompt], audio=[wav], sampling_rate=16000).to( device=model.device, dtype=torch.bfloat16) out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=64, do_sample=False) print(proc.tokenizer.decode(out[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)) # -> "A woman and a child are speaking..." ``` So the failure is on the vLLM side, not transformers. ### Background These checkpoints declare: ```json "architectures": ["MusicFlamingoForConditionalGeneration"], "model_type": "musicflamingo" ``` vLLM had a `MusicFlamingoForConditionalGeneration` implementation through v0.24.0. It was removed in #47263, partly on the basis that *"MusicFlamingo has been superseded by AudioFlamingo3 (new MusicFlamingo checkpoints use AudioFlamingo3)"*. That does not hold for the Audio Flamingo Next family — all three variants declare `musicflamingo`, not `audioflamingo3`. The architecture is still listed in `_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS`, but that error path is never reached, since the Transformers fallback resolves first and fails as above. I have it working locally with token-level output parity against transformers and I plan to submit a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: assistant_tokens_mask misaligned after multimodal placeholder expansion
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 CMake version : version 3.22.1 Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu129 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 12.9 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Nvidia driver version : 576.88 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.23.1rc1 transformers : 5.8.1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `assistant_tokens_mask` is built against the prompt before multimodal placeholders expand, and nothing expands the mask to match. Entry *i* stops describing token *i*, so a caller training on the mask scores the wrong tokens. `truncate_prompt_tokens` is not involved. transformers gets this right on the same input, so the divergence is vLLM's. Both produce 71 token ids; the masks differ. Reproduced on `main` at `dffbb714e`. No model weights, no GPU. The two APIs take audio differently, so the conversations differ only in how the same 4 seconds of silence is passed. ```python import base64, io, wave import numpy as np from transformers import AutoProcessor from vllm.config import ModelConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.renderers import ChatParams, TokenizeParams, renderer_from_config MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf" REVISION = "7f1569a48a89f3e3f4dc3a5c9d28bddd903bc76c" audio = np.zeros(4 * 16000, dtype=np.float32) buf = io.BytesIO() with wave.open(buf, "wb") as w: w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(16000) w.writeframes(np.zeros(4 * 16000, dtype=np.int16).tobytes()) wav = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode() text = {"type": "text", "text": "transcribe this"} reply = {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "hello there"}]} hf_conv = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "audio", "audio": audio}, text]}, reply] vllm_conv = [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "input_audio", "input_audio": {"data": wav, "format": "wav"}}, text]}, reply] hf = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL, revision=REVISION).apply_chat_template( hf_conv, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_assistant_tokens_mask=True) print("transformers:", len(hf["input_ids"][0]), "ids,", len(hf["assistant_masks"][0]), "mask entries") renderer = renderer_from_config(VllmConfig(model_config=ModelConfig( MODEL, revision=REVISION, dtype="float32", max_model_len=4096, mm_processor_cache_gb=0))) _, engine_inputs = renderer.render_chat( [vllm_conv], ChatParams(return_assistant_tokens_mask=True), TokenizeParams(max_total_tokens=4096)) out = engine_inputs[0] print("vllm :", len(out["prompt_token_ids"]), "ids,", len(out["assistant_tokens_mask"]), "mask entries,", out["mm_placeholders"]["audio"][0]) ``` Actual output: ```text transformers: 71 ids, 71 mask entries vllm : 71 ids, 20 mask entries, PlaceholderRange(offset=9, length=52, is_embed=None) ``` Expected: the mask has one entry per token, as transformers produces. vLLM's mask is short by 51, the 52-token audio span minus the single placeholder token it replaced. Every entry from offset 9 onward describes a token 51 positions earlier than the one it lands on. transformers tokenizes text and audio in one pass, so its mask covers the expanded audio. vLLM splits the two: `HfRenderer.render_messages` takes the mask from `apply_chat_template` against the unexpanded text (`hf.py:1109`), `_PARALLEL_TO_PROMPT_TOKENS` keeps it in step through tokenization, then `_process_multimodal` expands the placeholders and grows `prompt_token_ids` alone. `HfRenderer._process_tokens` attaches the unexpanded mask afterwards (`hf.py:1294`). Downstream, `scale_out/render/serving.py:129-148` pads the mask to length and logs "The mask may be positionally misaligned", which fixes the length and not the alignment. Stretching the mask after the fact does not look possible in the renderer: it needs to know how many original tokens each item consumed, and `mm_placeholders` records only where the content landed. `PromptReplacement` consumes its target sequence while `PromptInsertion` consumes nothing, so a 52-slot span could have come from one token, three, or none. That mapping only exists inside the processor pass that rewrites the prompt. Related work keeps the mask in step through tokenization and truncation (#54407, #54539, #54692, #54812); none covers multimodal expansion. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug][ROCm][Distributed] Custom all-reduce start barrier is fully relaxed — peer-data reads unordered against remote (XGMI) writes → torn reads
body:
### Your current environment

- Upstream vLLM @ `241e9391ed85f6c967432135427717a529776a63` (2026-09-15), ROCm 7.0 clang for codegen evidence
- 4× AMD Instinct MI100 (gfx908, XGMI full mesh), ROCm 7.14, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.1

### Describe the bug

### Current behavior

On multi-GPU ROCm where P2P goes over XGMI (on 4× MI100 / gfx908, ROCm 7.14; where the memory-model argument applies wherever peers are remote agents relative to device scope), the custom all-reduce kernels can pass their start barrier and read a peer's staged input buffer while the peer's writes are still in flight. Torn bf16 values seed NaN/huge-finite activations; in-engine this presents as episodic single-layer corruption and, at long context, junk-token output walls. Load- and timing-dependent; silent.

### Root cause (verified at HEAD `241e9391e`)

- `csrc/custom_collective_common.cuh` `barrier_at_start` (ROCm branch, lines 264–280): flag store to peers is `__ATOMIC_RELAXED` / `__MEMORY_SCOPE_SYSTEM`; flag load is `__ATOMIC_RELAXED` / `__MEMORY_SCOPE_DEVICE`. Fully relaxed — no release covers the producer's prior data stores, no acquire covers the consumer's subsequent data loads.
- `barrier_at_start_release` (lines 283–296) and non-final `barrier_at_end` (298–318) carry release/acquire, but **no kernel at HEAD calls `barrier_at_start_release`**: both `cross_device_reduce_1stage` (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:16`) and `cross_device_reduce_2stage` (line 51) synchronize the reduction start — the point that must order peer-data reads against peer-data writes — with the fully relaxed variant.
- SASS (gfx908, `-O3`, ROCm 7.0 clang): `barrier_at_start` emits a plain flag store and a bare spin (`global_load_dword ... glc` + `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`) with **zero fences**; the acquire variants emit `buffer_wbinvl1_vol`. Note: patching only the load scopes DEVICE→SYSTEM produced byte-identical device code on this toolchain — the **ordering** (relaxed → release/acquire) is the operative defect; scope promotion is required memory-model hygiene for remote-agent visibility but is codegen-inert on gfx908/ROCm 7.0.

### How to reproduce

Deterministic (no GPU, any machine with the repo + ROCm toolchain):

```bash
cd csrc && cat > /tmp/barriers.cu <<'EOF'
#include "custom_all_reduce.cuh"
__global__ void k_start(vllm::RankSignals sg, vllm::Signal* self, int rank) {
  vllm::barrier_at_start<4>(sg, self, rank);
}
__global__ void k_start_release(vllm::RankSignals sg, vllm::Signal* self, int rank) {
  vllm::barrier_at_start_release<4>(sg, self, rank);
}
EOF
clang++ -x hip --rocm-path=/opt/rocm --offload-arch=gfx908 -O3 -DUSE_ROCM \
  -I. -S /tmp/barriers.cu -o /tmp/barriers.s
# k_start spin loop: global_load glc + s_waitcnt, NO buffer_wbinvl1_vol
# k_start_release spin loop: same load + buffer_wbinvl1_vol (acquire)
grep -c buffer_wbinvl1_vol /tmp/barriers.s   # >0, but only from k_start_release
# And: neither reduce kernel at HEAD instantiates the acquire variant:
grep -n "barrier_at_start" custom_all_reduce.cuh   # both call the relaxed one
```

In-engine (4× MI100, XGMI): serve any TP=4 bf16 model with custom all-reduce on; drive long decode with speculative decoding at high concurrency, interleaving prefill chunks so all-reduces of many sizes run back-to-back; capture logits/hidden states across ranks vs a gather reference — episodic one-layer divergences (torn residuals); with enough steps, outputs collapse to token loops. Full protocol and knife-switch bisection: curvedinf/int8-vllm `docs/recipes/bug_rocm_batch_memcpy_graph_replay_race.md` and `PROBABLE_UPSTREAM_BUGS.md` BUG 1 (fix soak there: 24/24 long greedy legs after the fix vs ~5/8 boot failures before).

### How to characterize the bug as fixed

1. **Static/SASS (deterministic):** after the fix, both `cross_device_reduce_*` kernels' start-barrier spin loops emit `buffer_wbinvl1_vol` (acquire) before `__syncthreads()`, and all cross-rank flag loads/stores are `__MEMORY_SCOPE_SYSTEM`. Rebuild the two kernels and grep as above — the fences must now appear in the **reduce kernels** (not just the unused helper).
2. **Soak (rig):** the in-engine protocol above runs clean for ≥24/24 long greedy legs with no cross-rank one-layer divergence at matched positions.
3. **Unit:** a two-kernel spin-handshake test where the producer writes data then a flag with release, consumer acquires the flag then reads data, run under extreme SM contention, never observes stale data (a starting-point skeleton is attached: `kernels_barriers.cu`).

### Example solution

```diff
--- a/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh
+++ b/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh
@@ cross_device_reduce_1stage @@
-  barrier_at_start<ngpus>(sg, self_sg, rank);
+  barrier_at_start_release<ngpus>(sg, self_sg, rank);
@@ cross_device_reduce_2stage @@
-  barrier_at_start<ngpus>(sg, self_sg, rank);
+  barrier_at_start_release<ngpus>(sg, self_sg, rank);
--- a/csrc/custom_collective_common.cuh   (ROCm branch only)
+++ b/csrc/custom_collective_common.cuh
@@ barrier_at_start, barrier_at_start_release, barrier_at_end @@
-                                  __MEMORY_SCOPE_DEVICE) < flag);
+                                  __MEMORY_SCOPE_SYSTEM) < flag);
 (all three acquire/relaxed flag loads)
```

Verified: applying exactly this to the HEAD headers and rebuilding for gfx908, the 1-stage kernel's spin region goes from fences `NONE` to `['buffer_wbinvl1_vol']` (disassembly attached: `kernels_gfx908.s` = stock, `kernels_gfx908_release.s` = patched; the patched build's header `custom_all_reduce_release.cuh` is also attached). Measured cost on gfx908: none (the acquire invalidation is the only added instruction; XGMI paths are already coherent).

### Referenced code / evidence / example fix
[code.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32255309/code.zip)
