title: [Bug]: truncate_prompt_tokens does not bound the final prompt after multimodal expansion
body:
### Your current environment Reproduced on unmodified upstream vLLM production code at commit: 000c7df9ffd3e470980fd4cd6b8ec1b0585500ff The checkout lacks generated version metadata, so collect_env reports N/A (dev). This environment uses the checkout's Python source with existing vLLM 0.29 CUDA extensions, not a fresh CUDA build.
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) Kernel: Linux 5.15.0-190-generic Libc: glibc-2.35 Python: 3.13.15 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 Transformers: 5.15.1 NumPy: 2.4.6 GPU: NVIDIA H100 PCIe NVIDIA driver: 610.57.04 CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 Model: Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf Model revision: 7f1569a48a89f3e3f4dc3a5c9d28bddd903bc76c ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `truncate_prompt_tokens` is applied before multimodal placeholder expansion, so the final rendered prompt can exceed the requested token limit. With Qwen3-ASR, requesting 96 tokens returns 147 tokens. The complete audio span fits inside the expected 96-token window, so this does not require truncating or discarding audio. ### Minimal reproducer This uses four seconds of generated silence, the real Qwen3-ASR processor, and no model weights or external audio files. ```python import numpy as np from transformers import AutoProcessor from vllm.config import ModelConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.renderers import TokenizeParams, renderer_from_config model = "Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf" revision = "7f1569a48a89f3e3f4dc3a5c9d28bddd903bc76c" renderer = renderer_from_config(VllmConfig(model_config=ModelConfig( model, revision=revision, dtype="float32", max_model_len=4096, mm_processor_cache_gb=0, ))) audio = np.zeros(4 * 16000, dtype=np.float32) prompt = "<|audio_start|><|audio_pad|><|audio_end|>" + " text" * 128 request = {"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio, 16000)}} full = renderer.render_cmpl( [request], TokenizeParams(max_total_tokens=4096) )[0] limited = renderer.render_cmpl( [request], TokenizeParams( max_total_tokens=4096, truncate_prompt_tokens=96, truncation_side="right", ), )[0] native = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model, revision=revision) hf_ids = native(text=prompt, audio=audio, return_tensors="pt")["input_ids"][0].tolist() assert full["prompt_token_ids"] == hf_ids span = full["mm_placeholders"]["audio"][0] assert span.offset + span.length <= 96 # No need to cut or discard audio. print("Requested token limit:", 96) print("Returned tokens:", len(limited["prompt_token_ids"])) print("Audio tokens:", span.length) print("Matches full prompt[:96]:", limited["prompt_token_ids"] == hf_ids[:96]) ``` ### Actual output ```text Requested token limit: 96 Returned tokens: 147 Audio tokens: 52 Matches full prompt[:96]: False ``` The result should contain the first 96 tokens of the fully expanded prompt, with the audio features and placeholder metadata remaining aligned. ### Investigation and impact Truncation keeps 96 tokens before expansion. One audio placeholder then becomes 52 audio tokens, producing `96 - 1 + 52 = 147` tokens. The renderer does not subsequently enforce the requested bound. Complete sequences that already fit the requested window are unaffected. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

Attention backend `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` and Model Runner V2 in both arms, auto-selected. The checkpoint is 417 GiB, so TP2 is the smallest that fits on 275 GB cards; `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` would fit one card but HiSparse refuses DeepSeek V4 (`vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`), and every other DSA checkpoint is several hundred GiB, so we have no reproduction for an 80 or 141 GB part. ``` # broken vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \ --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}' # control: the same command without those two flags vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 # one request, identical against both curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8","prompt":"What is the capital of France?","max_tokens":32,"temperature":0}' ``` `choices[0].text` as returned, `finish_reason` `length`, 32 completion tokens in both cases: ``` observed " (, \"' .'CC\"1adad.ss))) of,,)..-1..) of-" expected " (Paris)\n\nI am an AI language model, so I don't have personal desires or wants. However, if you are referring to the integrated system of Brain" ``` Both start with the same first token, `" ("`; the second is `","` with HiSparse and `"Paris"` without. `"2 + 2 ="` behaves the same way, returning `" .,# Had,, of to S58"` against `" 5\nThe phrase \"two plus two equals five\"..."`. Repeating a request within one server returns byte-identical noise, and two separate boots of the same command return the same text, so the corruption is deterministic. We ran the two arms on different ports so both could be up at once; nothing else differs from the commands above. ### Prefill-only requests are correct on the broken server This is the one thing we found that does not reproduce. Against the broken server above, drive the same continuation one token at a time, so every token is produced by a prefill pass: ```bash M=RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8; T='What is the capital of France?'; G= for i in $(seq 8); do P=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "$(jq -cn --arg m "$M" --arg p "$T" '{model:$m,prompt:$p,max_tokens:1,temperature:0}')" \ | jq -j '.choices[0].text'; echo X); P=${P%X} T=$T$P; G=$G$P done printf '%s' "$G" | jq -Rsa . ``` The `jq -j` and the `echo X` sentinel matter: the third token of this continuation is `")\n\n"`, and command substitution would otherwise strip those newlines and feed a different prompt into the next step. The loop prints `" (Paris)\n\nI am an AI language"`, exactly what the control returns for one `max_tokens: 8` request, while one `max_tokens: 8` request on the HiSparse server returns `" (, \"' .'C"`. We also ran the chain with a fresh `cache_salt` per request, to rule out prefix-cache hits (prefix caching is on by default here), and got the same result. Same server, same weights, same boot: right while every token comes out of a prefill pass, wrong as soon as tokens come out of a decode pass. We found no HiSparse configuration that decodes correctly; the knobs below are the ones we varied. ## What was tried On the upstream `main` checkout above, at TP2, all through `vllm serve` plus `curl`: - `--enforce-eager`, so no CUDA graph is captured at all: still noise, byte-identical to the run above. - `hisparse_config.device_buffer_size` 2048 (the minimum for this model, one `index_topk`, no LRU slack) and 32768 (the maximum the config accepts, 8x the default 4096): still noise on both, byte-identical to the default 4096. - `--no-enable-prefix-caching`: still noise, byte-identical. - MTP speculative decoding, where `device_buffer_size` then resolves to 6144: still noise, different noise. This one arm ran through the offline `LLM()` API, not `vllm serve`. From an earlier sweep on a local branch at base `b443c1cc4`, whose HiSparse and FlashInfer code paths were unmodified upstream, at TP4 and TP8 with `host_pool_gib` 256 and a 14-prompt harness: - GSM8K 5-shot strict-match 0.0000 against 0.9409 for the control, 1319/1319 questions, all needle prompts missed, and the same first-token-right pattern. - `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, no full decode graphs: still noise, byte-identical on 10 of 14 prompts. - `hisparse_config.eager_host_mirror=false`: still noise, byte-identical on 10 of 14. - Prefix caching on in one run and off in the rest: noise either way. - `--distributed-executor-backend ray`, private per-rank host pools instead of the shared mmap: still noise. - `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` instead of the auto-selected `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`: still noise, so both sparse-MLA backends are affected. Not tested: `MultiConnector` with `NixlConnector`, because UCX needs a locked-memory limit above this account's 8 MB cap. ## Where the evidence points The split falls exactly on the prefill/decode boundary, and it is deterministic rather than a race: eager mode, piecewise graphs, non-eager host mirroring, private per-rank host pools and prefix caching on or off all produce byte-identical wrong output. Hot-buffer capacity does not change it either: at `device_buffer_size=2048` every decode step must evict a row, at 32768 it almost never does, and the output is the same to the byte, which argues against an eviction or LRU-pressure race and for a fixed error in how decode addresses the buffer. That points at the hot-buffer decode lane in `vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py`, where `_prepare_for_batch` sets `decode_batch` and `_resolve_residency` (`hisparse_resolve_residency`), `_swap_rows` (`hisparse_gather_compact`) and `mirror_write_target` all branch on it. We have not isolated which of those is wrong. #56158, missing host mirror writes under FULL cudagraph replay, does not cover this: `--enforce-eager` captures no graphs and still reproduces. The boot warning recommends `NixlConnector` or `MooncakeStoreConnector` instead, but `hisparse/layout.py` raises unless the host pool comes from a `HiSparseConnector`, so the configuration above is the only shape available for a single-node run, and it is the shape the e2e test uses. ## Why the e2e test does not catch this `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` runs with `load_format="dummy"` and a shrunk config, and its only output assertion is `assert actual == expected`, comparing generations before and after a spill. A consistently wrong decode path passes that test, because both sides are wrong in the same way, and random weights give no reference for what the output should have been.
HiSparse boot lines from the broken server ``` WARNING [vllm.py:1657] HiSparse host-resident KV is configured with connector HiSparseConnector. NixlConnector (GPU-staged host imports) and MooncakeStoreConnector (shared-store offload) are the validated paths; other connectors are treated as debug/fallback paths. INFO [cuda.py:536] Using FLASHMLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHMLA_SPARSE', 'FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE']. INFO [runtime.py:1276] Enabled experimental HiSparse HMA hot cache: top_k=2048, device_buffer_size=4096 (4096 LRU rows), max_num_seqs=1024. INFO [layout.py:340] HiSparse HMA: 32.0 GiB host source (5974 blocks), 34.3 GiB shared GPU indexer/resident/hot pool (124898 blocks). INFO [factory.py:62] Creating v1 connector with name: HiSparseConnector and engine_id: 5e430938-373a-4ce7-969b-ce4e6e402d18 INFO: Application startup complete. ``` No traceback, CUDA error, NaN or assertion appears anywhere in either server log.

The KV pool size and `--num-gpu-blocks-override` make no difference (checked both ways). As soon as **three or more** sequences are decoded in the same batch, **every request in the batch returns NaN log-probs** (HTTP 400 "Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan" when `logprobs` is requested; without `logprobs` the text is garbage, e.g. `"should should should ..."`). The engine logs nothing: no warning, no error, just NaN in the logits. | concurrent greedy requests (prompt 10-115 words, decode 16-640 tokens) | default (compile + CUDA graphs) | `--enforce-eager` | |---|---|---| | 1, or 2 (joining during the first's prefill or its decode) | fine | fine | | 3 (three repeats), 4, 5, 8, 16, 24, 32 | NaN on every request (in some 4-request rounds one survives) | fine, 3 and 5 alike | Preemption is not involved (the preemption counter stays at 0 up to 8 concurrent requests). Isolating the execution mode: | server | K=2 | K=3 | K=5 | |---|---|---|---| | default (torch.compile + CUDA graphs) | fine | NaN x3 | NaN x5 | | same, default KV pool size | fine | NaN x3 | NaN x5 | | torch.compile on, `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'` | fine | **fine** | **fine** | | `--enforce-eager` | fine | fine | fine | | default mode, `--max-num-seqs 2` | fine | fine (never three in a batch) | fine | So the NaN comes from **CUDA-graph replay of a decode batch of three or more sequences** on the `TRITON_MLA` + online-FP8 path; inductor alone is fine and the block pool is irrelevant. `--enforce-eager` or `cudagraph_mode: NONE` fixes it; `--max-num-seqs 2` sidesteps it. Online FP8 is the documented way to fit this model on a 24 GB card (the bf16 checkpoint is 32 GB), and the default configuration produces garbage for every request the moment the server has three in flight. ### Reproducer Standalone (only `httpx`), against a default server on one 4090: 1, 2, then 3 concurrent 16-token greedy requests with `logprobs`. Expected: three HTTP 200 rounds. Observed: 200, 200, then three HTTP 400 (`... not JSON compliant: nan`); with `--enforce-eager`, three 200s. vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000 python3 repro_dsv2lite_fp8_nan.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 # --k 3 (default), try --k 5 ```python # Standalone reproducer (no dependency on this repo): DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat with online FP8 on an # RTX 4090 (sm89, TRITON_MLA) returns NaN log-probs / garbage text as soon as three requests are # decoded in the same batch; two are fine; --enforce-eager or --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' is fine # (torch.compile without CUDA graphs), so the fault is in CUDA-graph replay of a >=3-sequence decode batch. # # vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --trust-remote-code --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 4096 --port 8000 # python3 repro_dsv2lite_fp8_nan.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 [--k 3] import argparse, math, random, threading import httpx def prompt(seed, n_words=80): rng = random.Random(seed) return " ".join(f"w{rng.randrange(10000)}" for _ in range(n_words)) def one(base, model, seed, n, out): r = httpx.post(base + "/v1/completions", json={"model": model, "prompt": prompt(seed), "max_tokens": n, "temperature": 0.0, "logprobs": 1}, timeout=600) if r.status_code != 200: out[seed] = f"HTTP {r.status_code}: {r.text[:90]}" return ch = r.json()["choices"][0] lps = ch["logprobs"]["token_logprobs"] nan = sum(1 for x in lps if x is None or (isinstance(x, float) and math.isnan(x))) out[seed] = f"HTTP 200, nan_logprobs={nan}/{len(lps)}, text={ch['text'][:32]!r}" ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000") ap.add_argument("--model", default="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat") ap.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=3) ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=16) a = ap.parse_args() for K in (1, 2, a.k): out, ths = {}, [] for s in range(K): th = threading.Thread(target=one, args=(a.base_url, a.model, 100 * K + s, a.max_tokens, out)) th.start(); ths.append(th) for th in ths: th.join() print(f"{K} concurrent request(s):") for s in sorted(out): print(f" {out[s]}") ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

============================== PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_user ((vllm-27) ) gpu-a6-7:~$ ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **My environment** (I have been copy and pasting the same env config above for a while so some info there maybe in accurate, but I have to be in queue for a compute node to run those command, which takes forever, so below is a short des of my enviroment nowadays) - vLLM 0.27.1 (pip wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130. - RTX 4090 (sm_89) and H100 80GB (sm_90), eager mode (`--enforce-eager`), `--max-model-len 4096`. - Experts backends selected by vLLM on both cards: "TRITON Unquantized MoE" (bf16) and "TRITON Fp8 MoE" (`--quantization fp8`). This is just a functional issue, not a security relevant bug :) The batch-invariance page lists MoE models, FP8 models and the DeepSeek family among the supported/tested configurations for `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. But with the flag set, a request's greedy output still depends on which other requests share its batch whenever the model's experts run through the Triton fused-MoE kernels with online FP8 weights,on both architectures; and on Hopper, with bf16 experts, a request served from its own fully cached prefix (a one-token prefill) is not bit-identical to the same request run cold. The dense linear path is batch-invariant in every case we tried, so the promise holds for `Linear` and fails for the experts. We did two tests (script below), 2-3 rounds each, all deterministic across rounds: * **co-batch**: A alone vs A started together with B, and with B' (same length, different content); "with B twice" checks determinism. * **writer-suffix**: a prefix P is written by a cold request P+S1 or P+S2 (equal length, different content) and read warm by P+X; on a batch-invariant engine the two reads must be bit-identical. Below is the table summarization by claude. | server (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`) | card | co-batched decode: A alone vs A with B | writer-suffix: read after S1 vs S2 | fully-cached prompt, warm vs cold | |---|---|---|---|---| | ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct **bf16** (on the tested list) | 4090 | identical | identical | identical | | same | H100 | identical | identical | **first token flip at 4, log-prob gap 0.14** | | granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct **`--quantization fp8`** | 4090 | **flip at token 4, gap 0.18** | **gap 0.20** | gap 0.02 | | same | H100 | **flip at 1** | **gap 0.07** | gap 0.42 | | Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat `--quantization fp8` | 4090 | flip at 21 | gap 0.09 | gap 0.25 | | same | H100 | flip at 4 | gap 0.53 | gap 0.35 | | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat `--quantization fp8` (MLA) | 4090 | flip at 12, gap 0.22 | (prefix caching is disabled by BI for TRITON_MLA) | -- | | Qwen/Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8` (dense, control) | both | identical | identical | identical | | Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 (dense, block-scaled checkpoint) | 4090 | identical | identical | identical | | Qwen/Qwen3-8B bf16 (dense) | both | identical | identical | identical | | Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (MoE, block-scaled fp8 checkpoint, same TRITON Fp8 MoE backend, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`) | H100 | identical | identical | identical | "with B twice" is bit-identical everywhere: the engine is deterministic, it is just not invariant to the batch. Without the flag every MoE server above is content-dependent, as expected. In 0.27.1 the only experts implementation that reads `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is the HUMMING backend (`model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/fused_humming_moe.py`,`quantization/utils/humming_utils.py`); `init_batch_invariance` replaces the aten matmul / bmm paths and pins cuBLAS, which is why the dense linear layers are invariant, but the Triton fused-MoE experts (bf16 and fp8) are not part of the override set, their kernel configuration is chosen per token count, and batch-invariant mode neither redirects them to an invariant implementation nor warns that the selected experts backend has none. The two failures have different causes: * **Online fp8 experts** (`activation_scheme: dynamic`, no weight block size): `Fp8MoEMethod.get_fused_moe_quant_config` builds the quant config without `per_act_token_quant`, so `moe_kernel_quantize_input` quantizes the expert inputs with `ops.scaled_fp8_quant(A, None, use_per_token_if_dynamic=False)` -- one dynamic scale for the whole activation tensor, i.e. the maximum over every token of every request in the batch. A request's inputs are quantized with a scale set by whoever shares the batch, which is batch-dependent by construction; that is why the effect is large (greedy tokens flip within the first few positions) and the same on both cards. The block-scaled checkpoint (`Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`, last row) takes the `per_token_group_quant_fp8` branch instead, so each token is scaled on its own, and it is invariant under the flag on the same backend and card. The dense online-fp8 linear layers are invariant for the same reason: `Fp8LinearMethod` selects per-token scales (`kFp8DynamicTokenSym`) when CUTLASS fp8 is available. * **bf16 experts on Hopper**: the Triton unquantized MoE kernel configuration is chosen per token count, so a one-token prefill after a full prefix hit and a 145-token cold prefill take different configurations and nothing pins them. **Consequence with prefix caching.** Because the K/V a request stores for a shared prefix depend on that request's own suffix through the experts' grouping, two users sharing a prefix get different cached bytes depending on who wrote them first -- under the flag that is supposed to make this impossible. ### Reproducer ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Does a request's output depend on the CONTENT of the requests it shares a batch with? Written for the DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MoE, online fp8, eager) strict hit of 2026-09-14 (`sm_hunt_dsv2lite-fp8-eager_2026-09-14_0642`, trace 002, request sm-p1_a_ext): four runs with the same per-step composition and the same hit-block provenance split 3:1. The composition key records batch SHAPE; on a mixture-of-experts model the grouped expert GEMMs also depend on which tokens the other requests route where, i.e. on their content. This probe separates the two: round: reset cache; A alone (cold) -> solo reset; A + B started together (cold) -> with_B reset; A + B again -> with_B_repeat (determinism) reset; A + B' (same length as B, other content) -> with_Bprime then, without reset, A again alone (prefix hit on the blocks written next to B') -> warm_after_Bprime and the same warm read after a solo cold prefill -> warm_after_solo If with_B == with_B_repeat but with_B != with_Bprime != solo, the numerics depend on batch content (expert grouping), not on a KV defect; if the warm reads differ as the cold co-batch differed, the dependence is baked into the cached KV. A dense model (--model Qwen/Qwen3-8B) is the control. VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --quantization fp8 --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager --port 8526 python3 scripts/repro_moe_batch_content.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8526 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --out out.json """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import concurrent.futures as cf import hashlib import json import os import sys import time import httpx sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) def markers(n: int, seed: str) -> str: h = hashlib.sha256(seed.encode()).hexdigest() return " ".join(f"{seed}{h[i % 64]}{i}" for i in range(n)) def gen(base: str, model: str, prompt: str, n: int, tag: str) -> dict: with httpx.Client() as c: r = c.post(base + "/v1/completions", json={"model": model, "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": n, "temperature": 0.0, "logprobs": 1}, headers={"X-Request-Id": tag}, timeout=900.0) r.raise_for_status() ch = r.json()["choices"][0] return {"tokens": ch["logprobs"]["tokens"], "lps": ch["logprobs"]["token_logprobs"]} def reset(base: str) -> None: with httpx.Client() as c: c.post(base + "/reset_prefix_cache", timeout=60.0).raise_for_status() time.sleep(0.3) def pair(base: str, model: str, pa: str, pb: str, n: int, tag: str) -> dict: with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex: fb = ex.submit(gen, base, model, pb, n, tag + "_B") time.sleep(0.02) fa = ex.submit(gen, base, model, pa, n, tag + "_A") return {"A": fa.result(), "B": fb.result()} def diff(a: dict, b: dict) -> dict: ta, tb = a["tokens"], b["tokens"] flip = next((i for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(ta, tb)) if x != y), None) upto = flip if flip is not None else min(len(ta), len(tb)) gap = max((abs((a["lps"][i] or 0) - (b["lps"][i] or 0)) for i in range(upto)), default=0.0) return {"identical": ta == tb and a["lps"] == b["lps"], "first_flip": flip, "max_logprob_gap_before_flip": round(gap, 4)} def writer_suffix(args) -> int: P = "Summarize the following list of markers. " + markers(args.a_markers, "p") S1, S2 = markers(args.b_markers, "s1"), markers(args.b_markers, "s2") X = markers(8, "x") rows = [] for r in range(args.rounds): reset(args.base_url); gen(args.base_url, args.model, P + " " + S1, 1, f"r{r}_w1") read1 = gen(args.base_url, args.model, P + " " + X, args.n, f"r{r}_read1") reset(args.base_url); gen(args.base_url, args.model, P + " " + S2, 1, f"r{r}_w2") read2 = gen(args.base_url, args.model, P + " " + X, args.n, f"r{r}_read2") reset(args.base_url); gen(args.base_url, args.model, P + " " + S1, 1, f"r{r}_w1b") read1b = gen(args.base_url, args.model, P + " " + X, args.n, f"r{r}_read1b") reset(args.base_url); cold = gen(args.base_url, args.model, P + " " + X, args.n, f"r{r}_cold") row = {"round": r, "read_after_S1_vs_read_after_S1_repeat": diff(read1, read1b), "read_after_S1_vs_read_after_S2": diff(read1, read2), "read_after_S1_vs_cold": diff(read1, cold), "read_after_S2_vs_cold": diff(read2, cold)} rows.append(row); print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) if args.out: json.dump({"model": args.model, "mode": "writer-suffix", "args": vars(args), "rows": rows}, open(args.out, "w"), indent=1) return 0 def main(argv=None) -> int: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url", required=True) ap.add_argument("--model", required=True) ap.add_argument("--a-markers", type=int, default=120) ap.add_argument("--b-markers", type=int, default=120) ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=32) ap.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=3) ap.add_argument("--out", default=None) ap.add_argument("--mode", choices=["co-batch", "writer-suffix"], default="co-batch", help="co-batch: A alone vs A next to B / B'. writer-suffix: the prefix P is written by a cold " "request P+S1 or P+S2 (same length, different suffix content), then read warm by P+X; on a " "mixture-of-experts model the writer's own suffix changes the expert grouping of the batch " "that computed P's K/V -- the hunt's cold_vs_warm arm (p1 reads what p0 wrote).") args = ap.parse_args(argv) if args.mode == "writer-suffix": return writer_suffix(args) A = "Summarize the following list of markers. " + markers(args.a_markers, "a") B = "Summarize the following list of markers. " + markers(args.b_markers, "b") Bp = "Summarize the following list of markers. " + markers(args.b_markers, "c") rows = [] for r in range(args.rounds): reset(args.base_url); solo = gen(args.base_url, args.model, A, args.n, f"r{r}_solo") warm_after_solo = gen(args.base_url, args.model, A, args.n, f"r{r}_warmsolo") reset(args.base_url); with_b = pair(args.base_url, args.model, A, B, args.n, f"r{r}_wb")["A"] reset(args.base_url); with_b2 = pair(args.base_url, args.model, A, B, args.n, f"r{r}_wb2")["A"] reset(args.base_url); with_bp = pair(args.base_url, args.model, A, Bp, args.n, f"r{r}_wbp")["A"] warm_after_bp = gen(args.base_url, args.model, A, args.n, f"r{r}_warmbp") row = {"round": r, "solo_vs_with_B": diff(solo, with_b), "with_B_vs_with_B_repeat": diff(with_b, with_b2), "with_B_vs_with_Bprime": diff(with_b, with_bp), "solo_vs_with_Bprime": diff(solo, with_bp), "warm_after_solo_vs_solo": diff(warm_after_solo, solo), "warm_after_Bprime_vs_warm_after_solo": diff(warm_after_bp, warm_after_solo), "warm_after_Bprime_vs_with_Bprime": diff(warm_after_bp, with_bp)} rows.append(row) print(json.dumps(row), flush=True) if args.out: json.dump({"model": args.model, "args": vars(args), "rows": rows}, open(args.out, "w"), indent=1) return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main()) ``` ``` VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct --quantization fp8 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096 --port 8533 python3 repro_moe_batch_content.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8533 --model ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct # co-batch python3 repro_moe_batch_content.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8533 --model ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct --mode writer-suffix # control: the same server without --quantization fp8 (bf16 experts): identical on Ada ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug **My environment** - vLLM 0.27.1 (pip wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 4090 (sm_89); also reproduced on H100 (sm_90) with vLLM 0.25.1 and 0.27.1, and on A100-40GB (sm_80) with 0.27.1. - The kernel source is unchanged on `main` as of 2026-09-14 (`csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/hadamard/hadacore/hadamard_transform_cuda.cu`, last touched by #42339). `torch.ops._C.hadacore_transform` returns wrong, run-to-run different values in the last `rows % 8` rows of its input whenever the input has more than 8192 rows and `rows % 8` is 1, 2, 3 or 4. Inputs with at most 8192 rows, or a remainder of 0, 5, 6 or 7, are correct. fp16 and bf16, d = 32 / 64 / 128 alike. ``` rows= 8192 rows%8=0: run-to-run differing rows [] max err vs exact 0.06 rows= 8193 rows%8=1: run-to-run differing rows [8192] max err 10.67 rows= 20004 rows%8=4: run-to-run differing rows [20000..20003] rows= 20005 rows%8=5: run-to-run differing rows [] rows= 65540 rows%8=4: run-to-run differing rows [65536..65539] max err 10.86 ``` repro: [repro_hadacore_tail_rows.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/1f812fc3a124d71d744e00e3b153c370#file-repro_hadacore_tail_rows-py) **Mechanism** (read from the source, row rule and nondeterminism measured). The kernel works in warps of `num_chunks` 256-element chunks (two chunks of 8 rows at d = 64). The copy loop always issues and commits `num_chunks` `cp.async` groups per warp. When the padded chunk count is odd, the last warp owns a single real chunk (`real_num_chunks = 1`, `diff_num_chunks = -1`). In the masked wait loop the `cp.async.wait_group` is issued through `switch (k + diff_num_chunks)`, which for `k = 0` evaluates to `-1`; there is no such case, so no wait is issued and that warp reads its chunk from shared memory before the asynchronous copy has landed. With few blocks the copy usually wins; with a thousand or more blocks it frequently does not. A one-chunk tail is exactly `rows % 8 in 1..4`. What the warp reads is whatever the previous kernel left in that SM's shared memory. Inverting the corrupted rows through the exact butterfly recovers those bytes: in 117 of 188 corrupted rows they are, whole, the input of the *previous* `hadacore_transform` launch (a constant-row tensor launched just before, at a correct shape); in 19 more they are a mix of that tensor and the row's own data at 16-byte (`cp.async` segment) granularity, i.e. the copy lands while the warp is already reading. The int4 per-token-head KV mode rotates Q with this kernel on every attention call (rows = tokens × num_query_heads) and K/V on every cache write (rows = tokens × num_kv_heads). With Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (14 query heads, 2 KV heads), single prompt, greedy, `LLM.generate(..., logprobs=1)`, 5 runs each: ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head # TRITON_ATTN is selected T=1000 tokens (Q rows 14000, %8=0): first token identical in all runs T=1002 tokens (Q rows 14028, %8=4): token 0 (logprob -11.9) or token 1023 with logprob NaN; 3 distinct outputs T=1003 tokens (Q rows 14042, %8=2): same T=1004 tokens (Q rows 14056, %8=0): identical ``` The K/V write path alone reproduces it and the damage persists: with `max_num_batched_tokens=8448` a single 4097- or 4101-token prompt (K/V rows 2T = 8194 / 8202, remainder 2, while Q rows 14T have remainder 6) returns NaN log-probs at every generated position in 5/5 runs, and 4096 / 4100 tokens are bit-identical across runs. The corrupted K/V sits in the cache and every later step (and any prefix-cache hit) reads it. Through the OpenAI server a request that asks for `logprobs` fails with HTTP 400 `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`; without `logprobs` it returns wrong tokens silently. We first saw it as sporadic 400s under a concurrent workload (the batch's token count decides the remainder). `int8_per_token_head` and the bf16 cache are unaffected (no Hadamard rotation). The compressed-tensors `transform` module also calls `hadacore_transform` and is exposed at the same row counts. Exposure follows from the head counts: a model is affected on the Q path when `num_query_heads` is not a multiple of 8 (Qwen2.5 0.5B / 1.5B / 7B: 14 / 12 / 28) and on the K/V path when `num_kv_heads` is not (Qwen2.5 0.5B / 1.5B / 3B: 2; 7B: 4); 32/8-head models never produce a bad remainder. ### Reproducer (kernel level, seconds, needs only vLLM and an sm_80+ GPU) ```python # Standalone reproducer (needs only vLLM): the Hadacore Hadamard-transform kernel # (`torch.ops._C.hadacore_transform`, used by --kv-cache-dtype int4_per_token_head for the # randomized Hadamard transform of Q on every attention call and of K/V on every cache write) # computes the LAST (rows % 8) rows from undefined data whenever rows > 8192 and rows % 8 != 0. # Those rows differ run to run and are wrong against the exact transform. Rows <= 8192, or a # multiple of 8, are correct. # # python3 repro_hadacore_tail_rows.py # any CUDA GPU with sm_80+ import torch from vllm import _custom_ops as ops def exact(x): # unnormalized Walsh-Hadamard butterfly in fp32, then /sqrt(d) rows, d = x.shape; y = x.float(); h = 1 while h < d: v = y.view(rows, d // (2 * h), 2, h); y = torch.stack([v[..., 0, :] + v[..., 1, :], v[..., 0, :] - v[..., 1, :]], -2).reshape(rows, d); h <<= 1 return (y / d ** 0.5).to(x.dtype) torch.manual_seed(0) d = 64 for rows in (8192, 8193, 8200, 8201, 16385, 65537, 65540, 70812): x = (torch.randn(rows, d, device="cuda") * 3).bfloat16() y1 = ops.hadacore_transform(x.clone(), inplace=True) y2 = ops.hadacore_transform(x.clone(), inplace=True) nondet = torch.nonzero((y1 != y2).any(dim=1)).flatten().tolist() err = (y1.float() - exact(x).float()).abs().amax(dim=1) wrong = torch.nonzero(err > 1.0).flatten().tolist() print(f"rows={rows:6d} rows%8={rows % 8}: run-to-run differing rows {nondet[:4]}{'...' if len(nondet) > 4 else ''} " f"rows with |err|>1 vs exact {wrong[:4]}{'...' if len(wrong) > 4 else ''} max err {float(err.max()):.2f}") ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

This environment uses the checkout's Python source with existing vLLM 0.29 CUDA extensions, not a fresh CUDA build. ### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) Kernel: Linux 5.15.0-190-generic Libc: glibc-2.35 GCC: 11.4.0 Python: 3.13.15, conda-forge, 64-bit CPU: Intel Xeon Gold 6444Y CPU sockets: 2 Physical cores: 32 Logical CPUs: 64 GPU configuration: 8 × NVIDIA H100 PCIe CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: 0 NVIDIA driver: 610.57.04 GPU 0 memory: 81559 MiB CUDA available: True CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0 CUDA toolkit reported by nvcc: 13.3.73 PyTorch imported version: 2.13.0+cu130 PyTorch debug build: False Relevant installed packages: numpy==2.4.6 transformers==5.15.1 torch==2.13.0 torchaudio==2.11.0 torchvision==0.28.0 torchcodec==0.16.0 triton==3.7.1 flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 nvidia-cublas==13.1.1.3 nvidia-cuda-runtime==13.0.96 nvidia-cuda-nvrtc==13.0.88 nvidia-cuda-nvcc==13.3.73 nvidia-cudnn-cu13==9.20.0.48 nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7 vLLM reported version: N/A (dev) vLLM build flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled Relevant environment variables: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_PLUGINS= PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 collect_env completed successfully (exit code 0). ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Qwen3-ASR's vLLM audio processor produces different audio-placeholder counts from the checkpoint's native Hugging Face processor for the same waveform. For example, a 16,001-sample clip at 16 kHz produces 14 audio tokens in vLLM versus 13 in Hugging Face. ### Reproducer This uses synthetic 16 kHz audio and does not load model weights. ```python import numpy as np from transformers import AutoProcessor from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY model = "Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf" revision = "7f1569a48a89f3e3f4dc3a5c9d28bddd903bc76c" prompt = "<|audio_start|><|audio_pad|><|audio_end|>" hf = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model, revision=revision) processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(ModelConfig( model, revision=revision, dtype="float32", max_model_len=4096, mm_processor_cache_gb=0, )) audio_id = hf.tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids("<|audio_pad|>") print("samples: vLLM audio tokens / HF audio tokens") for samples in (15999, 16001, 321): audio = np.random.RandomState(42).randn(samples).astype(np.float32) expected = hf(text=prompt, audio=audio, return_tensors="pt") actual = processor( prompt, mm_items=processor.info.parse_mm_data({"audio": audio}), hf_processor_mm_kwargs={}, ) print(samples, actual["prompt_token_ids"].count(audio_id), expected["input_ids"][0].tolist().count(audio_id)) ``` ### Actual output ```text samples: vLLM audio tokens / HF audio tokens 15999 13 13 16001 14 13 321 1 7 ``` ### Expected behavior For each clip, vLLM should match the checkpoint's native HF preprocessing, including audio features and audio-placeholder counts. ### Investigation Two preprocessing differences appear responsible: - Qwen3-ASR inherits Omni's waveform padding to a multiple of the hop length, which can change feature lengths and audio-token counts. - Its processor hardcodes `WhisperFeatureExtractor` instead of honoring the native checkpoint's `Qwen3ASRFeatureExtractor`, including its minimum-length padding. I have a candidate fix and regression tests. Of 48 new cases, 34 fail on unmodified upstream; all 48 pass with the fix. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 MSA crashes with quack-kernels 0.6.5 on the standard SM100 CUDA path
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Reproduction environment</summary>

The failure was isolated with an otherwise-identical A/B comparison using public
per-commit vLLM wheels. A complete interactive `collect_env.py` dump is not
available from that automated environment, but the relevant public environment
and dependency tuple is:

```text
Operating system: Linux
Architectures reproduced: aarch64 and x86_64
Python: 3.12
GPU architecture: NVIDIA SM100 (Blackwell-class systems)
CUDA runtime: 13.0.2
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
torchvision: 0.28.0+cu130
flashinfer-python: 0.6.18.post1

Last known good:
  vLLM commit: 31759ccb6d560e150849273b47e15680a0120169
  vLLM wheel: 0.1.1.dev44+g31759ccb6
  quack-kernels: 0.6.4
  nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.6.2

First known bad:
  vLLM commit: ec6b0494fef6bf665edc60ffbe315fcbab27bbd6
  vLLM wheel: 0.1.1.dev45+gec6b0494f
  quack-kernels: 0.6.5
  nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.7.1
```

The model path has reproduced with both BF16 MiniMax-M3 and the public
`nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` variant. The failure occurs during engine
initialization, before any request is served.

Current vLLM `main` was also checked at
[`2c2cbd84`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/2c2cbd84fdf199901f3f4e6b0e708ee0664aadd6):

- [`requirements/cuda.txt`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2c2cbd84fdf199901f3f4e6b0e708ee0664aadd6/requirements/cuda.txt)
  pins `quack-kernels==0.6.5` and `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.7.1`.
- [`cmake/external_projects/fmha_sm100.cmake`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2c2cbd84fdf199901f3f4e6b0e708ee0664aadd6/cmake/external_projects/fmha_sm100.cmake)
  still pins MSA commit
  `087c161814d4d9c735b46c21212a09e5f8eb92fa`.

</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

#### Summary

MiniMax-M3 fails during MSA sparse-attention kernel compilation on vLLM configurations that combine:

- `quack-kernels==0.6.5`;
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.1`; and
- vLLM's currently vendored MSA revision
  `087c161814d4d9c735b46c21212a09e5f8eb92fa`.

The failure is:

```text
AttributeError: module 'quack.activation' has no attribute 'sub_packed_f32x2'
```

This is not specific to Rubin builds. The incompatible Quack/CuTe DSL versions are pinned by the standard CUDA requirements, and the affected MSA revision is selected by the shared `fmha_sm100.cmake` integration. Consequently, the bug also affects non-Rubin MiniMax-M3 deployments using the standard SM100 CUDA path.

The failing code is the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention implementation under `vllm/third_party/fmha_sm100`, so the direct impact is MiniMax-M3 when that MSA SM100 path is selected.

#### Minimal reproduction

On an SM100 system with a vLLM build at or after [`ec6b0494`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ec6b0494fef6bf665edc60ffbe315fcbab27bbd6) and the standard CUDA dependency set:

```bash
export VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG
export VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1

vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-config \
    '{"minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend":"cutlass"}'
```

Tensor-parallel size and memory-related arguments can be adjusted for the available system. The important conditions are that MiniMax-M3 selects the vendored SM100 MSA implementation and that the environment contains `quack-kernels==0.6.5` with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.1`.

#### Observed result

CuTe DSL compilation fails while initializing the MSA sparse-attention kernel. A representative traceback is:

```text
File ".../vllm/third_party/fmha_sm100/cute/src/sm100/fwd/atten_fwd.py",
    line 2307, in _softmax_step
  ...
File ".../vllm/third_party/fmha_sm100/cute/src/common/softmax.py",
    line 394, in apply_exp2_convert
  ...
File ".../vllm/third_party/fmha_sm100/cute/src/common/utils.py",
    line 1009, in ex2_emulation_2
  xy_rounded_back = quack.activation.sub_packed_f32x2(
AttributeError: module 'quack.activation' has no attribute
'sub_packed_f32x2'

RuntimeError: Worker failed with error
'module 'quack.activation' has no attribute 'sub_packed_f32x2''

RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

The exception is raised during DSL tracing/JIT compilation, before the GPU kernel successfully launches and before the API server becomes ready.

It is independent of request concurrency and has reproduced with both BF16 and NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 configurations.

#### Expected result

MiniMax-M3 should initialize and compile its MSA sparse-attention kernels when using vLLM's declared standard CUDA dependencies:

```text
quack-kernels==0.6.5
nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.1
```

The server should reach readiness and serve requests without depending on the removed private Quack compatibility helper.

#### Regression boundary

A controlled comparison identified this boundary:

| vLLM revision | Quack | CUTLASS DSL | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [`31759ccb`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/31759ccb6d560e150849273b47e15680a0120169) | 0.6.4 | 4.6.2 | Pass |
| [`ec6b0494`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ec6b0494fef6bf665edc60ffbe315fcbab27bbd6) | 0.6.5 | 4.7.1 | Fails during engine initialization |

The first failing revision is the merge commit for [#54927, “[CI] Bump CUTLASS DSL to 4.7”](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54927).

All other relevant packages and runtime settings in the comparison were held constant. This indicates an incompatibility between the updated dependency contract and the older vendored MSA revision, rather than a model-weight, request, or host-specific failure.

#### Root cause

Quack 0.6.5 removed the private module-level helper:

```python
quack.activation.sub_packed_f32x2
```

The helper's functionality is now available from the public CuTe API:

```python
cute.arch.sub_packed_f32x2
```

However, the MSA revision currently pinned by vLLM still calls the removed Quack symbol twice in
[`ex2_emulation_2`](https://github.com/vllm-project/MSA/blob/087c161814d4d9c735b46c21212a09e5f8eb92fa/python/fmha_sm100/cute/src/common/utils.py#L1006-L1014).

This leaves vLLM's build contract internally inconsistent:

1. Standard CUDA requirements install Quack 0.6.5 and CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1.
2. `fmha_sm100.cmake` vendors MSA at `087c161`.
3. That MSA revision expects the Quack 0.6.4 private helper.
4. MiniMax-M3 reaches that code while compiling its sparse-attention kernel.
5. Engine initialization aborts with `AttributeError`.

This is especially easy to miss because another vendored CuTe implementation was updated for the same Quack change, while the MSA pin remained at its older revision.

#### Existing fix

The underlying MSA compatibility change has already been merged as [vllm-project/MSA #12](https://github.com/vllm-project/MSA/pull/12), “Fix packed subtraction compatibility with Quack 0.6.5.”

That change selects the public CuTe primitive when available while retaining a fallback for CUTLASS DSL 4.6:

```python
if hasattr(cute.arch, "sub_packed_f32x2"):
    sub_packed_f32x2 = cute.arch.sub_packed_f32x2
else:
    # CUTLASS DSL 4.6 uses the helper provided by older Quack releases.
    from quack.activation import sub_packed_f32x2
```

The fixed MSA revision is:

```text
f355c37eb4e1413f21ee2ad8bbad25079e6bef9d
```

[vLLM #56545](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56545) updates `fmha_sm100.cmake` from `087c161` to that fixed revision, so it appears to contain the correct integration fix.

The PR title and much of its validation focus on Rubin dependencies, however, while the MSA pin is shared by standard CUDA builds. The MSA portion should therefore also be treated and validated as a fix for the standard, non-Rubin SM100 path.

#### Workaround

Downgrading to `quack-kernels==0.6.4` and `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2` avoids this particular exception, but it only masks the incompatible caller and may conflict with the reasons those dependencies
were upgraded.

The preferred resolution is to update the vendored MSA revision to the commit
containing MSA #12, as proposed by vLLM #56545.

#### Related public issues and changes

- Regression-introducing dependency update:
  [vLLM #54927](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54927)
- MSA compatibility fix:
  [MSA #12](https://github.com/vllm-project/MSA/pull/12)
- Proposed vLLM integration:
  [vLLM #56545](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56545)
- Same removed Quack API in a different caller:
  [FlashAttention #2782](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/2782),
  fixed by [FlashAttention #2787](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2787)
- Similar but separate MSA/CuTe API incompatibility:
  [vLLM #49005](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49005), which concerns
  `cutlass.cute.core.ThrMma`, not `sub_packed_f32x2`

### 🐛 Describe the bug In dense data-parallel weight transfer, the complete `update_info` list is sent to every EngineCore. Each GPU worker selects its local payload using: ```python parallel_config.data_parallel_rank * parallel_config.world_size + self.rank ``` However, `reconfigure_for_independent_dp_rank()` resets `data_parallel_rank` to `0` for every dense DP engine. As a result, workers in non-zero DP replicas incorrectly select payloads belonging to DP0. With `DP=2` and `TP=2`: ```text DP0-TP0 → slot0 ✓ DP0-TP1 → slot1 ✓ DP1-TP0 → slot0 ✗ expected slot2 DP1-TP1 → slot1 ✗ expected slot3 ``` The DP1 workers therefore receive CUDA IPC handles belonging to GPU0 and GPU1 instead of GPU2 and GPU3. This causes an IPC UUID mismatch and makes `POST /update_weights` return HTTP 500. `data_parallel_index` preserves the original global DP identity after dense reconfiguration and should be used for payload selection. ### Reproduction environment ```text Model: facebook/opt-125m GPU: 4 × NVIDIA A40 DP: 2 TP: 2 Weight-transfer backend: IPC ``` GPU layout: ```text DP0-TP0 → GPU0 → slot0 DP0-TP1 → GPU1 → slot1 DP1-TP0 → GPU2 → slot2 DP1-TP1 → GPU3 → slot3 ``` ### 1. Start the vLLM server From the vLLM repository root: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \ VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 \ VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ .venv/bin/vllm serve facebook/opt-125m \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --data-parallel-size 2 \ --device-ids 0,1,2,3 \ --enforce-eager \ --load-format dummy \ --max-model-len 128 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.20 \ --port 8000 \ --weight-transfer-config '{"backend":"ipc"}' \ --disable-log-stats ``` Wait until both API servers report: ```text Application startup complete. ``` ### 2. Create the reproduction script Save the following as `/tmp/repro_dense_dp_tp2_ipc.py`: ```python from __future__ import annotations import os import requests import torch from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.clients import ( HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient, ) BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000" PARAMETER_NAME = "model.decoder.embed_tokens.weight" PARAMETER_SHAPE = (50272, 768) def make_payload( device: int, tensors: list[torch.Tensor], ) -> dict: tensor = torch.zeros( PARAMETER_SHAPE, dtype=torch.float16, device=device, ) tensors.append(tensor) _, rebuild_args = reduce_tensor(tensor) gpu_uuid = str(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).uuid) return { "names": [PARAMETER_NAME], "dtype_names": ["torch.float16"], "shapes": [list(PARAMETER_SHAPE)], "ipc_handles": [{gpu_uuid: rebuild_args}], } def main() -> None: assert torch.cuda.device_count() == 4 os.environ["VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION"] = "1" requests.get( f"{BASE_URL}/health", timeout=5, ).raise_for_status() # Keep the producer tensors alive until the IPC transfer completes. tensors: list[torch.Tensor] = [] # update_info[i] belongs to global worker i. update_info = [ make_payload(device, tensors) for device in range(4) ] client = HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient( BASE_URL, timeout=120, ) client.init_weight_transfer_engine({"packed": False}) client.start_weight_update() client.update_weights(update_info) client.finish_weight_update("dense-dp-tp2-e2e") print( "PASS: all four workers consumed " "their matching CUDA IPC payload" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Each payload contains only the UUID of its corresponding GPU. Therefore, selecting the wrong list element reliably produces a UUID mismatch. ### 3. Run the reproduction In another terminal: ```bash cd /data/home/xli49/lxy/vllm CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \ VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 \ .venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_dense_dp_tp2_ipc.py ``` ### Actual result The client receives: ```text requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 500 Server Error: Internal Server Error for url: http://127.0.0.1:8000/update_weights ``` The DP1 workers report: ```text GPU2 worker: IPC handle not found for GPU UUID 347b6e74... Available UUIDs: ['ad1baac4...'] # GPU0 GPU3 worker: IPC handle not found for GPU UUID 956d8c83... Available UUIDs: ['d132e9d7...'] # GPU1 ``` This confirms that: ```text DP1-TP0 selected slot0 instead of slot2 DP1-TP1 selected slot1 instead of slot3 ``` ### Expected result All workers should select their corresponding payload, and the request should succeed: ```text POST /update_weights HTTP/1.1 200 OK PASS: all four workers consumed their matching CUDA IPC payload ``` The worker index should be calculated using the preserved DP index: ```python parallel_config.data_parallel_index * parallel_config.world_size + self.rank ``` instead of the reset DP communication rank: ```python parallel_config.data_parallel_rank * parallel_config.world_size + self.rank ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash long-decode degeneration after accumulated reasoning decode
body:
### Your current environment

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA B300, ~267 GiB visible VRAM
Runtime: vLLM OpenAI-compatible server
vLLM: 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b
FlashInfer: 0.6.18
Transformers: 5.16.1
Torch: 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA: 13.0

Model: private W4A16 quantized GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint
TP: 1
Context length: ~372k

Reasoning parser: glm45
Tool-call parser: glm47
Native tools enabled

reasoning_effort=max
clear_thinking=true

MTP/EAGLE: disabled for the tests below
Prefix cache: tested on and off; issue happens in both cases

Workload: private long-running multi-agent / sub-agent coding workload with native tool calls.
I cannot post raw prompts or tool outputs publicly.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Purpose

I am running GLM-5.3-Flash in a long-running multi-agent / sub-agent coding workload with native tools and `reasoning_effort=max`.

The model works well for many turns, then after a long session it can suddenly collapse inside `reasoning`.

### Bug

The collapse is repetitive low-entropy output such as:

```text
= = = = = = = = ...
```

or:

```text
.0.0.0.0.0.0.0.0...
```

I logged raw SSE before the stream reaches the client. The bad output is already present in raw vLLM SSE, for example many deltas like:

```json
{"delta":{"reasoning":" ="}}
```

So this does not look like a client-side stream reconstruction issue.

When it happens, no tool call is emitted. The model stays stuck in `reasoning`.

### Already checked

- MTP on/off: issue happens in both cases.
- Prefix cache on/off: issue happens in both cases.
- Sampling/repetition settings: issue still happens.
- H200 and B300: similar issue, so not B300-only.
- SGLang: similar degeneration after 15-20 min.
- Lower reasoning or aggressive windowing can delay it, but they are not acceptable fixes for this workload.

Also tested/backported:

- Normalize assistant `content:null` + `tool_calls` to `content:""` before chat templating.
- PR #56635 / commit `b150783`.

The issue still happens.

### Reasoning replay

The client was originally replaying old assistant reasoning into later tool turns. I added a proxy that removes old `reasoning_content`, `reasoning`, and `thinking` before forwarding to vLLM.

In one failing session, the proxy removed ~471k chars of old reasoning and the forwarded request had zero historical `reasoning_content`.

This helped a lot, but the late-session collapse still came back.

### Replay tests

I replayed captured forwarded requests directly against vLLM, without the client.

1. Cold replay of the exact failing request: healthy, ended with `finish_reason=tool_calls`.

2. Five parallel cold replays of the same request: all healthy, all ended with `finish_reason=tool_calls`.

3. Sequential replay of historical requests: after 76 successful requests, request 77 collapsed into `.1.1.1...` then `.0.0.0...`.

4. Cold replay of request 77 only: healthy.

5. Prefill-only warmup: replayed the first 76 historical requests with `max_tokens=1`, then request 77 unchanged. Result: request 77 was healthy.

Key difference:

| Test | Prior prompt tokens | Prior decode/reasoning tokens | request 77 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Cold request 77 | 0 | 0 | healthy |
| 76 prefill-only requests, then request 77 | ~2.76M | ~76 | healthy |
| 76 full requests, then request 77 | ~2.76M | ~200k | collapsed |

So it looks more related to accumulated decode/reasoning than to prefill volume alone.

### Question

Could this be a correctness issue in the GLM-5.3 `glm5next` decode path, for example KDA/recurrent state lifecycle, slot reuse, hybrid KV/KDA mapping, CUDA graph replay, or numerical drift during long decode?

Is there a recommended branch or patch set for GLM-5.3-Flash long agentic workloads on single-GPU Blackwell/B300?

### Privacy

The workload is private and proprietary, so I cannot post raw prompts, raw tool outputs, or raw `forwarded.json` publicly.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: Startup memory-profiling assertion aborts whenever free memory grows, contradicting documented support for GPU co-tenancy
body:
### Your current environment ``` # primary reproduction -- discrete NVIDIA, stock published image GPU : NVIDIA H100 NVL (95830 MiB), x86_64 Driver / CUDA : 580.105.08 / CUDA 13.0 vLLM : 0.29.0 (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0) # secondary reproduction -- integrated GPU, no co-tenant at all GPU : NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), sm_121, aarch64 Driver / CUDA : 580.142 / CUDA 13.0 vLLM : 0.27.1 Memory : 119.67 GiB unified CPU+GPU pool ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug `Worker.determine_available_memory` aborts engine startup whenever free memory is higher after profiling than before it: ``` AssertionError: Error in memory profiling. Initial free memory 82.94 GiB, current free memory 90.17 GiB. This happens when other processes sharing the same container release GPU memory while vLLM is profiling during initialization. To fix this, ensure consistent GPU memory allocation or isolate vLLM in its own container. ``` The guard rests on an assumption stated only in a code comment: ```python # NOTE(woosuk): Here we assume that the other processes using the same # GPU did not change their memory usage during the profiling. assert init_free_memory >= free_gpu_memory, ( ``` Any co-tenant that *releases* memory during the ~10 s profiling window kills startup, on a plain discrete NVIDIA GPU, with vLLM alone in its own container. The reproduction below does this in about a minute on any CUDA device. ### Scope: this affects every device type | setting | what can move the measured value | fires? | |---|---|---| | discrete GPU, sole tenant | nothing | no | | discrete GPU, co-tenant (NVIDIA or AMD) | another process on that GPU releasing memory | yes | | integrated / unified-memory GPU | any process anywhere on the host | yes, **with no sharing at all** | Row 2 is reproduced below on NVIDIA; #53591 fixed the same row for AMD. Row 3 is covered by the GB10 section further down. ### Steps to reproduce (any single CUDA GPU, ~1 minute) Self-contained: two containers from the **same published vLLM image** on one GPU, no host Python and no vLLM checkout. Needs Docker + NVIDIA Container Toolkit and a GPU with roughly `HOLD_GIB + UTIL * total` free. - The co-tenant is plain PyTorch — no vLLM, no second engine. It holds 8 GiB, then releases it once vLLM logs `Model loading took`, i.e. during the profile run. It stays alive afterwards, so the only thing that changes is the *allocation*. - vLLM is a stock `vllm serve facebook/opt-125m`, explicitly capped with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.2`. - `RELEASE=0` runs the control: identical setup, co-tenant simply never releases.
repro.sh — save, chmod +x, run as GPU=<idx> ./repro.sh ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Reproduce vLLM's startup memory-profiling assertion on any single CUDA GPU. # # Two containers, one GPU: # * co-tenant: plain PyTorch, holds HOLD_GIB of device memory, releases it # once vLLM has loaded its weights (i.e. during the profile run) # * vLLM : a stock `vllm serve`, capped with --gpu-memory-utilization # # vLLM compares free device memory before and after profiling and aborts if it # went up, so the release makes startup fail deterministically. # # Requires: docker + NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and a GPU with roughly # (HOLD_GIB + UTIL * total) free. Nothing else -- no host Python, no venv. set -uo pipefail GPU=${GPU:-0} # index of the GPU to use IMAGE=${IMAGE:-vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0} MODEL=${MODEL:-facebook/opt-125m} UTIL=${UTIL:-0.2} # --gpu-memory-utilization HOLD_GIB=${HOLD_GIB:-8} # GiB the co-tenant holds RELEASE=${RELEASE:-1} # RELEASE=0 -> control run, startup succeeds WORK=$(mktemp -d) LOG=$WORK/vllm.log TAG=vllm-memprofile-$$ trap 'docker rm -f "$TAG-cotenant" "$TAG-vllm" >/dev/null 2>&1' EXIT echo "gpu=$GPU image=$IMAGE model=$MODEL util=$UTIL hold=${HOLD_GIB}GiB" echo "logs: $WORK" # 1. Co-tenant grabs HOLD_GIB and waits for a release signal on /sig. docker run --rm --name "$TAG-cotenant" --gpus "device=$GPU" \ -e HOLD_GIB="$HOLD_GIB" -v "$WORK:/sig" --entrypoint python3 "$IMAGE" -c ' import os, time, torch gib = int(os.environ["HOLD_GIB"]) buf = torch.empty(gib << 30, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda").fill_(1) torch.cuda.synchronize() free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info() print(f"[cotenant] holding {gib} GiB, device free {free/2**30:.2f}/{total/2**30:.2f} GiB", flush=True) open("/sig/held", "w").close() while not os.path.exists("/sig/release"): time.sleep(0.2) del buf torch.cuda.empty_cache() # hand the pages back to the driver free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info() print(f"[cotenant] released, device free {free/2**30:.2f}/{total/2**30:.2f} GiB", flush=True) time.sleep(1e6) # stay alive: only the allocation moved ' > "$WORK/cotenant.log" 2>&1 & for _ in $(seq 1 600); do [ -e "$WORK/held" ] && break; sleep 1; done [ -e "$WORK/held" ] || { echo "co-tenant failed to allocate:"; cat "$WORK/cotenant.log"; exit 1; } cat "$WORK/cotenant.log" # 2. Stock vLLM on the same GPU, in its own container. docker run --rm --name "$TAG-vllm" --gpus "device=$GPU" --ipc=host \ -v "$HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface" "$IMAGE" \ --model "$MODEL" --gpu-memory-utilization "$UTIL" > "$LOG" 2>&1 & VLLM_PID=$! # 3. Release once the weights are in, i.e. just before the profile run. if [ "$RELEASE" = 1 ]; then for _ in $(seq 1 1800); do grep -q "Model loading took" "$LOG" && break; sleep 1; done sleep 1; touch "$WORK/release" fi # 4. Wait for the outcome. for _ in $(seq 1 900); do grep -q "Error in memory profiling" "$LOG" && { echo "RESULT: reproduced"; break; } grep -q "Application startup complete" "$LOG" && { echo "RESULT: started (not reproduced)"; break; } kill -0 "$VLLM_PID" 2>/dev/null || { echo "RESULT: container exited"; break; } sleep 1 done cat "$WORK/cotenant.log" grep -E "Initial free memory|Error in memory profiling|Available KV cache|Free memory on device" "$LOG" | tail ```
**Result** — `GPU=6 ./repro.sh`, reproduced in 59 s, every run: ``` gpu=6 image=vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 model=facebook/opt-125m util=0.2 hold=8GiB [cotenant] holding 8 GiB, device free 83.45/93.09 GiB RESULT: reproduced [cotenant] holding 8 GiB, device free 83.45/93.09 GiB [cotenant] released, device free 90.30/93.09 GiB ``` ``` (EngineCore pid=835) ERROR [core.py:1374] File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 585, in determine_available_memory (EngineCore pid=835) ERROR [core.py:1374] assert init_free_memory >= free_gpu_memory, ( (EngineCore pid=835) ERROR [core.py:1374] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ (EngineCore pid=835) ERROR [core.py:1374] AssertionError: Error in memory profiling. Initial free memory 82.94 GiB, current free memory 90.17 GiB. This happens when other processes sharing the same container release GPU memory while vLLM is profiling during initialization. To fix this, ensure consistent GPU memory allocation or isolate vLLM in its own container. ``` **Control** — `GPU=6 RELEASE=0 ./repro.sh`, same co-tenant, same 8 GiB resident, never released: ``` RESULT: started (not reproduced) Available KV cache memory: 17.41 GiB Free memory on device (82.94/93.09 GiB) on startup. Desired GPU memory utilization is (0.2, 18.62 GiB). Actual usage is 0.77 GiB for consumed memory (weights + non-torch), 0.44 GiB for peak activation, and 0.13 GiB for CUDAGraph memory. ``` So co-tenancy itself is fine and the requested budget is respected. Only the *direction* of the co-tenant's memory change decides whether vLLM starts. Note also that `total_consumed` is 0.77 GiB here, so a co-tenant releasing as little as ~1 GiB is enough; 8 GiB just removes any timing sensitivity. Two things the result rules out: - **The suggested remedy does not apply.** The message says to "isolate vLLM in its own container". It already is — the co-tenant is a *different container*, and neither shares an address space with the other. Container isolation cannot make two processes on one GPU see different values of `cudaMemGetInfo`. - **No concurrent model loading is involved.** The co-tenant never loads a model and never touches vLLM. This is the distinction from #35929, which was declined on the grounds that vLLM "doesn't really expect multiple models to be loaded on the same device at once". ### The assumption contradicts vLLM's own documentation `gpu_memory_utilization` does not merely tolerate co-tenants — its reference documentation walks the user through sharing a GPU between two vLLM instances: ```python gpu_memory_utilization: float = Field(default=0.92, gt=0, le=1) """The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor, which can range from 0 to 1. ... This is a per-instance limit, and only applies to the current vLLM instance. It does not matter if you have another vLLM instance running on the same GPU. For example, if you have two vLLM instances running on the same GPU, you can set the GPU memory utilization to 0.5 for each instance.""" ``` Sharing a device is a documented, first-class configuration elsewhere too: - `docs/training/weight_transfer/ipc.md` — CUDA IPC weight transfer exists for *"Training and inference share the **same GPU(s)** (colocated)"*. - `docs/training/trl.md` — colocate mode: *"vLLM runs inside the trainer process and shares GPU memory with the training model."* - `docs/features/multimodal_inputs.md` — the video-decode backend **requires** MPS because *"multiple CUDA processes share the same GPU"*; here the co-tenant is vLLM's own API server. - `docs/configuration/optimization.md` — refers to *"hardware or **co-tenant** changes"* as an ordinary reason a cached `--kv-cache-memory` value goes stale. I could not find any documentation stating that vLLM requires exclusive use of a device. This matters because it is the stated reason a previous fix was declined. In #35929, the maintainer response was: > Regarding memory profiling during concurrent loading, vLLM doesn't account for > this even for non-UMA devices because it doesn't really expect multiple models to > be loaded on the same device at once. So I think this is out of scope in terms of > design. Please correct me if I'm wrong @youkaichao @mgoin That invitation to correct is the reason for this issue. If co-tenancy really is out of scope, then the `gpu_memory_utilization` docstring, the IPC weight-transfer engine, TRL colocate mode and the MPS requirement for video decoding all document something unsupported, and should be corrected instead. If co-tenancy is supported — which the documentation and #53591 both indicate — then aborting because a co-tenant released memory is a bug. ### Integrated GPUs fail without any co-tenant at all On integrated GPUs the assertion no longer concerns device memory. `MemorySnapshot.measure` substitutes a host-wide metric, because `cudaMemGetInfo` under-reports free memory when reclaimable page cache is large: ```python self.free_memory, self.total_memory = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(device) if current_platform.is_integrated_gpu(device.index): # ... cudaMemGetInfo underreports free memory ... self.free_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available ``` The substitution is correct and necessary. On a GB10 `cudaMemGetInfo` reports 0.94 GiB free while 108.92 GiB sits in reclaimable page cache: ``` device : NVIDIA GB10 vllm is_integrated_gpu : True cudaMemGetInfo free : 0.94 GiB (total 119.67 GiB) psutil available : 109.38 GiB MemorySnapshot.free_mem : 109.38 GiB ``` But it means `total_consumed = before_create.free_memory - after_profile.free_memory` is the difference of two readings of a *system-wide* gauge, taken ~60 s apart, and attributed entirely to vLLM. `MemAvailable` is non-monotonic by nature. Sampling it on a fully idle GB10 for 60 s: ``` initial available : 110.72 GiB max available : 110.80 GiB min available : 110.10 GiB samples above baseline : 64/240 (26.7%) ``` Each of those 64 samples would have tripped the assertion had it been the after-profile snapshot. No second engine, no other CUDA process, an idle machine. To make it deterministic rather than a 27 % coin flip, the same trick as above works, except that on a UMA device the interfering process need not touch the GPU at all. An ordinary **host** process — outside the container, no CUDA — that allocates ~20 GiB of anonymous memory and frees it once the log shows `Model loading took` is enough: ``` [holder] held; available now 90.61 GiB [holder] trigger seen, releasing in 1.0s [holder] released; available now 99.54 GiB AssertionError: Error in memory profiling. Initial free memory 88.37 GiB, current free memory 99.29 GiB. ``` ### Suggested fix The remedy already exists in the same function. #53591 added `maybe_rocm_profiling_fallback`, which detects this exact condition and sizes the KV cache from torch-reserved bytes rather than aborting — but gates it to one vendor: ```python if profile_result.total_consumed >= 0 or not current_platform.is_rocm(): return None ``` That gate is why the reproduction above still fails on 0.29.0, which ships the fallback: the H100 takes the `return None` branch and hits the assertion. When `total_consumed` is negative the measurement is meaningless on every platform, and torch-reserved is a valid process-local lower bound everywhere. That reasoning never depended on ROCm. Dropping the platform gate (and renaming the helper) covers integrated GPUs and shared discrete NVIDIA GPUs with the mechanism already in tree. The message text should also be corrected on both counts: container isolation is not a remedy (the reproduction has vLLM in its own container), and on integrated GPUs it has no bearing on the metric being compared. I'm happy to open a PR for this. ### Relation to existing reports - #35920 / #35929 — same failure on DGX Spark, framed as a *concurrent deployment* problem (three engines at once) and declined on the design grounds quoted above. This report is broader in scope but narrower in what it requires: no concurrency of any kind is needed to hit it. - #53591 — merged fix for the identical symptom on discrete AMD GPUs shared by two engines. Establishes the diagnosis, the remedy, and that co-tenancy is treated as a supported configuration in practice. - #49760 — caps the budget and profiling transient on integrated GPUs so an over-large run fails cleanly. Complementary: it does not touch this assertion, and this issue is not an over-allocation. - #48140 — discussion confirming the `psutil.virtual_memory().available` substitution is intentional and live on GB10. - #9232 — the same assertion on discrete NVIDIA hardware, from 2024. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues and asked in the vLLM forum/Slack. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Identical overlay in good and bad builds; unrelated to streams/decode. ### 🐛 Describe the bug The `eed1f3d0 → dc36fcce` range reintroduces an intermittent decode-throughput collapse on **context-load decode rows at depth 32768, concurrency 1** (and inter-sweep jumpiness on `pp2048 (c1)`), on a stack that PLE-CPU-offloads via UVA — i.e. exactly the path #56512 rewires. Benchmark: llama-benchy 0.4.0, identical command per build: `--pp 2048 --tg 128 --depth 0 8192 32768 131072 --concurrency 1 4 --runs 3 --latency-mode generation --enable-prefix-caching` | row (`t/s` mean ± sd) | eed1f3d0 (5 sweeps) | dc36fcce sweep #1 | dc36fcce sweep #2 | |---|---|---|---| | `ctx_tg @ d32768 (c1)` | 127–148, sd ≤ 8.7 | **82.50 ± 46.37** | **95.16 ± 61.63** | | `pp2048 (c1)` | stable | 17203 ± 209 | 12913 ± 53 | | `tg128 (c1)` | 139–169 | 151.63 ± 14.11 | 143.92 ± 8.84 | | `tg128 (c4)` | 354–406 | 408.72 ± 22.92 | 382.54 ± 18.20 | | `ctx_pp @ d131072 (c1)` | ~10003–10400 | 10406.56 ± 1.13 | 10379.13 ± 6.26 | *(good-build column: the V0/V3/V4/V4b/V5 sweeps on eed1f3d0 with this exact config; V1-eager and V2-no-spec sweeps excluded as different configs.)* ### Reproduction Boot the bad build (same command works for the good build by swapping the tag; requires the model checkpoint and a host with ≥60 GiB free RAM for the pinned PLE table): ```sh docker run --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size=8g \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \ vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-dc36fcce902a63eab06c1b93a5c4a5ee178a0c56 \ vllm serve dicksondickson/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-reshard-mtp-fix \ --quantization modelopt \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --max-num-seqs 12 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --trust-remote-code \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' ``` (Our production launch additionally sets `--enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --chat-template `; omitted above as irrelevant to decode performance.) Then run, per build, and compare the `ctx_tg @ d32768 (c1)` row between two independent full invocations: ```sh llama-benchy --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 \ --model dicksondickson/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-reshard-mtp-fix \ --served-model-name qwen-3-8-flash-next \ --pp 2048 --tg 128 --depth 0 8192 32768 131072 --concurrency 1 4 \ --runs 3 --latency-mode generation --enable-prefix-caching ``` Expected: `ctx_tg @ d32768 (c1)` ≈ 127–148 t/s with sd < 10 across runs (as on eed1f3d0). Actual on dc36fcce: one normal run (~145 t/s) plus one-to-two collapsed runs (~40–65 t/s) in every full sweep, mean sd 46–62. The identical command against the good build never collapsed in 5 sweeps. ### Isolation evidence (same bad build, same engine boot) - **Isolated 7-run repro of the sick cell** (`--depth 32768 --concurrency 1 --runs 7`): `ctx_tg @ d32768 = 150.08 ± 7.73` — clean. - **Replay of the sweep prefix** (d8192 c1+c4 then d32768 c1): `146.46 ± 15.60` — clean. - Only the **full sweep sequence** (all four depths, c1+c4, ~14 min sustained) reproduces, in 2/2 attempts. ### Ruled out - **KV pressure / preemption:** zero preemption-related engine log lines during either bad sweep window, and the KV pool (269,228 tokens) is byte-identical to the good build's boot report. - **Engine-visible graph fallback:** no capture/fallback/degrade log lines during either sweep. - **Host interference:** a monitoring-stack (Prometheus+Grafana) container start landed mid-sweep #1, but sweep #2 ran with no other containers active and reproduced identically. No Xid / throttling / OOM entries in `dmesg`/journal. - **#56654 (MRV2 Triton JIT warmup revert):** exonerated by construction — it byte-exactly reverts #56323, whose merge (2026-09-13T00:24) postdates the good base, so migration+revert cancel within the range. ### Prime suspects in the range 1. **#56512 — the prefetch side-stream** (`_prefetch_stream`, `record_stream`/`wait_stream` on per-step lookup tensors). The affected rows are exactly context-load decode (first decode steps after a 32k prefix load = the heaviest prefetch bursts). If the event/stream pattern interacts badly with CUDA-graph replay (e.g. captured graph vs live-event ordering under sustained mixed load), degradation would be silent — which matches: no log lines, no preemptions, only a subset of steps falling back or serializing. 2. **#56682 (dummy-init / CPU engram fill changes)** — alters what gets warmed at startup; possible lazy first-capture/compile during serving. (Less likely: a single one-time event would poison 1 run, not 2 of 3, and isolated short runs would likely also catch it.) ### Asks - Could #56512's maintainers check the prefetch event pattern against CUDA-graph replay and against `cudagraph_capture_sizes`/`FULL` decode-graph modes? Specifically: `record_stream` on inputs captured into a replayed graph, and `wait_stream`/event ordering when the current stream is a replayed graph's stream. - If there's a debug switch (e.g. env to disable prefetch while keeping `cpu_offload`), pointing it out would let me bisect on-host between "#56512 fault" vs "range collateral" within a single boot — happy to run any experiment and post results. - For calibration: the async prefetch measured **no** throughput win on this box (deep-context decode at 131k/c4: 8.45/6.49 t/s vs 6.91 on the good build — within noise), so if this is a known-risky interaction, it currently costs stability without visible benefit on a TP=1 UVA-offload setup. ## Additional context Two full result tables, the isolated-repro table, the prefix-replay table, and engine logs for both bad sweeps are available; I can attach them or provide the exact llama-benchy invocation and per-cell raw JSON (`llama-benchy --save-result`) on request. Host is a single-GPU community box (244 GiB RAM) running this as a daily driver, currently pinned to `nightly-eed1f3d0` and avoiding all nightlies containing #56512 until this resolves. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
