title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: SimpleCPUOffloadConnector crashes with `assert block_size % hash_block_size == 0` (block_size=8, hash_block_size=32)
body:
### Your current environment

## Environment

- Hardware: 8 × H100 80GB (HBM3), CUDA 13
- vLLM version: `0.1.dev20904+g179dd0fa9` (image `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909`)
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (fp8, hybrid KV cache: MLA full-attention group @ block_size 32 + SWA/circular-buffer group @ block_size 8; DSpark MTP speculative decoding)
- Python 3.12, TP=8, EP=8

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

Serving `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (hybrid KV: full-attention MLA + sliding-window/circular-buffer groups) with the `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` crashes the EngineCore on the **first scheduled request** with:

```
(EngineCore pid=536) [ASSERT-DEBUG] resolve_block_hashes: block_size=8, hash_block_size=32, modulo=8   <-- our instrumented print, see note below
(EngineCore pid=536) ERROR ... assert block_size % hash_block_size == 0
AssertionError
```

(The `[ASSERT-DEBUG]` line is **not** stock vLLM output — we volume-mounted a patched `kv_cache_utils.py` into the container that prints `block_size`/`hash_block_size`/modulo just before the assert, since the bare `AssertionError` carries no values. Stock vLLM produces only the assert line; details in *Extra context*.)

Note `block_size (8) < hash_block_size (32)` — the call asks `resolve_block_hashes` to view 32-token-granularity hashes at a *finer* 8-token granularity, but the function only supports the coarsening direction (`block_size >= hash_block_size`, enforced by the divisibility assert). With 8 < 32 the assert `8 % 32 == 0` can never hold, so the crash is deterministic on the first request.

## Deploy command (paths/ports/keys elided)

```bash
docker run --gpus all --privileged --ipc=host --net=host \
  <model-volume-mounts> \
  vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv41-flash-0909 \
  vllm serve <model-path> \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 120, 128, 136, 144, 152, 160]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":118111600640,"lazy_offload":false}}'
```

Note on `--compilation-config`: the default cudagraph capture sizes (up to 512 with profiling) OOM on this model+hardware, so capture sizes are explicitly capped at 160.

## Reproduction

1. Start the server with the command above. Startup completes normally (weights load, CPU offload pool allocates, CUDA graphs capture, "Application startup complete").
2. Send any request that triggers KV offload bookkeeping (e.g. a chat completion with a long prompt).
3. EngineCore crashes immediately in the scheduler step:

```
(EngineCore pid=536) [ASSERT-DEBUG] resolve_block_hashes: block_size=8, hash_block_size=32, modulo=8
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1430, in run_busy_loop
    self._process_engine_step()
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1373, in schedule
    meta = self._build_kv_connector_meta(self.connector, scheduler_output)
  File ".../vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py", line 268, in build_connector_meta
    return self.scheduler_manager.build_connector_meta(scheduler_output)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 453, in build_connector_meta
    store_gpu, store_cpu, store_req_ids, store_meta = self.prepare_store_specs(...)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 523, in prepare_store_specs
    return self._prepare_eager_store_specs(scheduler_output)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 638, in _prepare_eager_store_specs
    self._select_eager_blocks_to_store(state, block_ids_by_group)
  File ".../vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py", line 720, in _select_eager_blocks_to_store
    resolved_hashes = resolve_block_hashes(
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py", line 2788, in resolve_block_hashes
    assert block_size % hash_block_size == 0
AssertionError
```

## Root cause analysis

The offload path mixes up per-group block geometry with the global hash granularity:

1. `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes()` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:~726-792`) computes for multi-group models:
   - `hash_block_size = gcd(group_block_sizes)` over **prefix-cacheable** groups — for DSV4.1-Flash: gcd(32, 8) = 8? No — in our crash the resolved `hash_block_size=32` and the group's `group_size=8`, meaning the SWA/circular-buffer group (block_size 8) was **excluded** from the hashing_sizes GCD (its `prefix_cacheable` is False for `CircularBufferSpec`/Kpool-tail style specs), so `hash_block_size` followed the full-attention group (32).
   - `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` stores this as `self.hash_block_size` and asserts `self.block_size % self.hash_block_size == 0` at init (manager.py:129) — which passes because `self.block_size` is the **scheduler** block size (LCM), not any single group's size.

2. At request time, `_select_eager_blocks_to_store()` (manager.py:720) iterates **all** KV cache groups — including the non-prefix-cacheable SWA group — and calls:
   ```python
   resolved_hashes = resolve_block_hashes(
       request.block_hashes, self.hash_block_size, group_size)
   ```
   with `group_size = 8` (the SWA group) and `hash_block_size = 32`.

3. `resolve_block_hashes()` (kv_cache_utils.py:2770-2789) only supports viewing fine hashes at a **coarser** granularity (`block_size >= hash_block_size`, enforced by the assert). Receiving `block_size(8) < hash_block_size(32)` violates its contract.

Two contributing bugs:
- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` passes a group-local block size into a function whose contract assumes the caller wants a **scheduler-level** view; for groups with `block_size < hash_block_size` the call is meaningless (there are no per-group hashes at 8-token granularity — hashes only exist at 32-token boundaries).
- The init-time assert (manager.py:129) checks the wrong invariant (`scheduler_block_size % hash_block_size == 0`), which is trivially true and hides the per-group mismatch until the first request.

## Suggested fixes

Any of these would unblock DSV4.1-Flash-class hybrid models; (1)+(2) together are probably the right combination:

1. **Skip hash resolution for non-prefix-cacheable groups** in `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` (and the lazy variant): the SWA/circular-buffer group's KV is windowed/evicted anyway, so offloading it by content hash is not meaningful. Only resolve hashes for groups whose `kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable` is True and whose `block_size >= hash_block_size`.

2. **Clamp per-group block size in the manager**: when calling `resolve_block_hashes`, pass `max(group_size, self.hash_block_size)` or round `group_size` up to a multiple of `hash_block_size`, mirroring what `BlockHashListWithBlockSize` does for the coarser direction.

3. **Harden `resolve_block_hashes`**: replace the bare assert with a descriptive error, and/or support the `block_size < hash_block_size` direction by returning the finest available view with an offset warning — though semantically this case should be prevented by the caller (fix 1).

## Extra context

- Same model + same image **without** `--kv-transfer-config` serves and benchmarks fine (stable under 100K-prefix prefix-repetition load, and single-batch decode TPS ~330-350 tok/s with DSpark), so the regression is specific to the CPU offload connector path.
- An equivalent sglang deployment with hierarchical cache (`--enable-hierarchical-cache`, host pool ~127 GB/rank paged) serves the same workload without issue, for comparison.
- We patched `kv_cache_utils.py` inside the container with a debug print before the assert to capture the failing values (`block_size=8, hash_block_size=32, modulo=8`), which is how the numbers above were obtained.

---
*This issue report was generated with AI assistance.*

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

body:
### Your current environment

AMD MI308X

### 🐛 Describe the bug

First, a huge thank you to the entire vLLM engineering team and community. Your work on making high-performance LLM serving accessible across NVIDIA, AMD ROCm, Intel, TPU, and CPU backends is genuinely transformative — the pace of model coverage (DeepSeek V4, V4.1-Flash, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3, …), the unified frontends (Python + Rust), the disaggregation and KV-cache innovations all land in months, not years. The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support that merged today in PR #56201 is fantastic — thank you for sustaining this project as a true open-source effort and supporting the AMD ROCm path so thoroughly.

I'm reaching out to flag a reproducible inconsistency between the official recipe documentation and what is actually published on Docker Hub, which is currently blocking a production rollout on our side.

Problem

The official recipe for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on AMD MI300X ( https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash?hardware=mi300x ) instructs users to pull:

`docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:deepseekv41-flash-0909`

However, this tag does not exist on Docker Hub. Attempts to pull it from multiple mirrors consistently fail with:

Error response from daemon: pull access denied … repository does not exist or may require 'docker login' (404 / manifest unknown)
Error response from daemon: received unexpected HTTP status: 403 Forbidden
The same 403 / not-found responses are returned when retrying through Chinese registry mirrors (docker.1ms.run, docker.m.daocloud.io, dockerproxy.net, docker.xuanyuan.me).
This blocks following the recipe exactly as written, and is misleading for users who arrive at the recipe page expecting an official one-line deployment path.

where can I find the  `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:deepseekv41-flash-0909`  ？

thank you again~~~

3× AMD Instinct MI308X nodes (gfx942, ROCm), 192 GiB HBM each
OS: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 6.8, Docker 24.x
ROCm driver: 6.2.4

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Describe the bug The non-streaming `/v1/messages` response has no `stop_sequence` key unless generation stopped on a matched stop string. `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` serializes the response with `generator.model_dump(exclude_none=True)`, and `AnthropicMessagesResponse` declares `stop_sequence: str | None = None`, so the null value is dropped from the wire. `stop_reason` is dropped the same way when it is null. Anthropic's published schema lists both as required, nullable members of `Message` (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages, response fields `stop_reason` and `stop_sequence`; in the OpenAPI spec the SDKs are generated from, `Message.required` lists both and `stop_sequence` is `string | null`). Anthropic's own non-streaming examples carry `"stop_sequence": null`. The official SDKs tolerate the missing key; a schema-validating proxy does not, which is how this was found (vLLM Semantic Router, vllm-project/semantic-router#3500). This is the non-streaming twin of #55324. That one was `exclude_unset=True` on the streaming `message_delta`; this one is `exclude_none=True` on the buffered response, so the streaming fix does not cover it. `message_start` on the stream already carries both keys explicitly. Live, vLLM 0.26.0, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`, `"stream": false`, content elided: ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-b09cf4dae16a22a0","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[...],"model":"Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8","stop_reason":"max_tokens","usage":{"input_tokens":57,"output_tokens":16}} ``` Keys present: `content, id, model, role, stop_reason, type, usage`. No `stop_sequence`. Same on main at `828f4f19` (2026-09-10): `api_router.py` line 82. ### To Reproduce No GPU needed. Build the route's FastAPI app with a mocked handler that returns an `AnthropicMessagesResponse(stop_reason="end_turn")`, POST `/v1/messages` with `"stream": false`, and inspect `response.json()`: `"stop_sequence"` is not a key. Inspecting the model attribute hides the omission (`stop_sequence is None`); `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` reproduces it. With a server: ``` curl -s http://:8000/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'x-api-key: x' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{"model":"","max_tokens":16,"stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: OK"}]}' ``` ### Expected behavior `"stop_sequence": null` (and `"stop_reason": null` if ever null) on the non-streaming response, matching the schema and the streaming `message_delta` after #55325. What `exclude_none` prunes today should stay pruned: the vLLM extension fields (`kv_transfer_params`, `ec_transfer_params`) and the members of each content block that do not apply to its type. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Batch invariance is broken when sequence parallelism / async TP is enabled (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` + `pass_config.enable_sp`)
body:
### Your current environment - vLLM main @ 7470082f5 (2026-09-10), Python sources with the v0.29.0 precompiled kernels (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`); also reproduced with the v0.29.0 wheel - torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, NCCL 2.27.3 - 4x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 96 GB), PCIe only (no NVLink), driver 580.159.04 - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` (bf16), attention backend `TRITON_ATTN` ### 🐛 Describe the bug `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` is supposed to make outputs independent of the batch composition. With tensor parallelism it holds as long as sequence parallelism is **off**, but as soon as `pass_config.enable_sp=True` is set (or `fuse_gemm_comms=True`, which implies it), the same request produces different logprobs — and with greedy sampling different tokens — depending on how many other requests are in the batch. Nothing in the config guards against this combination: `enable_sp` / `fuse_gemm_comms` are never checked against `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (compare the existing guards for cascade attention and the fused allreduce+RMSNorm path in `vllm/config/vllm.py`). `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` also does not mention SP / async TP. **Measurement.** 64 prompts, greedy (`temperature=0`, `max_tokens=24`, `logprobs=1`, `ignore_eos=True`), `seed=0`, `max_model_len=512`, `max_num_seqs=64`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5`, default compilation (SP forces full-graph + `cudagraph_mode=FULL`). Each prompt is generated once alone (`bs=1`) and once with all 64 prompts in a single `generate()` call (`bs=64`); token ids and sampled-token logprobs are compared bitwise. `sp_min_token_num` is set explicitly because the SP threshold heuristic returns `None` on sm_120 (it only has SM90/SM100 buckets); on H100/B200 the heuristic enables SP automatically once `enable_sp=True`, so the same paths are hit there. | TP | `enable_sp` | `sp_min_token_num` | tokens with different logprob | prompts whose greedy output changed | max abs logprob diff | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4 | False | – | **0 / 1536** | 0 / 64 | 0 | | 4 | True | 64 | 1522 / 1536 | 17 / 64 | 2.98 | | 4 | True | 1 (SP on every compile range) | 1527 / 1536 | 15 / 64 | 2.04 | | 2 | True | 64 | 1239 / 1536 | 6 / 64 | 2.13 | | 2 | True | 1 | 4 / 1536 | 0 / 64 | 3.1e-6 | So: 1. Batch invariance under TP=4 is clean without SP (row 1), so this is not a general TP problem. 2. With SP it is broken both when batches straddle the SP threshold (rows 2, 4: below the threshold the graph keeps `all_reduce`, above it the `SequenceParallelismPass` rewrites `all_reduce + rms_norm` into `reduce_scatter + rms_norm + all_gather`) **and** when SP is applied to every compile range (row 3). The SP path itself is not batch-invariant. 3. TP=2 with SP everywhere is almost invariant (row 5), TP=4 is not (row 3). That is what you get if the reduction order of the reduce-scatter depends on which rank owns a token's output chunk: with 2 ranks `a+b` is commutative, with 4 ranks the ring order starting at the owner rank changes as the batch composition changes. (`reduce_scatterv` already has a deterministic root-0 reduce+scatter branch for the MoE combine under batch invariance, added in #45683 for exactly this class of problem; the plain `reduce_scatter` used by the SP pass has no such branch.) ### Reproduction
bi_sp_probe.py (run with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN python bi_sp_probe.py <tp> <off|threshold>) ```python import sys, json from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams tp = int(sys.argv[1]); sp = sys.argv[2] # sp: "off" or an int threshold N = 64 pass_config = {"enable_sp": False} if sp == "off" else {"enable_sp": True, "sp_min_token_num": int(sp)} llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B", tensor_parallel_size=tp, max_model_len=512, max_num_seqs=N, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, compilation_config={"pass_config": pass_config}, seed=0) cc = llm.llm_engine.vllm_config.compilation_config print("enable_sp =", cc.pass_config.enable_sp, "sp_min_token_num =", cc.pass_config.sp_min_token_num) base = ["The capital of France is", "def fibonacci(n):", "秋天的风", "In 1969, humans first", "The derivative of x^2 is", "Once upon a time in a small village", "SELECT name FROM users WHERE", "The mitochondria is", "Explain quantum entanglement briefly:", "import numpy as np\n", "The recipe calls for two cups of", "Dear hiring manager,", "翻译成英文：今天天气很好", "1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8,", "The theory of relativity states", "To be or not to be,"] prompts = [f"{base[i % len(base)]} ({i})" for i in range(N)] sp_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=24, logprobs=1, ignore_eos=True) def run(batch): out = [] for o in llm.generate(batch, sp_params, use_tqdm=False): toks = list(o.outputs[0].token_ids) lps = [float(d[t].logprob) for t, d in zip(toks, o.outputs[0].logprobs)] out.append((toks, lps)) return out single = [run([p])[0] for p in prompts] # bs=1, one request at a time batched = run(prompts) # bs=64, all requests together tok_mismatch = sum(a[0] != b[0] for a, b in zip(single, batched)) lp_mismatch = sum(x != y for (_, la), (_, lb) in zip(single, batched) for x, y in zip(la, lb)) maxd = max((abs(x - y) for (_, la), (_, lb) in zip(single, batched) for x, y in zip(la, lb)), default=0.0) print(json.dumps(dict(tp=tp, sp=sp, tokens=sum(len(l) for _, l in single), logprob_mismatch_tokens=lp_mismatch, prompts_with_different_tokens=tok_mismatch, max_abs_logprob_diff=maxd))) ```
Expected: `logprob_mismatch_tokens == 0` for every row, as it is for `sp=off`. ### Proposed fix 1. Short term: when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, force `pass_config.enable_sp = pass_config.fuse_gemm_comms = False` with a `warning_once`, next to the existing batch-invariance guards in `vllm/config/vllm.py`, and add a multi-GPU regression test (TP=4, prompts on both sides of `sp_min_token_num`) to `tests/v1/determinism/`. Document the limitation in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`. 2. Longer term: keep SP under batch invariance by giving the SP pass's reduce-scatter a fixed, owner-independent reduction order (e.g. the root-0 `reduce` + `scatter` path that `reduce_scatterv` already uses for the MoE combine), then re-enable it. I'm happy to send the PR for (1) with the test. @mosafariuk since #50505 is about custom allreduce under batch invariance and mentions AG/RS guards as a follow-up: does that follow-up already cover the SP reduce-scatter path, or should this be handled separately? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug This appears to be a Qwen3-VL runtime regression/inconsistency related to the modality-scoped `mm_processor_kwargs` support introduced in #53808, which fixed #52834. #53808 added modality-aware overlays so that vLLM-side reads such as token budgets and dummy-input sizing can correctly see HF-style nested `images_kwargs` / `videos_kwargs` without leaking an override across modalities. However, in the Qwen3-VL runtime processing path, the modality-resolved view can diverge from the kwargs representation ultimately passed to the HuggingFace processor. I can reproduce two manifestations of this with `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`: 1. A scoped partial `videos_kwargs.size` is resolved by vLLM and also materialized as a flat `size`, while the original nested `size` remains. Transformers therefore receives the same processor kwarg in both forms and rejects it as a duplicate. 2. A scoped partial `images_kwargs.size` is forwarded to the image processor without first resolving it against the processor defaults. The Qwen image processor requires both `shortest_edge` and `longest_edge`, so the partial override fails at runtime. Conceptually, both failures happen at the same boundary: ```text modality-scoped processor kwargs | +----------------+----------------+ | | videos_kwargs.size images_kwargs.size | | vLLM modality overlay partial size kept | | full flat size created sent unresolved while nested survives | | | v v flat size + nested size incomplete nested size | | v v HF duplicate-kwarg error HF incomplete-size error ``` ## Background #52834 reported that HF-style modality-scoped kwargs such as ```python { "videos_kwargs": { "size": { "longest_edge": ..., "shortest_edge": ..., } } } ``` were honored by the HF processor but ignored by vLLM's own sizing/profiling reads. Using a flat `size` instead made the override visible to vLLM, but also leaked it into the image budget. #53808 fixed that by adding a modality-specific overlay in `get_merged_mm_kwargs(..., modality=...)`. The intended contract is that this overlay is used for vLLM-side reads, while processor construction and the final HF `__call__` preserve the nested HF representation. The Qwen3-VL runtime path currently violates that separation in the video case. ## Reproduction The following reproductions use only synthetic media; no external image or video file is required. ### 1. Video: scoped `videos_kwargs.size` ```python import numpy as np from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY MODEL_ID = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct" model_config = ModelConfig(model=MODEL_ID) processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(model_config) num_frames = 8 fps = 30.0 video = np.zeros((num_frames, 128, 128, 3), dtype=np.uint8) metadata = { "fps": fps, "duration": num_frames / fps, "total_num_frames": num_frames, "frames_indices": list(range(num_frames)), "video_backend": "opencv", "do_sample_frames": True, } mm_items = processor.info.parse_mm_data( {"video": [(video, metadata)]} ) processor._apply_hf_processor_main( mm_items, { "videos_kwargs": { "size": { "longest_edge": 469_762_048, } } }, ) ``` On vLLM 0.29.0 with Transformers 5.17.0, this fails because Qwen3-VL keeps the nested `videos_kwargs["size"]` while also creating a flat `size` from the modality-resolved kwargs. Observed error: ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/danigarciaoca/anaconda3/envs/qwen3-vl-vllm-0-29-0/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py", line 343, in call_hf_processor output = hf_processor(**data, **allowed_kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/danigarciaoca/anaconda3/envs/qwen3-vl-vllm-0-29-0/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformers/processing_utils.py", line 670, in __call__ merged_kwargs = self._merge_kwargs( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/danigarciaoca/anaconda3/envs/qwen3-vl-vllm-0-29-0/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformers/processing_utils.py", line 1643, in _merge_kwargs raise ValueError( ValueError: Keyword argument size was passed two times: in a dictionary for videos_kwargs and as a **kwarg. ``` The relevant final exception is: ```text ValueError: Keyword argument size was passed two times: in a dictionary for videos_kwargs and as a **kwarg. ``` ### 2. Image: partial scoped `images_kwargs.size` ```python import numpy as np from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY MODEL_ID = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct" model_config = ModelConfig(model=MODEL_ID) processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(model_config) image = np.zeros((128, 128, 3), dtype=np.uint8) mm_items = processor.info.parse_mm_data({"image": [image]}) processor._apply_hf_processor_main( mm_items, { "images_kwargs": { "size": { "longest_edge": 16_777_216, } } }, ) ``` The equivalent partial size is handled by vLLM-side sizing as an override on top of the processor defaults, but in the runtime path the nested partial `size` reaches the HF image processor unresolved. Observed error: ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/danigarciaoca/anaconda3/envs/qwen3-vl-vllm-0-29-0/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py", line 343, in call_hf_processor output = hf_processor(**data, **allowed_kwargs) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/danigarciaoca/anaconda3/envs/qwen3-vl-vllm-0-29-0/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformers/processing_utils.py", line 679, in __call__ processed_images, images_replacements = self._process_images(images, **merged_kwargs["images_kwargs"]) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/danigarciaoca/anaconda3/envs/qwen3-vl-vllm-0-29-0/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformers/processing_utils.py", line 771, in _process_images processed_images = self.image_processor(images, ^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/danigarciaoca/anaconda3/envs/qwen3-vl-vllm-0-29-0/lib/python3.12/site-packages/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/image_processing_qwen2_vl.py", line 149, in resize raise ValueError(f"`size` dict must contain 'shortest_edge' and 'longest_edge' keys but got {size}.") ValueError: `size` dict must contain 'shortest_edge' and 'longest_edge' keys but got SizeDict(height=None, width=None, longest_edge=16777216, shortest_edge=None, max_height=None, max_width=None, min_pixels=None, max_pixels=None). ``` The relevant final exception is: ```text ValueError: `size` dict must contain 'shortest_edge' and 'longest_edge' keys but got SizeDict(height=None, width=None, longest_edge=16777216, shortest_edge=None, max_height=None, max_width=None, min_pixels=None, max_pixels=None). ``` ## Expected behavior Modality-scoped processor kwargs should remain scoped when crossing the vLLM -> HuggingFace processor boundary. In particular: - `videos_kwargs.size` should be usable by vLLM for its modality-specific runtime calculations without also forwarding a duplicate flat `size` to Transformers. - Partial image/video `size` overrides should be resolved consistently against the corresponding processor defaults before a complete `size` is forwarded where required. - Preparing modality-specific HF-bound kwargs should not allow a later merge of engine-level `mm_processor_kwargs` to reintroduce values that were intentionally removed from the final HF representation. ## Root cause ### Video In the Qwen3-VL video path, the original request kwargs are copied and kept in their HF-style nested representation: ```python video_mm_kwargs = dict(**hf_processor_mm_kwargs) ``` At the same time, vLLM obtains a modality-resolved view: ```python merged = self.info.ctx.get_merged_mm_kwargs( hf_processor_mm_kwargs, modality="video" ) ``` A scoped `videos_kwargs["size"]` is therefore visible as `merged["size"]`. Qwen3-VL resolves that value against the video processor defaults and writes the result back as a flat kwarg: ```python video_mm_kwargs["size"] = video_size ``` The original nested `videos_kwargs["size"]` is still present, so Transformers receives both forms and rejects `size` as a duplicate. ### Image In the image path, a scoped partial `images_kwargs["size"]` is kept in its nested HF representation and forwarded to the image processor without first being resolved against the image processor defaults. vLLM-side sizing treats `size` as an override on top of those defaults, but the runtime HF call receives the partial dictionary itself. For Qwen3-VL's image processor, that means a request containing only `longest_edge` reaches `resize()` with `shortest_edge=None`, which is rejected. There is also a second merge at the HF-call boundary: `InputProcessingContext.call_hf_processor()` currently merges `mm_processor_kwargs` again unconditionally. This makes it difficult for a caller that has already merged and prepared modality-specific HF-bound kwargs to guarantee that removed engine-level values are not reintroduced. ## Related issues / PRs - #52834 reported the original mismatch between HF modality-scoped kwargs and vLLM-side sizing/profiling. - #53808 fixed the sizing/profiling side by introducing modality-aware overlays. The video failure above is a runtime regression exposed by that change. - #54527 is a related follow-up extending modality-scoped vLLM-side reads to additional models, but it does not modify the affected Qwen3-VL runtime path or `InputProcessingContext.call_hf_processor()`. ## Possible fix A fix can keep the modality-resolved kwargs as the internal vLLM view, resolve the values Qwen3-VL needs against the corresponding processor defaults, and then normalize those values back into the HF modality-scoped representation before calling Transformers. The final HF call also needs a way to avoid re-merging engine-level `mm_processor_kwargs` once the caller has already merged and prepared the HF-bound kwargs. I have a working patch with regression tests for both the video and image cases and plan to submit a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Environment
vLLM      0.28.0

Python    3.14

torch     CUDA 13.2, driver 595.84

GPU       1 x RTX 5070 Ti, 16303 MiB (15.47 GiB visible to torch)

Model     Qwen/QwQ-32B-AWQ, 19.33 GB of weights

Entry     vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server (AsyncLLM path)
What happens
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager \

  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 44 --cpu-offload-gb 15.1

The server reports the flag back:

INFO [api_utils.py:273] non-default args: {..., 'cpu_offload_gb': 15.1, ...}

and then dies loading weights:

ERROR     + get_offloader().wrap_modules(

ERROR   File ".../vllm/model_executor/offloader/base.py", line 104, in wrap_modules

ERROR   File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 504, in __init__

ERROR     self.quant_method.create_weights(

ERROR   File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/auto_awq.py", line 479, in create_weights

ERROR     data=torch.empty(...)

ERROR torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 136.00 MiB.

      GPU 0 has a total capacity of 15.47 GiB of which 24.44 MiB is free.

      Of the allocated memory 15.06 GiB is allocated by PyTorch

base.py:104 is return list(modules_generator) inside NoopOffloader.wrap_modules. Nothing was offloaded, so the whole checkpoint was built onto the card.

NoopOffloader is announced at DEBUG (set_offloader), so on a default log there is no sign of any of this. The only place its name appears is a traceback.
Why it is not the obvious things
Each of these was checked separately, in this order.

The flag reaches the config.

from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs

c = EngineArgs(model=..., cpu_offload_gb=15.1).create_engine_config()

print(c.offload_config)

# OffloadConfig(offload_backend='auto',

#               uva=UVAOffloadConfig(cpu_offload_gb=15.1, cpu_offload_params=set()),

#               prefetch=PrefetchOffloadConfig(offload_group_size=0, ...))

The selector works.

from vllm.config.offload import OffloadConfig, UVAOffloadConfig

from vllm.model_executor.offloader.base import create_offloader

create_offloader(OffloadConfig(uva=UVAOffloadConfig(cpu_offload_gb=15.1)))

# -> UVAOffloader

create_offloader(OffloadConfig(uva=UVAOffloadConfig(cpu_offload_gb=0)))

# -> NoopOffloader

The global is one global.

import vllm.model_executor.offloader.base as b

from vllm.model_executor.offloader import get_offloader

b.set_offloader(b.create_offloader(OffloadConfig(uva=UVAOffloadConfig(cpu_offload_gb=15.1))))

get_offloader()      # -> UVAOffloader

b.get_offloader()    # -> UVAOffloader

The ordering is right. set_offloader(create_offloader(...)) is inside __init__ on both v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py and v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py, which runs before load_model.

It is not the backend selection. --offload-backend uva fails identically. So does the prefetch backend (--offload-group-size 8 --offload-num-in-group 7), which is a different code path and reaches create_offloader the same way.

It is not another process on the card. nvidia-smi shows 46 MiB in use, gnome-shell and snapd.

Five launches across those configurations produced OOM messages identical to the byte: 15.06 GiB allocated, 136.00 MiB requested, 24.44 MiB free. Identical output across different offload sizes and different max_num_seqs is the signature of a value that is not being read.
What that leaves
The config is correct in the API server process and create_offloader receives a zero budget in the worker. AsyncLLM spawns EngineCore unconditionally (VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING governs only the offline LLMEngine path), and vllm_config crosses that boundary as a pickled kwarg to context.Process in v1/engine/utils.py. That is the one link not directly instrumented above, and it is where we would look first.
Suggested fixes, independent of the cause
set_offloader should log at INFO when it selects NoopOffloader while cpu_offload_gb > 0 was requested. The silence is most of why this took a night to find.
create_offloader could warn when it is handed a zero budget by a config whose offload_backend is not auto, since that combination can only come from a value having been lost.
Reproducer
Any model larger than the card, with --cpu-offload-gb set to more than the difference. The failure is at weight loading, not at warm-up.

[vllm_offload_bug.md.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32062768/vllm_offload_bug.md.pdf)

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **How to reproduce**: ``` docker run ... vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0 ... --trust-remote-code --enable-auto-tool-choice --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops":["all"]}' ``` **Error**: ``` AssertionError: 4096 20 ``` at `vllm/forward_context.py:96`: ```python assert num_tokens_across_dp_cpu[dp_rank] == batchsize, ( f"{num_tokens_across_dp_cpu[dp_rank]} {batchsize}" ) ``` The `4096` is the target model's `max_num_tokens` (the profile-run batch size), and `20` is the speculator's `num_query_tokens` (`num_reqs * num_query_per_req`). ### Root Cause Analysis The crash occurs during `determine_available_memory` → `profile_run` → `_dummy_run` → `speculator.propose(dummy_run=True, skip_attn_for_dummy_run=True)`. The call chain is: 1. **`profile_run()`** (`model_runner.py:901`) calls `_dummy_run(max_num_tokens=4096, skip_attn=True, is_profile=True)`. 2. **`_dummy_run()`** (`model_runner.py:803`) calls `self.speculator.propose(..., dp_sync=dp_sync, dummy_run=True, skip_attn_for_dummy_run=True)`. The `dp_sync` comes from the main model's `execute_model` and has `dp_sync.num_tokens_across_dp[dp_rank] = 4096`. 3. **`DFlashSpeculator.propose()`** (`dflash/speculator.py:370-389`) takes the early-return dummy path: ```python if dummy_run and skip_attn_for_dummy_run: ... self._generate_draft( num_reqs, num_query_tokens, # = 20 attn_metadata=None, slot_mappings=None, num_tokens_across_dp=None, # <-- triggers the bug cudagraph_runtime_mode=CUDAGraphMode.NONE, ) ``` After PR #54856, this path passes `num_tokens_across_dp=None` instead of the previous `dp_sync.num_tokens_across_dp`. 4. **`DSparkSpeculator._generate_draft()`** (`dspark/speculator.py:258`) calls `self._run_model(num_tokens=20, ..., num_tokens_across_dp=None, ...)`. 5. **`DFlashSpeculator._run_model()`** (`dflash/speculator.py:246`) enters `set_forward_context(num_tokens=20, num_tokens_across_dp=None)` using `self.vllm_config` — which is the **target model's** config (a MoE model with `data_parallel_size > 1`). 6. **`set_forward_context()`** (`forward_context.py:282-310`): Since `data_parallel_size > 1`, `is_moe_model is not False`, and `num_tokens is not None`, the DP metadata path is entered. Because `num_tokens_across_dp is None`, it calls `coordinate_batch_across_dp(num_tokens=20)` — a **collective all_reduce** on the DP group. 7. **`DPMetadata.make()`** (`forward_context.py:96`): The all_reduce result at `dp_rank` is `4096` (contaminated by / inconsistent with the main model's earlier all_reduce with 4096 tokens), not `20`. The assertion `4096 == 20` fails. ### Why the normal (non-dummy) path works The normal path in `propose()` (lines 446-466) correctly computes `num_tokens_across_dp` via `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync(dp_sync, ...)` and passes it to `_generate_draft` → `_run_model` → `set_forward_context`. Since `num_tokens_across_dp` is not None, `set_forward_context` skips the `coordinate_batch_across_dp` call and goes directly to `DPMetadata.make()` with a consistent tensor. ### Relevant PRs since v0.28.0 | Commit | PR | Date | Description | |--------|-----|------|-------------| | `facd9a74a1` | [#54856](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54856) | Sept 3 | Changed the dummy-run path from `dp_sync.num_tokens_across_dp` to `None`. Added `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` for the normal path but left the dummy path without an alternative. | | `c268198715` | [#55472](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55472) | Sept 9 | Changed DSpark draft config to preserve target's `parallel_config` (including `data_parallel_size`). | ### Suggested Fix The dummy-run path in `DFlashSpeculator.propose()` (`dflash/speculator.py:381-388`) should not trigger a DP collective. Options: 1. **Pass `num_tokens=None` to `set_forward_context`** in the dummy path (the condition `attn_metadata is not None or num_tokens is not None` would be False when `attn_metadata=None` and `num_tokens=None`, skipping DP metadata entirely). This requires `_run_model` to accept `num_tokens=None` or have a separate dummy path. 2. **Compute `num_tokens_across_dp` for the dummy path** similarly to the normal path, e.g.: ```python num_tokens_across_dp = ( dp_sync.num_tokens_across_dp if dp_sync is not None else None ) ``` ...but this would also fail the assertion since `dp_sync.num_tokens_across_dp[dp_rank] = 4096 != 20`. Instead, build a correct tensor: ```python if dp_sync is not None: num_tokens_across_dp = torch.full_like( dp_sync.num_tokens_across_dp, num_query_tokens ) else: num_tokens_across_dp = None ``` 3. **Skip `set_forward_context` entirely for the dummy/profile run** since no DP coordination is needed during memory profiling. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Requests with Nemotron Image Embeddings Fail With `int(None)`
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `0.29.0` (docker image `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` when tested)
- Model: `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-NVFP4`
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- Server option: `--enable-mm-embeds`
- Embedding shape: `(384, 2688)`
- Embedding dtype: `torch.bfloat16`

The same code path is also present in the current vLLM `main` branch as of
September 10, 2026.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Start the server with multimodal embedding input enabled:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-NVFP4 \
  --enable-mm-embeds \
  --trust-remote-code
```

Serialize a post-projection image embedding with vLLM's utility and submit it
as an `image_embeds` content part:

```python
import torch
from openai import OpenAI
from vllm.utils.serial_utils import tensor2base64

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
image_embeddings = torch.randn(384, 2688, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

client.chat.completions.create(
    model="nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-NVFP4",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image concisely."},
                {
                    "type": "image_embeds",
                    "image_embeds": tensor2base64(image_embeddings),
                },
            ],
        }
    ],
    max_completion_tokens=128,
    temperature=0.0,
)
```


#### Observed Behavior
The server returns HTTP 400:

```text
int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'NoneType'
```

The equivalent request using an `image_url` content part succeeds.

#### Expected Behavior

The server should accept the precomputed embedding and generate a completion.
The embedding feature count should determine the number of image placeholder
tokens when patch-count metadata is unavailable.


#### Root Cause

In `vllm/model_executor/models/nano_nemotron_vl.py`,
`NanoNemotronVLMultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_repl_image()` deliberately uses
`None` because precomputed image embeddings do not include patch-count
metadata:

```python
elif "image_embeds" in out_mm_data:
    image_num_patches = [None] * len(out_mm_data["image_embeds"])
```

The nested replacement callback later converts the value without checking for
`None`:

```python
num_patches = int(local_image_num_patches[item_idx])
```

This raises `TypeError` before inference begins. The processor has already
obtained the required placeholder count from
`ImageEmbeddingItems.get_feature_size(item_idx)`. In addition,
`NanoNemotronVLProcessor.get_image_repl()` constructs the replacement from
`feature_size` and does not use `num_patches`.

The neighboring InternVL and H2OVL processors preserve `None` for embedding
inputs, which appears to be the intended behavior.

#### Proposed Fix

Only convert the patch count when it is present:

```diff
 if isinstance(local_image_num_patches, (list, tuple)) and item_idx < len(
     local_image_num_patches
 ):
-    num_patches = int(local_image_num_patches[item_idx])
+    local_num_patches = local_image_num_patches[item_idx]
+    if local_num_patches is not None:
+        num_patches = int(local_num_patches)
```

Alternatively, this block could follow the simpler pattern used by the
neighboring InternVL implementation.

#### Suggested Regression Test

Add a Nemotron multimodal processor test that:

1. Supplies one precomputed image embedding through `image_embeds`.
2. Exercises `_get_prompt_repl_image()` through the normal processor entry
   point.
3. Verifies that no exception is raised when patch-count metadata is absent.
4. Verifies that the generated image placeholder contains one image context
   token per embedding feature.

Typing `image_num_patches` as `list[int | None]` would also prevent the
nullable value from being hidden by `Tensor.tolist()` returning a broadly
typed value.


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug For a model output that contains text before AND after a tool call, the two delivery modes disagree: streaming returns the post-tool text, non-streaming drops it. The tool parser is inconsistent with its own streaming mode. Reproduction (CPU only, no GPU or model weights; tokenizer download only): ```python from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv3_tool_parser import DeepSeekV3ToolParser from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer MODEL_OUTPUT = ("let me check the weather.<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>" "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n```json\n" '{"city": "Paris"}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁calls▁end｜>It is 30 degrees.') tok = get_tokenizer("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1") p = DeepSeekV3ToolParser(tok) req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[]) # non-streaming parse print("full :", repr(p.extract_tool_calls(MODEL_OUTPUT, req).content)) # streaming parse, token by token ids = tok.encode(MODEL_OUTPUT, add_special_tokens=False) out, prev_text, prev_ids = [], "", [] for i, tid in enumerate(ids): text = prev_text + tok.decode([tid]) d = p.extract_tool_calls_streaming( prev_text, text, tok.decode([tid]), prev_ids, ids[:i + 1], [tid], req) if d and d.content: out.append(d.content) prev_text, prev_ids = text, ids[:i + 1] print("stream:", repr("".join(out))) ``` Observed: ``` full : 'let me check the weather.' stream: 'let me check the weather.It is 30 degrees.' ``` The trailing "It is 30 degrees." is dropped by the non-streaming parse and kept by the streaming parse. Downstream, `messages_full_converter` (`/v1/messages` non-streaming) then never sees that text, while `message_stream_converter` emits it as a text block after the tool_use block - for the same generation, /v1/messages streaming shows the trailing text and non-streaming loses it. ### Root cause Non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` implementations truncate content at the tool-call start token and never resume afterwards: - deepseekv3_tool_parser.py: content = text before `<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>` - hermes_tool_parser.py:109: `content = model_output[: model_output.find(self.tool_call_start_token)]` Streaming implementations emit post-tool text as content deltas (deepseekv3_tool_parser.py:248, `DeltaMessage(tool_calls=[], content=text)`). ### Expected behavior Both delivery modes return the same content for the same generation. ### Proposed fix Make the DeepSeek-V3 parser's non-streaming parse include the post-tool text, matching its own streaming mode. The same truncation exists in hermes_tool_parser.py and can follow separately if maintainers agree it is also unintended. OpenAI clients currently lose this text in non-streaming mode, so returning it is a correction, not a new feature. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: Beam Search ignores skip_special_tokens and exposes special tokens in decoded output
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug


Online and offline Beam Search do not honor `skip_special_tokens` when constructing the final decoded text.

This is especially visible with Voxtral Realtime transcription because the model intentionally generates control tokens such as `[STREAMING_PAD]` and `[STREAMING_WORD]` as part of its time-aligned decoding process.

With regular sampling, these special tokens are filtered from the returned text. With Beam Search, they are exposed to the user, producing a response containing hundreds of internal control tokens.

The generated token IDs are valid. The problem is limited to the final detokenization step.

### Steps to reproduce

#### Start the server:

```bash
vllm serve mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}' \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --port 8002
```

#### Use the vLLM public audio asset:

```bash
AUDIO_FILE="$HOME/.cache/vllm/assets/vllm_public_assets/mary_had_lamb.ogg"

```

#### Regular sampling:
```bash
curl \
  http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F "file=@$AUDIO_FILE;type=audio/ogg" \
  -F "model=mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602" \
  -F "language=en" \
  -F "temperature=0" \
  -F "max_completion_tokens=256"
```

```bash
{"text":" First words I spoke in the original phonograph. A little piece of practical poetry. Mary had a little lamb, it sleeps with quite a flow, and everywhere that Mary went, the lamb was sure to go.","usage":{"type":"duration","seconds":16}}
```

#### Beam Search:
```bash
curl \
  http://127.0.0.1:8002/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F "file=@$AUDIO_FILE;type=audio/ogg" \
  -F "model=mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602" \
  -F "language=en" \
  -F "temperature=0" \
  -F "use_beam_search=true" \
  -F "n=2" \
  -F "max_completion_tokens=256"
```

Beam Search, n=2 | 185 | 27

### Actual behavior

The exact counts can vary, but Beam Search consistently exposes control tokens in the returned text.

### Expected behavior

Beam Search should honor `skip_special_tokens`, consistently with regular sampling:

- When `skip_special_tokens=True`, tokenizer-defined special tokens should be omitted from the returned text.
- When `skip_special_tokens=False`, tokenizer-defined special tokens should be preserved.

### Cause
The final decoding performed by the online and offline Beam Search implementations calls tokenizer.decode(...) without forwarding skip_special_tokens. Additionally, the request's skip_special_tokens setting is not represented and propagated consistently through BeamSearchParams.

title: [Bug]: [Spec Decode Metrics] mean_acceptance_length overcounts tokens when EOS occurs inside the accepted draft prefix
body:
### Your current environment
vLLM version ```text 0.29.0 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Describe the bug In vLLM v0.29.0, speculative decoding reports ```text mean_acceptance_length = 1 + num_accepted_draft_tokens / num_spec_steps ``` The documentation describes this quantity as: > Mean tokens emitted per verification step, including the bonus token. However, `accepted_draft_tokens + 1` is not always equal to the number of tokens actually emitted/committed by a verification step. In particular, this identity fails for the terminal verification step when an EOS token occurs inside the accepted draft prefix. For example, suppose a speculative verification step produces the following verified sequence: ```text [draft_1, draft_2, EOS, draft_4, draft_5, bonus] ``` and all five draft tokens match the target model before stop handling. The current acceptance accounting records: ```text num_accepted_draft_tokens = 5 ``` and therefore this step contributes ```text 5 + 1 = 6 ``` tokens to `mean_acceptance_length`. However, generation terminates at EOS, so the request actually commits only ```text [draft_1, draft_2, EOS] ``` i.e. 3 tokens. The tokens after EOS are not emitted, and there is no emitted bonus token after EOS. More generally, if EOS is the `j`-th accepted draft token and the verifier reports `a >= j` accepted draft tokens, the current metric counts ```text a + 1 ``` while the number of actually emitted tokens in that verification step is ```text j ``` so the MAL numerator is overestimated by ```text a - j + 1. ``` Even when EOS is the last accepted draft token (`a == j`), the metric is still overestimated by one because the bonus token is not actually emitted. ### Why this matters This is not only a naming issue because `mean_acceptance_length` is commonly used to evaluate and compare speculative decoding methods. The current documentation defines it in terms of **emitted tokens per verification step**, but the implementation derives it from the number of accepted draft tokens plus an unconditional bonus token. Those quantities are equal for ordinary verification steps, but not for a terminal step that stops inside the accepted draft block. The same issue also affects the newly introduced per-request `mean_acceptance_length`, since `RequestSpecDecodeMetrics.to_dict()` computes ```python mean_al = 1.0 + num_accepted / num_spec_steps ``` from the acceptance histogram. ### Expected behavior I think the raw acceptance statistics can remain unchanged if `num_accepted_draft_tokens` is intentionally defined as the number of draft positions accepted by the verifier. However, `mean_acceptance_length`, when defined as mean **emitted/committed tokens per verification step**, should use the number of tokens actually committed after EOS/stop truncation: ```text mean_acceptance_length = num_committed_spec_decode_tokens / num_spec_steps ``` where: * EOS itself is counted; * tokens after EOS are not counted; * if EOS is an accepted draft token, no nonexistent bonus token is counted; * if the target residual/bonus token is EOS, that token is counted normally. An alternative would be to expose a separate `num_emitted_tokens` / `num_committed_tokens` counter and keep the existing raw acceptance metrics unchanged. ### Missing test case The current per-request speculative-decoding metric tests cover the histogram arithmetic but do not appear to include an EOS/stop-token terminal verification case. A regression test where EOS occurs inside an otherwise accepted draft block should expose the discrepancy between ```text 1 + accepted_draft_tokens ``` and the actual number of committed output tokens. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
label: bug

title: [Bug]: FixFunctionalizationPass crashes with "Tried to erase Node auto_functionalized but it still had N users" when the graph contains control_deps nodes
body:
### Your current environment



# Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| vLLM | 0.28.0 |
| PyTorch | 2.12.0 |
| Python | 3.13.13 |
| Platform | out-of-tree platform plugin (registered via the `vllm.platforms` plugin interface) |

Compilation config in use when the crash occurs:

```python
CompilationConfig(
    mode=CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE,
    backend="inductor",
    custom_ops=["all"],
    cudagraph_mode=CUDAGraphMode.NONE,
    splitting_ops=list(CompilationConfig._attention_ops),
    pass_config={                      # every fusion pass disabled
        "fuse_norm_quant": False,
        "fuse_act_quant": False,
        "fuse_attn_quant": False,
        "enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion": False,
        "enable_sp": False,
        "fuse_gemm_comms": False,
        "fuse_allreduce_rms": False,
    },
    inductor_compile_config={},        # -> vLLM injects enable_auto_functionalized_v2=False
    use_inductor_graph_partition=False,
)
```
### Observed failure conditions

In the failing graph, an `auto_functionalized` node handled by
`FixFunctionalizationPass` still had a `control_deps` user when the pass attempted
to erase it. Based on the code analysis above, a single such node appears sufficient
to trigger the failure; multiple supported ops are not required.

In our out-of-tree platform environment, this happened with a small **MoE** model.
Three smaller / simpler models compiled successfully under the same configuration.
We have not confirmed which graph-construction or scheduling step accounts for
that difference, so this observation does not establish that the issue is specific
to MoE models.

### Caveat on reproduction

The failure was observed on an out-of-tree platform backend. We have not verified
the end-to-end MoE path on CUDA, and we have not obtained a working standalone
reproducer in an upstream-only environment.

The proposed reproducer above illustrates the suspected graph pattern, but it
should not be treated as a verified upstream-only reproduction. The root-cause
analysis is based on the observed traceback and inspection of the graph-rewrite
code; it does not establish which upstream workloads naturally produce this
pattern.

Confirmation of the failure in an upstream-only environment, ideally with a
workload whose graph naturally acquires a `control_deps` edge referencing an
`auto_functionalized` node, would help establish the scope of the issue.

### Single-variable evidence

The following comparison was performed in the out-of-tree platform environment
described above, using the same model and configuration and changing only
`enable_auto_functionalized_v2`:

| `enable_auto_functionalized_v2` | Observed result |
|---|---|
| `False` (vLLM default) | Compile-time crash, as above |
| `True` | Compiles and runs successfully |

This comparison supports investigating the V1 functionalization path in that
environment. It does not demonstrate reproduction on CUDA or establish that V2
is a generally compatible workaround for other configurations.



### 🐛 Describe the bug

# Description

`FixFunctionalizationPass` de-functionalizes `auto_functionalized` HOP nodes and then
erases them from the FX graph. Before erasing, it re-points the node's users via
`replace_users_with_mutated_args()`, but that helper **only considers users that are
`operator.getitem` nodes**. Any other kind of user is silently left pointing at the node
that is about to be erased, and `torch.fx.Graph.erase_node()` then refuses to delete it.

PyTorch's `control_deps` HOP (`torch/_inductor/fx_passes/control_dependencies.py`) is
exactly such a user: it encodes an ordering constraint and therefore references the node
itself rather than its tuple output, so it never appears as a `getitem` user.

When both are present in the same graph, compilation fails with:

```
torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: RuntimeError: Tried to erase Node auto_functionalized
but it still had 1 users in the graph: {control_deps_3: None}!
```

This is a hard compile-time failure — the engine never starts.

# Minimal reproducer

Self-contained: no GPU, no model, no engine, no compiled kernels. It builds the FX
graph by hand, adds **one** ordering edge with PyTorch's own
`preserve_node_ordering()` helper, and runs the pass directly. The same script runs
the graph twice — once without the `control_deps` edge and once with it — so the
trigger is isolated to that single edge.

```python
"""Minimal repro for: FixFunctionalizationPass crashes when an
`auto_functionalized` node has a `control_deps` user.

Self-contained: no GPU, no model, no engine. It builds the FX graph by hand,
adds one ordering edge with PyTorch's own `preserve_node_ordering()` helper,
and runs the pass directly.

    python repro_fix_functionalization.py

Expected output: case [1] (no control_deps) completes, case [2] crashes.
"""

import operator

import torch
from torch._higher_order_ops.auto_functionalize import auto_functionalized
from torch._inductor.fx_passes.control_dependencies import preserve_node_ordering
from torch.utils._ordered_set import OrderedSet

from vllm.compilation.passes.utility.fix_functionalization import (
    FixFunctionalizationPass,
)
from vllm.config import CompilationConfig, VllmConfig
from vllm.utils.torch_utils import direct_register_custom_op

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The op under test: the one upstream's own
# tests/compile/passes/test_functionalization.py registers, which
# FixFunctionalizationPass already handles (fix_functionalization.py:224-231).
# Using it means the repro needs no compiled kernels.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _impl(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    ret = x + 1
    x.add_(2)
    return ret


def _fake(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    return torch.empty_like(x)


direct_register_custom_op(
    op_name="function_with_mutated_args_and_return",
    op_func=_impl,
    mutates_args=["x"],
    fake_impl=_fake,
)

TARGET = torch.ops.vllm.function_with_mutated_args_and_return.default

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compatibility shim -- ONLY needed on a source build without the compiled C
# extension (e.g. VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty). The pass walks an if/elif chain
# comparing `at_target` against these ops purely for identity; it never calls
# them, so schema-only declarations suffice. On a normal wheel this is a no-op.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
_C_OPS_TOUCHED_BY_THE_PASS = (
    "fused_add_rms_norm",
    "fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant",
    "fused_qk_norm_rope",
    "rms_norm",
    "rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant",
    "rms_norm_static_fp8_quant",
    "rotary_embedding",
    "silu_and_mul",
    "silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant",
    "silu_and_mul_quant",
)
_C_LIB = torch.library.Library("_C", "FRAGMENT")
for _name in _C_OPS_TOUCHED_BY_THE_PASS:
    if not hasattr(torch.ops._C, _name):
        _C_LIB.define(f"{_name}(Tensor! out) -> ()")


def build_graph_module() -> torch.fx.GraphModule:
    """The shape AOTAutograd produces for one mutating custom op:

        af  = auto_functionalized(TARGET, x=arg)
        out = af[0]     # return value
        mut = af[1]     # mutated arg
        add = out + mut
    """
    graph = torch.fx.Graph()
    arg = graph.placeholder("arg")
    af = graph.call_function(auto_functionalized, args=(TARGET,), kwargs={"x": arg})
    out = graph.call_function(operator.getitem, args=(af, 0))
    mut = graph.call_function(operator.getitem, args=(af, 1))
    add = graph.call_function(torch.ops.aten.add.Tensor, args=(out, mut))
    graph.output(add)
    return torch.fx.GraphModule(torch.nn.Module(), graph)


def run_case(with_control_deps: bool) -> bool:
    """Returns True if the pass completed, False if it crashed."""
    label = "[2] WITH control_deps" if with_control_deps else "[1] no control_deps"
    print(f"\n===== {label} =====")

    gm = build_graph_module()
    af = next(n for n in gm.graph.nodes if n.target is auto_functionalized)

    if with_control_deps:
        add = next(n for n in gm.graph.nodes if n.target is torch.ops.aten.add.Tensor)
        # One ordering edge: `add` must run after `af`. This is PyTorch's own
        # helper (Inductor calls it from e.g. overlap_preserving_bucketer.py).
        # It rewrites `add` into control_deps(deps=(af,), subgraph, ...) --
        # `af` is referenced DIRECTLY, not through a getitem.
        preserve_node_ordering(gm.graph, {add: OrderedSet([af])})
        gm.recompile()

    for user in af.users:
        kind = "getitem" if user.target is operator.getitem else str(user.target)
        print(f"  auto_functionalized user: {user.name:<14} target={kind}")

    vllm_config = VllmConfig(compilation_config=CompilationConfig())
    try:
        FixFunctionalizationPass(vllm_config)(gm.graph)
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        print(f"  -> CRASH: RuntimeError: {exc}")
        return False
    print("  -> pass completed")
    return True


def main() -> int:
    ok_without = run_case(with_control_deps=False)
    ok_with = run_case(with_control_deps=True)

    print("\n===== RESULT =====")
    print(f"  no control_deps   : {'PASS' if ok_without else 'CRASH'}")
    print(f"  with control_deps : {'PASS' if ok_with else 'CRASH'}")
    if ok_without and not ok_with:
        print("  => reproduced: the single control_deps user is what breaks the pass")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

### Observed output

```
===== [1] no control_deps =====
  auto_functionalized user: getitem        target=getitem
  auto_functionalized user: getitem_1      target=getitem
  -> pass completed

===== [2] WITH control_deps =====
  auto_functionalized user: getitem        target=getitem
  auto_functionalized user: getitem_1      target=getitem
  auto_functionalized user: add_tensor     target=control_deps
  -> CRASH: RuntimeError: Tried to erase Node auto_functionalized but it still had 1 users in the graph: {add_tensor: None}!

===== RESULT =====
  no control_deps   : PASS
  with control_deps : CRASH
  => reproduced: the single control_deps user is what breaks the pass
```

Two notes on the output:

* The offending user is reported by **name**, and the name comes from
  `preserve_node_ordering()`, which renames the wrapped node back to its original
  name (`control_dependencies.py:200` — `ordered_node.name = original_name`). That is
  why it prints as `add_tensor` here and as `control_deps_3` in the engine crash; in
  both cases the node's *target* is the `control_deps` HOP, as the `target=` column
  shows.
* The op used is `torch.ops.vllm.function_with_mutated_args_and_return`, the one
  vLLM's own `tests/compile/passes/test_functionalization.py` registers and which the
  pass already handles (`fix_functionalization.py:224-231`). Nothing device-specific
  is involved.

### Verified with no out-of-tree component in the process

To rule out our platform plugin as a factor, the same script was run with every
platform plugin disabled and PyTorch's out-of-tree backend autoload turned off, so
that vLLM falls back to the upstream CPU platform:

```bash
VLLM_PLUGINS= VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 \
    python repro_fix_functionalization.py
```

The output is identical (case [1] passes, case [2] crashes), with:

```
platform: CpuPlatform
```

and neither our platform package nor its PyTorch backend present in `sys.modules`.
The reproducer builds no tensors, runs no kernels and invokes no code generation —
it is a pure FX graph transformation — so the crash is not tied to any particular
backend.

### Requirements

* `torch._inductor.fx_passes.control_dependencies` must exist — that is the module
  providing the `control_deps` HOP. Verified on **torch 2.12**. On a PyTorch old
  enough not to have it, the import fails, but that build cannot hit the bug either.
* No GPU and no compiled vLLM C extension are required (see the shim in the script).

---

# Root cause

All line numbers are from vLLM 0.28.0.

**1. `defunctionalize()` re-points users, then queues the node for removal**
`vllm/compilation/passes/utility/fix_functionalization.py:257-271`

```python
def defunctionalize(self, graph, node, mutated_args, args=None):
    self.replace_users_with_mutated_args(node, mutated_args)   # :269
    self.insert_defunctionalized(graph, node, args=args)       # :270
    self._remove(node)                                         # :271
```

**2. `replace_users_with_mutated_args()` iterates only over `getitem` users**
`fix_functionalization.py:273` → `getitem_users()` at `:298-308`

```python
def getitem_users(self, node):
    users = {}
    for user in node.users:
        if is_func(user, operator.getitem):    # :305  <-- non-getitem users are dropped
            idx = user.args[1]
            users[idx] = user
    return users
```

A `control_deps` user is not a `getitem`, so it is never re-pointed.

**3. The erase then fails**
`fix_functionalization.py:240-241`

```python
for node in self.nodes_to_remove:
    graph.erase_node(node)          # :241
```

raising at `torch/fx/graph.py:1530`, which refuses to erase a node with live users.

### Why `control_deps` is in the graph

`control_deps` is a PyTorch Inductor HOP used to enforce explicit scheduling order
(`torch/_inductor/fx_passes/control_dependencies.py`; inserted through
`preserve_node_ordering()`, e.g. from `overlap_preserving_bucketer.py:371-374`).
vLLM itself never references `control_deps` — grepping the vLLM package returns zero
hits — so this looks like a vLLM pass that predates the HOP and was never updated for it.

---

The failure was observed with an out-of-tree platform backend. A standalone reproducer in an upstream-only environment is not yet available, and the end-to-end CUDA path has not been verified. The traceback points to FixFunctionalizationPass attempting to erase an auto_functionalized node that still has a control_deps user.

title: [Bug]: [ROCm] Whisper W8A8 fails because Triton scaled_mm receives a rank-3 activation
body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) Kernel : Linux 6.8.0-138-generic Python : 3.12.13 GPU : AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) vLLM : 0.28.0 PyTorch : 2.12.0+git6bbd260 ROCm/HIP : 7.2.53211 Triton : 3.7.1+gitf0b55c07 Transformers : 5.15.1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Bug `RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-quantized.w8a8` fails during engine initialization when vLLM selects `TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel`. The Whisper encoder produces a normal `[batch, sequence, hidden]` activation. `TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` passes the resulting rank-3 INT8 tensor directly to the 2D `triton_scaled_mm` function, which fails at: ```python M, K = input.shape ``` with: ```text ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2) ``` ### Reproduction ```bash export VLLM_PLUGINS= python repro.py ``` ```python from vllm import LLM LLM( model="RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-quantized.w8a8", revision="11d614fb6fc82faeaa7414b0e5613e2fc37768a5", dtype="float16", max_model_len=448, max_num_batched_tokens=1500, max_num_seqs=4, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1}, gpu_memory_utilization=0.8, enforce_eager=True, disable_log_stats=True, ) ``` No user audio is needed to reproduce it. vLLM triggers the failure while profiling the multimodal encoder during initialization. ### Observed result The checkpoint loads successfully: ```text Selected TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel for CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8 Model loading took 1.51 GiB memory and 2.89 seconds ``` Initialization then fails: ```text File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/triton.py", line 134, in apply_weights out = triton_scaled_mm( File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/ triton_scaled_mm.py", line 190, in triton_scaled_mm M, K = input.shape ^^^^ ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2) ``` The actual tensors at the failing call are: ```text input: (1, 1500, 1280), torch.int8 weight: (1280, 3840), torch.int8 scale_a: (1500, 1) scale_b: (3840, 1) ``` The rank-3 input is generated internally by the Whisper encoder. The checkpoint weights and scales load successfully. ### Expected result The quantized Linear implementation should support normal Linear input semantics for `[..., K]`: flatten the leading dimensions before the 2D matrix multiplication and restore them afterward. ### Diagnostic confirmation I temporarily wrapped `triton_scaled_mm` in the same Python process: ```python target_shape = (*input.shape[:-1], weight.shape[1]) input_2d = input.reshape(-1, input.shape[-1]) output = original_triton_scaled_mm( input_2d, weight, scale_a, scale_b, out_dtype, bias, ) return output.reshape(target_shape) ``` No installed vLLM files were modified. With this change: - Engine initialization completed. - Encoder profiling completed. - A request with valid 16 kHz `float32` PCM audio completed. - The process exited with code 0. This confirms that the failure is caused by the rank mismatch. ### Related changes PR #22278 added rank-3 flatten/restore handling to `_custom_ops.cutlass_scaled_mm`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/22278 PR #26668 changed the ROCm Triton fallback to invoke `triton_scaled_mm` directly: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/26668 The direct call does not pass through the wrapper fixed by #22278. The same Whisper W8A8 model previously exposed an analogous rank-3 issue in the CPU oneDNN backend: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33696 The CPU path was fixed by flattening the input and restoring the output: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33727 ### Current main The runtime reproduction was performed on vLLM 0.28.0. I have not run a build from `main`. However, main commit `95cf420ac171089d72d111b6cfbd0292cdc1d822` still contains the same direct call and rank-2 unpack: - Caller: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/95cf420ac171089d72d111b6cfbd0292cdc1d822/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/triton.py#L121-L136 - Callee: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/95cf420ac171089d72d111b6cfbd0292cdc1d822/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/triton_scaled_mm.py#L175-L190 I searched existing issues and pull requests but did not find one covering this exact ROCm Triton path. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Feature]: [Spec Decode] Support model-based drafters (target hidden states) via custom_class
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### Motivation
#39487 added `custom_class` for model-free drafters. Drafters that need the target's hidden states or KV cache can't use it. That covers DFlash-style drafters, self-speculative heads like Orthrus, and MTP variants. Here's why:

- The proposer is constructed with only `VllmConfig`, and `propose()` only gets token IDs ([[call site](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b8e9001bf9568c801985889deff34d3b9fe6d0b0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L4773-L4780)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b8e9001bf9568c801985889deff34d3b9fe6d0b0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py#L4773-L4780)).
- The runner never calls `dummy_run`, `initialize_attn_backend` or `initialize_cudagraph_keys` on it, and never enables aux hidden states for it.
- MRv2 rejects `custom_class` outright ([[here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b8e9001bf9568c801985889deff34d3b9fe6d0b0/vllm/config/vllm.py#L3030-L3031)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b8e9001bf9568c801985889deff34d3b9fe6d0b0/vllm/config/vllm.py#L3030-L3031)).

So these drafters either go in-tree or borrow another method's slot. MRv2 already does the second: `LiLiCorrSpeculator` and `DFlash2Speculator` are selected under `method == "dflash"`. 

### Proposal
If `custom_class` subclasses `SpecDecodeBaseProposer` (V1) or `BaseSpeculator` (MRv2), route it through the model-based path:

- Construct it like the built-in drafters: `(vllm_config, device, runner)` in V1, `(vllm_config, device)` in MRv2.
- Add `SpeculativeConfig.uses_target_hidden_states()`. Use it at the call sites where `use_eagle()` currently means "uses target hidden states" (this resolves the [`[TODO(ben)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b8e9001bf9568c801985889deff34d3b9fe6d0b0/vllm/config/speculative.py#L1991-L1995)`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b8e9001bf9568c801985889deff34d3b9fe6d0b0/vllm/config/speculative.py#L1991-L1995)). Include the custom class in `uses_draft_kv_cache()`.
- Keep the experimental warning. Built-in proposers and token-only custom proposers don't change.

**Non-goals:** no registry, no new abstract class, no new CLI flags.

### Open questions
(a) V1, MRv2, or MRv2 only?
(b) Resolve the class in `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__`? That runs in the engine process while the drafter runs in the worker, but it makes a bad class path fail early.
(c) Where should a separate draft checkpoint path go? A first version could support only self-speculative drafters.

### Test plan
Load an `EagleProposer` subclass via `custom_class` with an existing EAGLE test checkpoint. Assert the output is token-identical to `method="eagle"`, with CUDA graphs on and off. Add unit tests for the config predicate.

I can open the PR once we agree on direction, especially (a).

_No response_
