title: [Feature]: Harden logit_bias against absolute-logit leakage
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Following private triage with the vLLM security team, I am opening this as a hardening request, as they suggested.

Adding a user-provided bias directly to FP32 logits can make the greedy winner depend on a common offset of the input scores. This can happen even when all relative logits remain unchanged. Under the tested conditions, repeated bias queries can recover absolute pre-bias logits from token IDs alone. The practical impact demonstrated so far is limited.

I would like to discuss centering the FP32 logits before finite, nonzero bias addition, by subtracting the maximum score. Centering after the addition is too late to remove the rounding difference.

The main points to decide are where to apply this in the sampling pipeline and whether it should be enabled by default. Centering preserves softmax probabilities in exact arithmetic, but it can change near-tie decisions and later repetition penalties. It also adds a reduction over the vocabulary, so serving overhead needs measurement.


### Alternatives

- An operator-controlled option could preserve the existing default behavior.
- Operators could reject `logit_bias` requests, but this also removes useful token steering.
- Centering only after bias addition does not fix the example below.

### Additional context

**Small numerical example.** This uses only Python's standard library to show the FP32 rounding effect; it is not an end-to-end vLLM recovery script. Token IDs are 0 and 1, with the first index winning ties.

<details>
<summary>Reproducer and output</summary>

```python
import struct


def f32(x):
    return struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<f", x))[0]


def center(values):
    m = max(values)
    return [f32(x - m) for x in values]


def winner(values):
    return max(range(len(values)), key=values.__getitem__)


d = 2.0 ** -19
q = [17.0, 17.0 - 2 * d]
bias = [15.0 - d, 15.0 + 2 * d]

print("shift raw pre_center post_center")
for shift in (0.0, 1.0):
    shifted = [f32(x + shift) for x in q]
    raw = [f32(x + b) for x, b in zip(shifted, bias)]
    pre = [f32(x + b) for x, b in zip(center(shifted), bias)]
    post = center(raw)
    print(int(shift), winner(raw), winner(pre), winner(post))
```

Output:

```text
shift raw pre_center post_center
0 1 1 1
1 0 1 0
```

Adding exactly 1 to both input scores changes the raw winner. Centering before bias addition removes this difference; centering afterward does not.

</details>

**Relevant vLLM 0.31.0 code:** [FP32 conversion and processor order](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py) and [the bias addition kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logit_bias.py). The tested V2 runner applies bias after copying logits to FP32.

<details>
<summary>Serving experiment results and scope</summary>

Environment: vLLM 0.31.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, CUDA 13.0, RTX 4090 48 GB, BF16 models. Compilation, CUDA graphs, and prefix caching remained enabled.

Server options:

```text
--dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 512 --generation-config vllm --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --no-enable-log-requests
```

Requests used `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1`, token IDs only, no logprobs, and one warmup per prompt. Recovery queries were sequential; the load experiment added 16 background clients.

Exact recovery of two pre-bias logits and their tie priority, across 64 prompts per model:

| Model | Serial | 16 background clients, batch invariance OFF | 16 background clients, batch invariance ON |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 36/64 | 8/64 | 36/64 |
| SmolLM2-360M | 64/64 | 6/64 | 64/64 |

The OFF/ON columns are a paired experiment; the serial column is from an earlier run. These experiments used fixed windows selected using separate calibration logits. The windows covered 36 Qwen3 prompts and all 64 SmolLM2 prompts. Batch invariance is a server setting, not something the API client can force.

Predictions were frozen before evaluation against captured scores. After removing the evaluator hook, replaying the ON transcripts for eight prompts per model under load gave 0/416 and 0/424 token mismatches.

All models were public checkpoints on infrastructure we controlled. We have not demonstrated a private deployment's access-control bypass or a downstream exploit that depends on the recovered common component.

</details>

A regression should compare bias-query outputs across stored FP32 vectors related by an exact common shift. An implementation should also cover empty/zero biases, token masks and all-masked rows, and evaluate repetition penalties, logprob modes, generation quality, and serving overhead.

AI assistance was used to prepare this issue and the numerical example.

title: [Feature]: Support logprobs / top_logprobs for gpt-oss (Harmony) models in /v1/responses
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Follow-up to #23225 / #23319. In #23319, "logprobs + harmony" was listed as a remaining TODO, and it was never picked up after #23225 was closed.

Requesting output logprobs from `/v1/responses` with a gpt-oss model is currently rejected:

- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py` returns `400: logprobs are not supported with gpt-oss models` when `include=["message.output_text.logprobs"]` / `top_logprobs` is set.
- `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/harmony.py` (`_parse_final_message`) hardcodes `logprobs=None  # TODO`.

Non-Harmony models already return logprobs on this endpoint via `_create_response_logprobs`, so gpt-oss users can't get token confidence scores for evals, scoring, or RL workflows through the Responses API.

**Proposed approach**
1. Track token ids + sampled logprobs per Harmony message/channel in `HarmonyContext`.
2. Attach logprobs only to `final`-channel content tokens (excluding Harmony control tokens such as `<|channel|>`, `<|message|>`, `<|end|>`), reusing `_create_response_logprobs`.
3. Non-streaming first; streaming (`response.output_text.delta` logprobs) as a follow-up.
4. Remove the validation error and add tests under `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses`.

### Alternatives

Use `/v1/chat/completions` instead, but that loses Responses API features (built-in tools, stored responses).

title: [Feature]: TTL-based Eviction for KV Cache Blocks
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

As you may know, major LLM providers apply a retention period to stored KV cache. For example, OpenAI retains the KV cache for GPT-5.6 and later models for 30 minutes after its most recent read or write ([source](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime-gpt-5-6-and-later)). vLLM has only limited support for this. The only relevant option I could find is `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl` ([source](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease/#bidirectional-kv-transfer)), which sets time-based eviction for KV cache stored on the GPUs of the decode stage in PD disaggregation. Beyond that, based on [this discussion](https://discuss.vllm.ai/t/how-to-adjust-prefix-caching-timeout/1663) and [this GitHub issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/8333), vLLM doesn’t support TTL-based prefix cache eviction.

Note that what I have in mind is simpler than memory pinning, as discussed in GitHub issues #51428 and #37003. vLLM would keep its existing LRU eviction as is, but [`KVCacheBlock`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/624a5ddafd96df23fe2b9f6d4b8f52a08b9fe9ea/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L154) would gain an `expires_at` field, and a block would be lazily evicted after expiration time is passed.

So my question is: would this feature be useful for vLLM? I’ve already implemented the eviction method described above and would like to open a PR. Since a PR involves more than just sharing code, I wanted to check first whether there’s interest. If so, I’d be glad to clean up the code, add documentation, and submit it.

title: [Feature]: Enable batch-sharded sampling for GPT-OSS
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Batch-sharded sampling was introduced in #50465, but GPT-OSS does not implement the required `compute_logits_local` interface. With Model Runner V2, enabling `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` therefore logs a warning and falls back to regular sampling.

GPT-OSS uses the standard `ParallelLMHead` and `LogitsProcessor`, so it should be possible to enable the existing path by exposing rank-local logits with `skip_gather=True`.

This would allow GPT-OSS to distribute sampling work across TP ranks. In development benchmarks with GPT-OSS-20B on 2×L20, TP=2, and concurrency 256, enabling this path improved output throughput by approximately 4.5–6.0%.

### Alternatives

Continue using regular sampling. This works correctly but does not benefit from batch-sharded sampling.

### Additional context

The proposed change is limited to the model hook and regression coverage in the existing sharded-sampling E2E test. Logits redistribution and sampling remain handled by the shared runner.

Related: #56074, which addresses compatibility with lm_head LoRA.

title: [Feature]: Allow pooling tasks (token_embed / token_classify) to reuse prefix cache while returning full hidden-state sequences
body: ### The problem On vLLM 0.29.0, pooling requests with `task="token_embed"` or `task="token_classify"` are **forcefully excluded from prefix-cache reads**, even when prefix caching is explicitly enabled and the caller explicitly requests it. The mandatory behavior is in `vllm/pooling_params.py` (`_merge_default_parameters`, present in v0.29.0 through current `main`): ```python if self.skip_reading_prefix_cache is None: # If prefix caching is enabled, # the output of all pooling may less than n_prompt_tokens, # we need to skip reading cache at this request. if self.task in ["token_embed", "token_classify"]: self.skip_reading_prefix_cache = True else: self.skip_reading_prefix_cache = False ``` When the caller leaves `skip_reading_prefix_cache` as `None` (the default), it is forced to `True` for these two tasks. There is no supported way for an application to opt in to cache reads while keeping the pooling task. ### Why full hidden states + prefix caching are needed together Our workload is multi-candidate classification with a sequence-classification adapter (`vllm-jev`, serving Open-Jev-2B style decision heads). For each HTTP request: 1. The prompt is built as `fixed instructions + fixed candidate list (up to ~18 candidates) + per-request state`, so **the leading ~400+ tokens are identical across requests** and only the trailing state differs. 2. The adapter submits one pooling request per candidate (or a deduplicated set of shared-prefix sequences) with `task="token_embed"`, because the decision head needs **the hidden states at specific readout positions** of the full sequence — a scalar `classify` output is not sufficient. 3. Many candidates share the same leading tokens, and the fixed instruction/criteria block is repeated across every request. This is exactly the workload prefix caching is designed for. With the forced skip, every request recomputes the entire prompt. Measured on an RTX 4090 (vLLM 0.29.0, prefix caching enabled, same `cache_salt`, identical prompts re-submitted back-to-back): - `metadata.cached_tokens` is always `0` for both `token_embed` and `classify` pooling requests; - the engine-level `Prefix cache hit rate` metric does occasionally report small non-zero values (2.6%–5.1%), so the cache subsystem itself is alive — but per-request `num_cached_tokens` stays 0 and our throughput matches the "no reuse" expectation; - using `--decision-template` style reordering so that the fixed text truly leads the prompt does not change this (the skip happens before any block matching). With the forced skip, every request recomputes the entire prompt. Measured on an RTX 4090 (vLLM 0.29.0, prefix caching enabled, same `cache_salt`, identical prompts re-submitted back-to-back): - `metadata.cached_tokens` is always `0` for both `token_embed` and `classify` pooling requests; - the engine-level `Prefix cache hit rate` metric does occasionally report small non-zero values (2.6%–5.1%), so the cache subsystem itself is alive — but per-request `num_cached_tokens` stays 0 and our throughput matches the "no reuse" expectation; - using `--decision-template` style reordering so that the fixed text truly leads the prompt does not change this (the skip happens before any block matching). If prefix-cache reads were allowed for `token_embed` requests, the shared leading blocks (instructions + candidate list ≈ 400+ tokens per request, ×18 candidate variants deduplicated by shared prefixes) would be served from cache, which for our benchmark shape roughly halves the per-request prefill compute. ### Why full hidden states + prefix caching are needed together — the general pattern The pattern behind this request is **"encode once, read out at many positions"**: a decoder runs the prompt once, and lightweight heads (linear probes, small MLPs) read the hidden states at one or more token positions to produce decisions. This is how a growing family of classification/routing models works on top of decoder backbones. For these models: - a scalar `classify` output is insufficient — the head needs hidden vectors at specific positions; - the prompts typically share a large fixed prefix (instructions, schema, candidate definitions) with only a small varying payload; - request rate is high (classification/routing/moderation workloads), so prefill compute dominates. All three properties make prefix-cache reuse the single biggest performance lever for this model class, which is why the current forced skip hurts disproportionately. ### Why simply forcing `skip_reading_prefix_cache = False` breaks today We understand the guard exists for a reason. With cache hits, the scheduler marks the hit tokens as already computed, and the pooling runner processes only the non-cached tail — so `token_embed` would return hidden states for fewer positions than the prompt has tokens, while downstream consumers (decision heads over readout positions, token-level classifiers) require **one hidden vector per prompt token, position-aligned**. So the missing piece is not just the flag: the V1 pooling path (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pool/pooling_runner.py`) has no mechanism to reconstruct position-aligned full-sequence hidden outputs when part of the prompt was served from cache. ### Proposed solutions (any one would unblock this workload) 1. **Fill the gap in the pooling runner**: when a `token_embed`/`token_classify` request has prefix-cache hits, still run (or reconstruct) the hidden states for the cached prefix positions so the output remains position-aligned with the full prompt. Conceptually the KV cache already contains the states for those tokens; the runner would need to re-emit their hidden activations from cache rather than skipping them. 2. **Opt-in flag**: expose `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False` as a documented, caller-owned choice for pooling tasks (as it already is for generation tasks), with a clear caveat that the caller must tolerate/align partial hidden outputs. Applications that know their consumer reads specific positions can recompute or skip accordingly. 3. **Hybrid scheduling**: schedule cache-hit prefix tokens through a "read-only" pass that re-materializes hidden states from the cached KV without recomputing attention/MLP for them, if the architecture permits. ### Scope: this affects every pooling-based decision adapter, not just one model We audited the `vllm-jev` adapter family (mode-io/vllm-jev) — every Linux decision backend in it drives vLLM through `task="token_embed"` for its readout, because all of them place decision heads over specific token positions: This is not an accident of one model's architecture: **"encode a sequence once, read out decision heads at multiple token positions" is the defining inference pattern of this entire model family** (and of decoder-side classification heads generally). As long as `token_embed` cannot combine with prefix-cache reads, none of these models can benefit from prefix caching regardless of size — 2B, 9B, and 27B checkpoints are all equally affected. Conversely, if the pooling runner gains the ability to emit position-aligned full-sequence hidden outputs alongside cache hits, the entire family gets the benefit at once. We also verified this is orthogonal to model size, quantization, or `cache_salt` choice, and that the `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` / hybrid-model cache work in v0.30/v0.31 does not touch this path. ### Environment - vLLM 0.29.0 (also verified the same logic exists on current `main` in `vllm/pooling_params.py`) - Model: sequence-classification adapter over a Qwen3.5-architecture foundation (Open-Jev-2B), GDN + MoE - Workload: many short classification requests (~400–600 tokens each) with a large fixed prefix and varying tail; GPU RTX 4090 24GB - The behavior was cross-checked against `vllm-jev` (mode-io/vllm-jev), whose `/v1/systemone` endpoint is a consumer of exactly this pattern; their docs and issue mode-io/vllm-jev#7 describe the same limitation from the adapter side. Happy to provide additional profiling, a reproduction script, or test patches if helpful. Thanks!
label: feature request

title: [Feature]: Explicitly trust a selected preload daemon to avoid checkpoint rescans on engine restart
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

When an engine starts with `--load-format ipc_cache`, it computes the checkpoint fingerprint again before requesting weights from a preload daemon. On a high-latency filesystem, that scan can take a meaningful fraction of every engine restart even when the operator intends to reuse the same already-loaded daemon.

I propose an explicit opt-in mode in which the operator selects a particular live preload daemon instance and declares its resident weights authoritative. In this mode, the engine would skip reading checkpoint files to recompute the content fingerprint. It should still check the model architecture, dtype, quantization configuration, parallel layout, vLLM version, and physical GPU compatibility against the selected daemon.

This would be an operator-controlled invalidation contract: changing the source checkpoint would require starting a new preload daemon. The default behavior should continue to validate checkpoint content. The opt-in should be visible in startup logs, including the identity of the daemon being trusted and the requirement to re-preload after source changes.

The identity and lifecycle semantics need design discussion. In particular, the engine must not silently trust a different daemon that later occupies the same socket path. A daemon instance identifier or generation, rather than only a socket path or PID, may be needed.

#### Motivation and measured example

I measured the cost on **vLLM 0.31.0**, using a 66-shard, approximately 28.75 GiB Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 checkpoint on OSSFS and one H20-3e GPU (TP=1). Both variants used the same live daemon, `ipc_cache`, `zero_copy`, `fallback=false`, and the same warm compilation caches:

- A: run the original `hash_checkpoint()` on every engine start.
- B: reuse the fingerprint captured from that same daemon's initial computation, while retaining the other `WeightCacheKey` and GPU UUID checks.

The runs were ordered A → B → B → A.

| Variant | Checkpoint fingerprint | Model-loading stage | Total startup to `/health` 200 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | 32.374 s | 38.042 s | 79.492 s |
| B1 | 0.000120 s | 5.565 s | 47.253 s |
| B2 | 0.000106 s | 5.623 s | 46.452 s |
| A2 | 31.851 s | 37.275 s | 78.098 s |

Mean total startup was **78.79 s versus 46.85 s**, a difference of **31.94 s (40.5%)** in this environment. All four engines logged zero-copy mapping of 980 tensors, and a short deterministic completion smoke test produced identical output.

These results describe **v0.31.0**, not the concurrent fingerprint reader in PR #59648. I have not measured that PR's implementation on this OSSFS setup. Its parallel reads may reduce the incremental benefit of the proposed mode substantially. The results establish the cost of repeated source-file validation in this environment, not a general speedup claim.

The original measurements and discussion are in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59648#issuecomment-6058645240. This proposal is separate from PR #59648, which improves the correctness of the fingerprint when content validation is performed.


### Alternatives

- **Use the concurrent fingerprint reader in PR #59648.** This retains automatic detection of source-checkpoint changes and should reduce latency on network filesystems. It should remain the default. Its end-to-end effect on this OSSFS setup still needs measurement.
- **Copy the checkpoint to local storage.** This may reduce scan latency but requires additional capacity and a synchronization workflow.
- **Trust a checkpoint path without selecting a daemon instance.** This seems too weak: the path alone does not identify the resident GPU weights or protect against a daemon being replaced at the same socket.


### Additional context

Questions for the design discussion:

1. What should identify a trusted daemon instance across engine restarts and prevent accidental reuse after daemon replacement?
2. Should the mode require an explicit daemon identifier, or is an opt-in flag plus a verified daemon generation sufficient?
3. What startup log and error behavior would make the loss of automatic source-change detection unmistakable?
4. Should a missing or replaced selected daemon be a hard error rather than falling back to disk?

body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**The model to consider**

ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-480M-0826 — a 480M parameter Qwen3-based bidirectional embedding model for Russian and English.

HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/ai-sage/Giga-Embeddings-instruct-480M-0826

The config declares "architectures": ["Qwen3BidirectionalModel"] with "is_causal": false. This architecture string is not registered in vLLM.

**Current behavior**

Without --hf-overrides, vLLM falls back to TransformersEmbeddingModel (the generic Transformers backend), which misses vLLM's optimized kernels:
`WARNING: TransformersEmbeddingModel has no vLLM implementation, falling back to Transformers implementation. Some features may not be supported and performance may not be optimal.`

With --hf-overrides '{"architectures": ["Qwen3Model"]}', the model loads natively with full vLLM optimizations (fused QKV, fused gate/up, compiled RMSNorm). Users shouldn't need to know this workaround.

**The closest model vLLM already supports**
LlamaBidirectionalModel — same pattern: an empty class wrapping as_embedding_model(LlamaForCausalLM) in llama.py.

**Proposed fix**

Follow the LlamaBidirectionalModel precedent:

- Add Qwen3BidirectionalModel class in qwen3.py
- Register in _EMBEDDING_MODELS in registry.py
- Add test and docs entries

title: [Feature]: Restore multimodal requests from processed state and existing KV
body:
## The feature, motivation and pitch

Provide a supported vLLM API to export the processed state of a multimodal prompt and restore it for continuation from existing KV, without loading or preprocessing the media again.

For example, one vLLM instance has already processed an image prompt. A second instance receives the corresponding KV through an existing connector but has a cold multimodal processor/receiver cache. If the KV covers the required image-dependent computation and the model's continuation state is available, the second instance should be able to continue generation using the exact token sequence, media identities, and layout established by the first instance.

This capability should be reusable by Python callers and serving frontends, with explicit model support and recovery semantics. The input-state contract should be independent of a particular orchestrator or KV transport.

## Existing building blocks and the remaining contract

vLLM already has relevant capabilities to build on:

- [#52697](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52697) allows KV consumers to omit multimodal embedding tensors through `allow_missing_mm_embeddings`.
- [#54659](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54659), which closed [#54658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54658), exposes `features.mm_metadata` separately from full tensor data in the Render/Generate protocol.
- [#55639](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55639) discusses using KV or embedding reuse to avoid redundant encoder work. This request focuses on exporting and restoring the already-processed input needed to consume reusable KV; encoder admission and demand feedback are related work.

Open [#43608](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43608) exports Qwen-specific `image_grid_thw` on the older disaggregated serving protocol; it does not provide the engine continuation and lifecycle coverage contract requested here. [#55589](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55589) changes when NIXL Push transfers blocks, rather than how a receiving engine restores multimodal input state.

The request is to unify and extend these paths into a complete continuation contract. It should reuse their serialization and model metadata declarations where possible.

Two concrete boundaries in the inspected **v0.31.0** implementation deserve attention:

1. The [Generate request validator](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/protocol.py) requires `ec_transfer_params` for items supplied through `mm_metadata` without full kwargs. KV-backed continuation also needs a supported admission path when no encoder-output transfer is needed.
2. The [feature serialization helpers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/mm_features.py) export placeholder offsets and lengths. A general roundtrip must also preserve layout information such as `PlaceholderRange.is_embed` when present.

There is also an important distinction in the native input representation: [`MultiModalFeatureSpec.data=None`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.31.0/vllm/multimodal/inputs.py) can mean that the receiver should resolve the item from its media cache. That meaning must remain distinguishable from an input intentionally submitted without a media payload because its computation is expected to be covered by KV. Payload absence alone does not establish that KV is ready.

## Proposed engine contract

### Export the actual processed input

Expose an opt-in operation that returns both the processed `MultiModalInput` to submit for inference and a versioned, serializable continuation descriptor derived from that same input. Reuse the existing renderer so token expansion and media processing happen once.

The descriptor should preserve:

- The exact expanded prompt token IDs.
- Engine-resolved per-item media identities, including processing and cache-isolation semantics relevant to KV hashing.
- Per-item modality and complete placeholder layout: offsets, lengths, and embedding masks where applicable.
- Model-specific state needed to initialize continuation, using existing model interfaces and metadata declarations. M-RoPE models require an explicit supported contract; an `image_grid_thw` field name alone does not establish compatibility across models.
- Cache salt and compatibility information sufficient to validate the model/revision, adapter state when supported, and relevant engine configuration.

KV tensors and remote transfer handles remain outside this descriptor.

### Restore an input with explicit payload availability

Restore a native `MultiModalInput` without fetching media or rerunning its processor. The restored input must retain the metadata used for KV identity and model initialization, and explicitly describe which media payloads are unavailable for recomputation.

`MultiModalInput` describes the whole prompt; `InputProcessor` converts its per-modality fields into individual `MultiModalFeatureSpec` objects. The availability information must survive that conversion and engine IPC, so receiver caches and scheduling can interpret it consistently.

The exact API names, flag/type representation, and placement on the public engine interface are open design questions. Callers explicitly invoke export/restore and then use the existing generation interface. Prefer sharing code with the existing Render/Generate feature protocol over adding a parallel, incompatible schema.

### Enforce execution requirements inside the engine

An input without media payload must only execute when valid local or successfully loaded KV satisfies its required computation. The scheduler and connector must establish this using actual engine state. A descriptor or a configured KV consumer role is not proof of coverage.

If loading fails, coverage is partial, or preemption removes required KV, the engine must provide a clear request-level failure or an explicitly supported recovery path. It must never recompute an image-dependent span using absent or dummy media. A caller can then reacquire state, resubmit through prefill, or retry with media through a supported path.

This requirement should apply throughout the request lifecycle. A caller-side check performed before submission cannot account for later engine preemption.

## Responsibility boundaries

| Layer | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| vLLM input/model interfaces | Export and restore processed input, preserve identity/layout/position state, declare model capabilities and payload availability |
| vLLM scheduler and existing KVConnector | Load or reuse KV through existing mechanisms, track actual coverage/readiness, prevent unsupported recomputation |
| Caller or serving coordinator | Select instances, associate the descriptor with the correct request and KV transfer, deliver metadata, and choose recovery policy from engine results |

The input/restore API should not hard-code NIXL or another connector name. Capability checks should distinguish model/input support from connector-specific loading and recovery support. Existing callers sending full media inputs should retain their behavior.

## Initial scope and acceptance criteria

Start with image-only, decoder-only models with verified continuation behavior, such as LLaVA, and one validated connector. Expand model and connector coverage explicitly; reject or retain the existing full-input path for unsupported configurations.

- **Input fidelity:** roundtrip the actual processed prompt, multiple images, masks, changed processor parameters, cache scopes, and supported position state without expanding placeholders twice.
- **Identity and reuse:** with prefix caching enabled, equal-size images A -> B -> A remain distinct where required and reuse compatible state for repeated A. Preserve P/D block identities without per-request random salts or globally disabling caches.
- **Cold receiver:** continue with valid imported KV even when the receiving process has no media-cache entry.
- **No repeated media work:** on the supported successful continuation path, instrument and verify zero media fetches, image decodes, processor invocations, and vision-encoder executions.
- **Recovery:** cover malformed/incompatible descriptors, missing metadata, asynchronous loading, failed loads, partial coverage including an image-tail block, cancellation, and preemption.
- **Compatibility:** preserve legacy full-input/cache-reference behavior, and explicitly support or reject LoRA, speculative decoding, and models with additional position requirements.
- **Performance:** compare against the current correct media-loading baseline under cold/warm caches and concurrency. Measure latency, CPU work, media traffic, and metadata overhead. Performance gains remain hypotheses until measured.

## Alternatives

- Resending and processing media on the consumer retains a straightforward recovery path, but repeats media I/O and processing.
- Relying on warm media caches helps repeated requests on the same process, but does not cover a fresh consumer that only receives KV.
- Omitting all multimodal features loses the identities and layout required for correct KV reuse and model initialization.
- Implementing model-specific reconstruction in each coordinator duplicates engine knowledge and can drift as processors and models change.

## Additional context: Dynamo

This proposal was originally tracked in [HanFa/vllm#1](https://github.com/HanFa/vllm/issues/1) and is being moved upstream. It also tracks the engine capability needed by [HanFa/dynamo#2](https://github.com/HanFa/dynamo/issues/2). Dynamo's image P/D path is one motivating caller: prefill has already processed the image, while decode can still load and process it again to reconstruct a correct multimodal request. The correctness regression and restoration of that path are discussed in [ai-dynamo/dynamo#15343](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/15343) and [#15371](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15371).

The initial implementation is proposed in draft [vllm-project/vllm#60526](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60526).

An experimental implementation is available on [HanFa/vllm:codex/mm-kv-handoff-2](https://github.com/HanFa/vllm/tree/codex/mm-kv-handoff-2), paired with [HanFa/dynamo:codex/mm-kv-handoff-2](https://github.com/HanFa/dynamo/tree/codex/mm-kv-handoff-2). It currently limits model support to image-only LLaVA with ordinary sequence positions. Export/restore and admission no longer require NIXL: the scheduler checks actual local/imported KV coverage. Its `MultiModalKvHandoff`/`mm_requires_kv` names and separate descriptor schema are experimental choices to reconcile with the existing vLLM interfaces described above. Processed inputs are submitted directly to `AsyncLLM` or `LLMEngine`; the offline `LLM.generate()` rendering path explicitly rejects them.

The current vLLM prototype has 83 passing targeted CPU tests (34 handoff, 21 scheduler, and 28 renderer tests), with pre-commit checks passing. The companion Dynamo branch previously passed 17 adapter tests. Dynamo processor/handler suites were unavailable locally because the compiled bindings were missing. GPU end-to-end correctness, model evaluation, and performance have not been established. The prototype and this issue were developed with AI assistance.
label: feature request

title: [Tracking Feature]: Support vLLM with Python 3.15
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Tracking issue for Python 3.15 support, following #34096 for 3.14. As with 3.14, the vLLM wheel itself should need no change: the `abi3` extensions from a current precompiled wheel load unchanged on 3.15. What blocks us is upstream dependencies.

Tested on CUDA 13.0 with CPython 3.15.0rc3 and `main` at 32fbfa15e8, as of Oct 7, 2026. With the blockers below worked around, a model loads and the profile-run forward pass completes, so I have not found anything in vLLM's own Python code that needs to change yet. The engine does not get past the sampler, so generation and serving are untested.

Leading blockers:

* [ ] **PyTorch: `torch.compile` is not available on 3.15 in stable releases.** `torch==2.13.0` (our pin) and `2.14.1` (latest stable) have cp315 wheels on the PyTorch index, but both raise at call time. The nightly (`2.16.0.dev20261007+cu130`) works. vLLM applies `@torch.compile` at module import in many places (first hit is `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`), so most of `vllm` fails to import. This also gates `torchvision` (0.29.1 has cp315 but needs torch 2.14) and `torchaudio` (cp315 only in nightly).
```
  File "vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py", line 982, in <module>
    @torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=current_platform.simple_compile_backend)
  File "torch/__init__.py", line 2745, in compile
    raise RuntimeError("torch.compile is not supported on Python 3.15+")
```

* [ ] **Triton: kernel compilation fails on 3.15** with `triton==3.8.0` (latest). A trivial `@triton.jit` kernel compiles and runs, but the sampler kernel in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py` fails inside Triton's code generator. I have not isolated which construct triggers it.
```
  File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/gumbel.py", line 382, in gumbel_sample
  File "triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 80, in make_ir
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 37:17:
TypeError("ast.AnnAssign.__init__ missing 1 required positional argument: 'simple'")
```

* [ ] **NVIDIA CUDA Python packages: no cp315 wheels**, and these are wheel-only. Each one removes required vLLM dependencies from the resolution:
  * `nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-base` (4.8.0) blocks `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`, `quack-kernels`, `tokenspeed-mla`, and `flashinfer-python`
  * `cuda-bindings` (13.4.3) blocks `humming-kernels`
  * `nccl-extensions` (0.1.0), `nccl4py`, `cuda-tile` block `flashinfer-python`
  * `nvidia-cudnn-frontend`
  * `PyNvVideoCodec` (2.0.4)
```
hint: You require CPython 3.15 (`cp315`), but we only found wheels for `nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-base` (v4.8.0) with the following Python ABI tags: `cp310`, `cp311`, `cp312`, `cp313`, `cp314`, `cp314t`
```

Other dependencies without a working 3.15 install:

* [ ] `outlines_core==0.2.14`: no cp315 wheel, and the sdist fails to build because its pinned pyo3 0.27.2 does not compile against 3.15 (`no field tp_name on type &PyTypeObject`).
* [ ] `sentencepiece`: no cp315 wheel. The sdist build also failed on my machine, with a gcc/abseil error I did not investigate.
* [ ] `numba==0.65.0`: does not build on 3.15; `0.68.0` installs.

On the vLLM side:

* [ ] `requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.15"` in `pyproject.toml`. Release candidates slip under this bound, but 3.15.0 final will be rejected.
* [ ] DeepGEMM is built per Python version and we currently ship 3.10 to 3.14.
* [ ] `[build-system]` requires `torch == 2.13.0`, which has a cp315 wheel on download.pytorch.org but not on PyPI, so a source or precompiled install only resolves with `--torch-backend` or the PyTorch index.

Everything else resolves: 63 of the 77 direct requirements in `requirements/common.txt` and `requirements/cuda.txt` install as pinned, and `pyyaml`, `blake3`, `xgrammar`, `nvtx`, `fastsafetensors`, `instanttensor`, `pydantic-core`, `httptools`, and `ijson` build from source.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

Reproduce the dependency resolution with:
```
uv venv --python 3.15
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
```

title: [Feature]: Load the score template declared by the checkpoint (follow-up to #31563)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

I'd like to help move #31563 forward: let a reranker checkpoint declare its own score template so that
`vllm serve <model>` gives correct scores without `--chat-template`.

**Why now.** In #31563, the open question was whether models actually use `query`/`document`-role
templates. Since Sentence Transformers v5.4 they do, e.g.
[Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B/blob/main/chat_template.jinja)
and [zeroentropy/zerank-2-reranker](https://huggingface.co/zeroentropy/zerank-2-reranker/blob/main/chat_template.jinja)
ship one in `chat_template.jinja`. vLLM ignores them for scoring (the FIXME in
`entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py`), so every such model needs `--chat-template`, and
forgetting it fails silently: the server starts, requests return 200, and scores are wrong.

**Measured cost.** I converted zerank-2 to `Qwen3ForSequenceClassification`
([polaria-tech/zerank-2-reranker-vllm](https://huggingface.co/polaria-tech/zerank-2-reranker-vllm))
and compared vLLM 0.29.0 / 0.31.0 against the official `CrossEncoder.predict()` on 40 pairs (H100, bf16):

| setup | logit error vs the official model |
|---|---|
| no `--chat-template` (raw `query + document`) | 11.4 on average |
| `--chat-template` = the model's own `chat_template.jinja` | 9.9 on average |
| `--chat-template` = a dedicated score template | ≤ 0.14, within bf16 noise |

The second row is a separate pitfall: `get_score_prompt` renders the template without
`add_generation_prompt`, and the model's template (written for Sentence Transformers, which sets
`add_generation_prompt: true` in `sentence_bert_config.json`) only emits the final
`<|im_start|>assistant\n` when it is set. So even passing the model's own template gives wrong scores.

**Proposal**, following the design in #31563 (explicit opt-in, no default loading of `chat_template.jinja`):

1. Read `chat_template_path` (or the agreed key) from `config_sentence_transformers.json` and use that
   template for `/score` and `/rerank` when `--chat-template` is not given. `--chat-template` keeps
   precedence.
2. Pass `add_generation_prompt=True` when rendering score templates. vLLM's own templates in
   `examples/pooling/score/template/` ignore it, so they are unaffected.

I'm happy to open the PR for both, with tests, if this matches what you had in mind, @noooop.

### Alternatives

- Keep requiring `--chat-template` and warn at startup, as #56017 does for original Qwen3 rerankers.
  It helps, but the model's own template still gives wrong scores because of `add_generation_prompt`.
- Auto-apply `chat_template.jinja` when it handles the `query`/`document` roles. Ruled out in #31563
  in favour of an explicit opt-in.

### Additional context

Related: #30550 (score templates via `--chat-template`), #31335, #55501 / #56017.
Full parity method and measurements: https://github.com/polaria-tech/zerank-2-reranker-vllm/blob/main/NOTES.md

title: [Feature]: vllm run-batch --resume to continue an interrupted batch
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

With #52505, `vllm run-batch` writes each response as soon as it finishes, so an interrupted run leaves the finished responses on disk. There is still no way to continue from there. The output file is opened with `"w"` when the run starts, so rerunning with the same `-o` truncates it and recomputes everything. In a test with 4000 requests on an A10G (#52505 head), a run killed after 1664 responses was rerun with the same `-o`, and the file was back to 0 lines as soon as the writer opened it.

This matters most where batch jobs get interrupted routinely: spot or preemptible instances, Kubernetes evictions, Slurm preemption, or one bad node in a large sharded job. Today the options are to redo the whole shard or filter the input by hand.

Proposal: a `--resume` flag. When it is set and the local output file exists:

1. Read the existing output and collect the `custom_id`s that have a 200 response. Lines with an error status are retried, since some of them are not real failures (see below).
2. Drop a trailing line that isn't valid JSON. A SIGKILL can land in the middle of a write. I didn't hit this with ~4 KB responses, but large responses make it more likely.
3. Open the file in append mode and dispatch only the requests that are left.
4. Fail before the model loads if the input has duplicate `custom_id`s. `BatchRequestInput` already says they "Must be unique for each request in a batch", but nothing checks it, and resume can't be correct without it. `validate_batch` already parses every line before the engine starts, so the check is cheap.

Scope would be local output files. A URL output is only uploaded when the run succeeds, so there is nothing partial to resume from.

### Alternatives

### Alternatives

- A wrapper script that filters the input against the old output and appends to it. It works, but everyone ends up writing their own, and it has to know the error-line caveat below.
- Writing errors to a separate file, like the OpenAI Batch API's error file, would make "what is left" easier to compute, but it is a bigger change to the output format.

### Additional context

### Additional context

- Depends on #52505.
- On SIGINT, #52505 currently writes the in-flight requests it cancels as `400 "Client disconnected"` (951 such lines in my test). Resume would need to retry those, or #52505 should stop writing them. I suggested the latter in a review there.
- Killing the launcher leaves the EngineCore holding GPU memory (#55510), so an immediate rerun on the same GPU fails until that is fixed (#55846).
- The online Batch and Files API in #44445 could reuse the same skip-completed logic.

I'm happy to work on this once #52505 lands.

title: [Bug][ROCm] Slow EngineCore/worker teardown leaves VRAM held after shutdown, so the next engine fails its startup memory check
body:
### Describe the bug
On ROCm, after a vLLM engine is shut down, its GPU memory can stay held for tens of seconds. Anything that starts a new engine shortly after stopping one then fails the startup memory check:

    ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (171.76/191.98 GiB) on startup is less than desired GPU memory utilization (0.92, 176.63 GiB).

**Where it has been seen**
1. AMD CI, `(MI300) LM Eval Small Models Harness
   - The test runs 6 models back to back in one pytest process.
   - Model 5's EngineCore got SIGTERM at 09:22:27 and model 6 started at 09:22:30.
   - At model 6's memory check (09:22:56, 29 s after SIGTERM), about 20 GiB was still in use.
   - Models 1–5 each started with 191.46 GiB free.

**Possibly related:** in the same CI build, `(MI300) Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown` hung for 2400 s in `v1/shutdown/test_startup_error.py::test_async_llm_startup_error[forward-2-...]`. The EngineCore logged "EngineCore failed to start" and "all workers exited gracefully", but its process never exited, so `wait_for_engine_startup` kept polling. This has not reproduced locally (43 runs, with and without CPU load).

### Why ROCm teardown is slower (hypotheses, not yet measured)
- **Larger allocations to free:** at 0.92 utilization an engine holds about 176 GiB on MI300X and about 265 GiB on MI355X, mostly KV cache.
- **Spawn vs fork exit path:** ROCm uses spawn. Spawned children exit through `sys.exit()`, which runs full interpreter finalization (`atexit` handlers including torch/HIP, GC, finalizers). Forked children exit via `os._exit()` and skip all of that. Slow or hanging `atexit` work would delay process exit and therefore VRAM release. This would also explain the torch 2.13 zombie report.
- **Asynchronous VRAM release in the driver:** the amdgpu driver can free VRAM after the process exits. Existing vLLM comments already note this (`VllmRunner.__exit__`, `get_engine_process_shutdown_timeout` in `vllm/v1/engine/utils.py`).
- **Grace period:** `ROCM_ENGINE_PROCESS_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S = 15.0` only applies when both the request timeout and the process timeout are 0. Shutdowns from garbage collection or the finalizer use the generic 5 s.

### Current workarounds
- Tests that use `vllm_runner` already wait: 60 s ROCm engine shutdown, cleanup, then waiting for VRAM to settle (`VllmRunner.__exit__` in `tests/conftest.py`).
- #60100 applies the same teardown to `.buildkite/lm-eval-harness/test_lm_eval_correctness.py`, which can't use `vllm_runner` because `lm_eval` creates the `LLM` itself. It is ROCm-only.
- These fix the tests, not the underlying behavior. `vllm serve` restarts and user scripts are still affected.

### Proposed investigation / fixes
1. **Measure where teardown time goes on ROCm**, for TP=1 and TP=8:
   - SIGTERM → `worker.shutdown()` done
   - → worker process exit (watch for zombie or D-state)
   - → EngineCore exit
   - → VRAM actually released (read `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_vram_used` from outside the process)

   Compare spawn against `os._exit()` after cleanup, and torch 2.13 against an earlier torch.
2. **Make teardown faster:** if `atexit` or interpreter finalization is the slow part, exit workers and the EngineCore with `os._exit()` once vLLM's own cleanup is done (after flushing logs), or fix the offending handler in torch/HIP.
3. **Make shutdown report "done" only when resources are free:** on ROCm, `shutdown()` would return only after the EngineCore and its workers have exited and VRAM has dropped, with a bounded wait.
4. **Make startup tolerant:** if free memory is below the requested utilization but rising, wait a bounded time before raising.

### Reproduction (outline)
On MI300X or MI355X, start `LLM(model, gpu_memory_utilization=0.92)`, run a request, shut it down, and immediately start a second `LLM` on the same GPU. Or restart `vllm serve -tp 8` within a few seconds of SIGINT. Failure is intermittent and more likely on busy nodes. Holding about 20 GiB on the GPU while the second engine starts reproduces the exact error deterministically.

title: [Feature]: Per-request prefix-cache miss attribution (prompt divergence vs. eviction)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Automatic prefix caching is one of the biggest cost and latency wins for RAG and agent workloads, where every request re-sends a long, mostly identical scaffold (system prompt, tool schemas, few-shot examples).

vLLM already reports per-request cached tokens (`num_cached_tokens`, `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`), so you can tell roughly *where* the cache hit ended. What you can't tell is what happened to the first block after the hit. Users typically care about two common causes, which need very different fixes:

- **The prompt changed.** A timestamp or request ID in the system prompt, tool definitions serialized in a different order, a user name injected near the top. Each one invalidates every block after it. The fix is in the application.
- **The block was evicted.** The prefix was cached earlier but got pushed out under memory pressure. The fix is capacity, routing or cache offload, not the prompt.

vLLM can't infer the cause. The diagnostic below reports what it observed and leaves the interpretation to the user. Today both look identical from the outside: a short cache hit. Telling them apart means diffing tokenized prompts by hand and guessing about eviction.

**Proposal:** optional per-request diagnostics, disabled by default:

- a **miss reason** for the first uncached block after the longest hit: `evicted` (its hash was cached and evicted recently: with the flag on, hashes dropped in `BlockPool._maybe_evict_cached_block` are also recorded as `BlockHashWithGroupId` in a fixed-size LRU, e.g. sized to `num_gpu_blocks`, roughly one cache turnover; a hit there is definite) or `no_match` (not seen within that window: a changed prompt, a never-seen prompt, or an eviction older than the window; ambiguous by design). `no_match` covers both changed prompt tokens and changed extra keys mixed into the block hash (`cache_salt`, LoRA adapter, multimodal inputs), so on its own it is not proof that the text changed.
- a third outcome, `lookup_limit`, when the hit length reached the lookup cap (`num_tokens - 1`, rounded down to a full block). vLLM always recomputes the last prompt token for logits, so that next block is never probed; it is recomputed by design, not missed, and gets no miss reason
- the **kinds of extra keys** included in that block's hash (e.g. `cache_salt`, `lora`, `mm`), names only and never values, so users can rule out salt or adapter differences first
- optionally, an opt-in **comparison against a reference request** that returns a short decoded snippet around the first differing token, off by default for privacy

_Updated after discussion below: renamed `not_cached` to `no_match` and added extra-key kinds (`cache_salt` edge case), and added `lookup_limit` so fully cached prompts at a block boundary are not reported as misses. Test controls: 16/17/32/33-token prompts with block size 16. Later reworded so the labels state observations rather than inferred causes, and specified the eviction hook._

Scope: full-attention groups first, reported per KV-cache group; hybrid groups later if the approach holds up. Cost when enabled: one set lookup per request plus a bounded set; nothing when off.

These could be surfaced in debug-level logs and/or request-level metrics.

**Why it helps:** teams could catch cache-hostile prompt construction in CI or staging, and tie TTFT regressions to the right cause: a prompt change versus cache pressure in the serving stack.

### Alternatives

- Diffing tokenized prompts by hand against a known-good request. Works for divergence, but is slow, needs the exact tokenized input, and says nothing about eviction.
- Correlating with KV cache events (block stored / removed) externally. Possible, but requires running an event consumer and joining block hashes to requests outside vLLM.
- Re-hashing prompts client-side. This duplicates vLLM's block-hashing logic and drifts whenever that changes (block size, hash function, multimodal or LoRA extra keys).

### Additional context

Related: #43711 proposed a lower-level debug event at the lookup point (`KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks`, right after `find_longest_cache_hit`). It was closed for inactivity without maintainer feedback. That lookup point looks like the natural place to compute the miss reason above.

Happy to work on a PR if maintainers agree on the approach.

title: [Feature]: Support trainer-side pipeline parallelism with NCCL M2N weight transfer
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch


PR [[#51520] adds NCCL M2N weight transfer for resharing trainer weights directly into vLLM workers.

The current M2N source contract requires every trainer rank to follow the same parameter manifest and participate in every parameter transfer. This does not represent pipeline parallelism greater than one, where each pipeline stage owns only part of the model:

```text
PP stage 0: embeddings and early layers
PP stage 1: later layers and output head
```

In current vLLM `main`, the trainer integration must first normalize this stage-local ownership into the complete named-tensor stream expected by the weight-update interface. This can require additional collection or forwarding before transfer.

The requested feature is to let M2N transfer each parameter directly from its owning pipeline-stage ranks:

```text
PP stage 0 parameters ──M2N──▶ generator workers
PP stage 1 parameters ──M2N──▶ generator workers
```

All participants must still agree on a global parameter order and transfer plan before NCCL initialization to prevent mismatched collectives.

This is needed for models that require PP>1 to fit and to avoid unnecessary trainer-side gathering or relaying. The solution should be independent of the model, trainer framework, and number of pipeline stages.

This issue will be related to issue #46429 to generalize for more models

title: [Feature]: Support fused MoE weights with NCCL M2N weight transfer
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

In current vLLM main, online weight updates use the regular model-loading path for fused MoE weights:
```
Checkpoint-format expert weights
        │
        │ complete tensors delivered to each generator worker
        ▼
vLLM model loader
        │
        ├─ identifies locally owned experts
        ├─ maps global expert IDs to local expert IDs
        ├─ fuses gate and up projections into w13_weight
        └─ loads down projections into w2_weight
        ▼
Backend-specific local MoE parameters
```
This path is correct because the model loader understands expert ownership and the runtime-specific fused representation. However, every generator worker receives the complete logical expert weights before selecting the experts it owns.

PR [#51520](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51520) adds NCCL M2N weight transfer so trainer shards can be resharded directly into their destination layouts. Ordinary parameters can therefore avoid the existing full-tensor distribution path.

Fused MoE parameters cannot use a simple direct destination because their source names and layouts do not directly correspond to the runtime tensors. For example, separate gate and up projections may need to be combined into w13_weight, and each expert-parallel worker owns only a subset of the global experts.
As a result, these weights must still use the full-tensor fallback from PR #51520:

```
Trainer shards
      │
      │ reconstruct and replicate the complete logical weight
      ▼
Every generator worker
      │
      │ existing model loader
      ▼
Locally owned w13_weight / w2_weight shards
```

This feature is requested so NCCL M2N can transfer only the expert data required by each destination worker while preserving the existing model-loader behavior for expert mapping, fusion, validation, and backend-specific packing.

The desired result is:
```
Trainer shards
      │
      │ NCCL M2N reshard
      ▼
Only the experts owned by each generator worker
      │
      │ existing fused-MoE loading semantics
      ▼
Local w13_weight / w2_weight
```

The solution should apply generally to fused MoE models and expert-parallel configurations. Unsupported layouts can continue using the full-tensor fallback.

title: [Feature]: Logprobs on parsed path streaming `/derender`
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Streaming `/derender` with a reasoning or tool parser (#50550) doesn't return logprobs. #55029 added streaming logprobs but only on the unparsed path. The parsed path builds its stream choices without them. A client that streams with `logprobs: true` through a parser gets nothing back.

Agreed on #47161 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161#issuecomment-5893681568): the engine is the reference for logprob token strings. Standalone `/derender`, including the parsed path should use one shared resolver built on `convert_ids_list_to_tokens` and `_correct_decoded_token` with parity tests against the engine.

Scope:

- Resolve each chunk's logprobs and attach them to whatever delta the parser emits. `/v1/chat/completions` does the same, with one `logprobs.content` list no matter which field the tokens land in.
- Update `logprob_context_token_ids` on the parsed path, like the plain path does. Keep it starting empty, like the engine.
- Drop logprobs on every chunk when `include_reasoning=false` with a parser, like the engine does.
- Fix batch derender too. `_derender_chat` clears `reasoning` but still returns the logprobs.
- Add parity tests against `/v1/chat/completions` with `include_reasoning` on and off, a chunk the parser swallows (tool-call markup) and a multi-byte char split across chunks.

`DerenderStreamState` stays as is. Chunk logprobs already cover only that chunk's tokens and replay never touches them, so no cursor is needed. #59510 handles streaming stop with a 400, so no pending text field either.

~Blocked on #58181 (still open).~ The shared helper (`decode_token_ids`) and the parity tests depend on it.

@shimib has offered to take this. @hyeongyun0916 will review and help with repros.

### Alternatives

Re-resolving token strings separately in the parsed path. We ruled this out on #47161 because the paths already disagree (see #59241).

### Additional context

- #47161: RFC thread where this was agreed
- #55029: streaming logprobs for the unparsed path
- #50550: parser aware streaming derender
- #58181 / #57574: `GenerateLogProbs` with integer token IDs
- #59241 / #59252: SentencePiece leading space dropped in derender logprob strings
- #57052 / #59510: stop handling on derender. #59510 makes streaming `/derender` return 400 on `stop` and notes that logprobs aren't trimmed to the cut text.

title: [Feature]: Support configuring Triton unified-attention launch parameters
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Hi folks! We’re serving Gemma 4 on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) and currently patch `triton_unified_attention.py` to tune prefill for the model’s global-attention layers.

I wanted to ask whether there’s a supported way to configure these launch parameters, or whether you’d prefer a PR adding a targeted heuristic.

Our shape is head dimension 512, global attention, FP8 per-tensor KV, and GQA 8. The existing `tuned_large_head` branch covers head dimension 256 on SM100, so our layers use the default parameters.

For an isolated kernel benchmark with a 2,048-token prefill chunk against 64K of KV, we measured:

| BLOCK_M | num_warps | num_stages | Latency (ms) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | Default | Default | 15.556 | 1.00x |
| 16 | 4 | 2 | 14.577 | 1.07x |
| 32 | 4 | 3 | 15.551 | 1.00x |
| **32** | **4** | **2** | **8.492** | **1.83x** |
| 32 | 8 | 2 | 14.839 | 1.05x |
| 64 | 4 | 2 | 28.324 | 0.55x |

Changing `BLOCK_M` and `num_stages` together gave the improvement. Our patch sets:

```python
BLOCK_M = 32
BLOCK_Q = BLOCK_M // num_queries_per_kv
launch_num_warps = 4
launch_num_stages = 2
```

We apply this only to CUDA SM120-family devices with the shape above and `max_seqlen_q > 1`.

The patch works well for us, but carrying it across vLLM upgrades adds some maintenance overhead. Would it make sense to make these launch parameters configurable based on the GPU and kernel shape, or would you prefer we add a targeted heuristic for this case?

Happy to contribute either way. If there’s already a supported approach I’ve missed, I’d appreciate a pointer!

### Alternatives

- A targeted heuristic PR: This would be the smallest change, and I’m happy to start there if that’s preferred.
- Another attention backend: We tested FlashInfer’s native paged prefill and decode with head dimension 512 on this GPU. Both ran, but prefill was slower in our microbenchmark. The query dtypes and layouts differed, so this isn’t a direct serving comparison.
- Keeping the build-time patch: This is our current approach, but we’d like to avoid maintaining it separately if there’s a reasonable upstream path.

### Additional context

Environment

- NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, compute capability 12.0
- vLLM 0.28.0 
- CUDA 13.0
- Triton 3.7.1
- FP8 per-tensor KV on the global layers; BF16 KV on the sliding-window layers

title: [Feature]: shechduling using predicted decode output length
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

When prompts are long and concurrency is high, the scheduler can admit more requests than the KV cache can hold once decoding grows. A request then gets preempted and must be recomputed, which hurts performance.

This is especially costly in prefill/decode disaggregation. If the decode instance is under too much KV pressure and has to recompute, that raises TPOT on the decode instance and lowers throughput for the whole system.

`--watermark` can keep a fraction of the KV cache free and reduce this churn, but it is not flexible. It is a single value set at startup and cannot adapt to different workloads or to individual queries.

In some workloads the service already knows the average output length, or an external model can cheaply estimate it. If that estimate is passed into the vLLM scheduler, admission can reserve KV cache for the prompt plus the estimated output, instead of only for the tokens needed right now. That should lower the chance of preemption.

I can open a PR for this if it looks useful. thanks

title: [Feature]: Helm chart: add an optional ServiceMonitor with a configurable regex filter to reduce the number of exported metrics
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

#### Problem

vLLM exposes a very large number of time series on its `/metrics` endpoint, and there is currently no simple way to limit them when deploying with the Helm chart in `examples/deployment/chart-helm`. The chart does not ship a `ServiceMonitor`, so users who collect vLLM metrics through a `ServiceMonitor`-compatible operator have to write their own, and in practice they end up ingesting everything.

Most deployments only use a small subset of these metrics in their dashboards and alerts. The volume mainly comes from:

- **Histograms.** Each histogram (end-to-end latency, time to first token, inter-token latency, prompt and generation lengths, prefill and decode times, ...) produces one `_bucket` series per bucket, plus `_sum` and `_count`. This is then multiplied by the number of replicas.
- **Metrics that do not apply to a given deployment.** Depending on the setup, speculative decoding, LoRA or prefix cache metrics may never be used.
- **Default Python client metrics.** The `python_*` and `process_*` families are exported by default and are rarely needed.

At scale this increases scrape size, ingestion rate, storage and query cost in the metrics backend, for series that nobody queries. With several replicas, the cost grows linearly with the number of pods.

You can measure the breakdown by metric family on any instance with:

```bash
curl -s http://<host>:8000/metrics | grep -v '^#' \
  | sed -E 's/[{ ].*//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -30
```

#### Proposal

Add an optional `ServiceMonitor` template to the Helm chart, disabled by default so that current behavior does not change. It would expose the usual scrape settings (port, path, interval) and, most importantly, a way to filter metrics with regular expressions on the metric name, applied at collection time.

Two modes would cover the common needs:

- **Allowlist**: keep only the metrics whose name matches a regex. This is the most effective way to reduce the number of series, since anything not explicitly listed is dropped, including the default Python and process metrics.
- **Denylist**: drop the metrics whose name matches a regex, for users who prefer to remove only what they know is useless (for example a specific family of histogram buckets).

The filter would be empty by default, so nothing is dropped unless the user opts in. I would deliberately not hard-code a default list in the chart, because metric names change between vLLM versions (for example the KV cache usage metric was renamed), and a built-in list would silently break dashboards after an upgrade.

A few practical notes for users, which I would document in the chart README:

- Histogram metrics must be covered explicitly in the regex (`_sum`, `_count` and `_bucket` suffixes).
- Filtering happens after collection: the full payload is still generated by vLLM, but only the selected series are stored.
- The template requires the `ServiceMonitor` custom resource definition to be installed in the cluster. Since it is disabled by default, clusters without it are not affected.

This approach needs no change in vLLM itself and works with any operator or collector that supports `ServiceMonitor`.

#### Additional context

I will open a PR on the Helm chart to add the `ServiceMonitor` template and its filtering options as described above.

title: [Feature]: Add lifecycle management hooks for the worker extension class (--worker-extension-cls)
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

vLLM provides the` --worker-extension-cls` argument, which allows users to pass in a custom class that is injected as a base class of the worker abstraction.
However, in` vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py`, the current implementation only sets up the inheritance relationship — it does not define or invoke any lifecycle management interfaces. For example, there is no initialization hook being called, which means the actually running GPUWorker has no chance to initialize the injected functionality.
While it is possible to invoke methods on the engine through /collective_rpc, this is not a good solution for lifecycle hooks such as an initializer or a destructor:
* The caller has to trigger them manually at the right time, which is error-prone;
* Initialization/cleanup are semantically tied to the worker's own construction and teardown, not to an ad-hoc RPC from the client side;
* The extension itself has no way to guarantee its initialization runs before any other injected method is used.

**Proposal**: define a set of extension lifecycle interfaces (e.g., `init_worker_extension`, and symmetrically something like `destroy_worker_extension`), and invoke them at the corresponding points of the worker lifecycle. For example, in `WorkerWrapperBase.init_worker`:

```
# WorkerWrapperBase.init_worker
def init_worker(self):
    ...
    init_worker_extension = False
    if parallel_config.worker_extension_cls:
        worker_extension_cls = resolve_obj_by_qualname(
            parallel_config.worker_extension_cls
        )
        extended_calls = []
        if worker_extension_cls not in worker_class.__bases__:
            # check any conflicts between worker and worker_extension_cls
            for attr in dir(worker_extension_cls):
                if attr.startswith("__"):
                    continue
                assert not hasattr(worker_class, attr), (
                    f"Worker class {worker_class} already has an attribute"
                    f" {attr}, which conflicts with the worker"
                    f" extension class {worker_extension_cls}."
                )
                if callable(getattr(worker_extension_cls, attr)):
                    extended_calls.append(attr)
            # dynamically inherit the worker extension class
            worker_class.__bases__ = worker_class.__bases__ + (
                worker_extension_cls,
            )
            logger.info(
                "Injected %s into %s for extended collective_rpc calls %s",
                worker_extension_cls,
                worker_class,
                extended_calls,
            )
            # check whether the injected extension provides the init hook
            init_worker_extension = "init_worker_extension" in extended_calls
    ...

    with set_current_vllm_config(self.vllm_config):
        # To make vLLM config available during worker initialization
        self.worker = worker_class(**kwargs)
        if init_worker_extension:
            self.worker.init_worker_extension()
```
With this in place, an extension class can optionally implement init_worker_extension() (and potentially a matching teardown hook), and vLLM will call it automatically at the right point of the worker lifecycle — no manual RPC needed.

### Alternatives

1. **Calling the init/destroy functions via `/collective_rpc`**. This works mechanically, but lifecycle hooks invoked over RPC are detached from the worker's actual construction and destruction. Every client has to know about the hook and remember to call it in the right order, and there is no guarantee the extension is initialized before its other methods are invoked.

2. **Subclassing `GPUWorker` or monkey-patching it in downstream projects**. This duplicates effort across projects and is fragile to maintain as vLLM evolves, which defeats the purpose of having an official extension mechanism.

### Additional context

A typical use case is colocated training-and-inference frameworks (e.g., RL training stacks), which rely on `--worker-extension-cls` to inject custom functionality such as weight synchronization, custom collective operations, or auxiliary process groups. These extensions usually require one-time initialization (allocating buffers, setting up communicators) and proper cleanup when the worker shuts down. A standardized lifecycle hook would let such extensions initialize themselves deterministically right after the worker is constructed, and clean up during worker teardown, instead of relying on lazy initialization inside RPC entry points.

body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

This issue is to support `Prefix-LM` for `ROCM_ATTN` and `ROCM_UNIFIED_ATTN` backends. It is currently not implemented.   Please see this [PR ](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52395)to return `False `from `supports_mm_prefix` from these backends.  An implementation should:

     a.  tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py
     b. tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py,
  3. and return `True `from the appropriate backend so it can be used.

### Investigation of Prefix-LM support on `ROCM_ATTN`  and  `ROCM_UNIFIED_ATTN `

 I compared with `TritonAttentionMetadata` and `TRITON_ATTN `backend:
