body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**NOTE: automated unfinished PRs will likely not get reviewed. If you are an agent, do not open PRs autonomously before discussing here.**

`AiterExperts` should be tested more comprehensively.

Current https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L420 is a master do-everything class when it comes to using `aiter` MOE implementation.

Current CI lacks test cases of `AiterExperts.apply`, that would ensure it matches reference MoE result for:

- every supported `(weight_quant_key, activation_quant_key)` pair,
- and every `aiter.fused_moe.fused_moe` routing implementation / backend actually selected.

The primary test home could be extending [`test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py#L209-L376), with focused ROCm-only helpers in [`test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py#L1-L1096).

## Test every `_supports_quant_scheme` case

Test every pair from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L459-L480.

Each supported pair should run `AiterExperts.apply()` through the modular kernel and compare its result with the existing reference MoE implementation.

| Pair | Current modular-combination status | Required work |
|---|---|---|
| `(None, None)` | Present indirectly | Make the AITER case identifiable in the generated matrix. |
| `(kFp8Static128BlockSym, kFp8Dynamic128Sym)` | Present indirectly | Retain the known block-scaled topk=1 exclusion. |
| `(kFp8StaticTensorSym, kFp8StaticTensorSym)` | Present indirectly | Add an explicit AITER case ID/assertion. |
| `(kFp8StaticTensorSym, kFp8DynamicTensorSym)` | Present indirectly | Add an explicit AITER case ID/assertion. |
| `(kFp8StaticChannelSym, kFp8DynamicTokenSym)` | Present indirectly | Cover both normal top-k and the valid topk=1/tkw1 route. |
| `(kMxfp4Static, None)` | Missing | Add a GFX950-only W4A16 modular `apply()` case. |
| `(kMxfp4Static, kMxfp4Dynamic)` | Missing | Add a GFX950-only W4A4 modular `apply()` case. |

The current [`MK_QUANT_CONFIGS`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/mk_objects.py#L396-L446) matrix has no MXFP4 configuration or weight-conversion path, so it misses both MXFP4 pairs.

## Test every supported activation through `AiterExperts.apply()`

The modular-combination suite currently runs `MoEActivation.SILU`, but https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L483-L490 also accepts `GELU`, `SITU`, `SWIGLUOAI`, and `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE`.

We should e.g.

- Add one `AiterExperts.apply()` correctness case per supported activation and compare each result with the reference MoE implementation.
- Assert the AITER activation type and gate-mode arguments for SwiGLU interleaved versus uninterleaved, MXFP4 W4A16, and SiTU.
- Test both values of `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4`, including forwarding of the SiTU `beta` and `linear_beta` values.

## Test AITER backend and dispatch settings

Run supported correctness cases under `AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING`, `AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING`, `AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND`, and `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MOE_DISPATCH_POLICY`.

Use a fresh spawned child process per configuration because [`aiter.fused_moe`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/f2f8ed9b2b64ded51d7b8b228b7d99e9a09eaed6/aiter/fused_moe.py#L57-L68) reads its sorting environment variables at import time.

| Requested route | Settings to exercise | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| CK sorting | `AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING=1` | The CK route is observed and the output matches reference. |
| FlyDSL sorting | `AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING=0`, `AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1` | The FlyDSL route is observed and the output matches reference. |
| Opus/default sorting | Both sorting flags disabled and `AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND=opus` | The Opus route is observed and the output matches reference. |
| Adaptive MXFP4 sorting | `AITER_MOE_SORT_BACKEND=adaptive` | The adaptive route is observed for a supported W4A4 shape and the output matches reference. |
| vLLM dispatch policy | Each supported `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MOE_DISPATCH_POLICY` value | The value is forwarded from [`AiterExperts.apply`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L546-L560) to [`rocm_aiter_ops.fused_moe`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/vllm/_aiter_ops.py#L2534-L2587). |

Instrument the child process to observe `_moe_sorting_impl` and its `use_opus` argument, `_flydsl_moe_sorting`, or `_adaptive_moe_sort` as appropriate.

Skip an unavailable backend with a specific capability reason, but fail if a requested backend silently falls back to another route.

The existing [spawn launcher](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/tests/kernels/moe/modular_kernel_tools/parallel_utils.py#L85-L150) can be extended to pass the required environment before AITER is imported.

## Split AITER experts by weight quantization key

The [`SUPPORTED_W_A`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L464-L472) list currently combines unquantized, three FP8 weight formats, and MXFP4 weights in one `AiterExperts` class before forwarding them all to AITER.

We could split this by weight quantization key so each expert owns the layout conversion, scale contract, AITER backend availability, and `apply()` arguments for its weight format.

| Suggested expert | Weight quantization key | Supported activation key(s) |
|---|---|---|
| `AiterUnquantizedExperts` | `None` | `None` |
| `AiterFp8BlockExperts` | `kFp8Static128BlockSym` | `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` |
| `AiterFp8TensorExperts` | `kFp8StaticTensorSym` | `kFp8StaticTensorSym`, `kFp8DynamicTensorSym` |
| `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` | `kFp8StaticChannelSym` | `kFp8DynamicTokenSym`, including the topk=1/tkw1 route |
| `AiterMxfp4Experts` | `kMxfp4Static` | `None` for W4A16 and `kMxfp4Dynamic` for W4A4 |

Keep W4A16 and W4A4 together initially because they have the same weight key, but split them further if they require different AITER compute backends, weight layouts, activation layouts, scale formats, gate modes, padding contracts, or routing contracts.

Each class could implement only its supported key pairs, report clear unsupported reasons, and own the exact call arguments it passes to `aiter.fused_moe.fused_moe`. Exact preprocessing could also be owned by these classes (related suggestion in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52240)

In particular, `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` should own the topk=1/apply-router-weight-on-input dispatch to `asm_moe_tkw1`, its scale layout, and its `num_local_tokens` restriction rather than leaving that branch hidden inside the generic AITER expert.

## Test padding

Add `AiterExperts.apply()` tests with `VLLM_ROCM_MOE_PADDING` enabled and disabled. This could include:

- Cover no padding, hidden-dimension-only padding, intermediate-dimension-only padding, and both dimensions padded for each quantization family that supports padding.
- Use dimensions that require actual padding instead of the current modular defaults, which are already aligned, and compare against an unpadded reference result.
- Verify that the input, weights, scales, output slice, and `hidden_dim_unpadded` / `intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded` metadata agree with the selected AITER backend.

Additionally, test under **token padding** (HIP Graph case) where padding tokens may have inf/nan. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50859.

## Align with other AITER experts implementations

Align the resulting structure and test contracts with:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/aiter_mxfp8_moe.py#L62
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/314053177332342e47bd046f134a69ea324b864c/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe.py#L249

that are currently distinct from `AiterExperts`.


### Alternatives

N/A

### Additional context

Related work

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54580 This directly changes the test_modular_kernel_combinations.py harness so AITER receives the same 0/1 expert mask used in serving. It is an important prerequisite/complement: the proposed modular AiterExperts.apply() cases should build on this rather than recreate mask handling.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52240 This substantially refactors MXFP4 oracle/layout handling and adds W13-layout tests. Linked to W4A16/W4A4 correctness / layout test case.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53954 It covers the four environment-variable combinations for SiTU A8W4 layout selection. The new activation section would complement it by testing actual AiterExperts.apply() correctness and forwarded gate mode, rather than duplicating its enablement-table test.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53940 This is relevant to the proposed adaptive/W4A4/FlyDSL backend matrix.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53261 This overlaps the proposed EP and num_local_tokens coverage.

Related but less directly overlapping include:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51563 — W4A16 FlyDSL migration to the AITER API.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53222 — opt-in AITER fused-MoE token chunking.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53108 — trimming the AITER MoE GEMM input to valid-token prefixes.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50813 — opt-in Kimi-K3 SiTUv2 A8W4 routed MoE.

title: [Refactor] Complete the MOE oracle / linear kernel migration
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**NOTE: automated unfinished PRs will likely not get reviewed. If you are an agent, do not open PRs autonomously before discussing here.**

Some `LinearMethodBase` subclasses and `FusedMoEMethodBase` subclasses have not yet adopted the MOE oracle / linear kernel abstractions.

These `LinearMethodBase`/`FusedMoEMethodBase` classes should generally only handle weight creation and loading.

MOE/linear backend choice and processing is generally to be deferred to the linear kernel / MOE oracle. This allows to have wide compatibility between model-producers and execution backends.

The audit below gives a summary of classes that have not yet adopted:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear

abstractions.

## FusedMoEMethodBase audit

### Bypass the MoE oracle entirely

These are the concrete quant methods that do not use the `fused_moe/oracle/` layer for their MoE execution/setup:

- `CompressedTensorsW4A16FlydslMoEMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w4a16_flydsl.py#L87-L333

It performs its own GPTQ→FlyDSL packing and calls the monolithic `fused_flydsl_moe` directly. No oracle selection, conversion, or modular-kernel construction.

- `HummingMoEMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/humming.py#L595-L810

It has its own parallel flow: `select_humming_moe_experts`, `convert_to_humming_moe_kernel_format`, and `make_humming_moe_kernel`. It does create a modular kernel, but these helpers are outside `fused_moe/oracle/`, so it is a clear oracle-migration candidate.

- `QuarkW4A8Fp8MoEMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py#L976-L1132

This is the ROCm AITER W4A8 path. It requires AITER fused MoE and invokes `rocm_aiter_fused_experts` directly, rather than selecting/converting/building through an oracle.

### Partial oracle users / strongest refactor candidates

These do use some oracle helpers, but still own meaningful backend dispatch or preparation logic rather than following the complete oracle flow.

- `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_mxfp4.py#L46-L220

It calls `select_mxfp4_moe_backend` only for explicitly requested b12x:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_mxfp4.py#L56-L60

Otherwise it manually chooses CUTLASS, XPU, or Marlin:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_mxfp4.py#L61-L70

It also owns CUTLASS scale swizzling and Marlin preparation:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_mxfp4.py#L169-L209

It uses the oracle’s quant-config/kernel builders, but not its selection or conversion abstraction consistently.

- `INCMxfp4MoEMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/schemes/inc_mxfp4_moe.py#L42-L218

This is effectively the same split flow: explicit b12x/XPU selection goes through `select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, while CUTLASS and Marlin are selected directly. It duplicates the same CUTLASS scale swizzle and Marlin preparation pattern. This should likely be handled alongside compressed-tensors W4A4 MXFP4.

- `CompressedTensorsWNA16RDNA3MoEMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16_rdna3.py#L57-L140

It inherits the parent WNA16 method’s oracle setup, but overrides the forward execution with `_rdna3_fused_moe`, a direct provider-specific path. I’d classify it as partial rather than fully non-oracle.

- `QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py#L581-L974

It has an oracle/modular-kernel path, but retains a legacy monolithic `fused_experts` fallback for static-activation INT8. It is not a pure bypass, but it is not fully modular either.

### Methods already on the normal oracle flow

The remaining concrete MoE methods select and construct through their quantization-specific oracle functions. This includes:

- [UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/unquantized_fused_moe_method.py#L41)
- [AutoAWQMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/auto_awq.py#L522)
- [AutoGPTQMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/auto_gptq.py#L467)
- [Fp8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py#L462)
- [GptOssMxfp4MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py#L142)
- [Mxfp4MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py#L474)
- [MoeWNA16Method](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/moe_wna16.py#L204)
- [ModelOptFp8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L460)
- [ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L809)
- [ModelOptMxFp8FusedMoE](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L1185)
- [INCMxfp8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/schemes/inc_mxfp8_moe.py#L32)
- [Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py#L551)
- [Fp8PerBlockOnlineMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py#L608)
- [Fp8PtpcOnlineMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/fp8.py#L706)
- [Int8OnlineMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/int8.py#L33)
- [Mxfp4OnlineMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/mxfp4.py#L140)
- [Mxfp8OnlineMoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/mxfp8.py#L97)

- [CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_nvfp4.py#L47)
- [CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w4a8_fp8.py#L31)

- [CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w8a8_fp8.py#L51)
- [CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w8a8_int8.py#L38)
- [CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_w8a8_mxfp8.py#L34)
- [CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe_wna16.py#L57)
- [QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py#L228)
- [QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py#L1135)
- [QuarkNvfp4MoEMethod](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/quark_moe.py#L1559)

`FusedMoEModularMethod` is technically a `FusedMoEMethodBase` child but should not be counted as a missing-oracle quant method: it is an adapter that receives an already-built `FusedMoEKernel`.

## LinearMethodBase audit

There are 27 descendants of `LinearMethodBase`, again including wrapper/base classes.

### Concrete methods that bypass the stable linear-kernel abstraction

- `UnquantizedLinearMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py#L163-L239

It uses `dispatch_unquantized_gemm`, not a `kernels.linear` kernel object. This may be intentionally separate—the linear kernel package is presently centered on quantized/mixed-precision kernel selection—but it is a literal non-user of the abstraction.

- `FPQuantLinearMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp_quant.py#L96-L225

Its `apply` invokes the dedicated `quantized_forward` custom op directly.

- `HummingLinearMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/humming.py#L355-L592

It manually prepares Humming state and calls `_hm.humming_forward` directly. This is the linear analogue of `HummingMoEMethod`.

- `TorchAOLinearMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/torchao.py#L319-L390

It relies on TorchAO-packed tensor behavior and calls `torch.nn.functional.linear` directly.

- `GLM52LowLatencyLinearMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/glm52_low_latency_gemm.py#L158-L172

This is a model-specific fast path that directly runs a precomputed CuTe/skinny-GEMM plan, falling back to `UnquantizedLinearMethod`.

- `KimiK3LowLatencyLinearMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py#L899-L926

Similar model-specific CuTe plan bypass, with `UnquantizedLinearMethod` fallback.

- `Qwen4ExpLowLatencyLinearMethod`

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py#L193-L203

Directly invokes the custom `qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm` op, then falls back to the unquantized implementation.

The last three do use code located beneath `kernels/linear/cute_dsl` in some cases, but they bypass the common selector/factory exported by `kernels/linear/__init__.py`.

### Delegating wrappers with conditional gaps

`INCLinearMethod`, `QuarkLinearMethod`, `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod`, and `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod` are dispatching wrappers. The concrete schemes below are the relevant migration targets.

### Classes that need a linear-kernel abstraction migration

- `INCXPULinearMethod` directly calls the XPU `int4_gemm_w4a16` op.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/schemes/inc_wna16_linear.py#L344-L361

- `INCXPUW4A8LinearMethod` directly calls the XPU `int4_gemm_w4a8` op, with `INCXPULinearMethod` as its small-batch fallback.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/schemes/inc_w4a8_linear.py#L85-L112

- `INCARKLinearMethod` directly calls the ARK `inc_ark_woq_linear` op.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/schemes/inc_wna16_linear.py#L454-L471

- `QuarkW4A8_MXFP4_FP8` directly calls ROCm AITER `gemm_a8wfp4`, with dequantization + `F.linear` emulation.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a8_mxfp4_fp8.py#L150-L205

- `QutlassNvFP4LinearMethod` uses the selected `NvFp4LinearKernel` only to determine FlashInfer’s backend, then invokes `flashinfer_scaled_fp4_mm` directly rather than `apply_weights`.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/transform/schemes/linear_qutlass_nvfp4.py#L119-L149

### Classes already on the normal linear-kernel flow

- [INCFp8LinearScheme](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/schemes/inc_fp8_linear.py#L14)

- [QuarkNVFP4](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_nvfp4.py#L33)
- [QuarkOCP_MX](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2a4e3cc3dbddf4f44d69864209361f1e2a70c79a/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_ocp_mx.py#L40)

title: [Feature]: Tokenized Prompt as Input for Chat and Messages Endpoints when serving
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

# Feature Request: Tokenized Prompt Input for Chat and Messages Endpoints

## Summary

It would be useful for vLLM HTTP serving endpoints such as `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` to accept prompt token IDs as input and skip repeated tokenization, while still preserving normal handling for tools, reasoning, and multimodal content.

The concrete examples below focus on `/v1/chat/completions`, but the same need also applies to agent-style message APIs.

This is related to the earlier feature request in [vLLM issue #25051](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/25051) (Stale, closed, and maybe outdated).

## Motivation

The main goal is simple: if a frontend already has prompt token IDs, vLLM's HTTP chat/message endpoint should be able to consume those IDs directly and skip tokenization.

For example, an HTTP routing layer such as vLLM Router may tokenize requests before forwarding them to workers so it can reuse repeated prompt prefixes, estimate prefill cost, or make cache-aware scheduling decisions. If `/v1/chat/completions` cannot accept those token IDs, vLLM has to apply the chat template and tokenize again.

Current flow:

```text
Client chat request
  -> HTTP frontend/router
  -> apply chat template + tokenize for cache/scheduling
  -> vLLM HTTP API server
  -> apply chat template + tokenize again
  -> engine
```

Desired flow:

```text
Client chat request
  -> HTTP frontend/router
  -> apply chat template + tokenize once
  -> vLLM HTTP API server accepts prompt token IDs
  -> skip tokenization, preserve chat/tool/multimodal handling
  -> engine
```

For pure completion-style requests, vLLM already supports this pattern. `/v1/completions` can accept token IDs through the `prompt` field:

```json
{
  "model": "model-name",
  "prompt": [151644, 872, 198, 9906],
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```

Offline and lower-level generation paths also support token-ID-style inputs. Internally, tokenized multimodal inputs are represented as token IDs plus separate multimodal payload fields, not as token IDs alone.

For chat-style endpoints, however, users currently cannot cleanly provide the already-tokenized chat prompt through the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API. This blocks tokenization-cache reuse at the HTTP frontend layer and can cause duplicate work:

1. A frontend applies the chat template and tokenizes the prompt for tokenization-cache reuse or scheduling/cache logic.
2. vLLM receives the original chat request and applies the chat template/tokenizes again.

Using `/v1/completions` as a workaround is not equivalent, because chat-completion-specific logic can be missed, especially tool call handling, reasoning parser adjustments, and multimodal processing.

## Requested Behavior

Add a supported tokenized-input path for `/v1/chat/completions`, and ideally a similar shape for `/v1/messages`.

The key requirement is that this should not be interpreted as "token IDs are the whole request." For chat and multimodal workloads, token IDs only represent the text/token sequence. Other request semantics still need to be preserved or passed separately.

A safe design should support:

- pre-tokenized prompt IDs for the final model prompt
- normal chat metadata such as `messages`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, and chat options
- multimodal payload data separately from token IDs
- multimodal processor kwargs / UUIDs where applicable
- normal reasoning/tool parser adjustments
- normal response formatting and usage accounting

For text-only chat, one possible shape is:

```json
{
  "model": "model-name",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}
  ],
  "prompt_token_ids": [151644, 872, 198, 9707, 151645, 198],
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```

For multimodal chat, token IDs alone are not sufficient. The API should either keep the original multimodal `messages` so vLLM can extract/process multimodal data normally, or expose an explicit tokenized prompt object similar to vLLM's internal/offline representation:

```json
{
  "model": "model-name",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/image.png"}}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "prompt_token_ids": [151644, 872, 198, 1234, 5678, 151645, 198],
  "mm_processor_kwargs": {},
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```

Conceptually, this matches the internal idea of:

```python
TokensPrompt(
    prompt_token_ids=[...],
    multi_modal_data={...},
    mm_processor_kwargs={...},
    multi_modal_uuids={...},
)
```

The exact public HTTP shape does not need to be identical to the internal Python type. The important part is that multimodal data and multimodal processor metadata remain separate from `prompt_token_ids`.

## Proposed Semantics

When tokenized prompt input is provided:

- vLLM should use the supplied prompt token IDs as the final text tokenization result.
- vLLM should skip the final tokenizer encode call for the rendered chat prompt.
- vLLM should still validate/process the original chat request enough to preserve tools, reasoning, multimodal data extraction, and response behavior.
- For multimodal requests, vLLM should still build the correct multimodal engine input from the multimodal payload and the supplied token IDs.
- If supplied token IDs do not match the expected multimodal placeholder layout, vLLM should return a clear validation error rather than silently producing inconsistent engine input.

## Why `prompt_token_ids` Alone May Not Be Enough

A single optional `prompt_token_ids` field can be enough for text-only chat if the original `messages` and tool fields are still present and vLLM continues to run the normal chat-processing path.

It is not enough as a standalone replacement for the whole chat request. Token IDs do not carry:

- image/audio/video payloads
- multimodal UUID/cache metadata
- multimodal processor kwargs
- tool schemas and tool-choice semantics
- message roles and response-format context
- reasoning/tool parser context

So the feature should be documented as "pre-tokenized prompt plus normal chat/multimodal metadata," not "send only token IDs."

## Possible Implementation Direction

One possible approach for `/v1/chat/completions`:

```python
class ChatCompletionRequest(OpenAIBaseModel):
    messages: list[ChatCompletionMessageParam]
    model: str | None = None

    # vLLM extension for the final rendered prompt token IDs.
    prompt_token_ids: list[int] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Pre-tokenized final chat prompt IDs. When provided, vLLM uses "
            "these IDs as the prompt tokenization result while preserving "
            "normal chat processing for tools, reasoning, and multimodal data."
        ),
    )
```

And in the render path:

```python
if request.prompt_token_ids is not None:
    if len(request.prompt_token_ids) == 0:
        return error("prompt_token_ids must not be empty")

    # Still run normal chat rendering/validation enough to preserve semantics
    # not represented by token IDs: tool-call state, multimodal payload
    # extraction, optional prompt text, etc.
    conversation, prompt = await renderer.render_messages_async(
        request.messages,
        chat_params,
    )

    # Replace only the text tokenization result.
    prompt = dict(prompt)
    prompt["prompt_token_ids"] = list(request.prompt_token_ids)
    prompt.pop("prompt", None)

    # Continue normal tool/reasoning adjustment and multimodal processing.
    tok_prompt = await renderer.tokenize_prompt_async(prompt, tok_params)
    engine_input = await renderer.process_for_engine_async(tok_prompt, ...)
    return conversation, [engine_input]
```

This is only a code sketch. The exact implementation should be checked carefully against vLLM's current chat render path, multimodal processor, and tool parser internals.

## Correctness Requirements

The feature should be considered correct only if these cases continue to work:

- text-only chat request with supplied prompt token IDs
- chat request with tools/tool choice
- chat request with reasoning parser behavior
- multimodal chat request where image/audio/video data is still processed correctly
- validation failure when token IDs are inconsistent with required multimodal placeholders
- streaming and non-streaming responses
- usage accounting based on supplied prompt token IDs

## Expected Benefit

This would expose a clean HTTP-level path for advanced serving systems that already compute token IDs before sending requests to vLLM. It would avoid duplicate chat-template/tokenization work while preserving the correctness of chat, tools, reasoning, and multimodal behavior.

It would also make chat/message-style HTTP endpoints more consistent with existing token-ID support in `/v1/completions` and offline/lower-level generation APIs.



### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

title: [Feature]: Switch Python Harmony dependency to oss-harmony
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Summary
vLLM’s **Rust** path already uses [`oss-harmony`](https://github.com/oss-harmony/harmony) `v0.0.11` (`rust/Cargo.toml`, #46799). Python still depends on PyPI [`openai-harmony`](https://pypi.org/project/openai-harmony/), which is stuck at **0.0.8**.
Please switch the Python dependency to **`oss-harmony >= 0.0.11`** (same import name: `openai_harmony`) so serving, parsers, and tests share one Harmony implementation and air-gapped GPT-OSS no longer has to download tiktoken vocabs at runtime.
This is **not** a duplicate of #46799 (Rust only) or of docs-only work around `TIKTOKEN_*` (#22525). There is no open PR that migrates the **Python** package.
## Why `oss-harmony` instead of `openai-harmony`
1. **Air-gapped / offline load works.** Official `openai-harmony==0.0.8` downloads the tiktoken vocab at `load_harmony_encoding(...)`. With no network that fails as `HarmonyError: error downloading or loading vocab file`. `oss-harmony==0.0.11` **embeds** the vocabs (`include_bytes!` + zstd). GPT-OSS Harmony encoding loads with **no** `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` / cache env vars.
2. **Unblocks [openai/harmony#101](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/101).** That issue (vendor vocabs for offline use) is still **open**; upstream has not shipped a PyPI release past 0.0.8. oss-harmony already shipped the fix.
3. **Same public Python API.** Drop-in `openai_harmony` module: `load_harmony_encoding`, `Message`, `Conversation`, `SystemContent`, `StreamableParser`, `ToolNamespaceConfig`, `render_*`, `parse_messages_from_completion_tokens`, stop tokens, `is_special_token`, etc. vLLM call sites do not need a rewrite just to swap the wheel.
4. **Align Python with Rust.** One Harmony version and one render/parse behavior across the engine, instead of Python 0.0.8 vs Rust 0.0.11 (#46800 already noted that split).
5. **Parser coverage for both header layouts.** 0.0.11 parses **recipient-first** (0.0.8 / training-style) **and** **channel-first** commentary tool calls, including `<|constrain|>` adjacent to `to=...`.
6. **Correct `<|constrain|>` tokenization on render.** If `content_type` is set (vLLM does this for JSON/code tool probes), 0.0.8 emits a **literal** ` json` / ` code` string. 0.0.11 emits the **`<|constrain|>` special token**, which matches how the format is defined.
7. **No extra runtime HTTP for Harmony itself.** Removes a surprising network dependency from first GPT-OSS request / encoding load (CI, air-gap, HPC, locked-down clusters).
8. **Maintained fork used in production-shaped stacks.** oss-harmony is what vLLM Rust already pinned; Python should not be the outlier.
### Known render delta (accepted)
Commentary-channel messages (function tools, not python/browser on `analysis`) render **channel-first** in 0.0.11:
```text
# openai-harmony 0.0.8
<|start|>assistant to=functions.get_weather<|channel|>commentary<|message|>...
# oss-harmony 0.0.11
<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather<|message|>...
```
Python/browser **analysis** headers are **unchanged**. System/developer/user renders were **byte-identical** in a 0.0.8 vs 0.0.11 comparison. Parsing of both layouts still yields the same `recipient` / `channel` for routing.
## `gpt-oss` package
[`gpt-oss`](https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss) is **not** a default vLLM install dep. It is a **test extra** (`requirements/test/*.in`) and is only needed for:
- `--tool-server demo` wrappers (`SimpleBrowserTool`, `PythonTool`)
- `python -m gpt_oss.evals` (e.g. GPQA)
Serving GPT-OSS **models** only needs Harmony (`openai_harmony`), not the `gpt-oss` dist.
**Packaging catch:** PyPI `gpt-oss` still `Requires-Dist: openai-harmony`. Both wheels export `openai_harmony`, so installing **both** overwrites the module. vLLM should:
- Depend on `oss-harmony >= 0.0.11`
- **Exclude** `openai-harmony` when resolving test extras (`uv` `exclude-dependencies` / `uv pip compile --excludes`)
`uv pip check` may still warn that `gpt-oss` wanted `openai-harmony`. That is **metadata only**; imports work because `oss-harmony` provides `openai_harmony`.
### `gpt-oss` functional check (clone `openai/gpt-oss` 0.0.9)
Installed the clone with **only** `oss-harmony==0.0.11` (no `openai-harmony`):
- Harmony-using modules import: Responses API, `PythonTool`, `SimpleBrowserTool`, ollama inference helper
- **`pytest tests/` → 22 passed** (skipped live browser backend)
- Compared 0.0.8 vs 0.0.11 on the exact message shapes gpt-oss builds:
  - **No API removed.** Routing on `recipient` (`python`, `browser.*`, `functions.*`) still works
  - System / developer / user / **analysis** python+browser renders **identical**
  - Model-style completion tokens in **both** header orders parse to the same route
  - Only **commentary** function-call / function-output **re-render** changes (Responses API multi-turn, `chat.py --raw`)
Not run (need Docker / network / weights, not missing Harmony APIs): live `PythonTool.process`, Exa/You.com browser, GPU `chat.py`.
## How this was tested (vLLM Harmony swap)
Isolated **`openai-harmony==0.0.8`** vs **`oss-harmony==0.0.11`** (0.0.8 vocab loaded via `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` so official package could run at all).
**vLLM unit tests** (same files, both packages):
- `tests/parser/test_harmony.py`
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/parser/test_harmony_utils.py`
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/parser/test_harmony_render_parity.py`
- `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony_utils.py`
**258 passed** on both 0.0.8 and 0.0.11. GPU e2e `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_harmony.py` was **not** run.
**Additional probes:**
- Offline `load_harmony_encoding(HarmonyEncodingName.HARMONY_GPT_OSS)` on 0.0.11 with **no** tiktoken env
- Render/parse of commentary vs analysis tool calls; gpt-oss-style messages without `content_type` (gpt-oss never sets it; vLLM does for some probes)
- `gpt-oss==0.0.8` + `oss-harmony==0.0.11` with `--excludes openai-harmony`: `gpt_oss`, demo tools, `gpt_oss.evals`, encoding load all **OK**; `uv pip check` fails on declared dep only
## Proposed Python change (sketch)
- `requirements/common.txt`: `oss-harmony >= 0.0.11` (replace `openai-harmony >= 0.0.3`)
- Test lockfiles: pin `oss-harmony==0.0.11`, do not pin `openai-harmony`
- When compiling/installing test reqs that pull `gpt-oss`, exclude `openai-harmony` so the official wheel cannot shadow `openai_harmony`
- Optional: `[tool.uv] exclude-dependencies = ["openai-harmony"]` (single `[tool.uv]` table)
Happy to follow up with a PR if this direction is OK.
## References
- oss-harmony: https://github.com/oss-harmony/harmony (`v0.0.11`)
- openai/harmony#101 (vocab download / air-gap)
- vLLM #46799 (Rust → oss-harmony)
- vLLM #22525 (`TIKTOKEN_*` workaround docs)
- vLLM #23567 (discussion of forking / inlining Harmony)
- gpt-oss: https://github.com/openai/gpt-oss (declares `openai-harmony`; runtime uses `openai_harmony`)

### Alternatives

**1. Wait for official `openai-harmony` (tried; stalled)**
I filed [openai/harmony#101](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/101) (2026-03-10) asking upstream to make Harmony offline-first: bundle the `.tiktoken` vocabs in the package, ship the same files in GPT-OSS model repos, and add a deterministic lookup order (explicit path → env → model dir → package resources → optional download). That is the real fix for air-gapped GPT-OSS (`HarmonyError: error downloading or loading vocab file`).
There was **no OpenAI review or implementation**. I pinged `@scott-oai` on 2026-03-23; still no response. PyPI `openai-harmony` remains at **0.0.8**. Related offline issues ([#46](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/46), [#95](https://github.com/openai/harmony/issues/95)) are likewise still open. Treating `openai-harmony` as a supported dependency for vLLM is not realistic on the evidence: no release that embeds vocabs, no engagement on the air-gap design, and vLLM already had to document a `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` workaround (#22525).
**2. Keep `openai-harmony` and tell operators to vendor vocabs**
This is the current path. It works only if someone copies `o200k_base.tiktoken` / `cl100k_base.tiktoken` into the image and sets env vars. It is easy to miss until runtime, duplicates packaging in every air-gapped deploy, and leaves Python on 0.0.8 while Rust is already on oss-harmony 0.0.11.
**3. Vendor / inline Harmony inside vLLM**
Discussed in #23567. Higher maintenance than depending on the existing drop-in fork.
**4. Switch Python to `oss-harmony` (preferred)**
@bbrowning replied on #101 that the fork would **embed the vocabs with zstd** ([oss-harmony/harmony#7](https://github.com/oss-harmony/harmony/pull/7)). That shipped in `oss-harmony` 0.0.11 — the same crate vLLM Rust already pins (#46799). Same `openai_harmony` import; no `TIKTOKEN_*` required. This alternative is what actually landed, because upstream `openai-harmony` is not being maintained for this use case.

body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

While reviewing https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54238#pullrequestreview-5062756046, it was pointed out that the implementation follows the traditional per-parser approach:

> We recently introduced a new unified approach in #45802. However, that approach relies on Parser Engine, and MuseGlimmerReasoningParser hasn't been migrated to Parser Engine yet. I think it would make more sense to first refactor MuseGlimmerReasoningParser to use Parser Engine. Once that's done, support for counting reasoning tokens should come naturally.

This issue tracks migrating the MuseGlimmer parsers to the Streaming Parser Engine, following the same pattern as the Qwen3 and Inkling parsers (a single `ParserEngine` subclass with a declarative config, exposed through `make_adapters`).

The migration consists of two portings:

1. **Port `MuseGlimmerReasoningParser`** (`vllm/reasoning/muse_glimmer_reasoning_parser.py`)
   Express the channel grammar (`to=self` reasoning / `to=user` content) as engine terminals and transitions, replacing the regex-based text classification. Reasoning token counting then comes for free via the engine (#45802).

2. **Port `MuseGlimmerToolParser`** (`vllm/tool_parsers/muse_glimmer_tool_parser.py`)
   Express the ATEM tool-call format (`<atem:function_calls>` / `<atem:invoke>`) as engine tool states, replacing the regex-based message segmentation, while keeping the existing channel-scoping guarantees (ATEM echoed inside reasoning or user channels must not parse as tool calls).

I'd like to work on this.

title: [Feature]: Add explicit cache IDs for reusable multimodal and inference state
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

There are already several caching mechanisms in vLLM, including multimodal processing/encoder caching and prefix caching.

It would be useful to expose an explicit, application-level cache_id (or similar handle) for reusable cached state.

The idea is simple: an application sends a large context or image once, vLLM performs the expensive processing and returns a cache_id. Subsequent requests could reference that ID instead of sending and processing the same data again.

For example:

large document / image
        ↓
   process once
        ↓
    cache_id
        ↓
question 1
question 2
question 3
...

The handle would be implementation-independent: it could refer to multimodal/vision state, prefix/KV state, or other expensive intermediate state.

This would be particularly useful for workloads where the same document or image is queried many times, such as RAG, document analysis, multimodal agents, and batch processing.

The main goal is to let applications explicitly retain and reuse expensive computation, rather than relying only on automatic cache matching.

### Alternatives

The existing automatic prefix caching and multimodal UUID mechanisms are useful, but they still require the application to work with the specific caching mechanism.

An explicit cache_id would provide a simple, unified application-level handle while allowing vLLM to decide internally what representation is stored and how it is managed.

title: [Feature]: MORE VELOCITY TO INFERENCE
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Hello,

My name is José Antonio, and my email is [mail.snaj@gmail.com](mailto:mail.snaj@gmail.com).

I wanted to tell you this idea because I honestly don't know who else to tell.

I came up with something that I think could potentially accelerate the inference of medium-sized AI models dramatically using RAM alone.

Please, I'm not joking, and I don't think this is a silly idea. Give me two minutes and let me explain.

Imagine having a 27B model such as Qwen 3.8 27B that takes around 30 GB of storage.

For users who don't have two 16 GB GPUs or a 32 GB GPU, but who do have 128 GB of RAM — or even 64 GB or more — I was thinking about the following:

What if we loaded the same model into RAM two or four times?

In other words, we would replicate the model weights multiple times in RAM when extra memory is available, and distribute those copies across the memory channels of the system.

For example, a system with 64 GB of RAM might have two memory channels, while a 128 GB system could have four channels.

Then, the CPU's multithreaded cores could access specific layers that are read very frequently — for example, particular experts in a Mixture-of-Experts model or other frequently accessed layers — in parallel.

This would not simply be traditional memory interleaving.

The idea would be to create parallelism at the information level by duplicating the most frequently needed parts of the model in RAM, so that multiple memory channels could serve those reads simultaneously.

For example, with 128 GB of RAM, you could potentially have four copies of a ~30 GB model in memory and use different CPU threads to access the important layers in parallel.

The idea is that, because the model is replicated across the RAM channels, the system could potentially read the most important parts of the model much faster.

For example, in a server with 8 DIMM slots, you might have four memory channels with two DIMMs per channel.

I think this could potentially multiply inference performance significantly for medium-sized models running primarily from RAM.

Obviously, it would only make sense for medium-sized models and systems with a large amount of RAM. But if it worked, you could potentially get much higher inference performance without needing expensive GPUs.

I'm not claiming that this definitely works — I'm asking you to take a look at the concept and see whether there is something technically interesting here.

If you find any value in this idea or information, please send me an email at [mail.snaj@gmail.com](mailto:mail.snaj@gmail.com).

Thank you for your time.

José Antonio

title: [Feature]: KV cache group splitting assumes n:1 pattern between attention types
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### Location
`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1225-1231` (FIXME comment)

### Problem
The KV cache group splitting logic in `create_kv_cache_group_specs()` assumes that all open-source hybrid models follow an **n:1 pattern** between different attention types (e.g., Gemma3 5:1 between sliding window and full attention, LLaMA4 3:1 between local and full). 

The code uses `min_num_layers` as the group size:
```python
min_num_layers = min([len(layers) for layers in layer_buckets])
group_size = min_num_layers
```

This works for n:1 patterns but fails for more complex ratios like **20 full + 30 sliding window** (where optimal group size would be 10, not 20).

### Impact
- **Memory waste**: For complex patterns, excessive padding layers are added
- **Suboptimal KV cache utilization**: Padding layers consume memory without providing value
- **Pipeline parallelism complications**: As noted in the comment, PP requires specific layer distribution

### Current heuristic
```python
if max_num_layers < min_num_layers * 1.5:
    group_size = max_num_layers  # avoids too much padding
```
This 1.5x heuristic handles cases like gpt-oss-20b + eagle (12 sw + 13 full) but isn't general.

### Expected behavior
Support arbitrary ratios between attention types by computing the **greatest common divisor (GCD)** of layer counts across attention types, or allowing configurable group sizing strategies.

### Models affected
- Current: Gemma3, LLaMA4, Nemotron-H (work with n:1 pattern)
- Future: Any hybrid model with non-n:1 attention type ratios

### Related code
- `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`: `create_kv_cache_group_specs()` function
- `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`: KV cache spec definitions
- Model implementations in `vllm/model_executor/models/` that use hybrid attention

title: [Feature]: Entropy-Gated Dynamic Speculative Decoding (Dynamic k in {0, K}) via Real-Time Shannon Hysteresis
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

### Summary

Standard speculative decoding in vLLM operates with a static draft length ($k = \text{constant}$). However, during high-entropy generation steps (e.g., complex reasoning forks, multi-lingual syntax, or high-perplexity code tokens), the token acceptance rate $\beta \to 0$. This leads to frequent draft rejection rollbacks, net throughput degradation ($S < 1$), and wasted compute FLOPs/energy.

We propose an **Entropy-Gated Stochastic Speculative Controller** that evaluates output distribution Shannon entropy $H(t)$ in real-time and dynamically modulates the draft window:
- **$k = K$ (e.g., 5)** during low-entropy deterministic spans (~100% draft acceptance).
- **$k = 0$ (single-step fallback)** during high-entropy cognitive search forks, completely eliminating wasted draft passes.

To prevent rapid mode-thrashing (gear hunting) on borderline tokens, the controller uses an industrial **Schmitt-trigger hysteresis loop** with EMA smoothing ($\alpha = 0.35$).

---

### Mathematical Formulation

1. **Numerically Stable Float32 Shannon Entropy:**
   $$\log p_i = \text{LogSoftmax}(z_i) = z_i - \log \sum_{j \in \mathcal{V}} e^{z_j}$$
   $$H(X) = - \frac{1}{\ln 2} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{V}} e^{\log p_i} \cdot \log p_i$$

2. **Hysteresis State Transitions:**

$$
\bar{H}_t = \alpha \cdot H(p_t) + (1 - \alpha) \cdot \bar{H}_{t-1}
$$

$$
k_t = \begin{cases} 
0, & \text{if } S_{t-1} = \text{Active} \land \bar{H}_t > \theta_{\text{high}} \\
K, & \text{if } S_{t-1} = \text{Fallback} \land \bar{H}_t < \theta_{\text{low}} \\
k_{t-1}, & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$

*(Default baseline thresholds: θ_low = 0.55 bits, θ_high = 1.25 bits).*

---

### Empirical Validation on NVIDIA RTX 5090 (Blackwell)

We benchmarked this control mechanism on Llama-3.1-8B under 100 Hz NVML hardware power polling:
- **Electrical Energy per Token:** Reduced by **46.7%** ($6.40\text{ J} \to 3.41\text{ J/token}$).
- **Throughput:** Maintained **50.52 tok/s** on complex poetic generation (409 generation steps).
- **Draft Rejection Waste:** The clutch successfully locked at $k=5$ for 150+ continuous steps during deterministic couplets ($H \approx 0.0001$), and instantly disengaged to $k=0$ during high-entropy rhyme turns ($H = 2.98$).

The open-source reference implementation, standalone server, and IEEE paper are archived here:
- **Paper & Telemetry Data Room (Zenodo DOI):** [10.5281/zenodo.22129912](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22129912)
- **Repository (Apache-2.0):** [Creepybits/software-defined-stochastic-inference-engine](https://github.com/Creepybits/software-defined-stochastic-inference-engine)
- **Interactive Telemetry Explorer:** [sdsie.github.io](https://sdsie.github.io/)

---

### Proposed Integration with vLLM

We would like to collaborate with the vLLM maintainers on upstreaming this into vLLM's v0.28+ speculative decoding pipeline:

1. **Model Runner V2 / SpecDecode Scheduling:** Hooking the entropy calculator into the verification step to toggle between pre-captured CUDA graphs for $k=0$ (single step) and $k=K$ (multi-step drafting).
2. **Fused Sampling Kernel:** Fusing the Shannon entropy calculation directly into `vllm._C.ops` / sampling Triton kernels to prevent CPU-GPU host synchronization overhead.

Looking forward to feedback from the community and maintainers on the cleanest architectural hook point in vLLM v0.28+!

title: [Feature]: Per-request and per-session KV cache tier attribution in OpenTelemetry traces
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

When running hierarchical KV cache tiering (GPU -> CPU -> filesystem via `TieringOffloadingSpec`), operators have no way to trace a single request or session and see which tier served its cached blocks or how long promotion took.

The existing `llm_request` OTel span only includes latency and token count attributes. Aggregate per-tier Prometheus metrics exist (`block_hits`, `block_queries`, `read_time` by tier label), but they cannot answer: "Did this specific slow request hit the filesystem tier, and how long did promotion take?" or "How are tier hits distributed across requests in this agentic session?"

**Proposal:** Add per-request KV cache tier attribution as span attributes on the existing `llm_request` OTel span. When tiering is enabled and tracing is active, the span would include attributes such as:

- `kv_cache.request_id` :  the request ID
- `kv_cache.session_id` :  the session ID, if set (already available on requests via #48048)
- `kv_cache.tier_hit`  : which tier(s) served cached blocks (e.g., `cpu`, `fs`, `none`)
- `kv_cache.blocks_hit` :  number of blocks served from cache, by tier
- `kv_cache.blocks_missed` : number of blocks that required recomputation
- `kv_cache.promotion_latency_seconds` : total promotion time from secondary tier to primary, if applicable

Including `session_id` enables operators to filter traces by session, making this useful for agentic workloads where multiple requests share KV cache state within a conversation. This aligns with the session-centric KV cache orchestration direction proposed in RFC #48501.

`TieringMetricsTracker` already tracks per-request lookup state internally (`_request_states` dict keyed by `req_id`), including which tier each block resolved at. However, this data is aggregated into counters and the per-request identity is lost at stats collection time. The implementation would extend this existing state to surface a per-request summary through the stats pipeline into the OTel span.


### Alternatives

- **Structured logging**: Emit a structured log line per request with tier info. Simpler but not queryable in Grafana/Tempo dashboards, so less useful for operators diagnosing production issues.
- **Per-request/session Prometheus labels**: Add `req_id` or `session_id` as labels to existing metrics. Not viable due to Prometheus cardinality explosion — both can have thousands of unique values in a busy system.


### Additional context

- The offloading/tiering subsystem (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/`) currently has zero OTel tracing instrumentation. This would be the first tracing in that subsystem.
- The scheduler already carries `trace_headers` through to `SchedulerOutput` and `EngineCoreOutput`, but no spans or attributes are added in the scheduler or below.
- `session_id` is already available on the `Request` object (#48048, merged) but does not flow into `ReqContext` (the offloading layer). It does not need to as  tier attribution data flows up keyed by `req_id`, and `session_id` can be resolved at the span-creation point in `output_processor.py` where the `Request` is accessible.

title: [Feature]: Support auxiliary-GPU offloading for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next N-gram / PLE embeddings
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Motivation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next introduces a very large N-gram / PLE embedding table.

This part of the model is particularly suitable for offloading because it is fundamentally a lookup workload rather than a large GEMM-heavy compute workload.

A useful deployment topology would be:

```text
Primary GPU
- Main model
- Attention / GDN
- MoE computation
- KV cache
- CUDA graphs

Auxiliary GPU
- N-gram / PLE embedding table
- N-gram lookup / gather
```

For example:

```text
GPU 0: RTX PRO 6000 96GB
       -> main NVFP4/FP8 model

GPU 1: 64GB accelerator
       -> ~51GB FP8 N-gram / PLE table
```

This is especially useful in heterogeneous systems where the second GPU is not suitable for Tensor Parallelism because it has:

* significantly lower compute performance;
* a different GPU architecture;
* limited peer-to-peer bandwidth;
* or no high-speed NVLink connection.

Such a GPU can still be very useful as a high-bandwidth embedding store.

## Why this should be different from Tensor Parallelism

The goal is **not** to include the auxiliary GPU in TP or EP.

The primary model should remain entirely on GPU 0.

Only the N-gram / PLE embedding table should reside on the auxiliary device.

Conceptually:

```text
token IDs
   |
   +----------------------------+
   |                            |
   |                     auxiliary GPU
   |                    n-gram ID / hash
   |                           |
Primary GPU               PLE lookup
Layer 0                       |
Layer 1                       |
   |                          |
   +-------- P2P copy <-------+
              |
           Layer 2+
```

Only the selected embedding vectors need to be transferred to the primary GPU.

The full PLE table never needs to move between GPUs during inference.

Therefore, decode-time communication volume should be very small compared with TP/EP communication.

## Proposed interface

Something along the lines of:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --ple-offload-device cuda:1
```

or:

```bash
--ngram-embedding-device cuda:1
```

More generally, it could be exposed as model-specific device placement:

```bash
--model-device-map '{
  "default": "cuda:0",
  "ple": "cuda:1"
}'
```

The exact API is not important; the important requirement is that the auxiliary GPU is **not treated as a TP rank**.

## Suggested implementation

Ideally:

1. Load the PLE / N-gram embedding weights directly onto the selected auxiliary GPU.

2. Compute N-gram indices on the auxiliary GPU or transfer only the small index tensor to it.

3. Perform embedding gather on the auxiliary GPU.

4. Asynchronously transfer the gathered embedding vectors back to the main GPU using CUDA P2P.

5. Use a separate CUDA stream and overlap this operation with early layers of the main model.

For example:

```text
Primary GPU:

embedding -> layer 0 -> layer 1 ------------> layer 2 / PLE fusion
██████████████████████████████████████████████████████████

Aux GPU:

ngram ids -> lookup -> gather -> P2P
██████████████████████████████
```

If the PLE result is ready before the layer that consumes it, the decode overhead could potentially be almost completely hidden.

## P2P fallback

It would also be useful to support systems where CUDA P2P is unavailable:

```text
Aux GPU
  ↓
Pinned host buffer
  ↓
Primary GPU
```

This would obviously be slower, but would still allow the auxiliary GPU to serve as an embedding-memory device.

## Prefill

Long-context prefill transfers much more embedding data than decode, so ideally the implementation could support:

* chunked PLE lookup;
* asynchronous gather;
* double buffering;
* overlap between PLE lookup/copy and main-model prefill.

For example:

```text
Aux GPU:
PLE chunk 1
        PLE chunk 2
                PLE chunk 3

Primary GPU:
        process chunk 1
                process chunk 2
                        process chunk 3
```

## Why this is useful beyond one specific GPU combination

This feature would allow users to reuse otherwise underutilized GPUs as high-bandwidth model-memory devices.

Example configurations include:

```text
Blackwell main GPU + Ampere auxiliary GPU
Hopper main GPU    + older datacenter GPU
96GB main GPU      + 48/64GB secondary GPU
fast GPU           + slower high-memory GPU
```

Unlike TP, heterogeneous compute performance is much less problematic because the auxiliary device only performs embedding lookup.

This could substantially expand the number of systems capable of serving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next without CPU PLE offload.

## Possible future extension: quantized PLE

It may also be useful to eventually support quantized PLE storage independently of the main model quantization, for example:

```text
FP8 PLE
INT8 PLE
INT4 / row-wise quantized PLE
```

Embedding lookup does not necessarily need to use the same quantization scheme as MoE GEMMs.

An auxiliary GPU could perform:

```text
INT4 PLE lookup
      ↓
dequantize selected rows
      ↓
BF16 / FP8 vectors
      ↓
P2P to primary GPU
```

However, GPU device placement alone would already be very useful and could be implemented independently of PLE quantization.

## Expected behavior

Ideally a user could run:

```text
Main model + KV + compute : cuda:0
N-gram / PLE table        : cuda:1
TP size                    : 1
```

without vLLM attempting to distribute transformer layers or MoE experts across both GPUs.

I think this architecture is particularly well suited to Qwen3.8-Flash-Next because the very large PLE table represents a large amount of model capacity but relatively little inter-device communication during autoregressive decoding.

Would the maintainers be interested in supporting this type of model-component-specific auxiliary GPU placement?

title: [Feature]: Rust frontend: /v1/embeddings endpoint
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Right now, with VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1, hitting /v1/embeddings just returns a 404 Not Found. For example, a simple curl like this:
```
curl -X POST http://10.251.209.5:8200/v1/embeddings -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B","input":"hello"}'
```
gets back a `404` with an empty body. So the endpoint simply isn't there – you can't use embeddings at all with the Rust frontend enabled, and you're forced to fall back to the Python version. That's the pain point this PR fixes.

#### Feature
We're adding `/v1/embeddings` support to the Rust frontend. It handles text and token inputs, batched requests, float/base64 encoding, the dimensions param, LoRA adapters, and usage reporting – fully OpenAI-compatible.

#### Motivation
Right now the Rust frontend doesn't support embeddings, but a lot of common use cases (RAG, semantic search, classification) need it. If you enable the Rust frontend with VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1, you can't use embeddings and have to switch back to the Python frontend – which is a pain. Adding this endpoint makes the Rust frontend actually usable for embedding workloads.

#### Pitch
This is explicitly listed in the Rust frontend feature parity roadmap (#44280) under "Pooling / embedding APIs". We already have PR #53736 ready. Once merged, we're one step closer to making the Rust frontend the default option.

title: [Feature]: Support Pipeline Parallelism (PP > 1) in NixlConnector for Disaggregated KV Cache Transfer
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

#### Feature Description:
I propose supporting Pipeline Parallelism (PP > 1) in NixlConnector (under vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/) to enable disaggregated KV cache transfer when models are deployed with pipeline stage partitioning.

#### Motivation & Problem:
Currently, when attempting to run disaggregated prefill/decode setups with pipeline_parallel_size > 1 using NIXL as the KV connector, the initialization or handshake process fails during runtime with the following exception:

```text
ValueError: NixlConnector received pp_rank > 0 handshake metadata but does not support PP-disaggregated KV transfer.
```

In large-scale serving scenarios (e.g., deploying large MoE or deep architectures where single-node GPU memory/bandwidth is constrained), Tensor Parallelism (TP) alone is often insufficient, making Pipeline Parallelism (PP) or hybrid TP+PP mandatory. Without PP support in NixlConnector, users cannot leverage high-performance NIXL-based disaggregated prefill/decode transfers for PP-partitioned workloads.

#### Proposed Pitch:
Extend NixlConnector and its metadata exchange logic (set_xfer_handshake_metadata_pp_aware) to properly map and transfer layer-wise KV blocks across corresponding PP ranks between Prefill and Decode instances.

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the GPU tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU).

Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request.

GLM-5.x models using DSV3.2-style sparse MLA should be compatible through FlashInfer's SM100 TRT-LLM sparse-MLA kernel. vLLM currently derives the sparse token-to-request mapping from CPU query boundaries, and the target capability check also includes draft attention that is captured by a separate graph manager. title: [Feature]: Support per-request dynamic LoRA scale
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Currently `LoRARequest.lora_scale` is fixed at request creation and baked into the CUDA graph / kernel as a scalar. This prevents:
- same-adapter requests in one batch from using different strengths;
- adjusting LoRA strength mid-generation.

A real ASR service works around this by baking scale into separate adapter copies (one slot per scale). This wastes slots and limits scale to discrete presets.

**Proposal:** Add `LoRAScaleState` — a per-request `UvaBackedTensor` (`[max_num_reqs]`) following `SamplingStates`, passed to the LoRA kernel along with `token_to_req`. Effective scale = `base_scale * request_lora_scales[token_to_req[token_idx]]`. No per-token memory, CUDA-graph-compatible.

**Evaluation (real adapter + WER A/B):**

| Condition | CN mean \|B-A\| | EN mean \|B-A\| |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off (noise floor) | 0.022% | — |
| 1.0 pre-fix | 17.184% | — |
| 1.0 post-fix | 0.038% | 0.028% |

- 4 adapter slots → 1 slot.
- Arbitrary continuous scale values.
- Two bugs found & fixed: CUDA graph captured the scale-free kernel variant (`tl.constexpr`), and the all-ones buffer wasn't refreshed.

### Alternatives

- **Baking scale into separate adapter copies** (current workaround) — consumes one adapter slot per scale, limited to discrete presets such as `LORA_SCALES=0.5,0.7,0.9,1.0`.
- **Storing a per-token scale array** — would require more GPU memory (e.g. 128 KB per batch vs 1 KB per request) and does not follow vLLM V1 persistent-batch style.

### Additional context

- Full per-test-set breakdowns and logs are available on request.
- Happy to open a PR if this direction is reasonable.

title: [Feature]: Low-overhead asynchronous early-exit checks & KV-cache reclamation for Continuous Batching
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Problem Statement
In high-throughput production environments running long-context agent loops or strict JSON-enforcement pipelines, models frequently burn a significant portion of generation cycles on post-plateau tail-tokens (e.g., polite wrappers, redundant formatting) after the core semantic task is complete.

While stop_strings and custom LogitsProcessor hooks exist, evaluating them per-step in Python introduces severe bottlenecks:

CPU-GPU Sync & GIL Contenter: Per-step synchronous callbacks disrupt the execution loop, create heavy interpreter friction, and degrade throughput at scale (batch size > 64). Even in Python-heavy orchestration stacks, this creates unacceptable micro-lags.

KV-Cache Bloat & Fragmentation: Finished or logically complete sequences linger in the active batch until the explicit stop token hits or max tokens are reached, occupying precious blocks in PagedAttention and artificially inflating latency for concurrent requests.

An Economic Perspective
In high-volume enterprise deployments (e.g., fintech, customer ops, logistics), long-context generation loops routinely burn 20–30% of output tokens on post-plateau tail generation. For enterprise clients processing tens of millions of requests monthly, this translates to hundreds of thousands of dollars in wasted infrastructure costs annually, plus artificial latency inflation due to occupied KV-cache slots.

Has anyone in the community tackled token overconsumption and mid-batch memory reclamation from a production-economy standpoint? How are large-scale deployments justifying or mitigating these dead compute cycles today?

Proposed Solution
Introduce a lightweight, optimized mechanism at the scheduler level to handle dynamic early-exit flags and asynchronous KV-cache recycling without heavy interpreter roundtrips:

Allow registering low-overhead termination predicates directly within the vLLM scheduler loop.

Provide efficient memory reclamation hooks to instantly free PagedAttention blocks for completed sequences mid-batch, avoiding dead compute cycles.

Questions for Maintainers & Community
Are there existing internal plans or hooks to handle asynchronous early-termination predicates inside the vLLM engine core without hitting Python GIL limits?

What is the current accepted benchmark for evaluating per-step scheduling overhead in vLLM? We are currently profiling custom asynchronous volatile-flag checks and would like to share benchmarks if there is interest in contributing a PR.

### Alternatives

_No response_

title: [Feature]: Add torch.compile support for SiglipEmbeddingModel
body:
## 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Please add vLLM `torch.compile` support for the standalone `SiglipEmbeddingModel`. As of main commit [`8878ebd8`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8878ebd8fdfe286eb7cf00ccbb6919bc7a40b1dd) [Aug 17th], the class has no `@support_torch_compile` decorator. vLLM 0.24.0 consequently emitted its explicit "`torch.compile` is turned on, but the model ... does not support it" warning. This is a compile-support request, not a regression in supported eager serving.

The main compile blocker we found is [`_flip_sequences_by_position_ids()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/8878ebd8fdfe286eb7cf00ccbb6919bc7a40b1dd/vllm/model_executor/models/siglip.py#L985-L1028). The released implementation introduced by [#28365](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/28365) creates a compact boundary tensor with one-argument `torch.where`, then uses its value-dependent length in `repeat_interleave`. On a backend requiring static fullgraph compilation, vLLM 0.24.0 produced an unbacked `sym_sum` (`u0 + 1`) and failed during startup:

```text
torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='neuron' raised:
RuntimeError: Unimplemented call_function: target=<function sym_sum ...>
  File "vllm/model_executor/models/siglip.py", line 1108
    len(lengths), device=features.device
from_node: sym_sum
val: u0 + 1
```

We validated a fixed-shape replacement that avoids compact tensors and keeps every intermediate dimension tied to the input token count:

```python
def _flip_sequences_by_position_ids(
    self,
    features: torch.Tensor,
    position_ids: torch.Tensor,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    if len(features) == 1:
        return features

    num_tokens = features.shape[0]
    token_indices = torch.arange(num_tokens, device=features.device)
    boundary_mask = position_ids[1:] <= position_ids[:-1]
    segment_starts = torch.cat(
        (
            torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.bool, device=features.device),
            boundary_mask,
        )
    )
    segment_ends = torch.cat(
        (
            boundary_mask,
            torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.bool, device=features.device),
        )
    )

    rows = token_indices[:, None]
    columns = token_indices[None, :]
    starts = torch.where(
        segment_starts[None, :] & (columns <= rows), columns, 0
    ).amax(dim=1)
    ends = torch.where(
        segment_ends[None, :] & (columns >= rows),
        columns,
        token_indices[-1],
    ).amin(dim=1)
    flip_indices = starts + ends - token_indices
    return features[flip_indices]
```

This implementation matched the existing eager behavior exactly for 6,400 generated packed and padded cases covering token lengths 1 through 64. With the other required Neuron/plugin fixes held constant, replacing this helper allowed fullgraph warmup to pass at batch 1 and batch 4 on AWS Trainium2; text serving completed 100/100 requests at both batch sizes, and the complete text/image test reported `2 passed`. The temporary is `O(T^2)`, but the tested SigLIP text length is 64; a more efficient fixed-shape implementation would also satisfy the request.

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- Replace the value-dependent reversal with a compile-safe implementation that preserves packed and padded sequence semantics.
- Add exhaustive small-boundary and randomized length-64 equivalence tests.
- Add a test that exercises SigLIP text embeddings without `--enforce-eager`.
- Add `@support_torch_compile` once the complete model path passes vLLM's compile tests.

Current main changed the helper in [#43107](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43107) to perform the dynamic boundary calculation on CPU. It still has value-dependent boundary cardinality and the model still lacks `@support_torch_compile`. We have not run current main on Neuron and are not claiming that current main fails; the hardware validation above is against vLLM 0.24.0, so the proposed implementation must be adapted and tested against current main.

### Alternatives

- Continue serving SigLIP with `--enforce-eager`. This is the upstream-tested path from #28365, but it does not serve backends that require static fullgraph compilation.
- Carry the validated replacement as a downstream compatibility patch. This works, but duplicates model logic downstream and must be version-guarded.
- Insert a graph break around the dynamic reversal. This may help partial-compilation backends but does not provide fullgraph support and is unsuitable for static ahead-of-time backends.

### Additional context

- Latest release checked: v0.27.1.
- Current main inspected: `8878ebd8fdfe286eb7cf00ccbb6919bc7a40b1dd`, 2026-08-17.
- Hardware validation: `trn2.48xlarge`, vLLM 0.24.0, torch 2.11.0, torch-neuronx `2.12.3.0.26429+3f245a2.dev`, neuronx-cc `2.0.273779.0a0+c78bd1dd`, Python 3.12.11.
- Model validated: `google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384` at revision `9fdffc58afc957d1a03a25b10dba0329ab15c2a3`.
- Duplicate searches for `SigLIP torch.compile`, `SigLIP dynamic shape`, and `_flip_sequences_by_position_ids` found no matching issue on 2026-08-17.
